title: Dual-modal flexible sensors based on flexible Ti3C2Tx (MXene)-bacterial cellulose composites for neural network-assisted pronunciations, shapes, and materials perception
authors: Yihan Qiu, Bingzheng Zhang, Nuozhou Yi, Zhen Wang, Minghua You, Peidi Zhou, Chan Zheng, Qiaohang Guo, Kaihuai Yang, Mingcen Weng
conclusion: the combination of the dual-mode nature and the neural network model is utilized to provide new options for environmental sensing in areas such as robotics and human-robot interaction. 4 Conclusions In conclusion, MXene-BC composites obtained by combining MXene and BC via vacuum self-assembly technique have excellent electrical conductivity (conductivity up to 353.77 S m−1 ) as well as excellent mechanical properties (fracture stress of 41.09 MPa and Young's modulus of 7.34 GPa), which make up for the limitations of a single component. At the same time, the sensor combining this composite and the H2 SO4 -PVA hydrogel material is dual-mode that it can be used as a pressure sensor as well as a proximity sensor. In pressure mode, it has high sensitivity (5.11 kPa−1 ), fast response/recovery time (10 ms/10 ms) and ultra-low detection threshold (1 Pa) enable precise monitoring of subtle physiological signals such as vocal cord vibrations. With a MLP neural network model, the sensor achieves 98.33 % accuracy in speech recognition, bridging the gap between human-machine interaction through natural and intuitive communication. In addition, the proximity sensor offers excellent hysteresis, reversibility and stability with a sensitivity of 0.63 mm−1 . Combined with 3D printing technology, the 6 × 6 × 3 sensor array created in this study enables real-time 3D shape reconstruction, providing important spatial sensing capabilities for robotics and automation. Combining the dual-mode nature of this sensor (pressure mode and proximity mode), a material recognition platform is constructed in this study. Through the difference in dielectric constant as well as Young's modulus between different materials, this study uses a MLP neural network model to train the capacitive response signals collected by the sensor. The final model obtained has an accuracy of 99.85 %, demonstrating the potential of this sensor in the field of environmental sensing. This work not only advances the design of flexible sensing materials but also expands their applications in human-machine interaction, robotics, and wearable electronics. Future research could explore scalable manufacturing techniques, long-term stability under extreme conditions, and integration with advanced machine learning models for broader multimodal sensing scenarios. By addressing these challenges, MXene-BC composites may pave the way for next-generation smart systems with enhanced adaptability and intelligence. abstract: In the contemporary digital era, where human-machine interaction and robotics are rapidly evolving, the application of bacterial cellulose (BC) in the field of sensors is gradually gaining attention but still faces many challenges in practical applications. Here, Ti3C2Tx (MXene) was combined with BC by vacuum self-assembly technique to prepare MXene-BC composites. MXene-BC composites effectively combine the excellent electrical conductivity of MXene with the robust mechanical properties of BC, which significantly extends its application in flexible electronic devices. The results showed that the MXene-BC composites had excellent mechanical properties (fracture stress up to 41.09 MPa and Young's modulus up to 7.34 GPa) and good electrical properties (conductivity up to 353.77 S m−1). The pressure sensors made with MXene-BC composites have fast response/recovery times (10 ms/10 ms), low detection thresholds (1 Pa), and excellent stability. The proximity sensors have good hysteresis, reversibility, response and stability. Notably, sensors based on MXene-BC composites can function as both pressure and proximity sensors. Basing on these properties, our combine 3D printing technology to create a proximity sensor array with shape recognition function. At the same time, combined with a multilayer perceptron neural network model, the dual-mode sensors can recognize pronunciations, and materials. It provides new options for the field of robotics and human-machine interaction.

title: Polyaniline nanowires anchored on MXene quantum dots/graphene composite fibers with 0D-1D-2D hierarchical structure for high-performance wearable supercapacitors
authors: Xiaoyu Jia, Yuan Du, Fanyu Xie, Hongwei Li, Rui Zhang, Xinxu Niu, Mei Zhang
conclusion: In conclusion, we designed the high-performance polyaniline nanowires modified MXene quantum dots /graphene composite fiber with 0D-1D-2D hierarchical structure. PANI@MQDs/GF prepared by microfluidics technique combined with wet spinning strategy realizes a point-sheet structure at the nanoscale and uniform distribution of polyaniline nanowires, which impedes the restacking of graphene nanosheets, mitigates the structural changes of polyaniline during charge/discharge processes, and brings large specific surface area and more electrochemical active sites. The effective combination by covalent bonds and 0D-1D-2D hierarchical structure of PANI@MQDs/GF also enhance the interfacial charge transfer and provide more accessible pathways for ion kinetic migration and accumulation, exhibiting a superior specific areal capacitance of 1691 mF cm−2 and an excellent energy density of 214.4 μWh cm−2 . A self-powered system is designed to power electronic devices. This study provides an efficient and easy-to-implement feasible idea for the continuous preparation of fiber electrodes with excellent performance, which is valuable for the future practical application of portable energy storage devices and flexible electronic equipment. abstract: Two-dimensional graphene and MXene are promising and attractive candidates as energy storage materials for wearable supercapacitors. However, low energy density derived from a serious restacking problem restricts their charge storage capacity and actual application for portable electronic devices. In this study, we report a microfluidic technique assisted wet spinning method for the fabrication of polyaniline nanowires modified MXene quantum dots/graphene composite fibers (PANI@MQDs/GF) with 0–1-2 dimensional (0D-1D-2D) hierarchical structure. The effective combination of multicomponents, strong synergistic effect at the nanoscales and 0D-1D-2D hierarchical structure of PANI@MQDs/GFs not only alleviate the restacking of graphene nanosheets but also enhance interfacial charge transfer, more accessible sites and fast pathways for ion kinetic migration and accumulation, leading to excellent structural stability and electrochemical performance. Fiber-based flexible supercapacitors assembled by PANI@MQDs/GF exhibit a superior specific areal capacitance of 1691 mF cm−2 (for specific volumetric capacitance of 450 F cm−3), maintain a high capacitance retention of nearly 100 % after 9500 cycles, and achieve an excellent energy density of 214.4 μWh cm−2. The designed 0D-1D-2D hierarchical structure of composite fibers can also be extended to other lamellar materials, and exploit more possibilities of fiber-typed supercapacitors for portable/wearable electronics application.

title: Construction of novel bifunctional electrocatalyst CuCoTiO2/Mxene for supercapacitor and sensor application
authors: Ganesh Abinaya Meenakshi, Mahalingam Agalya, Rajendran Surya, Subramanian Sakthinathan, Shanmugam Kiruthika, Te-Wei Chiu, Sandhya Sukumaran
conclusion: A simple synthetic hydrothermal route has been employed for the synthesis of CuCoTiO2 /Mxene- 2,4, and 6 h. It has been confirmed by physicochemical characterization using XRD, FT-IR, EDX, SEM, and HR-TEM studies. The CuCoTiO2 /Mxene - 6, 4 and 2 h electrode material exhibited a capacitance of 500 F g−1 , 472 F g−1 , and 400 F g−1 at 5 mV/s in aqueous 2 M KOH by CV analysis. The as-fabricated CuCoTiO2 /Mxene- 6h exhibited an energy density of 19.6 Whkg−1 at a specific power of 742.7 Wkg-1 . Remarkably, a small capacitance loss was detected for CuCoTiO2 /Mxene- 6h electrode, and it retained Csp of 91 % after 4000 GCD cycles. These findings have suggested that CuCoTiO2 /Mxene- 6h electrode is a suitable candidate for electrochemical SC applications, and in combination with other materials, the supercapacitive behavior may be enhanced further. In addition, the GCE/CuCoTiO2 /Mxene - 2,4, and 6 h detected the antibiotic compound FZD with the higher sensitivity and low LOD 2.66 μA μM−1 cm−2 and 16.1 nM. Hence the GCE/CuCoTiO2 /Mxene- 6 h would serve as a potential bifunctional catalyst for supercapacitor and electrochemical applications. abstract: The dual challenges of reducing environmental pollution and meeting increasing energy demands necessitate innovative energy storage solutions. Supercapacitors, which bridge the gap between batteries and conventional capacitors, present a promising pathway. In this study, Cu-based delafossite-type materials (ABO₂) and MXenes are explored for their complementary properties. CuCoTiO₂ offers a layered structure with p-type conductivity, while MXenes, a class of 2D transition metal carbides, nitrides, or carbonitrides, exhibit atomic-layer thickness, high conductivity, tunable surface functional groups, superior hydrophilicity, and excellent electrochemical properties. A CuCoTiO₂/MXene composite was synthesized via a cost-effective hydrothermal method, optimized across different heating durations (2, 4, 6 h). Comprehensive characterization was performed using X-ray diffraction, field emission scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray microanalysis, Raman spectroscopy, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. The CuCoTiO2/Mxene - 6, 4 and 2 hr electrode material exhibited a capacitance of 500 F g−1 at 1 A/g. The CuCoTiO₂/MXene-6h//AC ASC composite demonstrated exceptional performance, achieving an energy density of 19.6 Wh·kg⁻1 at a specific power of 742.7 W kg⁻1. Additionally, it exhibited remarkable electrochemical sensing capabilities, with a sensitivity of 2.66 μA μM−1 cm−2 and a low detection limit of 16.1 nM for furazolidone. These results highlight the potential of CuCoTiO₂/MXene composites as bifunctional materials for high-performance supercapacitors and electrochemical detection applications.

title: Dual-molecule enhanced MXene films for high specific capacitance in supercapacitors
authors: Shiben Jiang, Yijie Shi, Linghong Lu, Changrui Hua, Yan Song, Jun Li
conclusion: In conclusion, we propose a new strategy for the synergistic modification of the surface of MXene nanosheets by ppy and 4-O-TEMPO dual-molecule, where self-supported film electrodes can be formed by vacuum filtration. Among them, 4-O-TEMPO can not only form hydrogen bonds with the surface of MXene, but more importantly, it is covalently attached to the edge of Ti3 C2 Tx through Ti-O. The nitroxide radicals provided by 4-O-TEMPO participate in the redox reaction, which can provide more pseudocapacitance. On the other hand, ppy is arranged on the surface of MXene through abundant hydrogen bonding interactions, which not only compensates for the low conductivity of nitroxide radicals, but also serves as a barrier to protect MXene from over-oxidation during the grafting process of 4-O-TEMPO. In addition, DFT elucidated the formation of an internal electric field at the interface of the dual-molecule with MXene, which accelerates the electron transport. As a result, the pMT electrode has a high specific capacitance of 530 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and still maintains 300 F g−1 at 50 A g−1 , exhibiting excellent rate performance. In addition, the constructed pMT//TPC ASC are able to achieve a maximum energy density of 23.8 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 300.2 W kg−1 . The present work not only successfully integrates the unique advantages of dual-molecule with the properties of MXene, but also provides a new perspective on the surface modification strategy of MXene. abstract: In order to solve the problem of restacking the two-dimensional layered structure of MXene without causing a decrease in its conductivity, electrochemical performance, and flexibility, this study innovatively proposes a dual-molecule synergistic strategy utilizing polypyrrole (ppy) and 4-O-TEMPO (TEMPO = 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidinyl-1-oxyl) to achieve high-capacitance MXene films. In this strategy, 4-O-TEMPO anchors to the surface and edges of Ti3C2Tx nanosheets through hydrogen and covalent bonds, with its nitroxide radicals participating in redox reactions to contribute additional pseudocapacitance. Additionally, ppy enhances the conductivity of the composite film by shortening the electron transport path and prevents MXene from excessive oxidized by 4-O-TEMPO. This bimolecular strategy effectively alleviates interlayer stacking in MXene while maintaining its conductivity and flexibility. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that Ti3C2O2 has stable interactions with 4-O-TEMPO, and the ternary system demonstrates excellent electronic and ion transport properties. As a result, the ppy/MXene/4-O-TEMPO (pMT) electrode achieves a specific capacitance of 530 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and retains 300 F g−1 at 50 A g−1. Additionally, the asymmetric supercapacitor reaches 23.8 Wh kg−1 energy density at 300.2 W kg−1 power density.

title: Recent advances in supercapacitors based on MXene surface modification: A review of symmetric and asymmetric electrodes material
authors: Ghobad Behzadi pour, Leila Fekri aval
conclusion: This review presents a comparative analysis of symmetric and asymmetric MXene-based supercapacitors, along with an examination of surface modifications applied to MXene electrodes through techniques such as doping, polymer decorations, anchoring of nickel materials, and the incorporation of coupled carbon nanomaterials. Most SSCs based on MXene exhibit a PD below 5000 W kg−1 and an ED lower than 70 Wh kg−1 . Furthermore, the cycling stability of these supercapacitors typically showed falls short of 25000 cycles. Moreover, it should be noted that the PD of most ASSCs based on MXene materials is below 8000 W kg−1 , while the ED is below 100 Wh kg−1 . Also, the cycling stability of most ASSCs based on MXene materials is less than 10000 cycles. In addition, a comparison between the Ragone plot and the SC of supercapacitors utilizing MXene highlights that the asymmetric electrode demonstrates a greater capacity to achieve higher PD/ED and SC. In the last two decades, the emergence of MXene-based supercapacitors has paved the way for advancements in high-efficiency energy storage technologies. The future of energy storage appears promising with MXene-based supercapacitors, which exhibit remarkable ED/PD and a high SC. These characteristics make them an ideal sustainable and efficient solution for storing energy.
abstract: MXene-based supercapacitors utilize symmetric or asymmetric electrodes. Symmetric electrodes use the same MXene material for positive/negative electrodes, providing balanced performance and stability. Asymmetric electrodes incorporate different MXene materials or combine MXene with other substances to enhance energy density (ED), stability, specific capacitance (SC), and power density (PD). The symmetric and asymmetric configurations make MXene-based supercapacitors versatile for various applications. In this review, we have summarized MXene-based supercapacitors using symmetric and asymmetric electrode materials. A comparative study has been done on the surface modification of the MXene-based supercapacitor electrodes using doping, polymer decorations, anchoring of nickel materials, and coupled carbon nanomaterials methods. The discoveries from this research serve as an invaluable reference for upcoming researchers, contributing to their comprehension of the performance and potential applications of MXene electrodes of supercapacitor technology.

title: Optimizing electrochemical performance of binder-free MXene-Templated zeolite electrodes via graphene quantum dots and hexagonal boron nitride doping for asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Syed Kashif Ali, Sajid Hussain, Md Rezaul Karim, Haseebul Hassan, Ahmed Althobaiti, Alsharef Mohammad, Yazen M. Alawaideh, Hala Ghannam
conclusion: This study successfully demonstrated the synthesis of MTZ, h-BN@MTZ, and GQDs@MTZ composites and evaluation in both half and full-cell configuration. Among the three materials, GQDs@MTZ exhibited superior specific capacity and capacitance, as confirmed by both CV and GCD analyses, owing to the high surface area, enhanced conductivity, and synergistic effects of the graphene quantum dots. The GQDs@MTZ//AC device demonstrated outstanding cycling stability with 97 % capacity retention after extended cycles and maintained a high coulombic efficiency of 95 % after 10,000 cycles. Furthermore, the GQDs@MTZ//AC device achieved an impressive energy density of 93.17 Wh/kg and a power density of 1240 W/kg, making it a promising candidate for high-performance energy storage applications. abstract: Supercapacitors gain significant attraction in materials science and energy storage due to their exceptional thermal stability, quick charging and discharging capabilities, environmental sustainability, and long cycle life. This study presents unique titanium based MXene-templated zeolites (MTZ) as a novel electrode for energy storage devices. Two variations are developed, one modified with 5 % hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN@MTZ) and another doped with 5 % graphene quantum dots (GQDs@MTZ). The h-BN enhances structural integrity and prevents MXene restacking, thereby facilitating more efficient charge transport, while the GQDs improve charge retention and transfer capabilities. In a three-electrode setup, GQDs@MTZ exhibits a remarkable specific capacity of 1873 C/g, surpassing MTZ (948 C/g) and h-BN@MTZ (1425 C/g). Furthermore, when combined with activated carbon, the GQDs@MTZ//AC asymmetric supercapacitor achieves an outstanding energy density of 93.17 Wh/kg and a power density of 1240 W/kg. The device shows 97 % capacity retention after 10,000 cycles. The work opens the path for more investigation of MXene-based blended electrodes in energy storage devices.

title: Hierarchy hollow Al-doped CoP nanocubes interconnected MXene composite for solid-state asymmetrical supercapacitors
authors: Emad S. Goda, Byung Gi Kim, Dong Hwan Wang
conclusion: We developed a novel hollow and hierarchical Al-doped CoP nanocubes@MXene composite through the room-temperature precipitation of AlCoPBA and phosphorization in a tube furnace using NaH2 PO2 as a phosphorus source. Functional groups on MXene can control the growth of CoP with a smaller size reaching ∼5 nm without any observable aggregation, and thus, it can provide a higher surface area and more reaction with electrolyte ions when applied as the SCs electrode. A large amount of energy can be stored by the AlCoP@MXene heterostructure with a capacitance value of 2577 F/g calculated at 1 A/g as an adjusted current density that is 1.5 and 3.61 times that of the pristine AlCoP and CoP, respectively, and prolonged cycle life (90.1 % after 7000 cycles). In addition, the device assembled using the anode from the ZnFeS@NG core-shell hybrid had an ultrahigh energy of 85.6 Wh/kg when the power density was altered at 678.5 W/kg with a considerable cycle life of 88 % after repetitive 10,000 GCD cycles. These electroactive properties were comparable to those of other formerly prepared ASCs that offer new avenues for the metal doping of cobalt phosphides as efficient electrodes for being integrated into flexible energy-storage devices. abstract: Cobalt phosphide (CoP) offers promising electroactive properties for energy storage due to its considerable theoretical capacity. However, interfacial instability during cycling and poor interfacial charge transfer significantly limit its practical application. In this study, a straightforward approach was introduced to synthesize hollow hierarchical Al-doped CoP nanocubes bridged by MXene sheets. The new composite was prepared using the room co-precipitation method of bimetallic AlCoPBA on the MXene surface, which was further phosphorated in a tube furnace using NaH2PO2 as a phosphorus source. Conductive MXene sheets upgrade the supercapacitive properties of the CoP-based electrode by integrating the advantages of 3D porous morphology and Al doping. Further, the AlCoP@MXene heterostructure can store a large amount of energy as indicated by the capacitance value of 2577 F/g calculated at 1 A/g as an adjusted current density (1.5 and 3.61 times that of pristine AlCoP and CoP, respectively) and the prolonged cycle life (90.1 % after 7000 cycles). In addition, the device assembled using the anode from the ZnFeS@NG core-shell hybrid achieves an ultrahigh energy of 85.6 Wh/kg when the power density is altered at 678.5 W/kg with a considerable cycle life of 88 % after repetitive 10,000 galvanostatic charge–discharge cycles.

title: Utilization of Ti3C2Tx MXenes on carbonyl functionalized carbon fiber electrodes
authors: Piers Coia, Bhagya Dharmasiri, David J. Hayne, Timothy Harte, Sabina Dann, Ben Newman, Elmer Austria, Behnam Akhavan, Mia Angela N. Judicpa, Kevinilo P. Marquez, Ken Aldren S. Usman, Jizhen Zhang, Joselito Razal, Luke C. Henderson
conclusion: This article represents a novel method to coordinate MXenes to carbon fiber to expand its potential uses and drastically increase specific capacitance and maintain improvements in mechanical properties. This research is intended to lead to a scalable modified CF tow to manufacture CF electrodes on an industrial scale. The first method of using anthraquinone moieties as a cheap and scalable surface modification to bind MXenes through their available carbonyl groups. Two different analogues named AQ-1 and AQ-2 were used to successfully bind MXenes through both ex-situ and in-situ preparation. AQ-2 , when prepared via both methods depicted the highest capacitance of 31.7F/g and 11.2F/g for the ex-situ method (labelled AQ-2-MX ) and in-situ method (labelled AQ-2 –3 min-MX ) respectively. This represents a 15.1 fold and 5.3 fold improvements in specific capacitance for AQ-2-MX and AQ-2 –3 min-MX respectively, over the control-MX sample. Importantly, when MXenes were applied to the samples prepared via ex-situ the improvements in IFSS were maintained. While the mechanical properties are varied across AQ-MX tows, the capacitance increases represent some of the highest capacitance values for carbon fiber based electrodes (Fig. 11 ). The second method was used to apply more high-value applications by using COF modified CF and coating in MXenes. All COF-MX tows exhibited significant increases in specific capacitance of up to a 29.2x between MXene modified and non-MXene modified for the MA-PMDA-MX sample. This depicts that while the initial capacitance was low, the affinity of the surface for MXene coordination is much higher than control unmodified CF. the MA-NTCDA-MX sample also depicted an excellent increase in capacitance to an excellent value of 29.4F/g representing a 17.3 fold increase over the control-MX fiber. Most improvements in IFSS were maintained when the MXene coating was applied, and the underlying properties were maintained. Future work involves being able to apply the in-situ AQ modification to an CF manufacturing plant to determine if similar improvements can be made to a continuous tow. On top of this, exploration into other COF properties can be completed to determine their viable use in high-value uses such as CO2 capture. abstract: MXenes possess unique properties such as their 2D structure which make them excellent for energy storage applications. However, the majority of benefits offered by the MXenes are diminished when transitioning to the macroscale. To overcome this, one effective method is to use MXenes as thin films or coatings. In this work, the surface of carbon fiber was modified to introduce carbonyl functional groups, facilitating a larger surface loading of MXenes. Anthraquinone (AQ) moieties were grafted via an ex-situ method and an in-situ method which was analogous to scale-up conditions. These modifications were then used to coordinate titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) MXenes to the CF surface. A maximum capacitance of 31.7 F/g for AQ-2-MX was observed, which represents a 14.8 fold increase over the control, along with an interfacial shear strength (IFSS) of 45.4 ± 4.5 MPa, an increase of 39 % for AQ-1-MX. Polyimide covalent organic frameworks (PI-COFs) were attached to CF via a graft-from approach and used to coordinate MXenes for high value applications. Excellent increases in capacitance to a maximum of 29.4 F/g for MA-NTCDA-MX were observed and cycling stability of 99.5 % in aqueous electrolyte for MA-PTCDA-MX. Increases in IFSS were maintained when the MXene coating was applied with a value of 51.7 MPa ± 4.2 MPa for MA-PTCDA-MX, a 58 % increase. This highlights the ability of MXenes to coordinate to carbonyl-modified CF, enabling both scalable applications via AQ and high value applications via COFs, while expanding the utility of CF beyond its structural applications.

title: Fabrication of binder-free MXene/reduced graphene oxide/W18O49 film electrode for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Ruidong Li, Baoquan Liang, Hong Gao, Jie Li, Qianwen Liu, Lihua Chen, Shuxin Song, Bingyue Zheng, Tingxi Li, Yong Ma
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  Herein, W 18 O 49 and rGO are separately synthesized using hydrothermal and reduction methods. Subsequently, MXene, MXene/rGO, MXene/rGO/W 18 O 49 films are successfully fabricated. The incorporation of W 18 O 49 or rGO results in films with increased ion-active sites as well as enhanced ion-transport channels, thereby exhibiting excellent electrochemical properties. Notably, MXene/rGO/W 18 O 49 film demonstrates particularly outstanding properties, achieving 581.2 F g −1 specific capacitance at 1 A g −1 . MXene/rGO/W 18 O 49 //AC ASC is fabricated on the basis of MXene/rGO/W 18 O 49 film as the positive electrode. ASC boasts 1.6 V voltage window and maintains 87.1 % capacitance even after 10,000 cycles at 3 A g −1 . Furthermore, device delivers 43.2 Wh kg −1 energy density at 799.8 W kg −1 power density. The prepared MXene/rGO/W 18 O 49 film offers the advantages of simplicity and ease of preparation. This approach serves as a valuable guidance to explore flexible devices.
abstract: MXene nanosheets tend to aggregate during operation, significantly impeding their utility. Yet, the defect can be validly solved by incorporating intercalation substances. Herein, binder-free MXene/reduced graphene oxide/W18O49 (MXene/rGO/W18O49) film is fabricated as supercapacitor electrode. W18O49 and rGO can foster the formation of interlayer structure with MXene nanosheets. This enlarging of interlamellar spacing facilitates establishing multidirectional ion transport routes and exposing more active sites. MXene/rGO/W18O49 manifests 581.2 F g−1 specific capacitance at 1 A g−1. Moreover, the assembled asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC), comprising of MXene/rGO/W18O49 and activated carbon (AC) as positive and negative electrodes, exhibits 1.6 V voltage window, along with 43.2 Wh kg−1 energy density at 799.8 W kg−1 power density. Notably, it retains 87.1 % capacitance after 10,000 cycles at 3 A g−1. Optimization strategy for MXene/rGO/W18O49 film as electrode not only illustrates the viability of MXene advancement, but also offers significant technical backing for its utilization in the next generation of flexible devices.

title: In-situ electrochemical XRD and raman probing of ion transport dynamics in ionic liquid-etched Ti3C2Tx MXene for energy storage applications
authors: Jeremiah Hao Ran Huang, Shih-Wen Tseng, I-Wen Peter Chen
conclusion: In this study, in-situ Raman spectroscopy reveals that during the discharge process, Ti3 C2 (OH)2 gradually loses H+ ions, leading to the formation of Ti3 C2 O2 . Conversely, during charging, the reappearance of H+ ions gradually convert Ti3 C2 O2 back to Ti3 C2 (OH)2 . By analyzing these H+ interactions between MXene layers, we can infer the overall charge–discharge mechanism. For further validation, in-situ XRD was employed to monitor these structural changes in real time. However, due to the small size of H+ ions, direct observation was challenging, so we introduced TMA+ ions to simulate the process. During discharge, as Ti3 C2 O2 forms, we observe a shift of the MXene (002) plane to lower 2θ value, indicating expansion of the interlayer spacing like the cation release seen with H+ ions. This observation suggests that TMA+ ions intercalate in a similar manner to H+ ions, which enhances the activation of Ti3 C2 O2 sites and increases Ti3 C2 O2 formation. This mechanism aligns with previous findings, where the presence of oxygen functional groups on the MXene surface facilitates water molecule insertion, increasing the D-spacing of the MXene (002) plane. Together, these results support our proposed charge storage mechanism, highlighting the role of oxygen surface groups and interlayer spacing changes as key factors in MXene’s electrochemical behavior. In conclusion, this study successfully demonstrates the etching of Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase using TMATFB, resulting in the formation of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene with oxygen-containing functional groups. The characterization results from Raman spectroscopy, FTIR, and XPS consistently indicate the presence of these functional groups, which significantly enhance the specific capacitance of MXene. The electrochemical analyses reveal that the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene exhibits a high specific capacitance of 417.4F/g at a scan rate of 1 mV/s in 1 M H2 SO4 . In situ Raman observations confirm the reversible transportation of H+ ions, leading to the conversion between Ti3 C2 O2 and Ti3 C2 (OH)2 . In situ XRD measurements further validate the interlayer spacing changes due to cation intercalation. Overall, the findings highlight the potential of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene in high-performance energy storage systems and provide a foundation for further exploration of different etching mechanisms to optimize MXene properties for various applications. I-Wen Peter Chen: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Supervision.
abstract: This study focuses on understanding the electrochemical behavior of Ti3C2Tx MXene synthesized using tetramethylammonium tetrafluoroborate (TMATFB) as an etching agent for the Ti3AlC2 MAX phase. Through in situ Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction (XRD), we investigate the charge storage mechanisms and surface transformations of TMATFB-etched MXene. The results indicate that Ti3C2Tx MXene undergoes reversible H+ ion intercalation, achieving a specific capacitance of 417.4F/g at 1 mV/s in 1 M H2SO4. This reversible process is characterized by a transformation between Ti3C2O2 and Ti3C2(OH)2 on the MXene surface, highlighting the role of oxygen-rich functional groups in enhancing pseudocapacitive behavior. These insights contribute to the understanding of MXene’s electrochemical potential in energy storage systems.

title: Synthesis and properties of 2D MXenes and their composite electrodes for supercapacitors
authors: Mengbin Li, Lizhong He
conclusion: 5  Conclusion and outlook  In summary, MXene is considered extremely promising for energy storage. Compared with carbon materials, conductive polymers, and conventional electrode materials, MXene has the advantages of high electrical conductivity, great specific surface area, and unique surface chemistry. Future investigation on MXene materials may focus on the effect of various precursor materials on the multiple performance, the design and construction of functionality MXenes, and synthesis approaches to optimize the bottom-up and top-down strategies by selectively etching the layered parent MAX precursors. Furthermore, the energy storage mechanism of the MXene-based composite electrodes is the main focus in the further because a deep understanding of the mechanism is prerequisite for design and construction of MXene-based electrode towards high performance supercapacitors. Also, some intrinsic properties such as chemical and thermal stability, and electronic properties is also the utmost importance to energy storage performance. Thus, the aim of this review is to present the intrinsic properties and fabrication methods of MXenes, as well as the latest achievements and progress in the MXene-based composite electrodes for supercapacitors.  Even though MXene was discovered by Yury's group in 2011 and several researchers have conducted extensive investigations in a variety of sectors throughout the past 13 years, certain shortcomings in synthesis and application still exist, which have an impact on the future development of MXene in commercialization: (1) MXene still needs to be further investigated in terms of antioxidant. Although cryogenic/inert gas modification and storage is the current approach to solve this problem, much efforts are still needed in this area; (2) As well all know, the energy storage performance of MXene is largely affected by the surface functional groups. In terms of surface functionalization, current investigations mainly focus on the random modification/regulation of the surface chemistries. Therefore, deep studies on the integration of specific functional groups in a controlled manner on the surface of MXene materials are important. (3) MXene has a certain advantage in weight capacitance because it belongs to two-dimensional materials, but there is a certain lack in volume-specific capacitance. Therefore, it is important to design special structures such as delamination or pleating to reduce the void space for a purpose of preventing capacitance loss. (4) Introducing defects into the MXene is an effective way to regulate its electrochemical performance, but the corresponding mechanism is unclear. Thus, it is necessary to delve into the defect-dominant mechanism for improving of electrochemical performance of MXene-based electrode. (5) MXene self-stacking is still a significant problem, which is closely related to the electrical capacity of the electrodes used in MXene-based supercapacitors. It is crucial to explore effective ways to add supports between MXene sheet layers to prepare the MXene-based composite electrode with hierarchical morphology to prevent nanosheets from self-stacking. Although MXene has advanced significantly in the field of supercapacitors just 13 years after its discovery, supercapacitors based on MXene are still in the beginning stage, and industrial production is also not realized. Nevertheless, as an emerging 2D material with many merits, we believe that MXene and its derivatives will shine in the field of energy storage.
abstract: MXenes, first discovered in 2011 by etching their parent MAX phase, represent a novel type of 2D materials with unique electrochemical and electronic characteristics, becoming the cutting-edge research materials in a wide variety of applications. Their unique merits, including metal-like conductivity, high density, abundant and tunable surface end-groups and unique two-dimensional planar structure, have positioned them as promising 2D material in the field of supercapacitors in recent years. Therefore, a timely overview of MXenes is essential to provide guidance for advanced research in energy storage materials. In this review, we aim to summarize the recent progress on MXene research on supercapacitors. This review begins with the intrinsic properties such as mechanical, electrical and stable properties, and then focuses on the multiple synthesis strategies of MXenes, including top-down and bottom-up methods. Most importantly, the application of MXenes and their composites (including MXene/Metal LDHs, MXene/Metal sulfides, MXene/Metal oxides, MXene/Conductive polymers and MXene/Carbon nanomaterials) in supercapacitors as electrodes are mainly analyzed along with the detailed mechanism and electrochemical performance. Finally, an outlook on the current challenges and future opportunities of MXene-based supercapacitors is presented.

title: Multi-electron redox asymmetric supercapacitors based on quinone-coupled viologen derivatives and Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: M. Boota, M. Rajesh, M. Bécuwe
conclusion: In summary, we have synthesized quinone-functionalized viologen molecules by simple mixing at room temperature for pseudocapacitive applications. When coated on rGO sheets and tested in a three-electrode setup, these hybrids exhibited distinct redox peaks and showed improved capacitance than their pristine counterpart under positive potentials. Optimized hybrids were paired with the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene as negative electrodes to manufacture all-pseudocapacitive asymmetric devices, which exhibited expanded voltage window of 1.5 V in 3 M H2 SO4 , high-rate electrochemical behavior (64 F/g (10 mV/s), 16 F/g (5000 mV/s)), good energy density (~20 Wh/kg), and capacitance retention of 80% after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles. We also found that the charge storage mechanism of single electrodes as well as asymmetric devices is predominantly capacitive at lowest tested scan rates where diffusion current dominates electrode performance. We stress that further performance of the electrodes can be achieved by designing electrode architectures, confining organic molecules within defined pores and by pairing optimized electrodes with other reported MXenes and conductive metal organic frameworks. Credit author statement Muhammad Boota : Conceptualization; Methodology; Formal analysis; Writing original draft; Writing -Review & Editing. Murugesan Rajesh : Methodology; Formal analysis; Writing -Review & Editing. Matthieu Bécuwe : Conceptualization; Methodology; Formal analysis; Writing -Review & Editing.
abstract: Organic materials are emerging for the pseudocapacitors as they offer high theoretical redox capacitance and can be derived from the renewable sources. They are composed of non-metals, resulting in light weight, flexible, and potentially low-cost devices. While there are hundreds of commercial organic molecules available and nearly unlimited can be synthesized, only a handful of them are suitable for the pseudocapacitive applications. Therefore, the discovery of innovative organic materials beyond conventional pseudocapacitive organic materials (e.g. quinones, conducting polymers, etc.) is much needed for the sustainable pseudocapacitors. Here, for the first time, we report quinone-functionalized viologen molecules as a high capacitance/rate pseudocapacitive organic electrode material on hybridization with reduced graphene oxide sheets. Given the reliable pseudocapacitance of quinone-functionalized viologen-based hybrids under positive potentials, optimized electrodes were paired with two-dimensional titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) MXene as negative electrodes to manufacture multi-electron redox asymmetric supercapacitors. The resulting full devices were capable to store charge within enlarged voltage window up to 1.5 V in 3 M H2SO4. In addition, these devices exhibited ultrahigh rate performance (~77% capacitance retention from 10 to 1,000 mV/s), energy density (~20 Wh/kg), and capacitance retention of 80% after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles.

title: Multiscale porous structured MXene: Synthesis, design and applications in batteries and supercapacitors
authors: Chen Chen, Xincao Tang, Mengjie Wang, Yanan Ma, Siliang Wang, Yang Yue
conclusion: Summary and outlook   Summary   Research advances in multiscale pore structures of 2D MXene provide important opportunities to regulate the diffusion behavior and chemical kinetics of active materials, thereby significantly advancing the development of energy storage devices. By scientifically designing and controlling pore parameters (such as pore size, pore orientation, shape and porosity), can effectively enhance the efficiency of ion/electron transport and promote the permeation of different electrolytes through various pores, thus optimizing the electrochemical performance of MXene. Particularly, the synergistic effects across multiple pore scales, the quantitative regulation of pore sizes from micropores, mesopores and macropores, and the precise control of pore geometries have been proven to be key strategies in achieving high-performance MXene electrode. Therefore, fully utilizing interdisciplinary knowledge in materials science, chemistry, and physics to precisely design and control pore parameters further advances the application of multiscale pore MXene, which will offer a more comprehensive solution to improving the electrochemical performance of energy storage devices.   Outlook   Multiscale porous MXene have demonstrated impressive performance in laboratory-scale energy storage applications, but still faces several unresolved issues. To bridge the gap between academic innovation and industrial translation, key scientific and engineering challenges must be addressed.   1.  Fluoride-dependent synthesis methods: Currently, large-scale fabrication of MXene still relies heavily on fluorinated etchants (e.g., HF, LiF/HCl), which raise environmental, safety, and cost issues, limiting industrial scalability.    2.  Lack of electrolyte-pore matching principles: How different pore sizes (and their hierarchical combinations) interact with various electrolytes, including differing in ionic size, solvation shell, or charge has not been systematically established, leading to deteriorated electrochemical performance.    3.  Unclear structure-performance relationship of multiscale pores: The optimal electrochemical performance and spatial distribution of micropores, mesopores, and macropores remain poorly understood, particularly regarding their integrated effect onion transport, mechanical integrity, and volumetric energy density.     To address these challenges, we make several recommendations:   1.  Green and scalable synthesis: Fluoride-free routes (e.g., molten salt etching [ 34 ] and electrochemical exfoliation) should be developed to enable safer, environmentally friendly, and industrially viable MXene production.    2.  Systematic electrolyte–pore compatibility studies: Future research should explore how pore size and hierarchy affect ion accessibility in electrolytes with different ionic radius, solvation shells, and charges. Understanding these interactions is crucial for tailoring MXene structures to diverse electrolyte systems and maximizing charge transport efficiency [ 339 ].    3.  Apply bio-inspired and data-driven design strategies ( Fig. 11  ): Principles derived from biological systems, such as Murray's Law and Fibonacci sequence-based distributions [ 340–342 ], can offer useful guidance for optimizing hierarchical pore design. In parallel, deep learning algorithms and data-driven models should be applied to predict ideal pore configurations and accelerate the design of high-performance MXene-based electrodes [ 343–347 ].
abstract: The porous structure of 2D MXene play a critical role in addressing ion transport and kinetic limitations of traditional electrodes, enabling significant improvements of electrochemical performance for energy storage applications. In contrast to previous reviews those have focused only on a specific type of pore structure, this review systematically summarizes the construction strategies and structural properties of micropores, mesopores, and macropores of MXene electrodes, and outlines their evolution from single-scale regulation to multiscale synergistic coupling enhancement. On the basis of a brief review of the synthesis methods and physicochemical properties of MXene, we detail the introduced key structural parameters (e.g. pore size, pore geometry), and elucidate their synergistic effect on ion/electron transport pathways, active site exposure, and electrolyte wettability. Furthermore, this review analyzes the unique roles and synergies of different pore scales in energy storage mechanisms, and discusses the application progress of multiscale porous MXene in lithium-ion batteries, zinc-ion batteries, supercapacitors, and so on. This review aims to provide practical insights into the rational design and application of multiscale porous MXene, thereby promoting advancements in energy storage technologies and related fields.

title: Self-standing porous MXene film via in situ formed microgel induced by 2- methylimidazole for high rate supercapacitor
authors: Sai Yan, Chenjing Shi, Zhen Tian, Dan Li, Yanjun Chen, Li Guo, Yanzhong Wang
conclusion: In summary, we purpose a new strategy to prepare the self-standing porous MXene film via the in-situ formation MXene microgel induced by 2-MeIM and vacuum filtration. The hydrogen ion released from the deprotonation of 2-MeIM and hydron bonding interaction between 2-MeIM and MXene nanosheets break the electrostatic balance of MXene nanosheets, resulting in the assembly of MXene nanosheets into 3D MXene microgel. The formed MXene microgel in MXene suspension not only reduces the time of vacuum filtration to prepare the porous M-MXene-5 film but also facilitates the electrolyte ions transport. Meanwhile, 2-methylimidazole acts as an intercalated agent to increase the layer spacing of MXene. As a result, the M-MXene film has an excellent rate performance, demonstrating the specific capacitance of 223.4 F g−1 even at a scan rate of 1000 mV s−1 . Moreover, the assembled M-MXene-5//AC ASC device displays 16.88 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 799 W kg−1 , and maintains 13.11 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 8 kW kg−1 . Meanwhile, the ASC device shows the exceptional cycling stability with the capacitance retention of 90.4 % after 10 000 cycles. This work opens a new way to prepare the porous MXene film with excellent electrochemical properties for high rate supercapacitors.
abstract: Ti3C2Tx MXene has been considered a potential supercapacitor electrode material on account of its fast electron transfer performance, large volume pseudocapacitance, excellent hydrophilicity and mechanical properties. However, the serious stacking of MXene nanosheets reduced the exposed active sites and hindered diffusion of ions, leading to bad electrochemical property. Here, we report a strategy to transform MXene nanosheets into 3D MXene microgels induced by 2-methylimidazole. Benefitting from the existence of microgels, it facilitates the rapid vacuum filtration to prepare the porous MXene film, thus enhancing the ion transfer efficiency. Furthermore, 2-methylimidazole can also act as an intercalated agent to increase the layer spacing of MXene nanosheets. Therefore, the as-prepared porous MXene film demonstrates a superior rate capacity, and its capacitance reaches 223.4 F g−1 at the scan rates of 1000 mV s−1. Moreover, the assembled MXene//AC asymmetrical supercapacitor displays a 16.88 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 799 W kg−1, and maintains 13.11 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 8 kW kg−1. This work develops a simple way to prepare the porous MXene film for supercapacitors with excellent electrochemical performance.

title: High-performance aqueous zinc-ion hybrid micro-supercapacitors enabled by surface-modified Ti3C2 MXene anode and polar organic molecule intercalated AlxV2O5 cathode
authors: Weifeng Liu, Jixuan Zhang, Jitao Li, Zhuang Ma, Lingling Sun, Yamin Feng, Long Zhang
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In this study, a high-performance, low-cost, and stable AZHMSCs (summarized in Table S3–S4 ) was engineered through rational material design and structural optimization. The key breakthrough of this study is the synergistic modification of anode and cathode materials to effectively address critical challenges such as sluggish ion kinetics, structural instability, and low energy density observed in conventional AZHMSCs. A deep alkali treatment was employed to synthesize the m-Ti 3 C 2 MXene anode material, wherein inactive –F functional groups were replaced with O-rich surface terminal functional groups. This modification not only alleviated the stacking effect of MXene layers but also enhanced the Zn 2+ adsorption capacity of the material, as confirmed by DFT calculations. The resulting 3D interconnected network generated rapid ion-diffusion paths, achieving a remarkable specific capacitance of 1231.8 mF cm −2 at 1.0 mA cm −2 and excellent rate performance. Further, Al  x  V 2 O 5 -NMP used as the cathode material to stabilize the layered structure and accelerate Zn 2+ migration. The strong electrostatic interaction between NMP and pre-intercalated Al 3+ minimized structural collapse of the cathode during cycling, and its weak binding with Zn 2+ ensured efficient ion mobility. The cathode exhibited a high specific capacity of 327.78 μAh cm −2 at 0.5 mA cm −2 and retained its structural integrity for 5000 cycles. By integrating the optimized m-Ti 3 C 2 MXene anode and Al  x  V 2 O 5 -NMP cathode, the assembled AZHMSCs exhibited exceptional performance: an energy density of 105.15 μWh cm −2 at 0.475 mW cm −2 , power density of 9.5 mW cm −2 at 39.53 μWh cm −2 , and 89.29 % capacity retention after 3000 cycles. In addition, the device demonstrated excellent mechanical flexibility, maintaining 93.27 % of its capacity under 90° bending, showing its potential for wearable electronics. This study highlights the significance of optimizing material properties and their synergies in enhancing Zn 2+ storage, and outlines a pathway for developing advanced micro-energy storage devices, with future work aiming to scale up production and explore hybrid designs for widespread use in portable and flexible electronics (summarized in Table S5 ).
abstract: The Ti3C2Tx MXene has emerged as an ideal anode material for aqueous Zn-ion hybrid micro-supercapacitors (AZHMSCs) due to its high conductivity, excellent stretchability, and modifiable surface functional groups. However, the interlayer stacking effect and inert –F functional groups limit its ion transport and charge storage capabilities. In this study, a deep alkali treatment strategy is proposed to convert Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets into m-Ti3C2 MXene nanofibers with oxygen-rich surface terminal functional groups. This structure not only alleviates interlayer stacking but also shows enhanced Zn2+ adsorption affinity via oxygen groups, resulting in a specific capacitance of 1231.8 mF cm−2 at 1 mA cm−2. Meanwhile, the cathode employs polar organic molecules, specifically NMP, intercalated into AlxV2O5. The strong electrostatic interaction between NMP and pre-embedded aluminum ions improves material structural stability (96.05 % capacity retention after 5000 cycles) and enhances specific capacity (327.78 μAh cm−2 at 0.5 mA cm−2). AZHMSCs assembled with these modified electrodes exhibit excellent electrochemical performance: an energy density of 105.15 μWh cm−2 at a power density of 0.48 mW cm−2, capacity retention rate of 89.29 % after 3000 cycles, and good bending stability. This study offers a novel approach for electrode design and the construction of high-performance micro-energy storage devices.

title: Advancements and approaches in developing MXene-based hybrid composites for improved supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Thibeorchews Prasankumar, Kaaviah Manoharan, N.K. Farhana, Shahid Bashir,  K. Ramesh, S. Ramesh, Vigna K. Ramachandaramurthy
conclusion: 8  Conclusion  This review examines supercapacitors in detail, including their specifications, applications, development of electrode materials, and principles of operation. It was briefly mentioned how supercapacitors are categorized based on their mechanisms. The review centers on the most recent advancements in MXenes and supercapacitor research. MXenes of various kinds are synthesized and their combinations are investigated. The most thoroughly studied material is Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene, and research is currently underway. Several synthesis techniques used during the MAX phase are briefly reviewed in the current review. There are many different etching procedures available for creating MXenes, including F-free, fluoride-based, and HF acid etching. It is crucial to remember that the range of unique morphologies and adjustable surfaces could be primarily attributed to the etching circumstances. It was discovered that combining MXenes with other materials, like carbon, polymers, transition metal oxides, and MOF, for the supercapacitor electrode material improved both the electrochemical and overall mechanical performance. Non-etheless, it is frequently noted that MXene/transition metal oxide composites have poor mechanical characteristics. As a result, we hope that our analysis will help researchers identify suitable MXene and activated carbon composite energy storage systems to help them overcome obstacles. Furthermore, the summary offered in this review will help future investigators to carry out their research on MXene dispersal and denudation techniques in order to produce MXene hybrids with enhanced electrochemical performance.
abstract: The rapid increase in population and widespread use of energy-consuming technologies are contributing to a substantial increase in the world's energy consumption. Supercapacitors have recently become a more desirable alternative due to their quick charging and discharging times, high power densities, and extended cycle lives. For many researchers, improving supercapacitor efficiency for multifunctional applications is a major area of study. Many elements have been employed as electrode materials to provide the best energy and power density while achieving the largest specific capacitance. Among these materials, 2D transition metal carbides and nitrides, commonly called MXenes, are emerging candidates, particularly in electrochemical energy storage applications. Because of their strength, flexibility, unique structure, increased electrical conductivity, large surface area, diversity of active sites, hydrophobicity, and hydrophilicity for cutting-edge energy storage technologies, MXenes are among the best active electrode materials. MXene, with its unique 2D layered structure, offers the infinite possibility of the intercalation of various capacitive materials. Also, MXenes have the properties of high hydrophilicity of metal oxides and high electrical conductivity of metals. Alongside, activated carbon (AC), graphene, carbon nanotubes (CNTs), transition metal oxides, and conducting polymers (CPs) act as excellent electrode materials owing to their outstanding thermal, mechanical, electrical, and morphological properties. According to recent studies, one of the perfect methods for energy storage applications is to integrate MXenes with other superior elements for generating MXene-based composite electrode materials. This review includes recent developments in the investigation of MXene-based hybrid composites for supercapacitors. It covers composite's synthesis strategies, electrode architecture, electrochemical performance, and their efficiency in supercapacitors.

title: Enhanced charge storage using in-situ grown NiGa-layered double hydroxide on V4C3Tx MXene for supercapacitor applications
authors: Dana Susan Abraham, Mari Vinoba, Margandan Bhagiyalakshmi
conclusion: In summary, NiGa-LDH was in situ grown on the surface of delaminated V4 C3 Tx MXene nanosheets via a facile hydrothermal procedure leveraging the electrostatic interactions between LDH and MXene. Various ratios of nickel and gallium were explored to optimize capacity performance, resulting in the Ni-Ga (1:1) LDH/V4 C3 Tx MXene (NGV-11) nanocomposite demonstrating a notable increase in specific capacity to 268.85 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1 . This enhanced capacity can be attributed to the synergistic interaction between NiGa-LDH and V4 C3 Tx MXene, where the abundant active sites of NiGa-LDH are complemented by the superior electrical conductivity and structural stability of V4 C3 Tx MXene. NGV-11//AC supercapacitor device attained a remarkable energy density of 56.41 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 800 W kg−1 , an impressive cycling stability with 93.24 % capacitance retention, and a coulombic efficiency of 96.96 % after 5000 cycles. Thus, the integration of NiGa-LDH with V4 C3 Tx MXene addresses common challenges in LDH-based materials, such as low conductivity and limited cycling stability, positioning the NGV-11 nanocomposite as a competitive candidate for next-generation energy storage systems. Hence, the study shows that NiGa-LDH/V4 C3 Tx MXene nanocomposite confers notable prospects as electrode material in the field of energy storage applications. Moreover, this study lays a strong foundation for advancing vanadium-based MXene-LDH hybrids in future energy storage research. CRediT authorship contribution statement Dana Susan Abraham: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Visualization, Software, Resources, Methodology, Investigation, Formal analysis, Data curation, Conceptualization. Mari Vinoba: Writing – review & editing, Validation, Investigation. Margandan Bhagiyalakshmi: Conceptualization, Resources, Methodology, Investigation, Validation, Writing – review & editing, Supervision, Project administration,
abstract: Developing remarkable hierarchical heterostructures in nanocomposites is crucial for enhancing electrochemical performance. Heterostructures combining layered double hydroxides (LDHs) and MXenes garner considerable attention as key candidates in energy conversion and storage. By fusing conductive 2D MXenes with LDHs, the advantages of both materials are effectively harnessed. Herein, nickel gallium layered double hydroxide (NiGa-LDH) is in situ grown on the V4C3Tx MXene surface to form NiGa-LDH/V4C3Tx MXene (NGV) nanocomposite. The robust interfacial interaction and superior electronic connection between NiGa-LDH and V4C3Tx MXene nanosheet bolster structural stability, enhances electrolyte accessibility, and boost electrical conductivity, thus delivers a specific capacity of 268.85 mAh g−1 for NGV-11 at 1 A g−1. The fabricated NGV-11//AC device achieves an impressive energy density of 56.41 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 800 W kg−1 and exceptional cycling stability of 93.24 % retention after 5000 cycles. The results show that the synergistic interaction between NiGa-LDH and V4C3Tx MXene significantly improves the charge storage capacity in the nanocomposite. This study presents a simple and effective approach for designing vanadium-based MXene with LDH for high-performance supercapacitors.

title: Fungus-modified wood anchor MXene constructs high-performance wood-based carbon electrodes for supercapacitor
authors: Shengzhang Deng, Jian Zhang, Lin Lin, Ziqi Li, Qingping Wang, Peng Li
conclusion: In this study, a self-supporting wood-derived carbon electrode has successfully been engineered with high energy density through a combination of fungus (Phanerochaete chrysosporium) treatment, low concentration KOH solution treatment and MXene anchoring. Fungi and KOH solution treatment induce the formation of layered porous structures in wood and generate many oxygen-containing functional groups, thereby improving the self-stacking problem of MXene in wood-derived carbon. Simultaneously, the integration of MXene into the wood-derived carbon enhanced its electrical conductivity, surface wettability, ion accessibility and provided abundant active sites. With a current density of 1 mA cm−2 , the ACW2 @WR-M3 has a capacitance of 10.5 F cm−2 (232.8 F g−1 ) and a retention of almost 97 % at 50 mA cm−2 after 10,000 cycles. Symmetric supercapacitor with two identical ACW2 @WR-M3 electrodes has high energy density (0.705 mWh cm−2 /3.53 mWh cm−3 ) and power density (54200 mW cm−2 /271000 mW cm−3 ). This work proposes a novel technique for increasing the electrochemical performance of wood-derived carbon electrodes, emphasizing their potential for high-performance supercapacitor applications. CRediT authorship contribution statement Shengzhang Deng: Writing – original draft, Investigation. Jian Zhang: Writing – review & editing,
abstract: MXene, a novel two-dimensional material, has gained widespread use in advanced energy storage equipment. However, its propensity for forming stacked structures, coupled with insufficient mechanical strength and plasticity, hinders its large-scale application. To overcome these limitations, this study developed MXene/Wood-derived carbon electrodes using a green approach. The synergistic effect of fungal degradation and low concentration KOH solution treatment disrupted the original pore structure of wood, leading to the formation of a hierarchical porous structure and exposing a large number of oxygen-containing functional groups. This not only mitigates the self-stacking issue of MXene in wood, but also enhances the affinity of electrode materials for electrolytes. The prepared electrode shows satisfactory capacitance of 10.5 F cm−2 (232.8 F g−1) at 1 mA cm−2. Moreover, the symmetric supercapacitor device prepared using the electrode exhibits a high energy density (0.705 mWh cm−2/3.53 mWh cm−3) and a comparatively excellent extended cycle life (93 % capacitance retention rate 10,000 times, 50 mA cm−2). This work paths a novel way for the use of renewable energy in supercapacitors.

title: Sandwich-like MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9S8 with rich pores and high charge transfer capability for boosted supercapacitor capability
authors: Ye Qu, Yanzi Zhang, Yali Zhang, Jun Song, Zhaoen Liu, Weixing Rao, Yu Liu
conclusion: In summary, this work successfully synthesized the sandwich structure MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9 S8 ternary nanocomposite. The high capacity of NiCo-LDH and Co9 S8 , and the exceptional electrical conductivity of MXene make the MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9 S8 composite a potential electrode material for a high-performance battery-type supercapacitor. The obtained hybrid structure generates a large number of channels, promoting the rapid transfer of ions and electrons, significantly improves electrochemical efficiency through synergistic effects. The obtained MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9 S8 composites showed a high specific capacity of 808.0 F g−1 . In addition, the assembled device (MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9 S8 //AC) achieved a superior energy density of 96.4 Wh kg−1 at 800 W kg−1 . Therefore, it can be concluded from the results that combining battery type and double-layer capacitive electrode materials to form a heterojunction is an excellent strategy for enhancing electrochemical performance. CRediT authorship contribution statement Ye Qu: Writing – original draft, Data curation. Yanzi Zhang: Visualization, Investigation. Yali Zhang: Formal analysis. Jun Song: Validation, Software. Zhaoen Liu: Formal analysis. Weixing Rao: Methodology, Conceptualization. Yu Liu: Writing – review & editing.
abstract: The multi-component synergy of electrode materials and structural engineering are crucial for high-performance supercapacitors. Herein, a novel sandwich-like MXene@NiCo-layered double hydroxides (LDHs)/Co9S8 nanostructure is rational synthesized, which with rich pores can significantly facilitate the diffusion of electrolyte ions and boost high charge transfer capability. Besides, the interaction forces between components promote the integration of multidimensional materials, and the resulting hybrid structure significantly improves the electrochemical efficiency through synergistic effects. Remarkably, the obtained MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9S8 composites exhibit a high specific capacitance of 808.0 F g−1 at a low current density of 1 A g−1, the value is nearly 1.4 times MXene@NiCo-LDH (586.2 F g−1), as well as good rate capability (512.0 F g−1 at 10 A g−1). Besides, the fabricated supercapacitor device (MXene@NiCo-LDH/Co9S8//activated carbon) showed an outstanding energy density of 96.4 Wh kg−1 at 800 W kg−1), and good cyclic performance of 70.26 % capacitance retention even over 9000 cycles. This research may provide a promising strategy for developing two-dimensional layered materials as an electrode material in energy storage applications.

title: Exploring the potential of MXene-based aerogels and hybrid nanocomposites for supercapacitor applications
authors: Suresh Sagadevan, Is Fatimah, J. Anita Lett, Babak Kakavandi, Tetsuo Soga, Won-Chun Oh, Hyacinthe Randriamahazaka
conclusion: The growing demand for energy storage with enhanced performance has driven the research toward innovative supercapacitor electrode materials. MXene aerogels, with their unique combination of properties, emerge as a promising candidate to address limitations that are faced by conventional electrodes. This review highlights the potential of MXene aerogels in supercapacitors, emphasizing their key advantages. Their strong and good conductivity, large surface area, and inherent MXene properties lead to remarkable capacitance values, enabling the efficient energy storage. Furthermore, MXene aerogels exhibit excellent cycling stability, demonstrating minimal performance degradation during extended charge-discharge cycles. This translates to long-lasting supercapacitors with reliable energy storage capabilities. The porous aerogel structure facilitates fast ion diffusion within the electrode, leading to fast charging and discharging rates thereby influencing the MXene aerogels suitable for the applications which are demanding high-power energy systems. Future research focused on optimizing fabrication methods and exploring composite structures with other conductive materials holds immense promise for delivering the full potential of MXene aerogels in the next-generation supercapacitors. This material has the advantage like cost-effective, high-capacity energy storage devices, which are beneficial for both industries and individuals. By enabling more efficient energy storage, MXene aerogels can revolutionize various productions. As research progresses, this technology development will play a major role in the viable and ecologically approachable for energy storage supercapacitor applications. CRediT authorship contribution statement Suresh Sagadevan: Writing – original draft, Methodology, Investigation,
abstract: MXene-based aerogel nanocomposites have significant attention as the promising supercapacitor electrode materials. This review highlights their potential by exploring the synergy between MXenes and aerogels. MXenes have good electrical conductivity and a high specific surface area due to their inherent characteristics. When combined with the high porosity and tunable pore structure of aerogels, these nanocomposites exhibit enhanced performance in supercapacitors. This review delivers the complete outline on the current advancements in MXene-based aerogel nanocomposites for supercapacitor applications. We delved into MXenes and their advantages as electrode materials. Also, explored various fabrication strategies, including hydrothermal synthesis, freeze drying, and templating methods. The discussion emphasizes the key factors influencing the aerogel morphology and pore structure, highlighting their impact on electrolyte accessibility and charge storage performance. Furthermore, the review analyzes the synergistic effects of these composite structures on critical parameters like specific capacitance, rate capability, and cycling stability. The challenges and future directions for the field are also discussed. By optimizing MXene-based aerogel nanocomposites, researchers can improve the electrochemical performance of the supercapacitors.

title: Electrostatic self-assembly assisted construction of MXene/MoO3 hybrid aerogel for free-standing supercapacitor electrodes
authors: Feitian Ran, Bowen Tan, Meijie Hu, Shulin Deng, Kai Wang, Wanjun Sun, Jifei Liu, Xiaobin Yang
conclusion: In summary, MXene/MoO3 hybrid aerogels were synthesized through electrostatic self-assembly and freeze-drying techniques. The incorporation of Ti3 C2 Tx establishes an efficient conductive network within MoO3 , significantly enhancing its intrinsic conductivity and facilitating rapid electron transport. Additionally, MoO3 nanobelts mitigate the restacking of Ti3 C2 Tx layers, thereby exposing more active sites for electrochemical reactions and resulting in a superior synergistic effect. The hybrid aerogels exhibit a larger pore size, providing accelerated ion diffusion pathways and improving electrochemical reaction kinetics. First-principles calculations reveal a marked enhancement in H+ adsorption and conductivity within the MXene/MoO3 hybrid aerogel. Consequently, the TM-50 hybrid aerogel achieves a specific capacity of 418.2 C g−1 at 1 A g−1 and maintains 92.3% of its capacity after 10000 cycles at 3 A g−1 . Furthermore, the assembled TM-50//AC asymmetric supercapacitors deliver an energy density of 20.9 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 491.5 W kg−1 This simple and controllable strategy for developing hybrid aerogels can be extended to other MXene-based functional materials. abstract: Designing multi-component coupled hybrid electrode materials serves as an effective strategy to enhance the energy density of supercapacitors, while simultaneously addressing the issues of insufficient interface activity and ion transport. Herein, we present a three-dimensional porous cross-linked MXene/MoO3 hybrid aerogel (TM-50) synthesized through an electrostatic self-assembly strategy. The porous structure enhances ion transport efficiency, while the incorporation of MXene improves the conductivity of MoO3. Additionally, the randomly interconnected MoO3 effectively suppresses the self-stacking of MXene nanosheets. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the TM-50 hybrid aerogel achieves a specific capacitance of 418.2 C g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 in 3 M H2SO4, with 92.7% retention after 10000 cycles. Additionally, the asymmetric supercapacitor assembled from TM-50 and activated carbon achieves an energy density of 20.9 Wh kg−1 at 491.5 W kg−1, retaining 90.3% capacitance after 5000 cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further confirm that the MXene/MoO3 hybrid exhibits lower H+ adsorption energy and a higher electronic state density near the Fermi level, enhancing its interfacial activity. This controllable approach to developing hybrid aerogels is promising for other MXene-based functional materials in diverse applications.

title: From 2D to 3D: Green synthesis of wrinkled MXene thin-film electrodes for ultra-high specific capacitance and structural resilience combination of supercapacitors
authors: Lanyun Di, Xuehua Yan, Chu Chu, Feng Zhang, Jamile Mohammadi Moradian, Zohreh Shahnavaz
conclusion: 2D MXene nanosheets are prone to self-stacking, which significantly hinders their application in supercapacitors. This study investigated a new path to synthesize a novel 3D porous MXene thin-film electrode. By leveraging the high-temperature pyrolysis of NaHCO3 , an annealing process was used to develop a 3D cavity structure and modify the surface end groups, reducing the harmful -F end groups. Additionally, the gas generated by the pyrolysis of NaHCO3 was used for in situ bubbling, inducing micron-scale 3D cavities combined with the remaining pores of CMC carbonization. This approach addresses the issue of self-stacking in 2D MXene nanosheets, which has hindered their application in supercapacitors. The abundant water molecule channels effectively accelerate the insertion and extraction of electrolyte ions. In addition, carbonized CMC improves the conductivity of the composite film and provides an additional double electric-layer contribution. Similarly, it acts as an interlayer spacer to inhibit the self-stacking of MXene nanosheets. Thanks to its favorable 3D structural design, the synthesized film electrode exhibits a mass-specific capacitance of up to 565 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , and the area-specific capacitance reaches 1582 mF cm−2 . After high-temperature annealing, the film still showed surprising mechanical flexibility, with a tensile strength of up to 34.2 MPa. When used as the positive and negative electrodes to assemble a symmetrical supercapacitor, at 1 A g−1 , the mass-specific capacitance could reach 71.25 F g−1 . Even under a power density of 400 W kg−1 , the energy density remained at 6.3 Wh kg−1 . The device also exhibited extremely high cycle stability, maintaining a capacity retention rate of 99.6 % after 20000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . This remarkable electrochemical performance opens up a novel avenue for the advancement of porous electrodes and high-efficiency flexible energy storage devices utilizing 2D nanomaterials. abstract: MXene, a new type of electrode material, is widely used in supercapacitors. However, the inherent self-stacking of this two-dimensional (2D) material impedes transport of electrolyte ions, limiting ion diffusion and pseudocapacitive performance. This study introduces a novel wrinkled three-dimensional (3D) structure of MXene films to avoid restacking of MXene nanosheets. At a current density of 1 A g−1, the mass-specific capacitance achieved 565 F g−1, while the area-specific capacitance attained 1582 mF cm−2. The film exhibits excellent mechanical flexibility and a tensile strength of up to 34.2 MPa at high strain rates. The film served as both the positive and negative electrode to assemble symmetrical supercapacitors. At 1 A g−1, the mass-specific capacitance can achieve 71.25 F g−1. Additionally, at a power density of 400 W kg−1, the energy density can reach 6.3 Wh kg−1. Demonstrating ultrahigh cycle stability, the capacity retention rate was 99.6 % after 20,000 cycles at 10 A g−1. This study suggests that optimizing the synthesis methods can enable 3D MXene thin-film electrodes with more tailorable properties, providing feasibility and reliability for engineering applications of supercapacitors.

title: High-performance asymmetric supercapacitors based on 2D MXene/NiCoP hybrid and ZIF derived porous nanocarbon
authors: Erdenebayar Baasanjav, K.A. Sree Raj, Hafis Hakkeem, Chandra Sekhar Rout, Sang Mun Jeong
conclusion: In summary, a 2D MXene-based NiCoP hybrid structure was successfully synthesized via a cost-effective hydrothermal reaction and phosphorization process. The designed and well-developed 2D MXene/NCP composite exhibits large porous active sites, abundant redox-active sites and exceptional electrical conductivity, which collectively promote enhanced Faradaic redox reactions, efficient electrolyte diffusion, and fast electron transport. The synergistic interaction between the MXene sheets and NCP nanorods leads to remarkable electrochemical performance, achieving a high specific capacitance of 1754.0 F g−1 at 3 mA cm−2 , along with good rate capability and higher stability, with minimal loss in activity after 5000 charge/discharge cycles. Additionally, a hybrid ASC device constructed using MX-3/NCP as the positive electrode and PNC as the negative electrode, delivered a high specific energy of 54.3 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 565.6 W kg−1 and maintained 32.6 Wh kg−1 at a high-power density of 6270 W kg−1 . The device also demonstrated exceptional cyclic stability by retaining 93.8 % of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles and excellent adaptability in practical applications. Moreover, TMP/MXene composites can be promising electrodes for the development of hybrid supercapacitor technologies.
