Hafis Hakkeem: Writing – original draft, Visualization, Data curation. Chandra Sekhar Rout: Writing – review & editing, Supervision. Sang Mun Jeong: Writing – review & editing, Supervision,
abstract: The performance of supercapacitors can be improved by strategically designing 2D MXene-based electrodes with excellent electrochemical properties. However, several challenges remain in developing hybrid materials based on 2D MXenes due to restacking, which hinders energy storage performance. In this work, we successfully synthesized a 2D MXene/Ni-Co phosphide (MX/NCP) hybrid material for supercapacitors via a facile hydrothermal reaction followed by phosphorization. The optimized MX/NCP positive electrode showed good energy storage performance with a specific capacitance of 1754.0 F g−1 at 3 mA cm−2 in a three-electrode configuration. The synergistic effect of MXene and Ni-Co phosphide has contributed towards the enhanced charge storage performance. Furthermore, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) fabricated with MX/NCP and porous nanocarbon (PNC) delivered a maximum energy density of 54.3 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 565.6 W kg−1 with a cycling stability of 93.8 % after 10,000 cycles. To evaluate the practical versatility of the ASC, a planar device was successfully fabricated making MX/NCP a promising electrode material in next-generation wearable and flexible supercapacitors.

title: Synergistically coupling of ternary hydrotalcite and Ti3C2Tx-MXene nanosheets boosting electronic transmission in energy storage
authors: Lu Luo, Qiuyan Kong, Qianqian Zhang, Jing Zhang, Mizi Fan, Weigang Zhao
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, the LDH/Ti 3 C 2 T x nanohybrids with intriguing “lace-like” structure were successfully developed via synergistically coupling Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene with ternary hydrotalcite (NiCoMn-LDH). The disordered crisscross arrangement of the NiCoMn-LDH arrays have enabled a high porosity and abundant active sites. Coupled with Ti 3 C 2 T x serving as an electronic transmission bridge, the LDH/Ti 3 C 2 T x nanohybrid exhibits outstanding electrical conductivity, showcasing a remarkable specific capacitance of 1102.9 F g −1 and demonstrating a rate capability of 66.87 % at 20 A g −1 . Further assembly of the LDH/Ti 3 C 2 T x -2//AC hybrid supercapacitor (HSC) yields a maximum energy density of 47.3 Wh kg −1 (at 800 W kg −1 ), maintaining a considerable energy density of 35.7 Wh kg −1 even at 8000 W kg −1 . Moreover, the HSC device demonstrates distinguished durability (91.7 %) and Coulombic efficiency (99 %) after 5000 cycles. This work highlights the rational combination of 2D Ti 3 C 2 T x with highly active transition metal compounds, showcasing their synergistic effects in enhancing the performance of nanohybrids. This presents thrilling possibilities for the design of devices for electrochemical energy harvesting and storage.
abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDH) and two-dimensional metal carbides (Ti3C2Tx) garner significant attention in recent years. LDH/Ti3C2Tx nanohybrids combine the unique characteristics of individual component, making them a promising option for high-power energy storage applications. Here, we present a composite electrode constructed by synergistic coupling of Ti3C2Tx and ternary hydrotalcite (NiCoMn-LDH). Strong interfacial interactions between the NiCoMn-LDH array and Ti3C2Tx nanoflakes, along with effective electron coupling, contribute to enhanced structural stability, conductivity, and electrolyte accessibility, thereby significantly promoting the kinetics of redox reactions. The intriguing “lace-like” structure fully utilizes the high activity of NiCoMn-LDH and the excellent conductivity of Ti3C2Tx, allowing LDH/Ti3C2Tx to exhibit an impressive output capacitance of 1102.9 F g−1 at 1 A g−1, coupled with notable rate capability (66.87 % at 20 A g−1). The constructed LDH/Ti3C2Tx//AC hybrid supercapacitor (HSC) achieves a remarkable energy density of 47.3 Wh kg−1 at 800 W kg−1. Following 5000 cycles, the specific capacity of HSC decreases by merely 8.3 %, while achieving a Coulombic efficiency of 99 %, showcasing remarkable durability and reversible reaction characteristics. This study provides a streamlined and effective methodology for crafting LDH/Ti3C2Tx nanohybrids, showcasing robust coupled interfaces and exceptional electrochemical energy storage application.

title: Enhanced electron conductivity, stability, and electrochemical performance of MXene-coated manganese and iron oxides as negative electrode of supercapacitors
authors: Moo Young Jung, Yongsuk Oh, Subin Eom, Jihye Park, Chanyong Lee, Sudeshana Pandey, Taemin Kim, Hae-Seok Lee, Ji-Won Son, Yong Ju Yun, Yongseok Jun
conclusion: In this study, a novel MXene/MnO2 /Fe2 O3 composite was developed and optimized as a negative electrode material for supercapacitors. The MXMFO-1.0 exhibited the best performance, achieving a high charging and discharging specific capacity of 1226.30 and 595.74 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 and retaining 78 % of its discharging capacity after 4000 cycles at 4 A g–1 . An asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) using this composite as the negative electrode demonstrated an energy density and power density of 61.70 Wh kg–1 at 426.21 W kg–1 and 17.88 Wh kg–1 at 2824.63 W kg–1 and excellent cycling stability, retaining 92.92 % of its initial capacitance after 25,000 cycles at 0.5 A g–1 . These findings highlight the potential of MXene/MnO2 /Fe2 O3 composites for high-performance supercapacitors, particularly in energy storage applications such as electric vehicles and grid systems. abstract: The fabrication and characterization of a novel MXene/MnO2/Fe2O3 composite as a negative electrode material for supercapacitors are reported in this study. The MXene is integrated by coating the MnO2/Fe2O3 particles, significantly enhancing the specific capacity. An optimal MXene ratio achieves a remarkable specific charging capacity of 1226.30 mAh g–1 at a current density of 1 A g–1. However, further increasing the MXene content does not result in proportional improvement of electrochemical performances, suggesting that an excessive amount negatively impacts the system. Additionally, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) using nickel–aluminum as the positive electrode and an optimized MXene/MnO2/Fe2O3 composite as the negative electrode is developed. This ASC exhibits an impressive energy density of 61.70 Wh kg–1 and a power density of 426.21 W kg–1, with a capacitance retention of 92.92 % after 25,000 cycles at 0.5 A g–1. These findings suggest that MXene/MnO2/Fe2O3 composites are promising candidates for high-performance supercapacitor applications.

title: A novel MnO2/Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposite as high performance electrode materials for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Hanmei Jiang, Zegao Wang, Qian Yang, Muhammad Hanif, Zhiming Wang, Lichun Dong, Mingdong Dong
conclusion: In summary, we have developed a novel MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite for flexible supercapacitor, which is synthesized by synergistically coupling one-dimensional (1D) MnO2 nanoneedles with two-dimensional (2D) Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheet. In the as-prepared materials, MnO2 nanoneedles, growing along the (001) direction, are anchored on Ti3 C2 Tx sheets with diameters of around 10–20 nm and length of around 200–300 nm. XPS characterization demonstrated the chemical interaction between Ti3 C2 Tx and MnO2 in the composites, which can improve the electrochemical performance of the MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite material by promoting the electron transfer between MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx . The synergistic effect between MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx is significantly affected by the MnO2 content, the 1 MT sample with the mass ratio between MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx = 1 exhibits the best electrochemical performance due to the maximizing electron transfer and ion diffusion. The flexible supercapacitor device fabricated by using the 1 MT nanocomposites as electrode materials can be freely bended and exhibits excellent capacitive behavior. The energy density of the device can reach 0.7 μWh cm−2 at the power density of 80.0 μW cm−2 , which is better than many of the reported MnO2 -based and carbon–basted flexible supercapacitor device. Moreover, the MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite flexible supercapacitor shows superior electrochemical stability (more than 100% capacitance retention after 1000 cycles at 0.2 mA cm−2 ). On the basis of these features, the good electrochemical behavior of the MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites makes it a promising electrode material for flexible supercapacitor. However, to close the theoretical specific capacitance of MnO2 , further optimizing the structure of this flexible supercapacitor device with higher capacitance and energy density are desired. Furthermore, this work provides a general route for preparing MnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposites and sheds light on the exploitation of MnO2 -based materials for advanced flexible energy storage devices. Conflicts of interest There are no conflicts to declare.
abstract: MnO2 is considered as one of the most promising electrode materials for flexible supercapacitors but it often suffer in poor conductivity, which limits practical applications according to industry needs. To enhance the performance, forming MnO2-based hybrid structures with conductive materials is a promising implement approach. Ti3C2Tx MXene sheets, a new kind of 2D transition metal carbides with metallic conductivity and hydrophilic nature, are promising candidate to couple with MnO2. According to the complementary principle, we design a novel structure MnO2/Ti3C2Tx hybrid nanocomposite by synergistically coupling one-dimensional (1D) MnO2 nanoneedles with two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx MXene sheet for flexible supercapacitor. XPS investigations suggest the obvious charge transfer from Ti3C2Tx sheets to MnO2 nanoneedles, where Ti3C2Tx sheets serve as a remarkable 2D conductive substrate to facilitate the electrons transfer in the nanocomposites. This strong synergistic effect between Ti3C2Tx and MnO2 resulting from the chemical interaction greatly enhance the electrical conductivity, specific capacitance, rate stability and structural stability of the MnO2/Ti3C2Tx nanocomposite. To show the potential application in energy storage, a symmetrical flexible supercapacitor device with good electrochemical performance, high flexibility and super cycling ability is fabricated by utilizing MnO2/Ti3C2Tx nanocomposites as electrode materials. This work has proposed a new approach of developing advanced nanocomposites from a MnO2-based electrode for high performance flexible electronics.

title: Highly matched porous MXene anodes and graphene cathodes for high-performance aqueous asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Shuaikai Xu, Yubing Li, Tangming Mo, Guodong Wei, Ya Yang
conclusion: 4 Experimental section 4.1 Preparation of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets 4.2 Preparation of BP nanosheets 4.3 Fabrication of AMF, P-MF, N-PMF, and N/P-PMF hybrid films 4.4 Fabrication of N/P-rGO 4.5 Assembly of the asymmetric supercapacitors 4.6 Material characterization 4.7 Electrochemical measurement CRediT authorship contribution statement Acknowledgements
abstract: Aqueous asymmetric supercapacitors (ASCs) provide promising prospects for electronic systems in the future that require high energy density, power density and cycling life, due to their advantages such as low cost, safe operation and environmental friendliness. However, developing well-matched anodes and cathodes with complementary potential windows and coordinated charge storage kinetics remains a significant challenge. Here, we constructed porous MXene- and graphene-based films with nitrogenous and phosphorous terminals as anodes and cathodes, respectively, alleviating the restacking of nanosheets, generating more electrochemical active sites and improving the electrolyte penetration. The assembled aqueous ASCs based on the porous MXene and graphene films could achieve an excellent energy density of 26.8 Wh kg−1 at 425 W kg−1, high rate performance, and remarkable cycling stability with 97.3 % retention after 20,000 cycles. This work demonstrates a novel concept to develop high-performance aqueous ASCs by surface engineering of two-dimensional porous electrodes with matched structural and electrochemical properties.

title: MXene-transition metal chalcogenide hybrid materials for supercapacitor applications
authors: Gopinath Sahoo, Chandra Sekhar Rout
error: Could not extract conclusion using any method
abstract: The rapid growth of technologies and miniaturization of electronic devices demand advanced the use of high-powered energy storage devices. The energy storage device are utilized in modern wearable electronics, stretchable screens, and electric vehicles. Due to their favorable electrochemical properties, nanomaterials have been used as electrodes for supercapacitors (SCs) with high power density, but they generally suffer from lower energy density than batteries. Compared to various nanomaterials, MXenes and transition metal chalcogenides (TMCs) have shown great potential for energy storage applications such as SCs. TMCs are gaining attention due to their stable electrochemical nature, adjustable surface activity, high electric conductivity, abundant chemically active sites, and stable cycling performance. However, the interlayer restacking and agglomeration of 2D materials limit their cycling performance. To overcome this, TMCs@MXene heterostructures have been developed, offering structurally stable electrodes with enhanced chemical active sites. In this review, we discuss recent advances in the development of different TMCs@MXene-based hybrids for the design of high performance SCs with improved specific capacitance, cycling life, energy density, and power density. The recent developments of this research field focusing on MXene-transition metal sulfides, MXene-transition metal selenides, and MXene-transition metal tellurides are elaborately discussed. Theoretical calculations carried out to understand the charge-storage mechanisms in these composites are reviewed. The importance of bimetallic TMCs and MXene heterostructure for enhanced energy storage is also highlighted.

title: Simultaneously addressing self-stacking and oxidative degradation issues of Ti3C2Tx MXene through biothermochemistry induced 3D crosslinking
authors: Haitao Zhang, Hanyu He, Yongxiang Huang, Shi Pu, Yanting Xie, Junfeng Huang, Xinling Jiang, Yongbin Wang, Shenglong Wang, Hongzhi Peng, Yuanxiao Qu, Weiqing Yang
conclusion: In conclusion, a variety of Ti3 C2 Tx with 3D crosslinking structure are constructed by a novel biothermochemistry method, in which bioagents are combined with Ti3 C2 Tx through electrostatic and/or the formation of Ti-N and S-S chemical bonds. On the one hand, 3D crosslinking effect expands the interlayer spacing and reduces self-stacking issue; On the other hand, bioagents reduce the number of exposed Ti atoms and effectively prevent the oxidation of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. Impressively, 3D-MX exhibits extraordinary antioxidant capacity as revealed by extremely-long on-shelf stability up to 550 days. In practical, as used as an electrode material for supercapacitors, 3D-MX-G exhibits high specific capacitance and excellent stability. This work solves the problems of self-stacking and oxidative degradation of Ti3 C2 Tx and provides an excellent solution for exploring the further application and long-term preservation of Ti3 C2 Tx .
abstract: As a recent rising star 2D material, MXenes have attracted great attention in many fields. However, the weak interaction induced self-stacking phenomenon and surface oxidation caused structure failure seriously hinder the practical application of MXenes. Herein we develop a biothermochemistry method to construct 3D crosslinked Ti3C2Tx (3D-MX). This novel structured 3D-MX can be prepared in five different kinds of biological reagents, showing good university. After crosslinking, 3D-MX not only resists layer stacking but also exhibits extreme on-shelf stability up to 550 days. We reveal that the formation mechanism originates from the electrostatic/chemical interaction between surface functional groups and the crosslinking agents. Interestingly, the biothermochemical treated Ti3C2Tx MXenes exhibit an extremely-rapid film-processed capability (only 3 min), addressing the long-standing issue of low-efficient and tedious solution-vacuum filtrated 2D films. To further verify its practical application, we assemble 3D-MX based supercapacitors that show a high specific capacitance of 265 Fg−1 at 1 A g−1, and moreover, no supercapacitance attenuation within 720 h. This proposed biothermochemistry method to simply and rapidly build 3D Ti3C2Tx crosslinked network provides a new perspective to promote the practical application of MXenes through simultaneously addressing their self-stacking and oxidative degradation issues.

title: Biomimetic and electrostatic self-assembled nanocellulose/MXene films constructed with sequential bridging strategy for flexible supercapacitor
authors: Shaowei Wang, Yuanyuan Ma, Sailing Zhu, Haoyu Ma, Yiying Yue, Qinglin Wu, Huining Xiao, Jingquan Han
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, biomimetic and hierarchical flexible CM-Al composite films with distinguished mechanical toughness, electrical conductivity and electrochemical energy storage capabilities were developed via the facile electrostatic self-assembly and vacuum filtration processes. The introduced CNFs enriched with hydroxyl and carboxyl groups served as an intercalation layer to connect the adjacent MXene nanosheets through hydrogen bonding interactions, which not only imparted the enhanced mechanical strength and flexibility to the composite film through constructing a “soft-hard” biomimetic microstructure, but also effectively suppressed the undesirable self-stacking of the MXene nanosheets, allowing the exposure of more active sites on MXene surface. The positively charged Al 3+ induced the self-assembly of the negatively charged CNFs and MXene via electrostatic attraction, resulting in the establishment of ionic bonds with oxygen-containing functional groups via charge transfer. The strong and rigid ionic bonds interlocked the adjacent CNFs and MXene, facilitating a denser internal structure and enhanced mechanical toughness of CM-Al. Furthermore, additional electron transport pathways acted by ionic bonds boosted the fast electron transfer, improving the electroconductivity of the composite films. Benefiting from the biomimetic structure with sequentially bridged hydrogen and ionic bonds, the robust and flexible CM-Al displayed optimal mechanical properties (tensile strength of 163.88 MPa, Young ' s modulus of 2.18 GPa and toughness of 8.64 MJ m −3 ), electrical conductivity (82.63 S cm −1 ) and extraordinary capacitive capability (762 mF cm −2 ), proving a remarkable dominance in electrochemical energy storage. The assembled symmetric quasi-solid-state supercapacitor with CM-Al as electrode material integrated the superior areal capacitance (679 mF cm −2 at 0.8 mA cm −2 current density), cycling stability (85.3 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles) and high energy density (16.2 μWh cm −2 ). Additionally, the basically constant electrochemical performance of the flexible supercapacitor was detected even after experiencing repeated non-stretching deformations due to the stable internal structure of CM-Al, indicating the noteworthy reliability in practical applications. This work delivered a simple and feasible strategy for the fabrication of flexible composite films combined with impressive mechanical toughness, electrical conductivity and brilliant electrochemical energy storage, facilitating the development of MXene-based flexible electronics in high-performance wearable energy storage devices.
abstract: Despite the two-dimensional titanium carbide MXene (Ti3C2Tx) has shown promising applications in energy storage, the inherent self-stacking and weak connectivity among nanosheets present a challenge in manufacturing robust MXene films for emerging flexible supercapacitors. Herein, inspired by the robust “soft-hard” structured exoskeletons of crustaceans, the biomimetic cellulose nanofibers (CNFs)/MXene-Al (CM-Al) film with integrated high mechanical toughness, electroconductivity and electrochemical behavior, sequential bridging with hydrogen and ionic bonds, is crafted via the facile electrostatic self-assembly strategy. The embedded CNFs guide the in-plane orientation of MXene through hydrogen bonding, forming a “soft-hard” microstructure and dramatically enhancing the mechanical toughness of CM-Al. The rigid ionic bonds established between the oxygen-containing groups on CNFs and MXene with Al3+ further elevate the mechanical strength (163.88 MPa) and act as additional electron transfer channels to impart the reinforced electroconductivity (82.63 S cm−1). Benefiting from the more active site exposure induced by the expanded MXene layer spacing after CNFs embedding and the weakened intrinsic resistance caused by the constructed ionic bonding, the assembled flexible quasi-solid-state symmetric supercapacitor with CM-Al as electrode delivers a high area capacitance (679 mF cm−2), energy density (16.2 μWh cm−2), cycling capability (85.3 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles) and intrinsic tolerance to various non-stretching deformations. Moreover, the selective principles for metal ions are summarized that involved a comprehensive consideration of ionic radius, charge density and basic chemical properties. This work demonstrates an accessible and feasible construction strategy for flexible composite films and provides an alternative pathway for wearable energy storage devices.

title: Nanoengineering of novel MXene (Ti3C2Tx) based MgCr2O4 nanocomposite with detailed synthesis, morphology and characterization for enhanced energy storage application
authors: Rubia Shafique, Malika Rani, Kiran Batool, Aqeel Ahmad Shah, Aboud Ahmed Awadh Bahajjaj, Mika Sillanpää, Hessa A. Alsalmah, Naveed Kausar Janjua, Maryam Arshad
conclusion: that MXene/MgCr2 O4 based electrode materials is most suitable for energy storage applications such as supercapacitors. 4 Conclusion A novel nanocomposite combining MXene and magnesiochromite has been investigated in the realm of energy storage particularly as electrode material for supercapacitors. The X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis distinctly reveals the characteristic peaks corresponding to both MXene and MgCr2 O4 phases within the nanocomposite spectrum. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) micrographs exhibit the attachment of magnesiochromite particles onto MXene nanosheets. Raman and photoluminescence spectra provide insights into the presence of functional groups and enhanced electron-hole recombination, resulting in a bandgap of 1.8 eV as determined from UV spectra. The Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra exhibit prominent peaks corresponding to C-F, C–H, and MgCr2 O4 at wavenumbers of 940 cm−1 , 2880 cm−1 and 505 cm−1 respectively. Notably, a tailored increase in electrostatic repulsion has been achieved for the colloidal solution, as evidenced by the measured Zeta potential of −19.9 mV. The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) spectra demonstrate the remarkable electron transfer rate constants of 4.097 × 10−9 (S/cm) in 1 M KOH and 2.66 × 10−9 (S/cm) in 0.1 M H2 SO4 underlining the material efficient charge transport properties. Notably in 1 M KOH electrolyte solution at 20 mV/s, a maximum capacitance value of 542.6F/g is achieved. Maximum power density increases from 104.99 to 271.2 kW/kg while energy density value reduces from 37.68 to 14.58 kWh/kg emphasizing the potential utility of this nanocomposite as an energy storage material particularly in the context of supercapacitor applications.
abstract: In this study, we presented a novel approach involving the co-precipitation synthesis of a two-dimensional MXene nanocomposite with spinel magnesiochromite MgCr2O4. The resulting nanocomposite was comprehensively characterized. The synthesized nanomaterial exhibited an average crystallite size of approximately 6.85 nm, and its surface morphology confirmed the presence of agglomerated grains with the elemental composition being confirmed by EDS spectra. Raman spectra provided evidence of prominent molecular vibrations, while photoluminescence spectroscopy revealed significant electron-hole recombination within the nanocomposite, leading to a reduced bandgap as corroborated by UV–Vis spectra. Zeta potential measurements shows minimum value of −19.9 mV comparable to MXene zeta potential value –23 mV indicating maximum stability. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) spectra highlighted a minimal charge-transfer resistance value of 64.99 Ω in a basic electrolyte, resulting electron transfer rate value about 4.097 × 10−9 (S/cm) resulting maximum conduction. Electrode capacitive behavior in both acidic (0.1 M H2SO4) and basic media (1 M KOH) demonstrates the potential of this novel nanocomposite material with the maximum capacitance value of 542.6F/g observed in basic media in comparison to the minimum capacitance value of 454.1F/g in acidic media. From GCD analysis, maximum power density of 271.2 kW/kg with an energy density value of 14.58 kWh/kg is achieved. These findings underscore its applicability in energy storage applications partially in the context of supercapacitors.

title: Binder-free Ti3C2Tx MXene electrode film for supercapacitor produced by electrophoretic deposition method
authors: Shuaikai Xu, Guodong Wei, Junzhi Li, Yuan Ji, Nickolai Klyui, Vladimir Izotov, Wei Han
conclusion: In summary, a general, simple MEPD strategy has been developed for preparing binder-free Ti3 C2 Tx -based supercapacitor electrodes with excellent electrochemical performances. The key novelty in this study is the use of a facile, time-saving method to produce layered self-assembled binder-free Ti3 C2 Tx films with adjustable mass loading and reduced agglomeration on different conductive substrates at room temperature by using organic colloidal solution containing well-dispersed few-layer d-Ti3 C2 Tx nanoflakes. The MEPD method facilitates the formation of a layered and interconnected self-assembled framework with a broad pore size distribution and reduced agglomeration, ensuring the high electrical conductivity and improved accessibility of electrolyte to the electrode. The film electrodes demonstrated good rate performance and long cyclic life with capacity retention close to 100% after 10,000 cycles. Moreover, the proposed MEPD as a universal method could also open a door to design high performance MXene-based supercapacitor by using arbitrary conductive substrates, especially for manufacturing flexible or micro supercapacitor with complex shapes and greatly promoting the practical applications of Ti3 C2 Tx -based supercapacitor devices in the future. abstract: Binder-free electrodes employed in supercapacitor devices can exhibit excellent electrochemical performances due to the improvement of electronic conductivity and the utilization rate of electrode materials. However, a simple, efficient and tunable strategy for preparation of binder-free MXene-based electrodes, especially for developing a general method for fabricating the MXene-based wearable flexible supercapacitors, still remains a challenge to meet the requirements of practical applications. In this study, we fabricated binder-free MXene-based films with adjustable mass loading and reduced agglomeration on the nickel foam and wearable flexible fabric substrates by the modified electrophoretic deposition method using organic colloid containing few-layers Ti3C2Tx nanoflakes. Their electrochemical performances are studied by cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge-discharge and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, respectively. The binder-free electrodes can deliver high capacitance (∼140Fg−1 in alkaline electrolyte), stable cycling performance with no capacitance loss after 10,000 cycles and good rate performance, which can be attributed to the reduced agglomeration of Ti3C2Tx films with a layer-by-layer self-assembled stackable structure, optimized pore-size distribution (∼4nm) and excellent electronic conductivity, enhancing the accessibility to electrolyte ions and enabling full utilization of the MXene nanoflake surfaces.

title: Achieving 3D Ti3C2TX hydrogel cathode by cation electrochemical intercalation and gelation for a zinc-ion hybrid supercapacitor with high energy density

abstract: Zinc-ion hybrid supercapacitors (ZHSCs) combine the characteristics of the high power density of supercapacitors (SCs), the high energy density of batteries, and cost benefits of zinc-ion technology, which have broad prospects. At present, Ti3C2TX shows great application potential in the field of SCs, but the electrochemical performance is seriously affected by the tight accumulation between the layers. In this paper, Ti3C2TX was assembled into a 3D structure to form Ti3C2TX-reduced graphene oxide (RGO) hydrogel by a low-temperature hydrothermal graphene oxide (GO)-gelation process. Subsequently, Zn2+ ions were inserted into the van der Waals (vdW) gap of the layered Ti3C2TX of the Ti3C2TX-RGO hydrogel by an electrochemical intercalation technology. The formative Zn2+-Ti3C2TX-RGO hydrogel has good mechanical strength, fast ion transport rate, and abundant active sites. The material was then used as free-standing cathode and zinc foil as the anode to construct a ZHSC, which possessed a large operating voltage (2.0 V), a high energy density of 172.8 Wh kg−1, a high power density of 9625.5 Wh kg−1, and a good cycling stability (retention of 79.5 % of the capacitance after 5000 cycles at 10 A g−1). This work highlights the unique potential of Ti3C2TX-based hydrogels as viable electrode materials for ZHSCs.

title: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis of Ti3C2Tx MXene: A sustainable and scalable approach using alkaline etchant
authors: Farah Ezzah Ab Latif, Mohammad Khalid, Arshid Numan, Norhuda Abdul Manaf, Nabisab Mujawar Mubarak, Haizum Aimi Zaharin, Ezzat Chan Abdullah
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  This study successfully demonstrates the synthesis of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene from the Ti 3 AlC 2 MAX phase using NaOH as the etching agent, with concentrations ranging from 5 to 30 M, through a microwave-assisted hydrothermal heating method. XRD analysis reveals slight shifts and a reduction in peak intensity at the (002) and (104) panes, suggesting effective structural modification caused by etching. The results confirm the successful alteration of the MXene structure. FTIR analysis highlights Ti-O, C=O, C-H, and O-H functional groups on the etched MXene surface, suggesting elemental substitution and introducing various functional groups. The findings align with the previously reported MXene compositions, demonstrating effective surface modification. Raman analysis confirms the formation of new bonds, such as Ti-C and Ti-O/Ti-OH, providing further evidence of Al removal from the precursor and validating the efficacy of the NaOH etching process through microwave-assisted hydrothermal heating.  FESEM analysis reveals the etched MXene's surface morphology, showing carved patterns and layered structures with increased interlayer spacing, especially at higher NaOH concentrations (27.5 and 30 M). Elemental analysis using FESEM-EDS demonstrates significant Al removal, with the remaining Al content as low as 2.19% and 0.46% for the 27.5 M and 30 M etched MXene, respectively. The combination of XRD and FESEM-EDS characterisation provides a comprehensive understanding of surface termination, elucidating the elemental composition and distribution. Furthermore, UV-Vis spectroscopy analysis using Tauc's plot reveals that the band gap energy changes after etching, likely due to surface functionalisation. Interestingly, the magnetic properties of etched MXene at lower NaOH concentrations (10 M and below) transition to semiconducting behaviour at higher concentrations (20 M and above), showcasing the material's electronic versatility and potential for various applications. Notably, Ti 3 C 2 T x etched MXene synthesised at 27.5 M NaOH concentration is a promising candidate for future MXene synthesis studies to optimise etching conditions. While this study has successfully reduced Al content and formed narrow interlayer spacing, future work should focus on refining etchant concentrations to maximise the etching process. In conclusion, this work demonstrates a fluorine-free, efficient NaOH etching approach for synthesising Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene, leveraging microwave-assisted hydrothermal processing to drastically reduce etching time to 45 min. The resulting etched MXene exhibits a unique, multilayered structure, modified surface features, and versatility in electronic properties, promoting its potential in a wide range of applications.
abstract: The present work demonstrates an enhanced method for synthesising titanium carbide (Ti3C2TX) MXene using an alkaline etchant to remove aluminium (Al) element from the ternary titanium metal carbide (Ti3AlC2) MAX phase. The synthesis process employs a microwave-assisted hydrothermal heating route, offering a fluorine-free and safer alternative to conventional etching techniques. This method achieved rapid heating within just 45 min at 180°C, significantly reducing the etching time compared to traditional etching, which often requires ∼2-3 days. The effects of different sodium hydroxide (NaOH) concentrations (5 to 30 M) on the etching process were analysed. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirmed structural modifications, showing a reduction of peak intensities and the existence of functional groups on etched MXene's galleries, such as Ti-O, C=O, C-H, and O-H. These structural modifications indicated a successful Al removal. Raman's analysis further verified bond formation within the etched MXene, such as Ti-C and Ti-O/Ti-OH bonds. Morphological analysis revealed a well-aligned, layered structure with substantial interlayer spacing at higher NaOH concentrations (27.5 and 30 M), indicating the formation of 2D MXene sheets. Elemental analysis showed significant Al reduction, especially at 27.5 and 30 M etched MXene, with remaining amounts of 21.9 % and 0.46 %, respectively. The UV-Vis spectroscopy identified etched MXene possessed magnetic properties at lower NaOH concentrations (5 and 10 M) with the band gap energy from 2 to 2.5 eV. Meanwhile, the etched MXene at higher NaOH concentrations (20 to 30 M) behave semiconductor-like with the band gap energy from 1.30 to 1.60 eV, corroborating the surface functionalisation of the MXene galleries. The findings suggest that NaOH concentrations of 27.5 M are ideal for potential applications, as higher concentrations improve functional groups and interlayer spacing. Future work will optimise this synthesis method, offering a fast and scalable approach to creating MXene for use in catalysis and electronic applications.

title: The Rise of Ti3C2Tx MXene synthesis strategies over the decades: A review
authors: Mohammed Askkar Deen, Harish Kumar Rajendran, Ragavan Chandrasekar, Debanjana Ghosh, Selvaraju Narayanasamy
conclusion: 6  Conclusion  Ti 3 C 2 T x has emerged as a robust 2D nanomaterial ascribed to its properties such as tunable conductivity, abundant surface functional groups, hydrophilicity, structural variations and mechanical pliability. However, there are challenges associated with Ti 3 C 2 T x in utilizing it effectively. One major obstacle is the need for safe and cost-effective synthesis techniques that can yield high quantities of Ti 3 C 2 T x . Although the chemical vapour deposition (CVD) method is considered safe and controllable, it is not explored for synthesizing Ti 3 C 2 T x . Currently, the only fabrication method available is wet chemical etching. An environmentally friendly process like molten salt substitution and halogen etching exist; nevertheless, etching based on HF and HCl-LiF is still the most sought-after approach because of their ease of synthesis. However, these approaches require hazardous etchants or harsher synthetic conditions to etch out the Al layers in Ti 3 C 2 T x successfully. For instance, HF etching allows synthesis at room temperature, while molten salts require a higher temperature of 700 ° C for successful synthesis. This demonstrates the demand to generate economically viable and efficient methods for etching and producing a large quantity of Ti 3 C 2 T x . Furthermore, complete control over the synthesis process of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene hasn't been achieved. It remains challenging to synthesis Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets with specific sizes, defects and surface terminations with desired spatial distribution. Being a material of active research interest, the list of synthesis routes of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene will get some add ons whereby there is a good scope on green solvent based Al etching and etching methods that require minimal energy to be developed in near future. In addition, facile exfoliation protocols must be developed to produce multi-layered Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene into single or fewer layers without any defects, resulting in a perfect crystal structure. This development will unveil detailed insights into the electronic, magnetic, mechanical, and photic properties of MXene. These insights help understand the interface properties between Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets and other substances, including surface functional groups, gas molecules, water molecules, and hybrid phases, through experimental and theoretical analyses (both in situ and ex-situ observations). Furthermore, a greater focus on the stability of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene in the form of nanosheets is needed, specifically in humid environments with oxygen and at high temperatures. The irreversible oxidation of MXenes is a significant obstacle that hinders their practical applications. The feasible ways to prevent this permanent degradation of MXenes must be unveiled to utilize their potential in practical applications fully. The preservation of Ti 3 C 2 T x 's properties over time remains challenging despite attempts to enhance its oxidation stability with antioxidizing agents. While this treatment improves stability, it does not entirely prevent oxidation. As a result, a method to improve the long-term storage of Ti 3 C 2 T x while keeping its properties intact is still elusive. Despite the challenges mentioned above, state-of-the-art research demonstrates that these challenges are expected to progress significantly soon. There is no doubt that Ti 3 C 2 T x  MXene has guaranteed the era of the next generation of 2D nanomaterials.  Some of the crucial state of the art challenges in Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene synthesis includes oxidation stability, environmental friendly synthesis procedure and scalability. The conversion of Ti in Ti 3 C 2 T x to TiO 2 is accelerated by the presence of dissolved oxygen during the etching process. Hence in many MXene synthetsis laboratory, the synthesis is accompanied by Argon purging or the etching is carried out in an inert atmosphere. One strategy used to reduce the dissolved oxygen levels in liquid is coating the liquid holding container with polymeric composites, which scavenges the oxygen present in liquid and reduced the oxygen level. This kind of polymer coatings are used in packagings that prevent the oxidation of food items [142] . Block copolymer made up of 1,6-hexanediol/tetrahydrophthalic anhydride polyester and polycaprolactone was found to scavenge 382 cc/m 2 oxygen [143] . Most of the etching protocol involves usage of direct HF or in situ generation of HF by reaction between metal fluorides and HCl and this demands the usage of polymeric containers rather than the glass material. Plastic containers made up of the above mentioned polymer or the inner walls coated using those polymers help to scavenge oxygen from the etching solution. Stability and purity of the MAX phase is anothern concern towards MXene synthesis. The purity of the MAX phase for etching process is not uniform and varies with suppliers and hence demands a reliable, simple synthesis protocol for high quanitity production, ensuring purity and minimal batch variations. The stability of MAX phase before it meets its end application is also a concern of discussion. The roughness of the surface and grain boundary diffusion of oxygen in MAX phase are to blame which compromises the stability of MAX phases. This was explained by Julian in terms of breakaway oxidation of Ti 2 AlC [144] . In MXene synthesizing laboratories, storage of MAX phase is carried out in glove boxes which is not offordable in many laboratories. In such cases researches can use anaerobic gas jars like GasPak jars to maintain oxygen free contidions while storing the MAX phases and the similar principle can be used for synthesizing and transportation of MAX phases. Few researchers have tried the strategy of increasing the concentration of aluminium during MAX phase synthesis, for example Roslyk et al. increased the molar ratio of Al 1.1 times to that of TiC, resulting in MAX phase of commendable stability against oxygen [145] . Also it has been found that utilization of Ti sponge for MAX synthesis could produce porous MAX phases helping in reducing the addition work for making MAX phase powders. These kind of strategies can be incorporated in large scale manufacturing of MAX phases which reduces the cost and also improves the stability of the material. Despite the challenges mentioned above, state-of-the-art research demonstrates that these challenges are expected to progress significantly soon. There is no doubt that Ti 3 C 2 T x  MXene has guaranteed the era of the next generation of 2D nanomaterials and synthesis of different nanohybrids of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene for various applications will takes place.
abstract: The Ti3C2Tx MXene has ignited a wave of excitement in the world of materials science due to its immense potential for diverse applications. However, a deeper understanding of the synthesis processes involved is crucial to unlock their potential. Here we review the various techniques for producing Ti3C2Tx MXene, covering everything from precursor selection to etching-exfoliation and intercalation-delamination steps. Furthermore, we also explore the oxidation stability of Ti3C2Tx and propose a reaction mechanism to help shed light on this critical aspect of Ti3C2Tx MXene. This review begins with the bibliography studies on Ti3C2Tx and then delves into the principle behind the chemical etching process. Followed by various etching strategies used for Ti3C2Tx synthesis and the impact of individual etching parameters on successful synthesis protocols. Finally, we address the challenges that still need to be overcome to fully realize the potential of Ti3C2Tx and highlight the exciting possibilities for its future development. We aim to inspire further research into this cutting-edge material and encourage the synthesis of Ti3C2Tx MXene with even more outstanding performance and a more comprehensive range of applications.

title: Nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots (NGQD) pillared Ta4C3Tx MXene as high-performance electrochemical supercapacitors
authors: Sabeen Fatima, M. Waqas Hakim, Xiaoxiao Zheng, Yu Sun, Ziheng Li, Nan Han, Muyang Li, Zeyuan Wang, Lei Han, Liang Wang, Safia Khan, Jiangwei Liu, Hu Li
conclusion: In this study, we have prepared Ta4 C3 Tx MXene and nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots (NGQD) using easy and cost-effective synthesis routes. Ta4 C3 Tx MXene sheets were surface engineered via NGQD by adopting a solvothermal synthesis approach. Various NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets were created by carefully regulating the surface engineering of Ta4 C3 Tx sheets with NGQD varying concentrations from 1.5% to 10%. For the assessment of working materials quality, shape, crystallinity, chemical structure, and elemental content, different supporting characterizations such as UV–vis, PL, Raman, XRD, TEM, FTIR, SEM and XPS were also performed. The effective synthesis and excellent quality of every material were explained by these characterizations. To test the charge storage capabilities NGQD, Ta4 C3 Tx , 1.5%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx , 3%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx , 5%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx , 7%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx, and 10%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets were employed as working electrodes in 1 M KOH electrolyte. With the attachment of nitrogen doped graphene quantum dots the charge storage of Ta4 C3 Tx nanosheets was not only enhanced up to sevenfold but also displayed excellent stability for 20k repeated cycles. The performance evaluation of 5%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx //AC capacitor device demonstrated charge storage characteristics in between pseudocapacitance and battery-like properties, along with long-term stability. Also, the increased specific capacity, power, and energy density of the device make 5%-NGQD/Ta4 C3 Tx a superior candidate for energy storage device applications. All things considered, this work offers guidance on how to modify dense MXene phases, such as tantalum carbide, to improve their electrochemical device performances relative to their plain forms. abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials are proved to possess outstanding energy storage capabilities for advanced supercapacitors, yet these materials require modification to overcome field obstacles and reach their full potential. Here, we prepared tantalum carbide MXene and nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots (NGQD) by adopting facile synthesis routes. Surface engineering of 2D tantalum carbide sheets is carefully performed with zero-dimensional graphene to achieve NGQD/Ta4C3Tx nanosheets. The compositional analysis demonstrated the attachment of quantum dots with MXene sheets. The modified 1.5%-NGQD/Ta4C3Tx, 3%-NGQD/Ta4C3Tx, 5%-NGQD/Ta4C3Tx, 7%-NGQD/Ta4C3Tx and 10%-NGQD/Ta4C3Tx nanosheets presented enhanced energy storage capability than NGQD and plain MXene. Graphene quantum dots enable Ta4C3Tx to have faster more stable reaction kinetics and enhance the gravimetric capacitance 7 folds (701 F/g) compared to plain MXene (100 F/g). Due to the exceptional working electrode performances, an asymmetric supercapacitor is also fabricated with NGQD/Ta4C3Tx nanosheets as working electrode. The device exhibited a pseudocapacitive battery-like storage mechanism with a specific capacity of 110 Cg-1, power and energy densities of 9000 W/kg and 55 W-h/Kg respectively. Due to the low corrosion rate exhibited by Tafel plots an excellent capacity retention is observed up to 20000 cycles. The study imparts valuable insights into engineering 0D/2D nanostructures for next-generation energy storage systems.

title: Improving the bimetallic interactions of CeO2@MnO2/MXenes for supercapacitor electrode applications
authors: Faiz Imran, Azmat Hussain, Ibrahim Aladhyani, Fawad Ali, Shahbaz Afzal, Raphael M. Obodo
conclusion: Summarily, CeO2 /MXene, MnO2 /MXene, and CeO2 @MnO2 /MXene nanocomposites have been effectively produced utilizing the SILAR deposition process. Nanocrystals with sizes ranging from 32.68 to 38.55 nm were evenly attached to the MXene sheets, making them suitable for use as electrode materials in supercapacitors. The results indicate that the composite electrode exhibited impressive specific capacitance values of 1123, 1270, 1520, and 873, 1020, 1265 F g-1 , respectively, when subjected to GCD tests at current densities of 0.5 Ag-1 and 1.0 Ag-1 . In addition, when these electrodes were used to interact with the CV at a scan rate of 1.0 mVs−1 , they exhibited specific capacitances of 972, 1125, and 1370 F g-1 , respectively. The CeO2 @MnO2 /MXene electrode demonstrated the highest specific capacitance, energy, and power densities. Remarkably, it maintained 73.4 % of its capacity after undergoing 10,000 full cycles. These electrodes exhibited high specific capacitance due to two charge storage mechanisms: electric double-layer capacitance from the Mene and pseudo capacitance from CeO2 and MnO2 , respectively. This can be attributed to an increase in the types and quantity of ions, as well as the presence of MXene, which promotes the formation of stronger connections between different ions and improves the structure and shape of nanoparticles. abstract: The characteristics of large surface area, high chemical firmness and virtuous electrical conductivity make MXene-based electrodes an emerging potential material for supercapacitor electrode applications. The qualities of invented electrodes were examined using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), UV–visible spectroscopy, and electrochemical analysis. The estimated specific capacitance of 1370 F g-1 from cyclic voltammetry (CV) at a scan rate of 1.0 mVs−1 and 1520 F g-1 from galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) at 0.5 Ag-1 current density, respectively, were obtained from the CeO2@MnO2/MXene electrode. The study's findings suggest that the addition of MXene caused the manufactured electrodes' electrochemical properties to improve. The electrodes CeO2/MXene, MnO2/MXene, and CeO2@MnO2/MXene have proven to be quite effective, which makes them a good option for supercapacitor electrode application. The CeO2@MnO2/MXene electrode was found to exhibit remarkable cyclic stability at 0.5 Ag-1 current density, maintaining 73.5 % of its initial measurements after 10,000 full cycles.

title: Interface engineering through embedding Co2O3 nanoparticles onto MXenes layered structure for boosting supercapacitor performance
authors: Chou-Yi Hsu, Waqed H. Hassan, Tapankumar Trivedi, Anjan Kumar, B.R. Sampangi Rama Reddy, Rishabh Thakur, Shirin Shomurotova, Hadi Yasir Abbood Aljanabi, Ahmed Ahmed Abbas Sahib, Hamad M. Alkahtani
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  This study successfully demonstrates the potential of Co₂O₃/MXene nanocomposites as advanced electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors, highlighting the pivotal role of interface engineering in enhancing their electrochemical properties. The unique morphology of the nanocomposite, characterized by an enlarged surface area, a highly conductive MXene support, and dual-layered configurations, facilitates efficient charge transfer and access to active sites. Additionally, the synergistic interplay between the MXene matrix and embedded Co₂O₃ nanoparticles contributes to remarkable improvements in the material's overall performance. This combination not only ensures robust phase stability and retention of electronic properties but also significantly enhances redox activity and capacitance. The supercapacitors with Co₂O₃/MXene electrodes exhibited a high specific capacitance of 448.8 F g⁻¹ at 0.5 A g⁻¹, as well as excellent long-term cycling stability, retaining 88 % of its capacitance after 5000 cycles. These outcomes underscore the potential of leveraging MXenes as conductive supports in tandem with metal oxide nanoparticles to achieve superior energy storage capabilities. Overall, the findings emphasize the prospect of Co₂O₃/MXene nanocomposites for scalable and efficient energy storage applications, suggesting a synergistic design strategy that could inspire the development of next-generation supercapacitor materials.
abstract: MXene-based materials hold great promise as catalyst candidates for energy storage and conversion devices, owing to their unique attributes such as a large surface area, excellent metallic conductivity, and rapid redox activity. However, their potential for widespread industrial use has been substantially hindered by challenges such as surface aggregation and susceptibility to oxidation. In this work, we report the fabrication of a Co₂O₃/MXene nanocomposite supercapacitor material on a conductive nickel (Ni) sheet substrate using a convenient and flexible dip-coating technique. The integration of Co₂O₃ nanoparticles into the layered MXene structure not only exposes a significant number of active sites but also effectively preserves the phase stability and electronic characteristics of the material throughout extensive galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) cycling. The specific capacitance of our Co₂O₃/MXene nanocomposite reaches an impressive value of 448.8 F g⁻¹ at a current density of 0.5 A g⁻¹, reflecting its high efficiency in energy storage. Moreover, after 5000 charge-discharge cycles, the device retains 88 % of its original capacitance, indicating excellent cycling stability. These results highlight the potential of Co₂O₃/MXene nanocomposites as advanced materials for supercapacitor applications, emphasizing their promising performance in energy storage systems.

title: NiCo2O4@MXene composite electrodes: Unveiling high-performance asymmetric supercapacitor capabilities through enhanced redox activity
authors: Abdul Jabbar Khan, Honggeng Ding, Yi Zhang, Daohong Zhang, Ling Gao, Guowei Zhao
conclusion: the NCO@MXene composite with enhanced conductivity improved the cyclability and rate performance of the electrodes. 4 Conclusion In summary, NiCo2 O4 @MXene composites (NCO@MXene) were synthesized using a facile hydrothermal technique. The NCO nanoflowers were evenly distributed over the MXene layers, which may have promoted an expressway for charge carriers. The resulting NCO@MXene composite has exceptional electrochemical properties, as demonstrated by its high capacitance value of 777.7 Fg−1 and retention of 88.5 %, respectively. Furthermore, the NCO@MXene electrode has exceptional long-term durability, with 90 % of its initial capacity after enduring 10,000 cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations proved the excellent performance of the NCO@MXene electrode with a proven enhanced conductive support. The synergistic effect between NCO and MXene contributed to the superior performance of the NCO@MXene//AC-ASC device, highlighting its potential for use in high-performance asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) applications. This work provides valuable insight into the design of advanced electrode materials for energy storage systems, offering a promising route for improving the performance and longevity of ASC devices. abstract: The deteriorated conductive nature and stacking of Ti3C2Tx MXene layers significantly restrict the electrochemical properties, which requires a proper spacer to avoid restacking and improve the conductive behavior. An asymmetric supercapacitor was designed by combining NiCo2O4@MXene composite (NCO@MXene) as the positive electrode and activated carbon (AC) as the negative electrode, forming the NCO@MXene||AC-ASC configuration. The NCO@MXene demonstrated outstanding pseudocapacitive performance in a three-electrode system, realizing an impressive capacitance of 777.7F/g at a current density of 1 A/g and an impressive 89.4 % capacity retention over 10,000 cycles within a potential range of 1.7 V. Moreover, the NCO@MXene||AC–ASC showcased remarkable energy performance, achieving an energy density of 73.3 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 849.9 W kg−1. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrated that the NCO@MXene composite electrode possessed enhanced conductivity with metallic properties. The calculated partial density of states (PDOS) of NCO@MXene HS was stronger than those of pure NCO and MXene. DFT results revealed that the NCO@MXene composite system favored the experimental results for the prepared electrode material. The synergistic effects of NCO and MXene enabled the outstanding electrochemical performance of the NCO@MXene||AC-ASC composite, making it a highly favorable option for high-performance ASC electrodes.

title: Carbon nanotubes modified V-Ti3C2Tx/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) composite as a high-performance electrode for supercapacitor
authors: Ze-Le Lei, Li Wan, Qiu-Feng Lü
conclusion: CVT/PEDOT composite was successfully prepared from EDOT monomers and CNTs modified V-Ti3 C2 Tx by chemical oxidation. The use of V-Ti3 C2 Tx and CNTs improved the electrochemical performance and thermal stability of the CVT/PEDOT composite. Because of the synergistic effect of the V-Ti3 C2 Tx , CNTs, and PEDOT components, CVT/PEDOT achieves a specific capacitance of 263 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1 , which is superior to that of PEDOT. CVT/PEDOT also exhibits excellent cycling stability with a capacity retention of 86 % after 5000 cycles at a current density of 10 A g−1 . Moreover, the energy density of CVT/PEDOT// CVT/PEDOT is up to 15.26 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 600 W kg−1 , which is higher than those of previously reported PEDOT-based composites. abstract: Poly (3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) is an electrically conductive polymer that is highly conductive and oxidatively stable. However, its poor cycling stability and small specific capacitance limit its application as an electrode material for supercapacitors. In this work, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) modified V-Ti3C2Tx/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) composite (CVT/PEDOT) was prepared by obtaining vanadium-doped Ti3C2Tx (V-Ti3C2Tx) using a simple hydrothermal method, and then polymerizing 3,4-ethylene-dioxythiophene monomers (EDOT) on the surface of carbon nanotubes modified V-Ti3C2Tx. The incorporation of CNTs with V-Ti3C2Tx results in better stability of CVT/PEDOT. The synergistic effect of the three components make the CVT/PEDOT composite have good electrochemical performance and excellent cycling stability as an electrode material for supercapacitor. The specific capacitance of CVT/PEDOT at a current density of 1 A g−1 is up to 263 F g−1, and the capacitance retention is 86 % after 5000 cycles at a current density of 10 A g−1, which is superior to that of the V-Ti3C2Tx/PEDOT composite. The energy density of CVT/PEDOT is 15.26 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 600 W kg−1, which is higher than those of previously reported PEDOTs and other PEDOT-based composites. So, the CVT/PEDOT composite can be a potential candidate for electrode materials of supercapacitor.

title: A one-pot strategy for modifying the surface of Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: Ken Aldren S. Usman, Mia Judicpa, Christine Jurene O. Bacal, Kevinilo P. Marquez, Jizhen Zhang, Bhagya Dharmasiri, James D. Randall, Luke C. Henderson, Joselito M. Razal
conclusion: We demonstrated a one-pot polymerization of acrylate monomers, facilitated by the spontaneous reaction of MXene with aryl diazonium species. Unlike most surface radical-initiated methods, we successfully tuned the MXene surface while achieving minimal damage to its inherent chemical composition. This polymerization strategy enabled the coagulation of extruded LC-MXene dispersions into strong and delamination-resistant fibers. The method allows for simultaneous MXene densification and surface functionalization and provides an efficient method for fabricating MXene-based macro-architectures with tailored interfacial properties. abstract: Surface modification of MXenes significantly expands their potential for a wide range of applications. Here, we demonstrate a one-pot spontaneous polymerization of acrylic acid onto MXene sheet surfaces using an aryl diazonium coupling agent (nitrobenzene diazonium salt) as an approach to tune MXene interfacial properties. We use this formation of polymer coatings as a coagulation strategy for spinning fibers from liquid crystal MXene dispersions, obtaining densified free-standing fibers with tensile strength and breaking energy of ∼155 MPa and ∼4.5 MJ m−3. This simple method potentially offers a scalable approach for fabricating functional MXene macroarchitectures.

title: Boosting electrochemical activity via manipulating the d-band center of CoNi2Se4/MXene heterostructure for supercapacitor application
authors: Minmin Hu, Lihong Chen, Yu Wang, Jun Dai, Yifan Bi, Yuanming Li, Jian Zhao, Guicun Li, Lei Wang, Alan Meng, Zhenjiang Li
conclusion: 3  Conclusions  In summary, we have successfully fabricated a P-doped CoNi 2 Se 4 /Ti 3 C 2 T x heterostructure with abundant Se vacancies as battery-type cathode for supercapacitor application through a one-step hydrothermal method followed by the phosphating treatment. The homogeneous dispersion of CoNi 2 Se 4 on MXene effectively mitigates the issue of nanosheet aggregation, thereby diminishing the ion diffusion barrier to the redox reaction sites. The incorporation of P leads to a decrease in the valence state of the metallic Ni/Co and the inoization energy of P is higher than that of Se, resulting in an upshift of the d-band center of Ni/Co. Consequently, the occupancy of the antibonding state decreases when the metal active sites react with the electrolyte ion OH − , fostering accelerated electron mobility and enhanced Ni/Co 3d-O 2p orbital hybridization. Additionally, the reduction in the valence state of Ni/Co facilitates the formation of Se vacancies, generating numerous exposed unsaturated dangling bonds carrying positive charges, which serve as robust adsorption sites for foreign anions OH − and facilitate the ion diffusion. Collectively, these advancements culminate in a higher capacitance of 1520 F g −1 at 1 A g −1 , with a mere 20% capacitance decay after 5000 cycles. Furthermore, by pairing this cathode with an AC anode, an HSC achieves a desirable energy density of 37.4 Wh kg −1 at the power density of 0.8 kW kg −1 . This work provides an effective method to heighten the electrochemical performance of transition metal compounds via the synergy of favorable architectures and electronic effect.
abstract: Heteroatom substitution stands as a promising strategy to boost the redox activity of transition metal selenides in supercapacitors; nonetheless, the underlying mechanisms that govern this enhanced activity have yet to be fully elucidated. It is presented that d-band center can be utilized as a descriptor to elucidate the redox activity. Within this context, we employ CoNi2Se4/MXene heterostructure as a paradigm, wherein CoNi2Se4 nanoplates are meticulously dispersed on MXene, thereby fostering a more efficient ion diffusion pathway to the redox reaction sites. Subsequently, phosphorus (P) heteroatoms, characterized by lower electronegativity and elevated ionization energy, are incorporated into CoNi2Se4/MXene architecture, which upshifts the d-band center of Ni/Co active sites in CoNi2Se4 close to the Fermi level, resulting in a depletion in the occupancy of antibonding orbitals upon interaction with the O 2p orbital from electrolyte ion OH−. This enhances the interfacial charge transfer and ensures robust OH− adsorption, thereby boosting redox activity. Meanwhile, P doping also introduces Se vacancies, facilitating the ion adsorption and diffusion. Leveraging these advancements, the prepared cathode delivers a higher specific capacitance and retains a better cycling stability. This investigation not only delineates criteria for heteroatom selection but also sheds light on the intricate mechanisms of heteroatom substitution, offering a fresh perspective on the orbital-scale manipulation to augment the redox activity of supercapacitor electrodes.

title: Facile synthesis of MnO2@Ti3C2Tx composite electrodes for superior performance supercapacitor
authors: Yinghao Lv, Jiaqi He, Yajie Yang, Meilin Huang, Dawei He, Yongsheng Wang
conclusion: Overall, the composite material of 1, 3, 6, and 9-MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx is effectively deposited onto the current collector (Ni foam) surface via a facile solution immersion method, culminating in the successful fabrication of the MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx electrodes. Varying the immersion cycles influences the deposition state of MnO2 , which significantly affects the electrochemical performance. Notably, the nanoflower-shaped 6-MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx demonstrates the highest electrochemical activity. This self-assembly synthesis approach eliminates the need for binders and conductive agents, allowing for precise characterization of the electrochemical behavior of the Ti3 C2 Tx and MnO2 composite. Importantly, 6-MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx exhibits a C s of 324.1 F g−1 , representing a 407.2 % improvement over 6-MnO2 in the identical three-electrode configuration with 0.5 M Na2 SO4 . This enhancement is attributed to Ti3 C2 Tx , which not only functions as a nucleation substrate for the deposition of MnO2 but also enhances the electrical conductivity of the composite material. Furthermore, the asymmetric supercapacitor, which combines 6-MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx and Ti3 C2 Tx , has an energy density of 30.8 W h kg−1 . This facile synthesis method for the large-scale self-assembly of MnO2 @Ti3 C2 Tx composite electrodes holds great promise for practical applications in the energy storage field. Furthermore, our study focused on a single synthesis condition, namely the number of impregnation cycles in the solution-immersion technique, and we investigated the electrochemical behavior of this self-assembled electrode in a low-concentration neutral electrolyte. It is anticipated that, in the future, the energy storage performance of such self-assembled electrodes can be further optimized and their application scope expanded by exploring alternative synthesis parameters, selecting compatible electrolytes, and optimizing anode materials. abstract: Supercapacitors are gaining traction in the energy storage sector due to their high power and energy density. MnO2 is identified as a promising supercapacitors electrode material due to its reversible Faraday reaction and great theoretical specific capacitance. However, its practical performance is hindered by poor electrical conductivity and structural instability. By incorporating Ti3C2Tx, a 2D MXene material known for its high conductivity and functional groups, the electrochemical behavior of the MnO2 composite is expected to be enhanced. This study introduces a novel method for synthesizing MnO2@Ti3C2Tx self-assembled electrodes (1, 3, 6, 9-MnO2@Ti3C2Tx composite electrodes) via a simple solution immersion technique at room temperature and ambient pressure. The state of manganese dioxide deposition can be influenced by varying the number of operations of the solution immersion technique. Among them, 6-MnO2@Ti3C2Tx has the largest specific surface area and achieves the best specific capacitance of 324.1 F g−1. When the current density is increased to 10 A g−1, the specific capacitance retention of 6-MnO2@Ti3C2Tx is 67.11 %. Furthermore, the 6-MnO2@Ti3C2Tx//Ti3C2Tx asymmetric capacitor demonstrated a maximum energy density of 30.8 W h kg−1 and a power density of 7493.3 W kg−1, maintaining a capacitance retention rate of 95.98 % (from 74.6 to 71.6F g−1) after 2000 charge-discharge cycles. This study presents an effective and scalable synthesis strategy for MnO2 composite electrodes, highlighting their potential for future energy storage applications.

title: MXene/Biomass-derived activated carbon composite for supercapacitor applications
authors: Rohit Sinha, P. Sai Kiran, K. Vijay Kumar, Niranjan Pandit, Chintham Satish, Saurav Keshri, Anup Kumar Keshri
conclusion: In this work, we have successfully synthesized the biomass-activated carbon incorporated in the Mxene composite. In this, biomass-activated carbon was prepared by utilizing the two-stage activation process with the help of KOH in different weight ratios. The KOH-activated carbon addition has attributed superior characteristics like induced defects and hierarchal porous structure in synthesized Mxene composite. In particular, the MxACK3 composite exhibited superior properties in terms of higher surface area (SSA) 2080.55 m2 g−1 with the coexistence of meso and micropores, hydrophilic nature (CA = 13.46°), increased interlayer spacing (d = ∼1.1 nm). Notably, the MxACK3 composite exhibited superior electrochemical performance with a specific capacitance (407 F g−1 ) at 5 mV s−1 . Further, measured capacitance calculation revealed a higher EDLC behavior contribution of 60.31 % at a lower scan rate (i.e., 5 mV s−1 ), exceptional than the pristine Mxene and other Mx composites. Additionally, the rate capability of ASSC showed up to 5000 cycles with an outstanding 96.36 % coulombic efficiency and 92.98 % capacitance retention, proving long-term stability in an aqueous environment. This improved electrochemical behavior can be ascribed to reduced restacking issues, the formation of a 3D open structure with incorporated activated carbon, and increased active sites for ion storage and transport. Our findings delve into a new pathway for utilizing biomass-activated carbon's capability to improve Mxene-based composites and nanomaterials in different electrolyte environments for energy storage applications. abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) MXenes (e.g., Ti₃C₂Tₓ) have garnered significant interest in supercapacitor applications because of their outstanding conductivity, hydrophilicity, and charge storage capabilities. However, the inherent tendency of MXenes to restack and agglomerate severely limits electrolyte accessibility and reduces their electrochemical performance. To address this limitation, creating three-dimensional (3D) porous architectures by introducing interlayer spacers has emerged as an effective strategy. Conventionally, expensive spacers like graphene, carbon nanotubes, polypyrrole, reduced graphene oxide, etc., have been employed, which restricts scalability and cost-efficiency. Herein, we present a sustainable and cost-effective approach by synthesizing porous activated carbon (AC) derived from biomass waste (orange peels) and incorporating it as a spacer within Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene layers. The resulting Ti₃C₂Tₓ/AC composite demonstrates enhanced structural stability through increased open spaces and expanded interlayer spacing (d = ∼1.1 nm), improved hydrophilicity (contact angle (CA): 13.46°), and superior electrolyte accessibility. Electrochemical evaluation in aqueous electrolyte shown a specific capacitance of 407 F g−1 at 5 mV s−1. Furthermore, the fabricated all solid-state supercapacitor (ASSC) showed the rate capability of up to 5000 cycles with an outstanding 96.36 % coulombic efficiency and 92.98 % capacitance retention, proving long-term stability in an aqueous environment. Our study underscores the dual advantage of valorizing biomass waste for creating porous carbon and achieving scalable, environmentally friendly MXene composites with optimized electrochemical properties for supercapacitor applications in aqueous electrolyte.

title: Cylindrical janus Mosse@CNT intercalated into Mxene: A high-performance supercapacitor electrode with high volumetric capacity and flexibility
authors: Nouf Alharbi
conclusion: To summarize, this study introduces a new and efficient approach for producing high-performance supercapacitor electrodes by integrating MoSSe@CNT into MXene sheets. The MoSSe@CNT hybrids function as effective spacers to inhibit the restacking of MXene while also making a major contribution to the overall pseudocapacitance. The MoSSe@CNT/MXene electrode has outstanding volumetric energy storage capacity (1819 F cm−3 ), impressive rate capability, and extraordinary adaptability. In addition, the artificially created symmetrical supercapacitor exhibits a remarkable energy density, emphasizing the potential of this method in the advancement of flexible and high-performance energy storage devices for supplying power to small and portable electronic gadgets. CRediT authorship contribution statement Nouf Alharbi: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Visualization, Validation, Supervision, Software, Resources, Methodology, Investigation,
abstract: Restoring MXene’s intrinsic capacitive function is essential for high-performance supercapacitors. This study presents a new approach to tackle the problem of restacking and improving energy storage. It involves incorporating MoSSe@CNT (MoSSe nanosheets wrapped around carbon nanotubes) into MXene films, which are exceptionally electrochemically active. After optimisation, the MoSSe@CNT/MXene electrode demonstrates remarkable volumetric and gravimetric capacitance values of 1819 F cm⁻³ and 585 F g⁻¹, respectively. The exceptional performance of MoSSe@CNT arises from the combined effects of MoSSe@CNT acting as both spacers and active contributors to pseudocapacitance. The electrode obtained exhibits exceptional rate capability, flexibility, and a high energy density of 47.5 Wh L⁻¹, making it a highly promising contender for advanced energy storage systems.

title: Nitrogen functionalization modulates interlayer spacing and surface composition in 2D MXene/Ti3C2Tx for enhanced ammonium ion (NH4+) storage
authors: Ayesha Irfan, Nimra Irshad, Inaam Ullah, Samira Saddique, Chenxi Li, Muhammad Irfan, Mamoona Sattar, Salamat Ali, Haotian Hu, Waqar ul Hasan, Mai Li, Ping Zhong
conclusion: This study highlights the exceptional potential of nitrogen-functionalized Ti3 C2 Tx (Ti3 C2 Tx – TiN) as a promising material for enhancing NH4 + ion storage in AA-HPCs. By strategically engineering the electronic structure through nitrogen functionalization, we effectively mitigate the challenges of sheet restacking, thus improving ion diffusion, and long-term stability. The Ti3 C2 Tx – TiN electrodes demonstrated superior capacitance, charge retention, and cycling stability compared to unmodified Ti3 C2 Tx , underscoring their potential for sustainable, high-performance energy storage. These findings not only position Ti3 C2 Tx – TiN as a leading material for NH4 + -based AA-HPCs but also pave the way for future advancements in alternative, safer energy storage systems. Further research should focus on optimizing material properties and scaling up these systems for broader commercial applications. abstract: Aqueous ammonium ions (NH4+) hybrid pseudocapacitors (AA-HPCs), utilizing NH4+ and SO42− as charge carriers, have garnered significant attention due to their higher sustainability and reduced fire risk compared to commercial lithium-ion batteries. NH4+, with their hydrogen bonding properties, form weaker bonds with nitrogen, oxygen, carbon, and fluorine atoms, enhancing ion diffusion and reaction kinetics. MXene/Ti3C2Tx, a novel two-dimensional (2D) material, effectively enhances NH4+ charge storage and mechanical stability, but its ion diffusion is hindered by strong van der Waals interactions between adjacent sheets, which is mitigated through nitrogen functionalization (Ti3C2Tx–TiN). In a three-electrode system, Ti3C2Tx–TiN electrodes showed superior electrochemical performance over pure Ti3C2Tx, with a specific capacitance of 509.44 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and 98.2 % charge retention after 10,000 cycles. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations revealed increased adsorption energy and improved electronic properties in Ti3C2Tx–TiN. Further, AA-HPCs with Ti3C2Tx–TiN as the cathode and activated carbon as the anode achieved capacitance of 113.03 F g−1, 99.44 % charge retention after 15,000 cycles, and an energy density of 40.19 Wh kg−1 at (800 W kg−1). These findings suggest that N-functionalized MXene-based AA-HPCs are promising for NH4+ storage.

title: Nanoflower-like hollow NiMnCo-OH decorated with self-assembled 2D Ti3C2Tx for high-efficiency hybrid supercapacitors
authors: Chenming Liang, Zikai Feng, Mingwu Chen, Xiaohui Xv, Min Lu, Weixue Wang
conclusion: In summary, nanoflower-like hollow NMCM composites were successfully prepared through a synergistic multi-element doping and self-assembly strategy. The fabricated hybirds not only address the inadequate capacitance issue of Ti3 C2 Tx but also increase the limited conductivity and unsatisfactory rate capability of hydroxides. The hierarchical structure prevented the re-assembly of 2D nanosheets and provided sufficient cavities and open channels for rapid ion transport, thereby enhancing electrochemical kinetics effectively. The optimized NMCM electrode material demonstrated exceptional rate capability, cycling stability, and a remarkable specific capacitance of 232.37 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1 . The NMCM-based ASC device had a great density of 54.1 Wh kg−1 (800 W kg−1 ). The fabrication of a hollow-structured energy storage device by using 2D nanosheets paves the way for producing energy storage equipment with exceptional electrochemical characteristics. abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) have gained awareness as promising energy materials due to their high electrochemical activity and tunable interlayer characteristics. However, inherent drawbacks limit them to achieve high capacitance. Introducing complementors with high conductivity and stability is an effective strategy for addressing these challenging issues. Therefore, we employed a simple and controllable method to synthesize nanoflower-like hollow NiMnCo-OH@MXene (NMCM) composites by multi-element doping and electrostatic self-assembly strategies. The MXene nanosheets formed a three-dimensional (3D) conductive network, which increased stability and promoted fast charge transport at interfaces. At the same time, the heterogeneous ternary hydroxides inhibited MXene aggregation and provided considerable capacitance. The NMCM showed ultra-long cycling stability of 91.7% after 5000 cycles at 5 A g−1 (compared to the initial specific capacitance) and achieved a capacitance capacity of 232.37 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1 in a three-electrode device. Furthermore, under 800 W kg−1 power density, the NMCM//Ti3C2 asymmetric device showed an impressive energy density of 54.1 Wh kg−1. This work demonstrates a simple and successful strategy for creating high-performance energy storage devices based on 3D hollow framework electrodes.

title: Self-assembled MXene(Ti3C2Tx)/α-Fe2O3 nanocomposite as negative electrode material for supercapacitors
authors: Ren Zou, Hongying Quan, Menghua Pan, Shuai Zhou, Dezhi Chen, Xubiao Luo
conclusion: MXene/α-Fe2 O3 nanocomposites were prepared through electrostatic attraction with the aid of surfactant. The prepared nanostructure could effective inhibit the restacking of Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes and facilitate electrolyte transport of α-Fe2 O3. Owing to the high conductivity of Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes and the high specific capacitance of α-Fe2 O3 , the fabricated MXene/α-Fe2 O3 nanocomposites exhibited a high specific capacitance up to 405.4 F g−1 at the current density of 2 A g−1 , and still 197.62 F g−1 (48.9% remaining) at the current density of 20 A g−1 . In addition, the MXene/α-Fe2 O3 electrode showed high cycling stability with 97.7% retention of the initial capacitance after 2000 cycles at a scan rate of 100 mV s−1 . The excellent electrochemical performance of the MXene/α-Fe2 O3 nanocomposites demonstrates their potential as negative electrode materials for supercapacitors, and our work provides some new thoughts for the synthesis of MXene/metal oxides nanocomposites.
