abstract: The present manuscript has synthesized the innovative nanocomposite of tungsten decorated reduced graphene oxide (TGO) based FeNi codoped MnO2 (TGO-3 % FeNi-MnO2) which has better supercapacitor performance than the tungsten carbide (TC) MXene-based nanocomposite sample (TC-3 % FeNi-MnO2). The first motive of the manuscript is to manufacture lower-cost materials with better properties with higher stability. Nowadays, worldwide researchers are focusing on MXene materials and reporting the best smart material for multiple applications but the present manuscript has done an innovative study and found that the graphene-based materials have good properties with higher stability like MXene samples. The prepared nanocomposite samples have been characterized by XRD, FE-SEM, BET, XPS, Fluorescence spectroscopy, and cyclic voltammetry. X-ray diffraction (XRD) investigation demonstrated that mixed phases of tetragonal α-MnO2 and cubic α-Mn2O3 were observed. The nanocomposite of tungsten decorated reduced graphene oxide-based FeNi codoped MnO2 has a nanorod-like morphology which was better than all synthesized samples. The higher capacitance found for the tungsten decorated reduced graphene oxide-based Fe-Ni codoped MnO2 sample is 883 F g−1. The impact of the surface area (317.42 m2/g), defects, and structural parameters on capacitance enhancement was studied in detail. The TGO-3 % FeNi-MnO2 sample has higher surface defects which was attributed by XPS and fluorescence spectroscopy.

title: Effectiveness of Nitrogen-Doping in MXene-Based Composites for Supercapacitor Electrodes
authors: Ghobad Behzadi pour, Leila Fekri aval, Hamed Nazarpour-Fard
conclusion: This review offers a comparative assessment of supercapacitors that utilize MXene materials, while also exploring the performance enhancements made to MXene composite electrodes via the N-doping method. The results demonstrate that within a typical comparative framework, the SC values have experienced a substantial increase between 1.3 times and nearly 8 times. This elevation in capacitance is largely connected to improvements in pseudocapacitance and surface redox activity due to N-doping. Furthermore, N-doping leads to an expansion of the interlayer spacing in MXene materials. The development of supercapacitors utilizing MXene materials has significantly contributed to the progress of high-efficiency energy storage systems. The prospects for energy storage are bright with the advent of MXene-based supercapacitors, which demonstrate exceptional energy density/power density ratios and a substantial specific capacitance. These attributes position them as a highly sustainable and effective option for energy storage solutions. CRediT authorship contribution statement Ghobad Behzadi pour: Writing – original draft, Supervision, Investigation. Leila Fekri aval: Validation, Methodology. Hamed Nazarpour-Fard: Software, Formal analysis.
abstract: The MXenes present a candidate for use as electrode material in the development of supercapacitors due to the presence of numerous interlayer ions, lightweight characteristics, and fast charge/discharge ability. Although MXenes have gained significant attention as an electrode material for supercapacitors, the inherent challenge posed by the stacking of layers due to interlayer van der Waals forces remains unresolved. The incorporation of nitrogen (N) into MXene materials and their composites represents a significant approach to improving their electrochemical properties. N-doped exhibits considerable potential for enhanced electrochemical performance, primarily by facilitating effective interaction between electrolyte ions and carbon-based materials. The N-doping has emerged as an effective modification technique to improve the electrochemical characteristics of MXenes. This review presents a comparative study of the performance enhancement of MXene-based supercapacitor electrodes and their composites through the N-doping technique. Results indicated by N-doping the specific capacitance (SC) of the MXene-based supercapacitors was increased. The SC improvement can be attributed to the synergistic interaction of optimum N levels, augmented interlayer spacing, and improved surface redox activity, facilitating rapid ion intercalation and electron transfer. Levels of doping have been reviewed by various techniques such as photochemical N-doping, ammonium decomposition, thermal treatment, and N sources.

title: High-performance fractal microsupercapacitors based on Ti3C2Tx MXene for kHz alternating current line-filtering applications
authors: Dong Wang, Lei Qiao, Maoyang Xia, Jingjing Huang, Chi Zhang, Jing Ning, Xin Feng, Jincheng Zhang, Yue Hao
conclusion: In conclusion, we fabricated Ti3 C2 Tx MXene-based FMSCs with a fractal structure design and superior electric field, enhancing their capacitance and frequency characteristic performance. Compared to conventional IMSCs, the optimized FMSCs, achieved by adjusting the width and thickness of microelectrodes, showed a maximum areal specific capacitance of 615.3 μF cm−2 , a cutoff frequency (f 0 ) of 1.21 kHz, and a high-power characteristic at an ultrahigh scan rate of 2000 V s−1 . These improvements can be attributed to the fractal structure design, which creates a superior electric field, accelerating the motion of ions in the electrolyte and facilitating greater ion absorption around these sites. Moreover, the integrated FMSCs exhibit excellent uniformity, meeting the customized requirements for operating voltage windows and capacity across various frequency ranges. Notably, they played a crucial role in the AC line-filtering circuit, effectively filtering various waveforms and high-frequency (20 kHz) AC signals to produce DC signals. This study provides novel guidance for designing MSC structures to meet the AC-DC conversion demands in micro/nano energy power management systems.
abstract: Microsupercapacitors (MSCs) are attracting attention as vital filter capacitors for microscale power conversion in alternating current (AC) line-filtering circuits due to their rapid frequency response characteristics. This study demonstrates the wafer-scale fabrication of Ti3C2Tx MXene-based MSCs with a high-potential device structure incorporating fractal microelectrodes. The experimental and simulation results show that the new structure enables increased ion-transport rates through increased absorption sites and a strong electric field, resulting in improved energy storage and frequency response performance. Therefore, by optimizing the size of the microelectrodes, the fractal MSCs (FMSCs) achieve a high specific capacitance of 615.3 μF cm−2 at 1 V s−1 and their highest frequency characteristic (f0) can reach kHz. Notably, the FMSCs exhibit excellent filtering performance in AC line-filtering circuits by successfully filtering different AC waveforms at a high frequency of 20 kHz into direct current.

title: Multilayered MXene electrodes in deep eutectic solvent ionic liquid electrolyte for supercapacitor applications
authors: Derya Kapusuz Yavuz, Abdulcabbar Yavuz
conclusion: This work examined the electrochemical performance of ml-Ti3 C2 Tx , a MXene family member, in several electrolytes, focusing on the cost-effective ionic liquid Ethaline. ml-Ti3 C2 Tx attained a capacitance of 356 mF/cm2 in Ethaline at a scan rate of 5 mV/s which increased to 640 mF/cm2 at 1 mV/s. This performance was observed throughout a large potential window of 1.7 V, exceeding several MXene capacitance values reported in the literature. The electrochemical performance of ml-Ti3 C2 Tx is markedly affected by the characteristics of the electrolyte. Alkaline (KOH) and neutral (Na2 SO4 ) aqueous electrolytes are unsuitable for MXene-based energy storage due to degradation and negligible electrochemical activity, respectively, within the 1.7 V potential window. The wider potential window noted in Ethaline was ascribed to improved ion intercalation and enhanced electrostatic interactions between the ionic liquid species and the Ti3 C2 Tx layers. The broadest potential range of 1.7 V, including both positive and negative voltages, resulted in the greatest capacitance of MXene in Ethaline. Narrower windows of 0.6 V (positive) and 1.2 V (negative) resulted in lower capacitance values. These findings underscore the importance of a higher potential window in increasing energy density, as it allows for the use of fewer or smaller supercapacitor units to obtain the same storage capacity. The contribution of this work is essential for advancing high-performance, durable supercapacitors that can satisfy the requirements of modern energy applications, such as renewable energy systems and electric vehicles.
abstract: Numerous studies have shown that two-dimensional titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx), a MXene family member, has promising electrochemical characteristics for energy storage. Ti3C2Tx, made by selective etching of A layers in MAX phases, is suitable to various applications owing to its high surface area, hydrophilic surfaces, variable interlayer spacing, and strong electrical conductivity. Its supercapacitor performance has received attention because it has the potential to bridge high-power capacitors with high-energy batteries. This work compares the potential window and capacitance performance of multilayered (ml-) Ti3C2Tx in non-aqueous ionic liquid electrolyte (Ethaline) to alkaline (KOH) and neutral (Na2SO4) electrolytes. LiF + HCl etching method was used to produce ml-Ti3C2Tx, which was tested in three potential windows: positive (0 to +0.6 V), negative (0 to −1.2 V), and combined positive-negative (+0.5 to −1.2 V). The areal capacitance of ml-Ti3C2Tx in Ethaline was determined as 40 mF/cm2 within a narrow potential window (0.6 V) and increased to 356 mF/cm2 within a wider potential window (1.7 V) at a scan rate of 5 mV/s. Aqueous KOH and Na2SO4 electrolytes were unsuitable for MXene based energy storage with 1.7 V potential window due to degradation. SEM-EDS, XRD, TEM, FTIR and CV indicated effective synthesis, functionalization, and electrochemical activity of ml-Ti3C2Tx. Surface modifications, such as O-H and C-O vibrational bands, demonstrate the importance of electrolyte interactions in improving performance. It was shown that ionic liquid electrolytes like Ethaline can improve energy storage. This study advances high-performance supercapacitors by widening the potential window and enhancing charge storage processes, meeting the growing demand for efficient and sustainable energy.

title: MXene mastery: Transforming supercapacitors through solid-solution innovations
authors: Yedluri Anil Kumar, Reddi Mohan Naidu Kalla, Tholkappiyan Ramachandran, Ahmed M. Fouda, H.H. Hegazy, Md Moniruzzaman, Jaewoong Lee
journal: Journal of Industrial and Engineering Chemistry
conclusion: Conclusions and future prospects  Researchers have increasingly focused on MXene solid-solution materials for advancing supercapacitor technology, driven by the distinctive properties of MXenes that make them highly effective for energy storage applications. Among the most notable advantages are their large specific surface area, high electrical conductivity, and the unique two-dimensional (2D) structure that enables fast ion diffusion and charge transport. In particular, titanium carbide-based MXenes like Ti 3 C 2 T x have emerged as strong candidates for supercapacitors due to their ability to achieve high capacitance, quick charge–discharge rates, and superior power and energy densities when compared to traditional carbon-based supercapacitors. One of the key advantages of MXenes is their tunable surface chemistry, which allows for precise control over their electrochemical properties. By modifying surface terminations (e.g., −O, –OH, −F), researchers can adjust the interaction of MXenes with different electrolytes, enabling the design of application-specific supercapacitors. This flexibility opens up opportunities to improve energy and power density simultaneously, something that has historically been difficult to achieve with conventional supercapacitors, which tend to favor either high power or high energy storage, but not both. Moreover, MXenes' intrinsic pseudocapacitive behavior contributes significantly to their outstanding performance. Unlike electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), which store energy through physical adsorption of ions at the electrode–electrolyte interface, pseudocapacitive MXenes can undergo fast surface redox reactions. This results in higher charge storage capabilities and better overall electrochemical performance. Recent studies have demonstrated that MXene-based supercapacitors can achieve specific capacitance values exceeding 1,500 F/g, positioning them as frontrunners for next-generation energy storage devices.  Additionally, MXenes' 2D layered structure allows for easy fabrication of flexible and lightweight electrodes, making them ideal for applications in portable electronics and wearable devices. The combination of flexibility, mechanical robustness, and high conductivity ensures that MXene-based supercapacitors can deliver consistent performance even under mechanical stress, such as bending or stretching. This makes them particularly attractive for use in emerging technologies, such as flexible and stretchable electronics, where traditional rigid materials are unsuitable. Despite these advantages, several challenges remain in the practical deployment of MXene-based supercapacitors. One major issue is restacking, where the 2D MXene layers tend to reassemble during electrode fabrication, leading to reduced surface area and limited ion accessibility. This negatively impacts the overall performance of the supercapacitor, especially in terms of ion transport and capacitance retention at high charging rates. To address this, researchers have explored various strategies, such as intercalating larger ions or molecules between MXene layers to increase interlayer spacing, thus preventing restacking and enhancing ion diffusion. Another significant challenge is the long-term stability and cycling performance of supercapacitors based on MXene in real-world scenarios. For real-world applications, it is essential to understand the causes of deterioration and discover solutions to improve durability. To guarantee the viability of large-scale manufacturing for commercial deployment, more research into the cost-effectiveness and scalability of MXene production is necessary. To fully realize the potential of MXene solid-solution materials as supercapacitors, which are currently at the crossroads of exciting advances and established obstacles, researchers must keep digging and working together across fields if we want to build high-performance supercapacitors of the future.  There is tremendous hope for the future of energy storage technology in the realm of supercapacitor research with MXene solid-solution materials. To satisfy the increasing need for effective, high-performance energy storage devices, researchers want to optimize MXene-based supercapacitors further and overcome existing restrictions. Investigating the reasons for deterioration and creating ways to make the materials more resilient are two possible ways to solve the problems with cycle performance and long-term stability. Materials with enhanced structural integrity and electrochemical performance might be the goal of future research into MXene synthesis processes, which could lead to materials with longer operational lives and maintain functioning. Continuous efforts are being made to optimize production processes and minimize costs related to MXene manufacture, with an eye on ensuring commercial viability and scalability. Supercapacitors based on MXene would be more widely available for use in a variety of applications if large-scale manufacture were possible due to developments in scalable synthesis processes. Furthermore, to discover new combinations of characteristics that might further improve energy storage capability, researchers will likely investigate newer MXene compositions and hybrid materials. To drive innovation and put laboratory results into practical applications, multidisciplinary research including material scientists, electrochemists, and engineers must be prioritized. Supercapacitor research with MXene solid-solution materials has exciting prospects as we tackle present obstacles, discover new possibilities, and finally realize their promise as a game-changing technology in the ever-changing energy storage landscape. Better and more efficient energy storage solutions for many uses, from handheld devices to grid-level power storage, may be possible with the further development of the field and the incorporation of MXenes into supercapacitors.
abstract: Exploring innovative materials for supercapacitors has been a focus to broaden energy storage alternatives. The distinctive properties and applications of solid-solution MXenes have garnered significant attention in this regard. This research delves into the application of solid-solution MXene materials in supercapacitor energy storage, examining aspects such as manufacturing, electrochemical behaviour, and structural characteristics. The article begins with an overview of the MXene family, highlighting its potential for energy storage, a highly sought-after quality. The solid-solution approach is particularly favoured for its ability to enhance MXenes electrochemical properties by introducing additional components. This study explores how etching, and intercalation impact the material’s structure and energy storage capabilities. Detailed analyses of the crystallographic, surface chemical, and morphological properties of solid-solution MXenes are conducted. The study emphasizes the influence of these factors on the electrochemical performance of MXene supercapacitors, stressing the importance of tailored design. The research extensively investigates the durability, electrical storage capacity, and charge retention mechanisms of these materials. Understanding the effects of dopants and intercalants on charge storage dynamics could lead to improvements in MXene electrode energy storage. The paper reviews the current advancements, challenges, and the potential of solid-solution MXenes in supercapacitors. With a careful examination of existing research and strategic selection of constituents, solid-solution MXene materials could play a crucial role in future energy storage systems, providing a valuable tool for engineers and scientists exploring renewable energy storage technologies.

title: Functional integrated electromagnetic interference shielding in flexible micro-supercapacitors by cation-intercalation typed Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: Xin Feng, Jing Ning, Boyu Wang, Haibin Guo, Maoyang Xia, Dong Wang, Jincheng Zhang, Zhong-Shuai Wu, Yue Hao
conclusion: 3  Conclusion  In summary, a highly conductive Mn ions introduced Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene was developed as a promising material for MSCs functional EMI shielding. The cation intercalation mechanism of Ti 3 C 2 T x was explored as that Mn ions were inclined to be bonding with interfacial oxygen-contained terminal, performed as the orbital hybridization of Mn 3d and O 2p. Cation intercalation enabled to expand the d-space and improve the electrical conductivity of Ti 3 C 2 T x . With the unrivaled features of Mn ions-introduced Ti 3 C 2 T x , the as-prepared MSCs delivered excellent energy storage ability and outstanding EMI shielding efficiency. This study can provide powerful information on the surface structure and the intercalation mechanism of Ti 3 C 2 T x at the atomic level, enrich the understanding of interlayer engineering of the MXenes. More importantly, this work also can propose new views of functional MSCs with EMI shielding for special on-chip application in microelectronics, endowing great significance for the stability of integrated circuits and micro-systems.
abstract: Multifunctional and flexible micro-supercapacitors (MSCs) have attractive prospects in integrated micro electronic systems fields owing to its high power density, fast charge/discharge rates and small volume feature. Here, a flexible MSC functional electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding is designed based on Mn ion-intercalated Ti3C2Tx MXene, presenting a high areal capacitance of 87 mF cm−2 at 2 mV s−1, remarkable energy density of 11.8 mWh cm−3 and outstanding shielding effectiveness of 44 dB. By density functional theory (DFT) calculation, the interaction between Mn ions and surface terminal (-F, –O, and –OH) of Ti3C2Tx is emphatically discussed, finding that the intercalated Mn ions are inclined to be bonding with O-contained groups with the orbital hybridization of Mn 3d and O 2p. It is intriguing to provide enhanced electrochemical performance in energy storage and additive interlayer EM waves absorption in EMI shielding. The present work can offer new insights about underlying mechanism of cation intercalation in Ti3C2Tx MXene and multiple functional devices application in integrated micro electronics systems field.

title: Insights into the synergistic effect of V3S4 decorated Ti3C2 MXene as an electrode for asymmetric supercapacitor
authors: Sandra Mathew, Kalathiparambil Rajendra Pai Sunajadevi, Arun Varghese, Dephan Pinheiro, B. Saravanakumar
journal: Journal of Physics and Chemistry of Solids
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  A novel MXene-based binary composite material was synthesized by incorporating V 3 S 4 through hydrothermal method and evaluated for its electrochemical supercapacitance performance. The innovative approach has resulted in a composite that leverages the unique properties of both Ti 3 C 2 MXene and V 3 S 4 , leading to reduced self-stacking of Ti 3 C 2 , increased accessible surface area, and exposure of more active sites for charge transport, thereby enhancing conductivity. The Ti 3 C 2 /V 3 S 4 electrode exhibits an enhanced C sp of 1323.7 Fg -1 at 1 Ag -1 , with a remarkable capacitance retention rate of 90.5 % over 2000 cycles. It also maintains a lower R ct value of 4.6 Ω, that is significantly less than that of pristine Ti 3 C 2 and V 3 S 4 . The fabricated device, Ti 3 C 2 /V 3 S 4 //AC exhibited a high energy density of 60.6 Whkg −1 at a power density of 649.2 Wkg -1 . Our findings underscore the promise of MXene-based materials for advancing next-generation energy storage solutions, highlighting their potential to deliver high performance and reliability.
abstract: As the globe moves toward sustainable energy options, effectively storing and managing energy becomes increasingly crucial. Advanced energy storage technologies can bridge the gap between energy generation and consumption, ensuring a reliable and stable supply even when renewable sources are intermittent. In this context, the rise of two-dimensional layered Ti3C2 MXene as a promising electrode for supercapacitors is particularly noteworthy, owing to its unique physical, chemical, and electrocatalytic attributes. Despite its potential, the immediate collapse and aggregation of MXene layers pose significant obstacles to their widespread usage in energy storage applications. This study explores advanced energy storage technologies using V3S4 coupled Ti3C2 MXene as electrodes in asymmetric supercapacitors. By combining the unique properties of V3S4 and Ti3C2 MXene, new avenues for improving the performance of supercapacitors are being unlocked. The experimental results indicate that the Ti3C2/V3S4 electrode exhibits an enhanced specific capacitance (Csp) of 1323.7 Fg-1 at a current density of 1 Ag-1, with an outstanding capacitance retention of 90.5 % after 2000 cycles. An assembled asymmetric supercapacitor, Ti3C2/V3S4//activated carbon shows superior energy storage efficiency, achieving a Csp of 258.4 Fg-1 at 2 Ag-1. The device exhibits a high energy density of 60.6 Whkg−1 at a power density of 649.2 Wkg-1, while holding onto a capacitance retention rate of 91.1 % over 10,000 cycles.

abstract: We present a successful synthesis of a composite material comprising antimony (Sb) and MXene (MX), demonstrating its potential as a high-performance material for future energy storage devices. A facile thermal annealing method is employed to produce Sb@MX hybrid materials, exhibiting enhanced electrochemical performance in asymmetric devices for electrical energy storage. Detailed materials characterization, particularly through field emission transmission electron microscopy (FE-TEM), reveals de-laminated two-dimensional layers of MXene decorated with ball-milled antimony nanoparticles. Electrochemical characterizations confirm the optimal electrochemical window range (0–0.6 V vs. Ag/AgCl) in a three-electrode system. In the two-electrode system, configured as an aqueous asymmetric supercapacitor in pouch cell form, the Sb@MX//AC device outperforms Sb-ball mill and MXene//AC devices, showcasing maximum specific capacitances of 184.72 F/g, 65.10 F/g, and 36.61 F/g, respectively, at a fixed current density of 1 A/g within the voltage range of 0.00 - 1.44 V. The Sb@MX//AC device exhibits superior cyclic voltammetry electrochemical behavior, charge-discharge curves, pseudo-capacitance energy storage performance, and exceptional capacity retention (53.10%) over 10,000 cycles. This remarkable stability positions it as a promising candidate for future supercapacitor devices, highlighting its potential for long-lasting and efficient energy storage applications.

title: Optimizing ZnSe microspheres through 2D MXene for asymmetric pseudocapacitive supercapacitors and efficient hydrogen production via water splitting
authors: Inaam Ullah, Ayesha Irfan, Mai Li, Samira Saddique, Tiantian Yang, Hanxue Zhao, Nimra Irshad, Kaishuai Yang, Chunrui Wang, Paul K. Chu
conclusion: In this study, the morphological and crystallographic properties of hydrothermally synthesized ZnSe microspheres are optimized. The synergistic effects rendered by the 2D-MXene nanosheets enhance the electrochemical performance in the APSC device as well as the water-splitting setup. The ZnSe electrode shows good electrochemical performance, but self-aggregation and side reactions of Zn restrict the performance of the cathode and applications. The Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets function as a physical barrier to alleviate agglomeration and impeding side reactions of Zn, thereby enabling ZnSe to expose more sites in addition to a consistent supply of Zn2+ , ultimately augmenting the reversibility, enhancing the cyclic stability, and diminishing the overpotential. The composite electrode demonstrates superior integrity and dispersion, resulting in a longer discharging time than the ZnSe electrode. The ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx electrode shows outstanding cyclic stability (98.81 % capacity retention for 10,000 cycles), high specific capacitance of 1673.8 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , and remarkable pseudocapacitive behavior of 88 % at 60 mV s−1 . DFT results confirm the higher adsorption energy, high electron density, and stable structure of the composite electrodes. The AC//ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx -APSC device demonstrates remarkable cyclic stability, energy density, and high specific capacitance boding well for energy storage applications. LSV reveals that the ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx electrode has a remarkable tafel slope in OER (∼51.3 mV dec−1 ) compared to ZnSe (68.7 mV dec−1 ) besides outstanding properties of ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx in HER. This innovative approach effectively mitigates the inherent limitations of ZnSe and significantly enhances the overall electrochemical performance, positioning the ZnSe@Ti3 C2 Tx as a promising candidate for energy storage and water splitting applications. abstract: In response to the increasing demand for sustainable energy, recent efforts have focused on developing novel composites with improved crystalline structures, chemical stability, and conductivity for electrochemical applications. Self-assembled zinc selenide (ZnSe) microspheres are synthesized by a simple hydrothermal process, and their electrochemical applications as a positive electrode/electrocatalyst in asymmetric pseudocapacitive supercapacitor (APSC) and water splitting are investigated. ZnSe is integrated into the two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx/MXene nanosheets that serve as a physical barrier to mitigate agglomeration, prevent side reactions of Zn, provide ZnSe with more sites and a steady Zn2+ supply, ultimately enhancing the electrochemical performance. Composite electrode demonstrates superior specific capacitance of 1673.8 F g−1 at 1 A g−1, remarkable cyclic stability (98.81 % capacity retention over 10,000 cycles), and excellent pseudocapacitive performance of 88 % at 60 mV s−1. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations displayed highest adsorption energy for ZnSe@Ti3C2Tx, showcasing stable structure and strong electron interaction. To demonstrate the commercial viability, active carbon (AC) is employed as the cathode to fabricate the AC//ZnSe@Ti3C2Tx-APSC device. In the water splitting assessment, ZnSe@Ti3C2Tx shows the lowest Tafel slopes (∼51.3 mV dec−1 for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and ∼36.9 mV dec−1 for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER)). This novel approach significantly advances the overall performance of APSC and water-splitting.

title: Construction of proton channels in POMCPs@MXene electrodes for flexible all-solid-state symmetrical supercapacitors
authors: Xiaoyi Li, Yifu Wu, Tingting Chen, Qian wang, Cuiwen Lu, Hongru Hao, Bo Wei, Haolin wang, Chengbao Yao, Feng Zhang, Haijun Pang, Guangning Wang
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, this study demonstrates notable advancements in the development of POMCPs-based flexible supercapacitor materials. We successfully fabricated a 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ-based FSS device, showcasing a combination of favorable electrochemical performance and mechanical flexibility. Through structural design, we fine-tuned the arrangement of water molecules to customize a novel Ni(itmb) 4 [H 2 SiW 12 O 40 ]·5H 2 O (Compound 1 ) with proton-conductive channels. The Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene nanosheets and the customized POMCPs are combined through a simple composite method to produce the 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ composite material, which exhibits an ultrahigh proton conductivity of 0.16 S cm −1 . This represents a promising advancement in ion-conductive materials for supercapacitors. This work also innovatively presents a comprehensive study of the influence mechanisms governing the relationships among wettability, impedance, composition ratio, and capacitance within the 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ material system. Results indicate that optimizing the composition ratio of POMCPs to Ti₃C₂Tₓ effectively enhances material hydrophilicity, as evidenced by a contact angle of 83.4° with 2 M H₃PO₄. This improvement subsequently reduces impedance and increases C s. As expected, the supercapacitor performance of the 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ composite significantly outperforms that of individual POMCP and MXene components: at 5 A g −1 , its C s reaches 892.3 F g −1 , four times that of 1 -GCE; its rate capability is 81.6 %, 1.56 times that of 1 -GCE; and its cycle stability is 96.8 % (vs. 60.3 % for 1 -GCE). Additionally, the FSS device assembled with 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ demonstrates satisfactory energy and power densities, capable of powering a red LED. Notably, it retains 90 % of its C s under significant bending, highlighting its potential for flexible energy storage applications. Overall, the 1 @Ti₃C₂Tₓ composite offers new perspectives for supercapacitor material development, contributing to efforts to meet the demands of high-performance, flexible energy storage in modern electronics. These data can be obtained free of charge from The Cambridge Crystallographic Data Centre via www.ccdc.cam.ac.uk/data_request/cif .]
abstract: Flexible all-solid-state energy storage devices that can meet the needs of portable and wearable electronics are very promising owing to their high safety and high energy density. Here, we first report a novel flexible all-solid-state symmetric supercapacitor (FSS) based on a polyoxometalate-based coordination polymer (POMCPs)@Ti3C2Tx composite film. Its key breakthrough lies in overcoming the limitations of traditional materials through an electrode design featuring customizable proton channels. By finely adjusting the arrangement of water molecules through structural design, we prepared a novel POMCP, Ni(itmb)4[H2SiW12O40]·5H2O (1), with water-assisted proton channels, thereby improving the ionic conduction efficiency. The ingenious structural design effectively facilitates charge transfer, endowing the POMCPs@Ti3C2Tx composite with an ultrahigh proton conductivity of 0.16 S cm−1 at 70 °C while achieving an exceptional specific capacitance of 892.3 F g−1 and maintaining the intrinsic flexibility of MXene materials. The surface wettability of 1@Ti3C2Tx showed that the film exhibits hydrophilic properties, as evidenced by 2 M H3PO4 contact angle of 83.4°. The assembled symmetric supercapacitor showed excellent electrochemical performance, maintaining 84.9 % of its capacitance after 10,000 charge-discharge cycles and 90 % specific capacitance when bent at 90°. In addition, the device successfully powered the red LED. These findings highlight the practical application potential of POMCPs@Ti3C2Tx composites for high-performance, flexible portable energy storage systems.

title: Revealing the ionic storage mechanisms of Mo2VC2Tz (MXene) in multiple aqueous electrolytes for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Xiaodie Xuan, Yangyang Xie, Yi Tang, Jianghong Zhou, Zhao Bi, Junhui Zou, Yu-ang Lei, Jiahang Gao, Lu Li, Aibo Zhang, Chenhui Yang
conclusion: To sum up, 2D few-layer bimetallic Mo2 VC2 Tz MXene nanomaterials have been successfully prepared by introducing high electrochemical activity V atoms into the precursor MAX. The unique bimetallic solid-solution structure of Mo2 VC2 Tz has an enlarged layer spacing and oxygen-dominated surface termini, which together enhance ion accessibility and redox active site density. The electrochemical results indicate that at a current density of 0.1 A g−1 , the Mo2 VC2 Tz electrodes in 1M H2 SO4 , 1M Al2 (SO4 )3 , and 1M KOH have a top three high specific capacitances in 257.6, 143.4, and 134.4 F g−1 , respectively. In an acidic electrolyte, the oxidation-reduction reaction is effectively promoted by the strong interaction between hydrated hydrogen ions (protons) and oxygen-containing functional groups on the surface of the electrode materials, so that the specific capacitance of the system is significantly higher than that of other electrolytic liquid systems. After 20,000 cycles, the Mo2 VC2 Tz film electrode retains a capacity retention rate of 95.71% in the 1M H2 SO4 electrolyte and the Coulomb efficiency is close to 100%. Confirmed by DFT calculations showing increased density of states near the Fermi level and reduced H+ adsorption energy. These structural and electronic modifications synergistically promote rapid proton diffusion and reversible multivalent redox reactions, establishing Mo2 VC2 Tz as a high-performance electrode material for acidic electrolyte-based supercapacitors. In general, this study not only provides theoretical guidance for the application of bimetallic solid-solution MXene materials in the field of energy storage, but also establish an innovative research foundation for the development of high-performance electrochemical energy storage devices by combining experiment and theory. abstract: It is evident that 2D MXene nanomaterials have considerable potential in the domain of electrochemical energy storage. However, the majority of extant studies concentrate on monometallic MXene, and the structural evolution and energy storage mechanisms of bimetallic solid-solution MXene (e.g. Mo2VC2Tz) remain to be elucidated. In this work, flexible, self-supported Mo2VC2Tz films have been fabricated by in situ solid-solution sintering of Mo2VAlC2 and liquid phase etching of the Al layer. The as-prepared Mo2VC2Tz features a unique bimetallic solid-solution structure with expanded interlayer spacing (15.0 Å vs. 9.2 Å in precursor), oxygen-dominated surface termination groups, and enhanced electronic conductivity (258.4 S cm−1) owing to strong Mo-V d-orbital hybridization. The electrochemical properties in hybrid supercapacitors (HSCs) were systematically evaluated in acidic (H2SO4), neutral (Na2SO4, Li2SO4, ZnSO4, Al2(SO4)3, Zn(CF3SO3)2), and alkaline (KOH) electrolytes. The results demonstrate that the Mo2VC2Tz film electrode in 1M H2SO4 exhibits superior pseudocapacitance performance, achieving a gravimetric capacitance of 257.6 F g−1 at 0.1 A g−1, which is nearly four times higher than in neutral electrolytes (e.g., 65.8 F g−1 in 1M Li2SO4). Furthermore, the Mo2VC2Tz exhibited exceptional cycling stability in 1M H2SO4, retaining 95.71% of its initial capacity after 20,000 cycles. Density functional theory calculations revealed the evolution of the electron state distribution before and after V doping in Mo2VC2Tz. Additionally, the interfacial interaction mechanisms between V atoms and cations (H+, Li+, Na+, Zn2+, Al3+ and K+) were elucidated. Therefore, this study provides a theoretical basis for the design of bimetallic MXene in various electrolyte systems, and promotes the development of high-performance HSCs.

title: Electromagnetic interference shielding, mechanical, and flame retardant behaviors of Ti3C2Tx-MXene/glass fabric epoxy hybrid composites
authors: Ayten Nur Yuksel Yilmaz, Ayse Celik Bedeloglu, Doruk Erdem Yunus
conclusion: In this study, fiber-reinforced composites consisting of six layers with different configurations were produced using both MXene-coated and uncoated glass fabrics. The MXene-coated fabrics received 5 and 10 layers of coating. The effect of the number of coatings and various fabric configurations on EMI-SE in the X-band range was investigated. It was observed that increasing the number of conductive layers in the composites led to higher SET . Compared to the pure composite (C1), the composites with 5 and 10 layers of MXene coating (5MXC5 and 10MXC5) showed total shielding effectiveness values that were 147.05 % and 205.80 % higher, respectively. Among the 5MX and 10MX composite groups, the samples 5MXC5 and 10MXC5, which demonstrated the highest shielding effectiveness, underwent bending, ILSS, hardness, and flammability tests. The MXene coating on glass fabric was found to reduce the burning rate of the composites, with 5MXC5 and 10MXC5 showing 15.25 % and 26.31 % lower burning rate than C1, respectively. Moreover, the addition of MXene, a two-dimensional ceramic material with high hardness, increased the hardness of the composites. The hardness values of 5MXC5 and 10MXC5 were 133.29 and 145.05 HV, respectively, representing increases of 10.03 % and 19.74 % over C1. According to the results from bending and ILSS tests, a decrease in composite strength was observed with MXene reinforcement. The increased presence of MXene flakes on the glass fabric surfaces hindered the epoxy's ability to sufficiently impregnate in the thickness direction, weakening the interfacial bond between the fiber and the matrix, which led to a reduction in strength. After the bending test, the fractured surfaces of the composites were examined under a microscope, revealing tensile, compression, and delamination damages were observed. Compared to the neat composite, 10MXC5 showed reductions of 23.88 % and 24.37 % in flexural and ILSS strength, respectively. This study demonstrates that MXene can provide high electromagnetic shielding efficiency to insulating glass fiber-epoxy composites due to its high electrical conductivity. It is anticipated that the total electromagnetic efficiency in the X band range can be further improved through different configurations and increased the amount of fillers. Moreover, this research lays the groundwork for developing glass fiber-reinforced composite materials with electromagnetic shielding and radar-absorbing properties, particularly for aerospace applications. abstract: This study investigates the manufacturability and electromagnetic shielding effectiveness (EMI-SE) of Ti3C2Tx/MXene-coated glass fabric laminated composites for aerospace applications. MXene-coated fabrics were produced using a dip-coating method. The effects of varying dipping counts (5 and 10) and different configurations of fabric arrangements on the EMI-SE of the composites in the X-band range (8.2–12.4 GHz) were investigated. Glass fabrics with 5 and 10 dips showed average surface resistances of 38.56 Ω/sq and 23.17 Ω/sq, respectively. In both the 5- and 10-dip composite sets, the total EMI-SE increased with the number of MXene-coated glass fabric layers in the composite. The 5MXC5 and 10MXC5 specimens, with conductive fabric in all layers, had average total shielding effectiveness (SET) of −18.75 dB and −23.21 dB, respectively. These values are 147.05 % and 205.80 % higher than the neat glass fiber-epoxy composite (C1). Flammability, bending, ILSS, and hardness tests were conducted on these composites. Increasing the MXene content reduced the burning rate, with 10MXC5 exhibiting a 26.31 % lower burning rate compared to C1. However, higher MXene content slightly decreased bending and ILSS values. Optical microscope examination of the fracture surfaces revealed that this decrease was due to delamination damage.

title: MXene (Ti3C2Tx) anodes for asymmetric supercapacitors with high active mass loading
authors: Xuelin Li, Jianfeng Zhu, Wenyu Liang, Igor Zhitomirsky
conclusion: We developed a high-performance Ti3 C2 Tx -CNT composite electrode containing 20% CNT with a 40 mg cm−2 high AML, which can deliver excellent rate performance, a 2.26 F cm−2 high areal capacitance, and long-term cyclic stability in a negative potential range. The enhanced capacitive behavior benefits from the synergy between Ti3 C2 Tx layers and a proper amount of CNT to form more interconnected nanopores for efficient electrolyte ions transfer, improved electronic conductivity, and build more accessible nanostructure for effective reactions. The high mass loadings benefit from an advanced PMMA binder, in which solution multilayered Ti3 C2 Tx and multiwalled carbon nanotube can be well dispersed and mixed. A MnO2 -CNT composite electrode with a 20% carbon nanotube was also fabricated by the same procedure and tested in a positive potential window. Asymmetric devices operating in a cell voltage of 1.6 V consisted of Ti3 C2 Tx -CNT-20 anodes and MnO2 -CNT-20 cathodes, possessing a 1.24 F cm−2 maximum areal capacitance, good cyclic stability after 1000 cycles, as well as a 0.44 mWh cm−2 maximum energy density. The proposed approach in this study provides an idea to design and fabricate advanced electrodes for asymmetric devices in industrial energy-storage applications, which can be operated in large voltage windows with enhanced energy-power characteristics. abstract: MXene (Ti3C2Tx) is an emerging material choice for advanced energy storage. However, the relatively low areal capacitance is a bottleneck in developing asymmetric supercapacitors with enhanced energy-power characteristics in large voltage windows. A simple and straightforward approach is proposed to design and fabricate Ti3C2Tx-multiwalled carbon nanotube (Ti3C2Tx-CNT) composite electrodes. Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) is used as a binder for electrodes with 40 mg cm−2 high active mass loadings (AML); meanwhile, both multilayered Ti3C2Tx and CNT are efficiently dispersed in PMMA solution. The fabricated Ti3C2Tx-CNT electrodes with different CNT contents are tested in a −1.1~-0.3 V negative potential window and analyzed by different electrochemical techniques. The optimization of Ti3C2Tx-CNT-PMMA composition facilitates the design of anodes with capacitance of 2.26 F cm−2 in Na2SO4 electrolyte, which is essentially higher than literature results for Ti3C2Tx. The ability to obtain high capacitance in the Na2SO4 electrolyte is a crucial result, which facilitates the fabrication of asymmetric aqueous devices operating at 1.6 V. The Ti3C2Tx-CNT anode is combined with a MnO2-CNT cathode in an asymmetric cell, which shows a 1.24 F cm−2 capacitance at 3 mA cm−2.

title: Nickel-infused cobalt ferrite/MXene nanocomposites: Structural insights and electrochemical properties for high performance supercapacitors
authors: W. Trinisha Infancy, T. Jaqulin Jenila, R. Rathikha, S. Maruthasalamoorthy, Belina Xavier, R. Navamathavan, Manikandan Ayyar, V. Mohanavel, M. Santhamoorthy, S. Santhoshkumar, Saravanan Rajendran
conclusion: The slick coprecipitation approach was used to produce nickel doped cobalt ferrite with incorporation of MXene nanocomposite. The single-phased cubic spinel structure's emergence was validated by structural analysis (XRD), and the average crystallite size was ascertained using XRD pattern analysis for Co1-x Nix Fe2 O4 (x = 0.03, 0.05, 0.07, 0.10 and 0.10/MXene) samples were spotted within a range of 1.5 and 2.5 nm. The clustering of the nanoparticles was revealed by FESEM pictures. HRTEM micrographs demonstrate the formation of nanosized particles, the elements Ni, Co, Fe, Ti, and O were confirmed to be present in the EDX patterns without any impurities. The elemental composition has been examined using XPS. Bands lower than 1000 cm−1 in the FTIR spectra have been induced due to the ferrite groups' vibrations. For each individual sample, the tetrahedral metal–oxygen stretching vibration was the cause of the band (ν 1 ) that was seen at about 550 cm-1. The band (ν 2 ) 420 cm-1 emerged by the metal‑oxygen stretching vibration at the octahedral sites in the produced samples. Saturation magnetization increased when Co1−x Nix Fe2 O4 doped with MXene. Electrochemical characteristics derived from GCD plots showed pre-eminent capacitance values, 96.33 Cg−1 , 121.63 Cg−1 , 210.15 Cg−1 , 361.2 Cg−1 and 367.2 Cg−1 for Co1-x Nix Fe2 O4 (x = 0.03, 0.05, 0.07, 0.10 and 0.10/MXene) at a precise scan rate 10 mV /s and thereby intending it to be a strong contender for applications involving supercapacitors. abstract: In view of the unique magnetic characteristics of the ferrites, inverse spinel cobalt ferrite/MXene nanocomposites (Co1-xNixFe2O4/MXene NCs) have garnered significant attention. These vital characteristics make Co1-xNixFe2O4/MXene NCs an ideal material for supercapacitor application. To synthesize Co1-xNixFe2O4/MXene NCs, a simple and cost-effective low-temperature co-precipitation approach was used, and samples were synthesized at different nickel concentrations (x = 0.03, 0.05, 0.07, 0.10) further integrated with MXene. Several characterization studies were used to investigate their crystallinity, morphology, and electrochemistry using different techniques such as X-ray powder diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectrum (FT-IR), elemental composition analysis (X-ray photoelectron spectra - XPS), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Co1-xNixFe2O4 (x = 0.10) with MXene exhibited smaller crystallite size compared to other produced samples. The results showed that increase in nickel concentration decreases the crystallite size and lattice constant. The FT-IR spectra showed two strong absorption bands near 560 cm−1 (v1) and 400 cm−1 (ν2). SEM was used to corroborate the shape of the cubically spherical structure. The electrochemical behaviour for the produced samples were investigated using cyclic voltammetry (CV) with a electrolyte solution of 1 M KOH. The voltage has been constrained to 0.0 volts to 0.5 volts, with potential scan speeds ranging 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, and 75 mV/s. A cyclic voltametric investigation found that the nickel doped cobalt ferrite with MXene incorporation enhanced the specific capacitance over Co1-xNixFe2O4 (x = 0.10). The specific capacitance of nickel-doped cobalt ferrite (x = 0.10) and (x = 0.10/MXene) samples were 361C g−1 and 367C g−1 respectively.

title: Ionic liquid induced gelation of Mo1.33C i-MXene for enhanced supercapacitor and Li-Ion storage performance
authors: Zhaohui Chen, He Chong, Peng Hei, Hongyun Guo, Zhen Ma, Qiang Wang, Yu Song, Weibin Cui
conclusion: In conclusion, the introduction of ionic liquids (ILs), specifically [Bmim]Cl and [Omim]Cl, effectively induces rapid gelation in Mo1.33 C i -MXene aqueous solutions. A three-dimensional network is formed and extended d spacing is realized by the ion exchange of TBA+ by [Bmim]+ and [Omim]+ . Additionally, a significant increase in surface −O functional group is also observed. These modifications lead into significant enhanced supercapacitance of 552.6 F·g−1 at 1 A·g−1 and Li-ion storage capacity of 1056 mAh·g−1 at 50 mA g−1 along with the long-term cyclic stability. The computational results reveal that the increased content of −O functional groups on the surface of Mo1.33 C enhances Li adsorption capacity. In addition, the expanded layer spacing enhances both the Li-ion storage capacity and diffusion kinetics. Through interlayer and surface engineering, the Li-ion adsorption capacity of Mo1.33 C is enhanced, and Li-ion diffusion during lithiation is accelerated, enabling Mo1.33 C to exhibit superior Li-ion storage performance. These results suggest that the Mo1.33 C i -MXene can be applied as the promising electrode in the supercapacitor and Li-ion batteries through our efficient and easy strategy. abstract: Two-dimensional Mo1.33C i-MXene is highly promising for electrochemical energy storage applications. We present a novel and facile approach to induce rapid gelation of Mo1.33C suspensions by ionic liquids (ILs), thereby significantly improving the supercapacitance and Li-ion storage performance of Mo1.33C i-MXene. The introduction of ILs weakens the electrostatic repulsion between nanosheets, triggering their interconnection and the formation of a three-dimensional network. Cation exchange with TBA+ cations in the interlayer alters the spacing, with larger cations leading to increased interlayer distances. Additionally, a notable increase in surfacial −O functional groups has been observed and leads into the enhanced electrochemical energy storage. First-principles calculations indicate that the adsorption of Li-ion is significantly enhanced for the Mo1.33C i-MXene after treatment with ILs. Mo1.33C–[Omim] + exhibits outstanding supercapacitor performance (552.6 F·g−1 at 1 A·g−1) and Li-ion storage capacity (1056 mAh·g−1 at 50 mA·g−1). This work presents a simple yet effective strategy for improving the electrochemical performance of Mo1.33C i-MXene, offering significant potential for practical applications in energy storage.

title: Synergistic MXene/NiCo2S4 composite for high-performance flexible all-solid-state supercapacitors
authors: Wei Li, Yuxin Li, Liaoyuan An, Zhuojun Zou, Ziyang Cong, Miaomiao Liu, Junyu Yang, Shangru Zhai, Qingda An, Kai Wang, Yao Tong
conclusion: In summary, our study successfully synthesized MNCS-0.02 composites via a one-step hydrothermal method, integrating NCS into exfoliated Ti3 C2 Tx -MXene nanosheets. This process facilitated the formation of a continuous and efficient conductive network with exceptional conductivity and electrochemical properties. The optimized MNCS-0.02 electrode exhibits an impressive specific capacity of 2675 F g−1 (1070 C g−1 ) at a current density of 1 A g−1 , along with excellent cycling stability (96.51 % retention of initial capacity after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles). Furthermore, by utilizing MNCS-0.02 as the positive electrode and AC as the negative electrode, we fabricated f-ASCs with an energy density reaching up to 61 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 763 W kg−1 , accompanied by outstanding electrochemical cycling stability (retaining 95.48 % of capacity after 10,000 cycles) and remarkable mechanical flexibility. These findings underscore the potential application of layered nanometallic composites in the development of high-performance flexible energy storage devices. abstract: The scientific community has been captivated by flexible all-solid-state supercapacitors, which can meet the growing demand for portable electronic devices. In this study, a novel MXene/NiCo2S4 (MNCS) composite material was synthesized via the hydrothermal method, with NiCo2S4 uniformly distributed on the surface or within the interlayers of MXene. The aim of this study was to enhance energy storage applications by developing a positive electrode material using a composite of MNCS. The architecture of the composite was carefully designed to prevent the stacking of MXene and the accumulation of NiCo2S4 nanoparticles, effectively suppressing these issues. It is worth noting that when utilized in a three-electrode system, the MNCS electrode demonstrates outstanding electrochemical performance. Specifically, at a current density of 1 A g−1, the electrode exhibits a specific capacity of 2675 F g−1 (equivalent to 1070 C g−1). Furthermore, even after undergoing 10,000 cycles of charging and discharging, the electrode retains an impressive 96.51 % of its initial capacity. These results clearly indicate that the exceptional performance observed in this supercapacitor can be attributed to the synergistic collaboration between NiCo2S4 nanoparticles and MXene nanosheets which significantly enhances charge transfer during both charging and discharging processes. Moreover, we synthesized MNCS composites for use as positive electrodes in asymmetric flexible solid-state supercapacitors while employing activated carbon (AC) as negative electrodes. The resulting device exhibits high specific capacitance (256 F g−1) and impressive energy density (61 Wh kg−1) at a power density of 763 W kg−1 under a large voltage window (1.7 V) and current density (1 A g−1). Additionally, favorable cycling stability is observed with minimal capacitance variation even under various bending deformations. This study presents an innovative approach for developing composite materials with superior electrochemical properties and flexible devices with high energy density and power density.

title: Tunable interlayer spacings Ti3C2Tx MXene/Ni/C for enhanced electromagnetic microwave absorption
authors: Jingyu Song, Yongqian Shen, Guibin Zhang, Mingxuan Sun, Mengyao Han, Xueyan Du
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this study, xDA-Ti 3 C 2 with controllable layer spacing was prepared via a dehydration condensation reaction between xDA and –NH 2 functionalized Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene layers. Subsequently, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/Ni/C composites with unique layered structures were prepared using a simple mechanical stirring and carbonization strategy. Compared to traditional MAs, the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/Ni/C composites retained the accordion structure of pure Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene. The increase in layer spacing exposes the material to a wider interface, preventing agglomeration and providing a favorable interface for subsequent nickel metal doping. Moreover, the electromagnetic parameters could be accurately controlled by changing the doping amount of Ni metal. Several highly dispersed magnetic particles are doped into the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheet layer or attached to its surface, imparting the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheet with magnetic characteristics and significantly improving its magnetic loss capability. Finally, the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/Ni/C composites exhibit excellent EMWs absorption performance (RL = −42.3 dB) owing to the synergistic effect of multicomponent complementary effects, conduction loss, interfacial polarization, and dielectric loss. Molecular welding offers an inimitable method for controlling the interlayer spacing between the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene layers and other two-dimensional materials, providing theoretical guidance for designing high-performance, two-dimensional wave-absorbing materials.
abstract: While two-dimensional lamellar materials, specifically Ti3C2Tx MXenes, have shown great promise as wave-absorbing materials, the precise design of interlayer spacing poses a persistent challenge. In this study, Ti3C2Tx MXene layers with adjustable interlayer spacings were crafted using a straightforward molecular welding technique. Through the incorporation of Ni nanoparticles onto the Ti3C2Tx MXene layers using a combination of simple mechanical stirring and carbonation reactions, we successfully developed Ti3C2Tx MXene/Ni/C composites featuring a distinct lamellar structure. A uniform dispersion of Ni nanoparticles on the surface of the Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets was found with some of the nanoparticles intercalated into the layers. The Ti3C2Tx MXene/Ni/C composites exhibited a maximum reflection loss (RL) value of −42.3 dB at 12.3 GHz, accompanied by an impressive effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 5.6 GHz. This outstanding absorption performance could be attributed to various factors, including the dielectric loss of the Ti3C2Tx MXene lamellae, reflections and scattering of multiphase heterostructures, the magnetic loss of the Ni nanoparticles, and their synergistic attenuation. Furthermore, Ni nanoparticles with high electrical conductivity induced vortex currents under the alternating influence of electromagnetic waves (EMWs), resulting in a substantial depletion. This study introduces an innovative approach for synthesizing Ti3C2Tx MXene/Ni/C composites with tunable interlayer spacing, showing their potential for applications in microwave absorption (MA).

title: Enhanced electrochemical performance of Ti3C2Tx MXene film based supercapacitors in H2SO4/KI redox additive electrolyte
authors: Jianjian Fu, Lei Li, Damin Lee, Je Moon Yun, Bong Ki Ryu, Kwang Ho Kim
conclusion: In summary, freestanding Ti3 C2 Tx film was prepared through vacuum filtration process. The electrochemical performance of the Ti3 C2 Tx //Ti3 C2 Tx RAESs was systematically studied in H2 SO4 /KI electrolyte. Owing to the combinational effect of the pseudocapacitance performance of the MXene and reversible redox reaction of KI additive, the Ti3 C2 Tx //H2 SO4 /KI//Ti3 C2 Tx RAESs exhibits an optimized volumetric specific capacitance of 601 F cm−3 (gravimetric specific capacitance of 166 F g−1 ) at current density of 1 A g−1 . Moreover, the device delivered a volumetric energy density of 83.5 Wh L–1 at a volumetric power density of 1800 W L–1 . This excellent electrochemical performance of the RAES device suggests the importance of KI additive with enhanced redox reactions for high performance Ti3 C2 Tx based energy storage devices. abstract: The introduction of redox additives into the electrolyte is considered to be an effective and facile approach to increase the specific capacitance of supercapacitors (SCs), as these additives facilitate redox reactions at the electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Herein, a freestanding titanium carbide Ti3C2Tx (MXene) film was prepared through lithium fluoride/hydrochloric acid (LiF/HCl) etching method and subsequent vacuum filtration process. Subsequently, the electrochemical behavior of freestanding Ti3C2Tx film based symmetric SCs was improved via the addition of potassium iodide (KI), as a redox additive. The optimized Ti3C2Tx//H2SO4/KI//Ti3C2Tx redox additive electrolyte SCs (RAESs) assembled using Ti3C2Tx film as both positive and negative electrodes and H2SO4/KI as electrolyte show a volumetric capacitance of 601 F cm−3 and a volumetric energy density of 83.5 Wh L–1 at a power density of 1800 W L–1. These results suggest the importance of KI redox additive electrolyte in developing Ti3C2Tx based SCs.

title: Blade-coated Ti3C2Tx MXene films for pseudocapacitive energy storage and infrared stealth
authors: Haoxiang Ma, Junqi Wang, Jingfeng Wang, Kun Shang, Yang Yang, Zhimin Fan
conclusion: In this work, a free-standing MXene film was prepared using the blade coating method, and the electrochemical capacitance and infrared stealth behavior of the blade-coated MXene film was investigated. Since the blade-coated MXene film had a more regular interlayer lamellar arrangement and denser structure than the traditional MXene film prepared by vacuum-assisted filtration, the density and conductivity reached 3.95 g cm−3 and 8000 S cm−1 , respectively. In addition, the blade-coated MXene film exhibited superior mechanical properties to the filtered MXene film. At a scan rate of 5 mV s−1 , the blade-coated MXene film had a gravimetric capacitance of 347 F g−1 and a volumetric capacitance of 1353 F cm−3 . Meanwhile, the capacitance retention rate at a scan rate of 100 mV s−1 was almost consistent with that of the vacuum-assisted filtered MXene film. Furthermore, the blade-coated MXene film exhibited outstanding infrared stealth performance because of its low mid-infrared emissivity. Therefore, it has the potential for infrared camouflage applications in the military field. Besides, the size of the blade-coated MXene film is scalable, rendering such film more suitable for industrial-scale production. This work is of considerable significance for promoting the practical applications of MXene film in the field of electrochemical energy storage and infrared stealth. abstract: As a significant macrostructure of 2D MXene nanosheets, MXene (Ti3C2Tx) films made by vacuum-assisted filtration have considerable application prospects in the field of energy storage and infrared stealth. However, using vacuum-assisted filtration to assemble 2D MXene nanosheets into films is energy-intensive, inefficient, and thereby detrimental to the further development of MXene films. This work involves the first investigation into the electrochemical capacitive and infrared stealth behavior of MXene films prepared by the blade coating method. Blade-coated MXene films have a more regular and dense structure than traditional films prepared vacuum-assisted filtration. Thus, the electrical conductivity can reach as high as 8000 S cm−1 and the film exhibits good mechanical properties. When the blade-coated MXene film is used for supercapacitors, it has a specific capacitance of 347 F g−1 at 5 mV s−1, which is similar to that of the filtered MXene film. Additionally, the blade-coated MXene film demonstrates excellent infrared stealth performance, benefitting from its low mid-infrared emissivity. As a result, this form of MXene film assembly has broad application prospects in the field of military infrared camouflage. This work lays an important foundation for the further application of MXene films in practice.

title: A review of how to improve Ti3C2Tx MXene stability
authors: Wei Cao, Junli Nie, Ye Cao, Chengjie Gao, Mingsheng Wang, Weiwei Wang, Xiaoli Lu, Xiaohua Ma, Peng Zhong
conclusion: 5  Summary and outlook  Recently, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene has attracted considerable attention in many fields, such as energy, electronics, and biomedicine, due to its excellent electrical, optical, mechanical, and catalytic properties, and so on. However, the degradation of MXene into TiO 2 and amorphous carbon by exposure to air and water can significantly compromise the microstructure of the material, thus reducing its physical and chemical properties in a myriad of ways. Consequently, the large-scale synthesis of MXene and its practical applications are severely constrained. Thus, effective measures to slow or inhibit the degradation of MXene are urgently called for to ensure its extended service life in natural and extreme environments. This review begins with a brief introduction to MXenes, which serves to show their structures and synthesis processes, as well as the areas where they can be applied. Secondly, the degradation mechanism of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene are discussed, focusing on oxidation and hydrolysis. Oxidation and hydrolysis are the main degradation reactions for MXene in the environment, which always initiate from defective sites of MXene. Upon exposure to harmful factors (e.g., water and/or oxygen), MXene might undergo microscopic changes in morphologies, structures, and surface functional groups etc, which further influence the diverse properties and applications of this unique material. It is of great importance to unveil the degradation mechanisms of MXene from the angle of microstructural evolutions, so as to find targeted methods to enhance the MXene stability. Thirdly, MXene has attracted great attentions because of its excellent physicochemical properties and thus the wide applications. The effects of MXene degradation on its electronic, optical, mechanical, and catalytic properties are comprehensively discussed. The changes in physical and chemical properties of MXene are mainly attributed to its variations of morphologies, structures, and surface functional groups, e.g., the formation of cavities and TiO 2 nanoparticles on the surface of MXene, and changes in terminal compositions and proportions. Finally, the current strategies to improve the stability of MXene are systematically summarized. These strategies can be divided into four main categories: optimization of the MXene preparation process, post-processing of MXene, promoting the storage environment of MXene, and encapsulation of MXene.   (1)  Several specific methods can be employed to optimize the preparation process of MXene so as to obtain a high-quality product. By selecting a high-quality MAX phase, the surface of the as-synthesized MXene would have few defective sites after etching, leading to substantially enhanced MXene stability due to the improved quality of the material itself. By selecting an appropriate etchant and dosage, the terminal type and proportion of MXene (i.e., −F, –OH, −O) can be directly adjusted during synthesis. Generally, the oxygen-terminated MXene shows higher stability than the fluoride-terminated one. However, it should be noted that the surface functional groups greatly influence the specific properties of MXene. For example, the −F functional group promotes the electrical conductivity of MXene, while the −O group gives MXene a higher electrocatalytic activity. Different etchants and dosages can be used selectively by balancing the stability and required properties. Large lateral sizes of MXene are closely related to high conductivity and stability due to high-quality single crystals. Preparing large-size sheets could guarantee ideal stability for MXene. However, in some cases, the sizes of MXene need to be tailored within an optimal range to adapt to specific applications. For example, as for the MXene ink for inject printing, the MXene sizes should be controlled to less than 1 μm due to the limit of the nozzle size. For electrocatalysis, the MXene sheets with small sizes provide plentiful active sites, resulting in enhanced catalytic performance. Meanwhile, many defective sites exist in the small-size MXene, which might induce decreased stability.    (2)  After the synthesis of MXene, post-treatments could be employed to enhance its stability, including ionic shielding of the MXene edges or surfaces, surface modification, annealing treatments, and the formation of MXene-based composites. The surface of MXene is negatively charged due to the presence of functional groups, while the edges of MXene have been shown to be positively charged. Degradation often initiates at the edges first. The use of anionic surfactants or polyanionic salts in combination with positively charged edges can largely prevent water and oxygen from intruding into the MXene. However, the introduction of these substances might also affect the electrical conductivity and other properties of MXene. In addition, cations can be employed to interact with the negatively charged surface of MXene, which forms a dense shielding layer to block water and oxygen. Similarly, surface modification can be employed to impede water intrusion into MXene by grafting hydrophobic substances onto the MXene surface. However, the poor dispersion of the modified MXene in solutions might restrict the applications. Annealing is an effective method for removing residual water molecules at the interlayers of MXene nanosheets. With an appropriate temperature and duration, a protective layer could also be formed on the MXene surface, thereby enhancing its stability. Given the limitations of stability and functionality for individual MXene, the use of MXene-based composites is a feasible and facile option to prolong MXene life. Nanocomposites can provide a quick way to enhance the stability of MXene by taking advantage of the antioxidant properties of other materials.    (3)  Once MXene has been prepared, it is necessary to consider whether it can be stored for an extended period, whether the properties of the material change after long-term storage and so on. These factors would directly affect the large-scale production and commercial applications of MXene. Optimizing the storage environment of MXene can enhance the long-term stability of the material through the use of simple operations    (4)  In addition to optimizing the stability of MXene itself, it is also possible to consider the use of commercial processes to treat MXene-based devices. One such process is the encapsulation technology, which can be used to separate the device from the external environment. The encapsulation can effectively exclude the intrusion of water and oxygen, enhancing the stability of the MXene device in various environments. However, the research on the use of existing mature processes to enhance the stability of MXene still needs to be sufficiently comprehensive and systematic. A more detailed and extensive investigation of mature processes to deal with MXene-based devices would greatly facilitate the commercialization of MXene.     Although many methods have been developed to enhance the environmental stability of Ti 3 C 2 T x , from material synthesis and storage to applications, the role that one single strategy is limited. However, few reports on enhancements of the MXene stability by combining multiple strategies. One simple example is the first synthesis of a high-quality MAX phase, which can secondly be etched by selecting the appropriate etchant and dosage, followed by a heat treatment to remove the excess water molecules. It is anticipated that a combination of a series of suitable techniques would render the synthesized MXene with substantially enhanced stability. However, it remains unclear whether the various treatments will interact with one another and whether subsequent treatment operations will compromise the efficacy of previous ones. Further in-depth research and analysis in this area may facilitate the development of MXene with optimal environmental stability through a limited number of operations.  In addition, the accelerated advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) in recent years, driven by its extensive data collection and sophisticated computational capabilities, can be projected to research the stability of MXene and its family. The application of AI for deep learning and analysis of MXene degradation mechanisms would prompt AI to learn, analyze, and use its powerful computational ability to predict effective methods to enhance the stability of MXenes. Furthermore, it is important to deepen our understanding of the degradation mechanisms of MXene. As the research depth and analysis methods for materials continue to evolve, it is essential to carry out deeper study of the degradation mechanism of MXene in line with technological advancements. For example, the continuous development of in - situ characterizations and deep learning simulation might enable more effective and in-depth studies. A deeper understanding is expected about how MXene is invaded by oxygen, water and other adverse factors during the degradation process, how this invasion affects the surface of MXene, and what structural changes occur as a result. A comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the degradation mechanisms of MXene would enable researchers to more accurately and effectively direct their efforts towards stabilizing MXene.
abstract: Recently, the two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx (MXene) has attracted more and more attentions in energy, electronics, environment, biomedicine, etc., due to its unique features such as high conductivity, unusual layered structures, adjustable surface chemistry, and outstanding mechanical properties. However, the easy degradation of MXene in the presence of oxygen and moisture would induce the destruction of its microstructures and thus affect the physical and chemical properties of MXene, resulting in minimal practical applications of MXene-based functional devices. To this end, increasing efforts have been made in the MXene community to improve the environmental stability of MXene, from theories to experiments. It is important to timely summarize the recent progress on the stability of MXene. In this review, firstly, the structures and synthesis of MXenes are briefly introduced. Secondly, the mechanisms of Ti3C2Tx MXene degradation are analyzed from the angles of oxidation and hydrolysis. Thirdly, the effects of MXene degradation on its physical and chemical properties (i.e., electronic, optical, mechanical, and catalytic properties) are carefully discussed, which are often missed in other review articles on MXene stability. Lastly and most importantly, recently reported strategies for effectively inhibiting or slowing down the degradation of MXene are systematically summarized from four aspects of optimizing the MXene preparation process, performing post-treatments on MXene, promoting the storage conditions of MXene, and encapsulation of MXene. This timely review is helpful for preparations, storage, and applications of MXenes in widespread fields.

title: Ti3C2Tx MXene-based multifunctional wearable integrated sensor for simultaneous detection of humidity and pressure stimuli
authors: Kai Wang, Jia-Nan Ma, Qian Zhao, Jia-Hui Zhang, Kang-Dong Zhang, Yu Zhang, Ling Wang, Sheng-Bo Sang
conclusion: In conclusion, we developed a multifunctional Ti3 C2 Tx -based integrated pressure-humidity sensor, which can be applied to monitor physiological signals of humans. By employing Ti3 C2 Tx as the sole sensitive material for both sensing modes without signal decoupling, we significantly simplify the device structure while ensuring high performance. The pressure sensing unit of the integrated sensor exhibits a high sensitivity of 1878.05 kPa−1 and a broad response range of 8–125 kPa and the humidity sensing unit possesses a high sensitivity of 0.67 % (%RH)−1 and rapid humidity response (response 3.46 s, recovery 1.50 s). Meanwhile, the sensor has excellent repeatability and anti-interference. The above results make the sensor perform well in practical applications such as the monitoring of respiratory patterns, sweat levels, joint movements and so on. Compared with existing multifunctional sensors, this work overcomes the common limitations of signal crosstalk and material incompatibility by integrating both sensing functions into a unified MXene-based platform. abstract: Although wearable electronic sensors have demonstrated promising applications in the fields of health monitoring, human-machine interaction, and soft robotics, they still face challenges in multifunctionality, integration, facile production and low cost using conventional materials. MXene, as an emerging two-dimensional material, integrated with favorable physical/chemical properties is expected to solve these problems. Herein, we propose an integrated pressure-humidity sensor using Ti3C2Tx MXene as the sole sensitive material, which can precisely detect and distinguish pressure and humidity signals without cross-talk. Notably, the integrated pressure-humidity sensor exhibits not only a wide response range (8–125 kPa) with high sensitivity (1878.05 kPa−1) for pressure detection, but also wide response range (11.5 %-98.1 % RH), high sensitivity (0.67 % (%RH)−1) and rapid response (response 3.46 s, recovery 1.50 s) for humidity detection. Based on the above outstanding dual-mode sensing performances, the sensor is applied in monitoring diverse physiological parameters of human such as respiratory patterns, sweat levels, and joint movements, revealing great potential for health monitoring and human-machine interaction.

title: Advanced MOF/MXene heterostructure with carbon aerogel to boosts the ions movement in asymmetric supercapacitors and hydrogen production
authors: Haseebul Hassan, Khakemin Khan, Sidra Mumtaz, Arslan Ahmed Rafi, Ahmed Mahmoud Idris, Ahmed Althobaiti, Alsharef Mohammad
conclusion: In this work, the MIL-101(Cr), Ti3 C2 Tx , and their composite CA@MIL-101/Ti3 C2 Tx were successfully synthesized for energy storage and electrocatalysis applications. The CA@MIL-101 (Cr)/Ti3 C2 Tx demonstrated a remarkable energy density of 38 Wh-kg−1 along with 1280 W-kg−1 power density. After 10,000 galvanostatic charge-discharge cycles, the CA@MIL-101 (Cr)/Ti3 C2 Tx//CA device showed 84 % capacity retention. Moreover, an anti-self-discharge test using a PVDF electrode on CA@MIL-101 (Cr)/Ti3 C2 Tx//AC showed a meager 2 % voltage loss over a 30-h period. The CA@MIL-101 (Cr)/Ti3 C2 Tx//CA showed an overpotential of 158 mV in HER. These findings suggest that material CA@MIL-101 (Cr)/Ti3 C2 Tx has a great deal of potential for use in high-efficiency supercapacitor applications.
