abstract: The energy storage capacity of MXenes can be significantly augmented by increasing their specific surface area, which can additionally amplify the number of active sites available for electrochemical reactions. Herein, we have presented a method to enhance the energy storage capacity of Ti3C2Tx MXenes by growing the TiO2 nanogrooves on the surface of Ti3C2Tx (termed as Ti3C2Tx-NG) without drying the exfoliated MXene layers using hydrothermal treatment. The Ti3C2Tx MXene flakes dimensions ranged from 500 to 1000 nm, whereas the decorated TiO2 nanogrooves have a size of ∼10 nm. The Ti3C2Tx MXene demonstrates a specific surface area (SSA) of ∼ 11 m2/g, while the Ti3C2Tx-NG exhibits an enhanced SSA of ∼40 m2/g. The Ti3C2Tx-NG utilized in the fabrication of symmetric supercapacitors exhibited a significantly higher specific capacitance (∼81 F/g) compared to Ti3C2Tx MXene (∼62 F/s) at a scan rate of 100 mV/s. Reversible oxidation and reduction reactions between TiO2 and Ti3C2Tx, accompanied by the adsorption or release of hydroxide ions (OH-) contribute to charge transport in the supercapacitors. Additionally, due to the layered structure of Ti3C2Tx MXene, a smaller number of ions can exist between two adjacent MXene layers due to the small spacing, whereas more ions can exist between two adjacent Ti3C2Tx-NG layers as interlayer spacing between adjacent layers is relatively broader due to the nanosized TiO2 nanogrooves, facilitating in the higher charge storage.

title: Recent advances in supercapacitors based on carbon nanomaterials/MXene: Material design and functional integration
authors: Jinyuan Cao, Zhe Liu, Xuanxuan Wu, Jin Duan, Gege Hang, Yuxin Fu
conclusion: 7  Summary and outlook  This paper reviews recent research developments in carbon nanomaterials/MXene composites as supercapacitor electrodes. Overall, there have been significant breakthroughs in structural engineering between carbon nanomaterials and MXene over the past few years. The combined use of electrical double-layer carbon materials and pseudocapacitive MXene solves two major problems: self-stacking and oxidation of MXene. This synergy also drives the enhancement of other properties of supercapacitors, such as energy density, cycle life, rate performance, mechanical properties, low-temperature resistance, biocompatibility performance, and wearability. Carbon nanomaterials/MXene composites play a great role in flexible wearable supercapacitors, micro-supercapacitors, self-powered supercapacitors, and low-temperature resistant supercapacitors. The universality of the properties of carbon nanomaterials/MXene composites makes them worth being investigated in other applications.  Solving the problem of MXene self-stacking involves more than just interpolating spacer materials, as imprecise preparation methods often decrease the density of MXene-based composites, especially top-down methods. Ideal optimization of the MXene structure should enable precisely regulated layer spacing, providing enough space between layers to prevent stacking while keeping the spacing small enough to ensure high density and capacity. For the oxidation of MXene, adding antioxidants such as l -ascorbic acid and L-cysteine successfully solved this problem. The heating-free method circumvents the binding of MXene with oxygen in water or air. In-situ sacrificial metal templates (Zn, Fe, Al) as the reductant and crosslinking agent have been demonstrated to achieve the same antioxidant effect. Hence, it is necessary to investigate other sacrificial metal templates.  0D carbon nanoparticles/MXene composites are well suitable for the preparation of solar supercapacitors due to their excellent light harvesting and photothermal conversion capabilities. This will help to promote the multifunctional integration of practical supercapacitors. For 1D carbon nanomaterials, the high aspect ratios not only connect the MXene nanosheets to create a stable structure with high mechanical strength but also form a connecting ion-transportation channel, which is good for the electrical conductivity of the composite materials. The wide adaptability of CNT/MXene electrode materials can be concluded from the strategies of changing CNT structural features, introduction of third conductive materials, gelation, etc., which leads to a great potential for exploitation in other fabrication methods. Nanocellulose makes an excellent contribution to the mechanical properties of MXene composites, up to 340 MPa for films (cellulose nanofibers/MXene films) and 74 MPa for fibers (cellulose nanocrystals/MXene fibers). Due to the inherent insulating characteristics of nanocellulose, researchers generally introduce a third active substance to enhance the electrochemical properties of the composites. Currently, the conducting polymer has the greatest influence on the electrical conductivity, specific capacitance, and energy density of nanocellulose/MXene composites. For example, the MXene/CNF/PANI-based SSC exhibited a voltage window of 1.2 V, an ultra-high volume specific capacitance of 522 mF cm −2 (5 mA cm −2 ), and an energy density of 94.7 μWh cm −2 at power density of 573 μW cm −2 . For 2D rGO, improves overall interfacial structure, contributing to the expansion of the contact area between the electrolyte and the electrode material, which greatly increases the ion-accessible sites and improves the charge transfer efficiency. Especially in the preparation of gel composite electrodes, the 3D interconnect structure enables the material to maintain a capacitance retention rate of over 90 % after 10,000 cycles of charging/discharging, providing excellent long-term cycling stability. For 3D carbon materials, the multilevel pore properties make them show great advantages in material structure design. Derived carbon materials exhibit significant differences in interfacial effects when composited with MXene due to the diversity of precursor sources. Therefore, further investigation of the interfacial binding mechanisms of different precursor-derived carbons with MXene is of great scientific significance and application value for optimizing the electrochemical properties of the composites.  Overall, the main issues that still exist in the current development of supercapacitors are i) low energy density; ii) high cost and low yield; and iii) difficulty in meeting commercial-grade standards. Therefore, a better balance between the electrochemical performance, mechanical stability, and processing technology of SCs is still needed in the future. Here, the future development trend of SCs in terms of performance optimization is summarized ( Fig. 16  ):   1)  In recent years, Ti 3 C 2 T x /carbon nanomaterials have made significant progress in the field of energy storage, but there is a lack of research on other types of MXene (Zr 3 C 2 T x , Nb 2 CT x , Mo 2 CT x , etc.)/carbon nanomaterials composites. This research imbalance limits the overall optimization of MXene-based composite properties and the expansion of potential applications. Different species of MXene have unique electronic structures, surface chemistry and interlayer interactions. For example, Zr 3 C 2 T x exhibits enhanced oxidative stability, while Mo 2 CT x has a higher intrinsic conductivity. Therefore, the interfacial interactions between various MXene and carbon nanomaterials need to be investigated;    2)  Surface modification is used to modulate the microstructure of materials to stimulate the maximum potential of MXene-based materials. For example, the density and distribution of defects on the surface of the material can be precisely controlled by plasma treatment and chemical vapor deposition to build abundant active sites. The electronic conduction efficiency and ion diffusion kinetics of the electrode materials can be effectively improved by modulating the type and concentration of surface termination groups (e.g. -OH, -COOH, Cl, etc.). Or doping with heteroatoms to modulate the electronic structure of the composite material. The doping of heteroatoms such as N, P, and S has already appeared, in the future, we can continue to explore the enhancement effect of doping with other heteroatoms;    3)  Binary composites are limited by the limited properties of the materials and not as good as ternary composites or multicomposites. Ternary composites are able to achieve a good balance between the preparation strategy and the electrochemical and mechanical properties of the materials through the multidimensional charge transport network, hierarchical structural design and synergistic reinforcement of the materials. Currently, conductive polymers (e.g., PANI) contribute significantly to the specific capacitance and energy density of carbon nanomaterials/MXene-based SCs, but the cycling stability of SCs is poor. Therefore, a combination of advanced characterization and intelligent algorithms is needed to achieve accurate and practical material design;    4)  Currently, interlayers, stacked structures, core-shell structures, honeycomb structures, cellular lattice networks, and dot-wire-sheet hetero-structured fibers have greatly influenced the properties of MXene-based hybrid electrodes. Therefore, building precise 3D porous interconnections to expose active sites and mitigate the volume expansion effect, is a key strategy to improve the performance of carbon nanomaterials/MXene-based SCs;    5)  Nanocellulose is a promising carbon nanomaterial because it is in line with the requirements of sustainable development. Currently, the application of CNC in MXene composites has not been fully explored. CNC can not only significantly enhance the mechanical properties of the materials, but also act as a spatial stabiliser to effectively inhibit the stacking of MXene flakes. CNF and BC have similar effects and are biocompatible, which can provide a new research direction for the development of high-performance MXene-based composites;    6)  Advanced manufacturing technologies such as microfluidic spinning and 3D printing can be used to accurately construct the microstructure (including orientation arrangement, pore distribution and interfacial interactions) and multi-scale morphology (such as fiber, film, or three-dimensional porous network structure) of carbon nanomaterial/MXene composites, thereby achieve the directional optimization of the electrical conductivity, mechanical and electrochemical properties of the composites;    7)  The limitation of the low energy density of MSCs can be broken through by studying multi-scale regulation strategies such as hybrid electrode combinations and new electrolyte systems;    8)  For different application scenarios such as flexible wearable and self-powered systems, the development of multifunctional MXene-based supercapacitors that combine high energy density, excellent mechanical flexibility and environmental adaptability will be a promising direction. For example, biological supercapacitors (BSCs) can be integrated with various energy capture technologies such as sweat energy harvesting and solar energy conversion. The unity of efficient energy storage and self-powering is achieved by integrating biocompatible electrode materials and clever supercapacitor structural design;    9)  Both the synthesis strategy of composite electrode materials and the fabrication method of SCs should aim at saving more time and cost with multiple advantages such as simpler, finer, more efficient, and more convenient.
abstract: Supercapacitors are a major research topic in energy storage with interesting properties. The discovery of the new two-dimensional material MXene opens up new horizons in studying high-performance electrode materials for supercapacitors. However, the excellent electrochemical performance of MXene is limited by its self-stacking and oxidation problems. Currently, the intercalation of MXene nanosheets to establish a three-dimensional structure is the most effective solution, Carbon-based nanomaterials have emerged as a favored option due to their abundance, cost-effectiveness, and superior electrochemical properties. Based on the above background, this paper presents a comprehensive review of the current research status of different dimensions carbon nanomaterials/MXene composites in terms of preparation methods and material design. The functional design of supercapacitors based on carbon nanomaterials/MXene composites is further discussed. Additionally, problems and challenges are described and future research directions for supercapacitors are proposed in light of current developments.

title: Microfluidic-oriented assembly of MXene composite fibers for flexible zinc ion supercapacitors with high energy density
authors: Fanyu Xie, Yuan Du, Menghan Chu, Xiaoyu Jia, Hui Cao, Rui Zhang, Hongwei Li, Mei Zhang
conclusion: In summary, the three-dimensional rGO/ MXene fibers with the ordered sheets were fabricated by microfluidic combined wet spinning technology. The constructed flexible symmetric supercapacitors exhibit a high specific areal capacitance of 1613 mF cm−2 in PVA/H2 SO4 electrolyte. 70 % rGO/MXene@Zn fibers as anode materials were prepared by electrochemical deposition method to assemble the high-performance ZIHSCs in PVA/Zn(CF3 SO3 )2 gel electrolyte. The flexible ZIHSCs expand the operating voltage window of 0–1.6 V and realize a high specific areal capacitance as high as 1180 mF cm−2 , which achieve an excellent energy densigy of 104.9 μWh cm−2 , outstanding bending stability and good capacitance retention of 90 % after 6500 cycles. The multiple ZIHSCs in series further expand the energy outputs for practical applications in wearable electronic area. Three-dimensional network structure with the axial ordered sheets and good interfacial effect of cathode materials, and the optimized anode electrode contribute the superior electrochemical performance of ZIHSCs. This research proposes an avenue for the controllable construction of the advanced fiber electrode and high-performance zinc ion supercapacitors, broadening the practical application for wearable electronics. abstract: Fiber-typed zinc ion hybrid supercapacitors (ZIHSCs) have become the potential electrode materials for new generation of energy storage devices due to its low cost, abundant source and its low redox potential can expand the operating voltage window and increase energy and power density. But, the development of ZIHSCs is still in its infancy, and it is necessary to optimize the structure of electrode materials and design fibrous devices. Two-dimensional MXene materials are widely used in electrode manufacturing, which is of great significance to the development of fiber-typed supercapacitors and is expected to become excellent cathode materials for zinc ion supercapacitors. However, assembling them into regularly arranged macrofibers is challenging. Here, we precisely regulated and constructed the ordered and porous reduced graphene oxides/MXene fibers (rGO/MXene) by microfluidic assisted wet spinning technology. Graphene oxide (GO) was used as a spinnable material and lamellar spacer to achieve 10 % rGO/MXene fiber with high MXene loading. Among them, 10 % rGO/MXene was used as a symmetric supercapacitor electrode material, and the specific capacitance in PVA/H2SO4 electrolyte was as high as 1613 mF cm−2. The 10 % rGO/MXene fiber and 70 % rGO/MXene@Zn fiber were used as cathode and anode materials, and assembled into a zinc-ion hybrid supercapacitors (ZIHSCs) under PVA/Zn(CF3SO3)2 gel electrolyte, and an outstanding specific areal capacitance of 1180 mF cm−2, wide voltage window of 0–1.6 V, high energy density of 104.9 μWh cm−2 and good practical applications can be realized. In addition, the capacitor has good stability at different bending angles. The expansion of energy and power output can be achieved by series or parallel configuration. This study provides a new way for the design of the high-performance flexible zinc ion supercapacitors.

title: A novel strategy for high energy density supercapacitors: Formation of cyanuric acid between Ti3C2Tx (MXene) interlayer hybrid electrodes
authors: Chao Feng, Bingzhe Jia, Han Wang, Yan Wang, Xinming Wu
conclusion: during the formation of Ti3 C2 Tx /CA composite electrode, CA replaced the -F group that does not participate in the pseudocapacitive reaction, but did not change the original –OH and -O groups, and the pseudo capacitance of MXene was fully retained [13,21–23,45] . In addition, thanks to the unique hydroxyl structure of CA terminal and symmetry of CA, CA can form short chains during charging in aqueous electrolytes and the formation of short chains can realize the storage of electrons. At the same time, the formation of short chains further provides a large number of new pseudocapacitive reaction sites for MXene and the highly electronegative N and O atoms in CA also improve the electric double layer capacitor of the composite electrode to a certain extent. Therefore, the energy density of Ti3 C2 Tx /CA composite electrode (51.1 Wh kg−1 ) is much higher than that of Ti3 C2 Tx electrode (29.7 Wh kg−1 ) (Fig. 5 (e), Table S3 and Table S4 ). 4 Conclusions In summary, we synthesized a novel highly N-doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene through multi-step reaction by introducing small organic molecules, dicyandiamide, into the interlayer of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. Benefiting from the unique hydroxyl structure and symmetry of CA terminal, CA enables charge storage by forming short chains, providing new pseudocapacitive reaction sites and higher bilayer capacitance. The prepared Ti3 C2 Tx /CA composite electrode has a high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability. More notably, it achieves an amazing energy density of 51.1 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 2000 W kg−1 , which exceeds the energy density of MXene based electrode reported in the current literature. This work provides a new idea for the design of commercial MXene based electrodes by the method of Ti3 C2 Tx doping with small organic molecules.
abstract: Ti3C2Tx (MXene) are attractive for electrode materials because of their high electrical conductivity, abundant interlayer ions and low density. However, the low energy density hinders its commercial application. Herein, a novel N-doped Ti3C2Tx MXene is synthesized by introducing a small organic molecule dicyandiamide (DCD) to tune the complex terminals. DCD can be inserted into the layers of Ti3C2Tx nanosheets while forming melamine by catalyst-free trimerization reaction. Then, melamine is converted into gt-C3N4 through high-temperature sintering. Finally, gt-C3N4 is oxidized to cyanuric acid (CA) through simple hydrothermal reaction. The prepared Ti3C2Tx/CA composite electrode exhibits up to 4.8 at.% nitrogen doping and has a stable triazine ring structure. It is also shown that the Ti3C2Tx/CA composite electrode has high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability. More notably, it achieves an energy density of 51.1 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 2000 W kg−1, which exceeds the energy density of MXene based electrodes reported in the current literature. This excellent performance is attributed to the unique hydroxyl structure of the CA terminal and the excellent symmetry of CA in the composite electrode. In aqueous electrolytes, CA can form short chains during charging and the formation of short chains enables the storage of electrons and further provides a large number of new pseudocapacitive reaction sites for MXene. At the same time, the high electronegativity of the N and O atoms in CA also increases the electric double layer capacitor of the composite electrode to a certain extent, thus resulting in a high energy density of the composite electrode.

title: Ti3C2Tx-MXene based 2D/3D Ti3C2–TiO2–CuTiO3 heterostructure for enhanced pseudocapacitive performance
authors: Muhammad Noman, Mirza Mahmood Baig, Qazi Muhammad Saqib, Swapnil R. Patil, Chandrashekhar S. Patil, Jungmin Kim, Youngbin Ko, Eunho Lee, Jinwoo Hwang, Seung Goo Lee, Jinho Bae
conclusion: In this paper, we have demonstrated that the pseudocapacitive charge storage of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene can be significantly improved by developing oxidation-controlled MXene-derived 2D/3D heterostructures via a two-step process. In the first step, partial oxidation led to the formation of in-situ 3D floral Ti3 C2 –TiO2 nanoribbons. Afterward, in the second step, further controlled oxidation in the presence of Cu ions successfully transformed these 3D floral nanoribbons into a 2D/3D Ti3 C2 –TiO2 –CuTiO3 heterostructure. This transformation harnessed the synergistic effects of MXene, TiO2 , and CuTiO3 , which resulted in increased interlayer spacing, a higher concentration of redox-active sites, and mitigation of the conductivity issues associated with TiO2 nanoribbons. At an applied current density of 2 mA/cm2 , the Ti3 C2 –TiO2 –CuTiO3 heterostructure exhibited a notably improved capacitance, achieving 599.2 mF/cm2 (437.3F/g @ 1.46 A/g), surpassing both the pure MXene 249.16 mF/cm2 (158.7F/g @ 1.46 A/g) and the 3D floral Ti3 C2 –TiO2 nanoribbons 498.5 mF/cm2 (352.1F/g @ 1.46 A/g). Furthermore, the practical application of this material was demonstrated through the fabrication of an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device, Ti3 C2 –TiO2 –CuTiO3 //AC, which achieved an energy density of 31.1 Wh/kg, power density of 1041.7 W/kg and capacitance retention of 83.7 % after 5000 continuous charging/discharging cycles. These findings highlight the potential of the controlled oxidation technique to develop MXene-derived 2D/3D Ti3 C2 –TiO2 –CuTiO3 heterostructures, enhancing the pseudocapacitive properties. abstract: Ti3C2Tx MXene family is a promising electrode material for electrochemical energy storage, but it suffers from insufficient pseudocapacitive charge storage because of self-aggregation and oxidation degradation. To resolve the issue, this paper proposes a two-step process for synthesizing oxidation-controlled MXene-derived 2D/3D heterostructures that beneficially utilize oxidation and simultaneously improve conductivity. The first step generates in-situ 3D floral Ti3C2– TiO2 nanoribbons under partial oxidation of MXene. As the second step, further controlled oxidation with Cu ions transforms the 3D floral Ti3C2–TiO2 nanoribbons into 2D/3D Ti3C2–TiO2–CuTiO3 heterostructure. Leveraging the synergistic effects of MXene, TiO2, and CuTiO3, this 2D/3D heterostructure enhances the interlayered spacing, redox-active site concentration and alleviates low conductivity issue associated with TiO2 nanoribbons. At 2 mA/cm2, the proposed 2D/3D Ti3C2–TiO2–CuTiO3 heterostructure achieved a significantly higher capacitance of 599.2 mF/cm2, compared to MXene with a capacitance of 249.16 mF/cm2 and 3D floral Ti3C2–TiO2 nanoribbons with 498.5 mF/cm2. For practical evaluation, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device (Ti3C2–TiO2–CuTiO3//AC) was fabricated, which exhibited an energy density of 31.1 Wh/kg, power density of 1041.7 W/kg and capacitance retention of 83.7 % after 5000 continuous charging/discharging cycles. It opens new avenues for utilizing controlled oxidation to enhance pseudocapacitive properties.

title: High-performance flexible supercapacitor based on PEDOT:PSS wrapped delaminated Ti3C2Tx composite: Experimental and DFT validation
authors: Gourab Nandy, Swati Shaw, Subhradip Ghosh, Ashok Kumar Dasmahapatra
conclusion: In this work, we have adequately synthesized delaminated Ti3 C2 Tx (d-Ti3 C2 Tx ) by a low-cost method, integrating the mixed acid etching method followed by DMSO intercalation. Furthermore, PP/d-Ti3 C2 Tx binary composites have been prepared with different ratios by the solvent mixing method and coated on the flexible activated carbon cloth. The conformation of the prepared composites was validated by several characterization techniques such as XRD, RAMAN, UV–Vis, FTIR, FESEM, EDS, and FETEM. In three electrodes electrochemical performance PP, and d-Ti3 C2 Tx with a ratio 1:2 respectively (P1M2) exhibit great results in 1 M H2 SO4 electrolyte. The P1M2 electrode shows a brilliant specific capacitance value of 741. 23 F g−1 at a scan rate of 5 mV/s, and 718. 67 F g−1 at a current density of 3. 5 A g−1 . P1M2 electrode shows brilliant E s 35. 93 Whkg−1 (at P s 1049. 90 Wkg-1 ), and 5. 68 Whkg−1 (at Ps 5996. 48 Wkg-1 ). Detailed DFT calculations confirmed that the charge transfer is doubled in the case of PEDOT:PSS@Ti3 C2 Tx in comparison to PEDOT@Ti3 C2 Tx . The charges flow from PEDOT and MXene to PSS. Consequently, PSS possesses the electron-rich region. The DFT calculated solar absorption spectrum for PEDOT:PSS, Ti3 C2 Tx , and PEDOT:PSS@Ti3 C2 Tx agree very well with the experiments. Such excellent agreement substantiates the proposed morphology of the composite i.e. PEDOT wrapped d-Ti3 C2 Tx , aided by multiple PSS carrier pathways. For a flexible and wearable electronic device, we prepared a P1M2-P1M2 SSC and a P1M2-rGO ASC assembly using a gel electrolyte (PVA-H2 SO4 ). The highest specific capacitance has been achieved at 260. 23 F g−1 (at 0. 5 A g−1 ) by the P1M2-P1M2 SSC device; whereas P1M2-rGO ASC has a value of 176. 46 F g−1 (at 0. 1 A g−1 ). The specific energy (specific power) was from 13. 01 Whkg−1 (600 Wkg-1 ) to 2. 63 Whkg−1 (12035 Wkg-1 ) for the SSC device; and from 35. 29 Whkg−1 (240 Wkg-1 ) to 26. 22 Whkg−1 (1200 Wkg-1 ) for ASC device. Both SSC and ASC exhibit excellent performance over various bending and twisting cycles, ASC can operate in a larger potential window and longer durations at low current regions. Moreover, the ASC device shows excellent specific capacitance retention of 89.03 % for 5000 GCD cycles. Subsequently, a red LED was glowed using three ASC devices in series. Hence the P1M2 electrode possesses enormous potential to be used in portable and wearable electronics. abstract: Exploring new electrode materials with cyclic stability and energy storage capacity is crucial for high-performance energy storage in portable electronics. Herein, we present PEDOT:PSS (PP)/delaminated MXene (d-Ti3C2Tx) binary nanocomposites for electrode material for flexible supercapacitor (FSC). PP/d-Ti3C2Tx (1:2 wt ratio, P1M2) on activated carbon cloth results in an excellent specific capacitance of 718.67 F g−1 at a current density of 3.5 A g−1 in 1 M H2SO4. PEDOT chains wrap the d-Ti3C2Tx nanosheets by an opposite electrostatic interaction, while PSS chains act as web-like carrier pathways between two adjacent nanosheets. First principle DFT simulations demonstrate that charge storage in PEDOT:PSS@Ti3C2Tx is enhanced compared to PEDOT@Ti3C2Tx, which describes the effect of PSS chains in the composite. Computationally obtained absorption spectra align well with experimental results, validating the proposed morphology. To employ the P1M2 electrode for FSC, P1M2-P1M2 symmetric solid-state supercapacitor (SSC) and P1M2-rGO asymmetric solid-state supercapacitor (ASC) have been fabricated using 1 M PVA-H2SO4 gel electrolyte. P1M2-P1M2 SSC and P1M2-rGO ASC exhibit a high specific capacitance of 260.23 F g−1 (0.5 A g−1) and 176.46 F g−1 (0.1 A g−1) receptively. Larger potential window, excellent specific capacitance retention of ∼89 % for 5000 GCD cycles, and great performance retention over the bending and twisting conditions make the ASC device a marvelous candidate for the portable energy storage device. The ASC device shows change in specific energy (specific power) from 35.29 W h kg−1 (240 W kg−1) to 26.22 W h kg−1 (1200 W kg−1). An assembly of three such ASC devices glows a red LED for ∼2 min.

title: Hierarchical MXene/NiCo2S4 electrodes derived from MXene/ZIF-67 composites for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Jiawei Wu, Yuanqing Chen, Xujiang Liang, Haolin Dong, Ying Zhang, Huan Cao, Weibai Bian
conclusion: To summarize, the MXene/NiCo2 S4 composite material, synthesized using MXene/ZIF-67 as a precursor, boasts a distinctive structure and morphology. This composite is characterized by spherical NiCo2 S4 nanoparticles that are uniformly loaded onto MXene nanosheets. This architecture not only provides a large specific surface area but also enriches the number of active sites. Leveraging the synergistic effects between the 3D nanospheres and 2D MXene nanosheets, the MXene/NiCo2 S4 composite delivers exceptional electrochemical performance. Specifically, at a current density of 3 mA/cm2 , the area-specific capacity reaches an impressive 1.99 mAh/cm2 , representing a nearly threefold increase compared to its pre-sulfidation state. Moreover, the CV curves maintain excellent symmetry across various scan rates, underscoring the composite’s superior rate capability. After undergoing 10000 charge-discharge cycles, the composite retains 86.17% of its initial capacity, highlighting its remarkable cycling stability. Of even greater significance is the MNCS-1//AC HSC hybrid supercapacitor device assembled from this composite. The voltage windows of the positive and negative electrodes are well-aligned, ensuring efficient energy storage. The CV curves remain stable across different scan rates, and the area-specific capacity peaks at 2.73 mAh/cm2 within a current density range of 5 to 30 mA/cm2 . After 10000 cycles, the device retains 86.19% of its initial capacity. It achieves a maximum energy density of 0.97 mWh/cm2 and a power density of 34.20 mW/cm2 , outperforming numerous previously studied supercapacitor devices. Investigations into the energy storage mechanism reveal that the electrochemical reactions of MXene/NiCo2 S4 are predominantly governed by diffusion-controlled battery-type behavior. This allows ions to penetrate deep into the bulk of the material, facilitating reactions and endowing the composite with robust energy storage capabilities. Beyond its material innovations, this study successfully fabricates high-performance composite electrode materials, offering new directions for the design and preparation of supercapacitor electrodes. abstract: MXene-based electrode materials are highly desirable for their remarkable combination of high specific surface area, excellent chemical stability, and superior electrical conductivity. However, these materials face a significant challenge during the charge-discharge process. Specifically, the intercalation and deintercalation of ions can induce changes in the interlayer spacing, thereby compromising the structural integrity and adversely affecting the cycling stability of the electrodes. In this study, we have developed a layered MXene/NiCo2S4 composite electrode material using MXene/ZIF-67 as the precursor. By leveraging the synergistic interaction between 3D nanospheres and 2D MXene nanosheets, the MXene/NiCo2S4 composite demonstrates exceptional electrochemical performance. When assembled into a hybrid supercapacitor (MNCS-1//AC HSC), the device exhibits an impressive areal specific capacity of 2.73 mAh/cm2 at a current density of 20 mA/cm2. Moreover, it delivers an energy density of 0.97 mWh/cm2 at a power density of 34.20 mW/cm2. After 10,000 cycles, the capacity retention rate remains at a commendable 86.19%. These experimental results clearly indicate that the electrochemical performance of the MXene/NiCo2S4 composite electrode material has been significantly enhanced. This work not only highlights the potential of MXene-based composites but also opens up new avenues for the design and preparation of advanced supercapacitor electrode materials.

title: Flexible, self-supporting Ti3C2Tx thin film electrodes prepared through vacuum filtration and applied for supercapacitors
authors: Runchen Shi, Mengyang Zhang, Xuehua Yan, Jianmei Pan, Jamile Mohammadi Moradian, Zohreh Shahnavaz
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In this work, we successfully exfoliated the Al layer to obtain d-Ti 3 C 2 T x by in-situ etching and ultrasonic assistance. Moreover, MXene thin films with a layered structure were utilized by vacuum filtration. The thin film electrode's structure, morphology and physicochemical properties were systematically explored to analyze its potential as electrode materials in supercapacitors. The microstructure and morphology of the thin film electrode were analyzed. The single-layer Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets have been successfully peeled off by AFM, XRD and TEM characterization methods, and this unique low-layer structure enables Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets to assemble into self-supporting films. In addition, the cross-section SEM showed the thin film's orderly, parallel, and compact stacked nanosheets composition leading to the excellent flexibility of thin films. The thin film electrode exhibited excellent electrochemical performance to achieve a specific capacitance of 293.3 F g −1 at the current density of 1 A g −1 . After 8000 cycles, the capacity retention rate is as high as 91 %, indicating the high stability of the layered structure of the MXene film. The energy density of the device assembled with MXene thin film electrode can still reach 5.8 Wh kg −1 at 1000 W kg −1 power density. The charge storage mechanism of MXene thin films as electrode materials is revealed by distinguishing current types. The energy storage mechanism of MXene thin film electrodes includes both diffusion control and surface control processes, and diffusion control contribution plays a dominant role at a low scan rate.
abstract: The remarkable characteristics of 2D MXene enable its use in energy storage. However, challenges associated with their oxidation and aggregation can limit their performance in energy storage devices. This study systematically explores the unique low-layer Ti3C2Tx nanosheet microstructure with various thicknesses to analyze their potential as electrode materials in supercapacitors. The morphology analysis revealed the excellent lamellar structure and flexibility of prepared MXene thin film electrodes. The cross-section SEM shows the thin film's orderly, parallel, and compact stacked nanosheets, leading to the excellent flexibility of thin films. The thin film electrode with 17.3 μm thickness exhibited the best electrochemical performance among other samples to achieve a specific capacitance of 293.3 F g−1 at the current density of 1 A g−1. After 8000 cycles, the capacity retention rate is as high as 91 %, indicating the high stability of the layered structure of the MXene film. The energy density of the device assembled with MXene thin film electrode can still reach 5.8 Wh kg−1 at 1000 W kg−1 power density. The diffusion control process dominates the electrochemical energy storage behaviour. The assembled symmetric supercapacitor presents a specific capacitance of 54.3 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1.

title: 1T-VS2/MXene network-like heterostructure realizes ultra-high energy density aqueous ammonium ion hybrid supercapacitors and their charge storage mechanism
authors: Xiaofeng Zhang, Salamat Ali, Peiao Lu, Qian Zhang, Wei Xu, Jiakun Luo, Dan Zhao, Bing Bai, Kui-Qing Peng
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In this work, 1T-VS 2 nanosheets were grown in-situ at MXenes via a hydrothermal method to construct a network-like heterostructure. The 1T-VS 2 nanosheets are vertically and uniformly arranged on the surface of the MXene nanosheets. This unique structure considerably increases the specific surface area, which provides more active sites for NH 4  + . In addition, the heterostructure effectively inhibits the recombination of carriers, thereby improving the efficiency of redox reactions. The HS-1T-VS@MXene//AC-AAHSC provides an ultrahigh energy density of 156.9 Wh/kg at a power density of 3,240 W/kg and still has a capacitance retention of 96.2 % after 10,000 cycles. The DFT calculations confirmed the electronic properties of the HS-1T-VS@MXene electrode material. The results show that, compared with pristine 1T-VS 2 and MXene, HS-1T-VS@MXene possesses enhanced conductivity, which benefit the rate performance of the electrode material. This work provides a new idea for the development of AAHSCs devices with high energy density.
abstract: Aqueous ammonium ion-based (NH4+) hybrid supercapacitors (AAHSCs) are attracting great attention because of their environmental friendliness and excellent electrochemical performance. MXenes are highly considered as cathode materials for AAHSCs due to their exceptional electrochemical properties, which include high electrical conductivity, large surface area, tunable surface chemistry, good mechanical stability, and hydrophilicity for aqueous electrolytes. However, the self-stacking effect of 2D materials limits their wide application. In this work, a network-like heterostructure was constructed via in-situ growth of 1T-VS2 nanosheets on the surface of an MXene via a one-step hydrothermal method. The results show that HS-1T-VS@MXene has a high capacitance of 570 F/g at 1 A/g and cycling stability of 96.3 %. In addition, the HS-1T-VS@MXene//AC-AAHSC provides an ultrahigh energy density of 156.9 Wh/kg at a power density of 3,240 W/kg and still has a capacitance retention of 96.2 % after 10,000 cycles. The superior performance is attributed to the heterostructure, which effectively prevents the recombination of carriers and promotes redox reactions. The 1T-VS2 nanosheets are evenly distributed and perpendicular to the MXene surface, reducing charge transfer resistance. This structure increases the specific surface area of the material and provides abundant active sites for the attachment of NH4+. Additionally, the versatile multi-valent redox chemistry and redox activity of Vanadium substantially promote the kinetics of surface redox reactions.

title: Practicality of MXenes: Recent trends, considerations, and future aspects in supercapacitors
authors: Iftikhar Hussain, Abdullah Al Mahmud, Sabarison Pandiyarajan, Karanpal Singh, Essam H. Ibrahim, Pritam J. Morankar, Sajjad Hussain, P. Rosaiah, Muhammad Zubair Khan, Zeeshan Ajmal, Bhargav Akkinepally, Ho-Chiao Chuang, Kaili Zhang
conclusion: MXene emerges as a promising class of two-dimensional materials with enormous potential to transform the landscape of new supercapacitor electrode materials. Its outstanding features, including as strong conductivity, abundant surface functional groups, and intercalation capacitance, have attracted the interest of researchers and driven it to the forefront of supercapacitor innovation. abstract: MXenes, a family of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal carbides and nitrides have garnered significant interest owing to their unique properties, making them suitable for electrode materials in flexible and wearable supercapacitors (SCs). A significant portion of MXenes has predominantly been utilized in a three-electrode configuration, lacking practical applications. Herein, we have conducted a comprehensive review of recent advancements concerning the practical application of MXenes in two-electrode SCs. Critical considerations such as expanding the potential/voltage window, optimizing electrolytes, electrode selection, limitations of both electrodes and electrolytes, and exploration of electrode hybridization have been thoroughly investigated. Moreover, we have discussed the latest progress in MXenes and their prospective contributions to advancing SC applications. The future aspects of MXene-based SCs have been proposed, thereby facilitating advancements in energy storage technologies and their tangible integration into real-world electronic applications.

title: Enhanced electrochemical energy storage via MXene-doped graphene amine nanohybrids for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Muskan M. Momin, Bipin S. Chikkatti, Ashok M. Sajjan, T.M. Yunus Khan, Abdul Saddique Shaik, Nagaraj R. Banapurmath, Narasimha H. Ayachit, Shivashankar A. Huddar
conclusion: This study successfully demonstrates the fabrication and performance of GA/MXene nanocomposite electrodes. The GA/MXene composite electrodes were comprehensively analyzed using FTIR, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, SEM, and EDS to investigate their structural, chemical, morphological, surface, and elemental characteristics. The results confirmed the successful integration of GA and MXene, with strong interfacial interactions enhancing the electrochemical response of the hybrid system. Nyquist plots revealed a minimal charge-transfer resistance and improved ion diffusion at lower frequencies, validating the efficient charge transport at the electrode-electrolyte interface. The GA/MXene electrode exhibited excellent energy storage capabilities, achieving a specific capacitance of 652.1 F g−1 at 0.75 A g−1 , alongside a maximum energy density of 326.9 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 7600 W kg−1 . The electrode also maintained 91 % capacitance retention after 6000 cycles, indicating high long-term stability. These results highlight the GA/MXene system as a promising candidate for high-performance, durable supercapacitor applications. CRediT authorship contribution statement Nagaraj R. abstract: This work presents the electrochemical performance of graphene amine (GA) and GA/MXene nanocomposite electrodes for supercapacitor applications. Structural and morphological characterization using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the successful integration of MXene within the porous GA matrix, forming a well-interconnected structure that mitigates the restacking tendency of MXene and enhances ion accessibility and charge transport. Electrochemical measurements including cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), and galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD), demonstrated that GA/MXene achieved a high specific capacitance of 652.1 F g−1 at 0.75 A g−1, significantly outperforming pristine GA (105.8 F g−1). The GA/MXene composite also delivered an impressive energy density of 326.9 Wh kg−1 at 2850 W kg−1, maintaining 183.7 Wh kg−1 at a high power density of 7600 W kg−1. Compared to other MXene-based hybrids, GA/MXene offers superior electrochemical stability, rate capability, and structural integrity, retaining 91 % capacitance over 6000 cycles. These findings underscore the potential of GA/MXene as a stable, high-performance electrode material for next-generation energy storage devices.

title: Ni nanorods with various morphologies on the surface of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets accelerate alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction
authors: Zengkun You, Kai Ou, Tian Tang, Yajing Cui, Wenting Zhang, Yuxiang Ni, Yudong Xia, Hongyan Wang
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this study, through the simple GLDA technique, precise morphology control was carried out on the surface of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene, and upright/one-fold/oblique nanorod-coated electrodes were grown. Among the fabricated electrodes, Ti 3 C 2 T x @upright exhibited excellent HER performance, showing a low overpotential of only 131 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 and remarkable catalytic stability. Both experimental and theoretical analysis demonstrate that the Ti 3 C 2 T x and Ni nanorod heterojunction structure enhances electron transfer, offers a relatively large reaction area, and increases the effective active sites for water splitting and hydrogen desorption. The electrode produced in this study exhibit excellent economic efficiency and broader applicability, providing a novel approach for designing high-performance, non-precious metal HER catalysts. Meanwhile, this technology is expected to be able to produce low-cost and high-performance HER catalysts on a large scale in the future.
abstract: Under the background of sustainable energy development, the development of efficient, stable and low-cost electrocatalysts to improve electrochemical performance has become a research hotspot in the field of energy conversion. In this work, upright, one-fold and oblique Ni nanorods were designed and grown on Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets via glancing angle deposition technique of physical vapor deposition. For the hydrogen evolution reaction, the composite Ti3C2Tx@upright exhibited a low overpotential of only 131 mV@10 mA/cm2, along with excellent 24 h stability in 1 M KOH. Its excellent performance is mainly attributed to the high porosity of the upright nanorods, the fast electron transport channels provided by Ti3C2Tx MXene, and the stable interface structure. This research provides new ideas for constructing high-performance electrocatalytic catalysts and achieving efficient electrocatalytic conversion in sustainable energy systems.

title: Mechanically endurable Ti3C2Tx MXene incorporated P(AM-AA) hybrid hydrogel electrolyte with enhanced Zn2+ conductivity for flexible zinc-ion batteries
authors: Aakash Carthick Radjendirane, Senthilkumar Ramasamy, Saradh Prasad Rajendra, G. Murali, Insik In, Seung Jun Lee, Subramania Angaiah
conclusion: In summary, the 3D-P(AM-AA)/Ti-MXene (0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 wt.%) are successfully prepared via the in-situ free radical polymerization technique. Among the different concentration samples, 0.2MX/P(AM-AA) HHGE exhibit superior thermal (>400 °C) and mechanical properties (1.6 MPa). Further, the as-prepared 0.2MX/P(AM-AA) HHGE is subjected to electrochemical properties, and it exhibits the highest ionic conductivity of 20.52×10−3 S cm−1 with a transference number of 0.68. It also displayed a larger electrochemical window of 2.4 V. Furthermore, the 0.2MX/P(AM-AA) HHGE delivered a stable stripping/platting behaviour of 1000 cycles without any short-circuiting that effectively inhibited the dendrite growth and byproducts on the zinc anode. Finally, the as-fabricated Zn//V2 O5 @CNTs pouch cell delivered a high specific capacity of 174 mAh g−1 at 0.1 Ag−1 and also excellent long-term cyclic performance of 78% capacity retention over 500 cycles with a coulombic efficiency of 100%. Overall, this work provides profound insight to the development of novel 0.2MX/P(AM-AA) HHGE, which could be highly beneficial for a large-scale fabrication of high-performance ZIBs. abstract: Zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) are severely affected by poor Zn stripping/platting behaviour that causing dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution and uncontrollable passivation reaction at the Zn metal anode. To overcome the aforementioned concern and also to construct flexible batteries, high ionic conductivity and mechanically robust hybrid hydrogel electrolytes (HHGE) are used as the best alternatives. Herein, a highly stable 2D-Ti-MXene incorporated Poly(acrylamide-co-acrylic acid) based HHGE is developed by a facile one-step chemical crosslinking method. Among three different concentrations of Ti-MXene (0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 wt.%) incorporated Poly(acrylamide-co-acrylic acid), 0.2 wt.% of Ti-MXene incorporated P(AM-AA) exhibited excellent ionic conductivity of 20.52×10−3 S cm−1 with a wider 2.4 V electrochemical stability window. The as-prepared hybrid hydrogel displays an outstanding tensile strength of 1.6 MPa than pristine (0.4 MPa). Furthermore, the electrochemical performances of stripping/platting clearly demonstrate the dendrite-free behaviour of the Zn-metal anode over the prolonged life span of 1000 h without any short circuits. For the ZIB (Zn//V2O5), it achieved an initial capacity of 174 mAh g−1 at a current density of 0.1 Ag−1 with a remarkable long-term stability over 500 cycles with 100% coulombic efficiency. It also remains stable under different bending conditions, indicating its potential candidate for high-performance flexible ZIB.

title: Fabrication of MXene/reduced graphene oxide/MoO3 film electrode for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Ruidong Li, Lihua Chen, Shuxin Song, Bingyue Zheng, Tingxi Li, Wenhui Zheng, Yong Ma
conclusion: 3  Conclusions  Herein, MoO 3 nanowires and rGO nanosheets were synthesized utilizing hydrothermal and ascorbic acid reduction techniques, respectively. Following this, MXene, MXene/rGO, and MXene/rGO/MoO 3 films were effectively produced through vacuum-assisted filtration. The incorporation of MoO 3 and rGO significantly improved the ion transport pathways within the films and augmented the ionic active sites of MXene, resulting in remarkable electrochemical characteristics. Notably, the electrochemical properties of the MXene/rGO/MoO 3 film are particularly exceptional, achieving a specific capacitance of 854.2 F g −1 at 1 A g −1 . An ASC was constructed based on the high-performance MXene/rGO/MoO 3 film. This device demonstrated a voltage window of up to 1.6 V and maintained a capacitance retention of 85.6 % after 14,000 cycles at 3 A g −1 . Furthermore, the ASC exhibited a high energy density of 54 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 800 W kg −1 . The MXene/rGO/MoO 3 film produced via vacuum-assisted filtration offers a straightforward and efficient preparation method, providing valuable insights for the development of flexible advanced electrode materials.
abstract: MXene nanosheets exhibit a tendency to agglomerate in electrochemical processes, significantly impairing the electrochemical performance and diminishes their practical applicability. However, this problem can be effectively suppressed by introducing functional intercalation materials. Herein, MXene/reduced graphene oxide (rGO)/MoO3 films synthesized utilizing a vacuum-assisted filtration technique. MoO3 nanofibers and rGO nanosheets serve as essential intercalation materials, establishing a highly stable interlayer configuration within MXene nanosheets. This arrangement significantly increases the spacing between the MXene layers, thereby facilitating the development of a multidimensional and efficient ion transport pathway and exposing more active sites. Under the synergistic effect of this composite structure, the film exhibited a specific capacitance of 854.2 F g−1 at 1 A g−1. In addition, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) assembled with MXene/rGO/MoO3 film as the positive electrode and activated carbon (AC) as the negative electrode shows a wide voltage window of 1.6 V and achieves a high energy density of 54 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 800 W kg−1. More importantly, at 3 A g−1, this ASC maintained 85.4 % capacitance retention after 14,000 cycles, demonstrating excellent cycling stability. The optimization strategy for the MXene/rGO/MoO3 electrode not only illustrates the technological progress of MXene within the domain of energy storage but also establishes a robust technological framework and theoretical underpinning for its utilization in flexible energy storage devices.

title: Nonhazardous in-situ exfoliation approach for Ta-Nb2CTx MXenes as sustainable supercapacitor electrode applications
authors: Uzair Ahmed, Ghulam Nabi
conclusion: Concussively, the successful exfoliation of Nb2 CTx and Ta doped Nb2 CTx in a non-hazardous way has been explored for application as super capacitor electrode material. The study reveals that the enhancement of specific capacity of Ta-Nb2 CTx is attributed to the accordion-like 2D layered structure with intercalated ions inserted between layers causing layers to expand and provide more space for ion transportation as observed by SEM. XRD peaks, HRTEM and SAED confirmed that the doped samples have high crystallinity. Presence of different surface attachments (OH− , O− , F− , Cl− ) with different Nb2 CTx MXene samples were confirmed by EDS, XPS, FTIR and Raman analysis. EDS analysis shows that 6 wt % Ta- Nb2 CTx contains optimal values of these surface attachments that enhance electrochemical energy storage properties. From the doping effect, it has been concluded that 6 wt % Ta-Nb2 CTx has superior electrochemical properties with specific capacity of 454.4 Cg-1 (improved∼68.68 %) at a scan rate of 5 mVs−1 with excellent cyclic stability accompanied with 88 % capacitance retention after 12000 cycles as compared to other doped materials. GCD analysis revealed that 6 wt % Ta-Nb2 CTx based electrode material has specific capacity of 477.87 Cg-1 at current density of 1 Ag-1 . The fabricated asymmetric supercapacitor have ability to deliver a high energy density (ED) of 47.5 Whkg−1 and a power density (PD) of 500 Wkg-1 with ∼89 % retention over 12000 cycles at 1 Ag-1 and at scan rate of 5 mVs−1 showing excellent energy storage capability. This performance has been attributed to excellent exfoliation and Ta-ions doping resulting large interlayer spacing which provided enough surface for ions diffusion. abstract: Utilization of hydrofluoric acid (HF) for exfoliation of MXenes by etching is common but it is extremely hazardous due to its toxic and corrosive nature. Here, direct use of HF is avoided and an in-situ exfoliation approach has been developed which successfully exfoliates the MAX phase of Nb2AlC into multilayered Nb2CTx and Ta-doped Nb2CTx MXenes. Being MXene family, the Nb2CTx owing a set of characteristics with tunability by ions doping based material defects making it a promising contestant for supercapacitor electrodes applications. It has been observed that 6 wt % Ta-Nb2CTx exhibited enhanced specific capacity of 454.4 Cg-1 and highly sustainable cyclic stability of 88 % retention after 12000 CV cycles, attributed to additional active sites by Ta doping, intercalation, increased exfoliation and optimal surface terminations. The power law displays a pseudocapacitive nature (b = 0.61) and the Dunn method shows increasing trend of capacitive contribution with scan rate. The fabricated asymmetric 6 wt% Ta-Nb2CTx//AC (Activated Carbon) based supercapacitor showed energy density (ED) of 47.5 Whkg−1 and a power density (PD) of 500 Wkg-1. These findings open up a perspective way of environment friendly and nonhazardous exfoliation, incorporation of metallic ions into Nb2CTx MXene, and their application in energy storage devices.

title: Green synthesis of MXene@TiO₂ nanocomposites for high-performance flexible supercapacitors: Synergistic enhancement via polypyrrole polymerization and dopant engineering
authors: Hatice Yasemin Ulgunar Iskender, Osman Eksik, Melih Besir Arvas, Sibel Yazar
conclusion: In this study, flexible and conductive nanocomposite films—PPy, PPy/MXene, PPy/MXene/TiO₂GC, and PPy/MXene@TiO₂GC—were successfully fabricated on ATCC substrates and utilized as supercapacitor electrodes. The introduction of MXene into the polypyrrole matrix significantly improved the capacitive performance. Among the synthesized materials, the PPy(10 mg)/MXene@TiO₂GC(20 mg) electrode exhibited the highest specific capacitance of 467.7 F g⁻¹ at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ in a three-electrode system. The co-doping of TiO₂GC was also found to enhance electrochemical performance, suggesting a strong synergistic interaction among the components. The Dunn method analysis further confirmed that the charge storage mechanism is hybrid in nature, with diffusion-controlled processes dominating at low scan rates due to effective ion intercalation pathways, while surface capacitive contributions increase at higher scan rates, emphasizing the role of redox and electric double-layer mechanisms. This dual behavior highlights the complementary electrochemical roles of PPy, MXene, and TiO₂GC. In symmetric supercapacitor configuration, the highest energy and power densities achieved were 5.0 Wh kg⁻¹ at 0.1 mA cm⁻² and 1000 W kg⁻¹ at 1.0 mA cm⁻², respectively. Moreover, the device retained 82.03 % of its initial capacitance after 10,000 cycles, demonstrating excellent cycling stability. These results affirm the potential of PPy/MXene@TiO₂GC as a high-performance electrode material for flexible and durable energy storage applications. Such performance characteristics make this electrode material a promising candidate for next-generation flexible energy storage systems, particularly in applications such as wearable electronics, portable devices, and integrated energy-storage components in smart textiles and microelectronic systems. abstract: Titanium dioxide (TiO2) is a material with high chemical stability and safety characteristics, offering a large energy storage capacity. MXene (Ti₃C₂Tₓ transition metal carbides), on the other hand, is notable for its high electrical conductivity and excellent ion transport properties. These materials serve as ideal electrode materials for high-capacity, fast-charging, and long-cycle-life batteries and supercapacitors. In this study, nanoparticles with dimensions of 13–60 nm were successfully synthesized using the green synthesis method. The interface size that enhances electrode/electrolyte interaction in supercapacitor electrode materials and the presence of materials exhibiting redox behavior increased the supercapacitor performance of polypyrrole (PPy) by 16 times. The charge storage properties of PPy/MXene, PPy/MXene/TiO2GC, and PPy/MXene@TiO2GC electrode materials at different concentrations and through different synthesis methods were compared. The electrode material manufactured at PPy(10 mg)/MXene@TiO2GC(20 mg) weights exhibited a specific capacitance value of 467.7 F g−1, determined at a scan rate of 5 mV s−1 in the 3-electrode system. A symmetrical device was created from the electrodes formed by coating this electrode material on wearable flexible carbon felt. According to the results obtained, the highest energy density achieved was 5.0 Wh/kg at 0.1 mA cm−2, and the highest power density value achieved was 1000 W/kg at 1.0 mA cm−2. It was observed that the symmetrical supercapacitor with 10,000 cycles retained 82.03 % of its capacitance.

title: MXene-modified and electrochemically enhanced polyaniline hydrogels for flexible asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Yubo Zou, Huili Liu, Guocong Liu, Binyi Yang, Jiajia Li, Shanxing Wang, Kaiping Xie, Chunhua Wang, Shahid Iqbal
conclusion: In summary, a novel strategy was suggested for creating M-PANI hydrogels using hydrothermal assembly to modify PANI with highly conductive MXene. The electrochemical performance of PANI is successfully improved by the modification of MXene. A high specific capacitance of 483.1 F g−1 is shown by the prepared M-PANI hydrogel electrodes with a current density of 1 A g−1 . Additionally, when the current density is raised from 1 to 20 A g−1 , M-PANI electrodes have a much-anticipated rate capability of 79.8 %. Furthermore, the electrodes show good cycling stability, retaining 80 % of initial capacitance after undergoing 6000 charge/discharge cycles. The flexible asymmetric supercapacitors (MXene//M-PANI) were further assembled by MXene as anode and M-PANI as cathode materials. The electrochemical findings demonstrate that high specific capacitance of 128.2 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , exciting energy density of 23.6 W h kg−1 at 575 W kg−1 , and cycling stability of 89.4 % retention of the original capacitance after 9000 cycles are all achievable with MXene//M-PANI supercapacitors. abstract: Efficiently preparing polyaniline (PANI) supercapacitor electrode materials with exceptional electrochemical performance is vital for their utilization in energy storage devices, notwithstanding the difficulties involved. We developed a direct hydrothermal assembly approach to construct MXene-modified PANI hydrogel (M-PANI) using PANI dispersion modified by highly conductive MXene. The findings suggest that the breakdown of MXene nanosheets and the conversion into TiO2 from part of MXene by hydrothermal treatment may notably boost the electrochemical performances of M-PANI hydrogels. The prepared M-PANI hydrogel electrodes exhibit high specific capacitance (483.1 F g−1 at 1 A g−1), superior rate capability (79.8 % from 1 to 20 A g−1), and valuable cycling durability (80 % of initial capacitance after 6000 cycles). The flexible asymmetric supercapacitors (MXene//M-PANI) were further assembled using MXene as anode and M-PANI as cathode materials, which achieve high specific capacitance (128.2 F g−1 at 1 A g−1), satisfying energy density (23.6 W h kg−1 at 575 W kg−1), and favorable cycling durability (89.4 % retention of the initial capacitance after 9000 cycles). The generated M-PANI hydrogels with remarkable electrochemical performances as supercapacitor electrodes suggest their enormous potential in the field of cutting-edge energy storage technology.

title: Synthesis and electrochemical performance of a novel CuCoTex/Mn3O4/MXene ternary nanocomposite electrode for hybrid-supercapacitor
authors: Padmanaban Annamalai, Kanimozhi Selvadhas Nirmala, Sivaraj Durairaj, Hector Valdes, Anandan Sambandam, Arunachalam Arulraj, Manoj Devaraj, Chandra Kumar
conclusion: This study demonstrates the successful synthesis and characterization of the CuCoTex /Mn3 O4 /Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite, which significantly enhances the supercapacitor electrode performance. The combination of CuCoTex ’s conductivity, Mn3 O4 ’s redox activity, and Ti3 C2 Tx MXene’s structural stability resulted in improved energy and power densities, along with enhanced cycling stability, and efficient charge storage capacity. The synergistic interaction among the three components paved the way for contributes to increased surface area, better charge transport, and superior structural integrity, leading to enhance the overall electrochemical performance. The nanocomposite exhibited excellent electrochemical behaviour across a range of scan rates and current densities, emphasizing its suitability for high-performance supercapacitor applications. Electrochemical analysis confirmed the nanocomposite’s high charge storage capacity and favourable ion diffusion characteristics. Furthermore, bending measurements at various angles revealed the minimal changes in electrochemical performance, which proved the mechanical flexibility and robustness of the nanocomposite for flexible device integration. The successful fabrication and testing of an asymmetric supercapacitor using this material demonstrate its practical applicability for large-scale energy storage systems, particularly in the context of renewable energy integration. These findings accomplished valuable insights into the design and development of novel bimetallic telluride-based nanocomposite and lay the groundwork for future advancements in efficient energy storage systems. abstract: The increasing global shift towards renewable energy emphasizes the urgent need for improved energy storage technologies, particularly in supercapacitors, where the advanced electrode materials can significantly enhance the performance. The rise of metal chalcogenides as electrode material in supercapacitors offers promising electrochemical conductivity with abundant electroactive sites. However, the traditional metal chalcogenides cannot meet the requirements for high energy density due to their inherent low conductivity and slower ionic diffusion channels which is necessary for commercial viability due to their inherent low conductivity and slower ionic diffusion channels. Among the different metal chalcogenide materials being studied, bimetallic copper-cobalt telluride (CuCoTex) is gaining attention due to its high specific capacitance, excellent conductivity, and strong electrochemical stability. Despite these promising properties, the application of CuCoTex as an electrode material in supercapacitors remains relatively underexplored. In this study, a novel ternary nanocomposite consisting of copper cobalt telluride (CuCoTex), manganese oxide (Mn3O4), and titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) MXene was synthesized via a one-pot method for the first time as an electrode material for supercapacitors. This new nanocomposite leverages the strengths of each constituent: CuCoTex provides superior conductivity and electrochemical reactivity, Mn3O4 offers rich redox chemistry and high theoretical capacitance, and Ti3C2Tx MXene delivers exceptional conductivity and mechanical stability. The ternary nanocomposite achieved a specific capacitance of 127 F/g at 1 mA/cm2, surpassing the 100 F/g of CuCoTex alone, and demonstrated an energy density of 6.2 Wh/kg and power density of 54 W/kg. It also exhibited excellent cyclic stability with 91 % retention after 2500 cycles. The incorporation of MXene further optimizes charge transport and enhances the structural integrity of the nanocomposite, addressing the conductivity limitations of Mn3O4. These findings represent the first successful integration of CuCoTex, Mn3O4, and MXene in a single hybrid electrode and offer a scalable pathway towards high-performance, durable energy storage systems for renewable energy applications.

title: Nitrogen-doped MXene for supercapacitor: A review
authors: Ahmed Jalal Salih Salih, Ahmad Huseyin
conclusion: 6  Conclusion and recommendations  Doping MXene with nitrogen gives it improved morphological, chemical, and physical properties. This review demonstrates that nitrogen doping addresses the issue of MXene layer restacking, providing greater freedom for electrolyte ion movement and better accessibility to the MXene electrode surface. Simultaneously, the presence of nitrogen atoms increases electronic density and enhances redox activity. These improvements contribute to a higher electrode capacitance. Additionally, doping with nitrogen enhances conductivity, structural stability, and wettability. In light of the discussion on doping mechanisms, doping methods, and the effects of doping on electrochemical performance, several recommendations can be proposed here;   1.  Doping MXene with nitrogen has demonstrated clear success in supercapacitors, suggesting the potential for expanding theoretical and experimental studies of nitrogen doping to include other MXenes beyond Ti 3 C 2 Tₓ.    2.  Although doping in many studies occurs through multiple mechanisms simultaneously, one mechanism tends to dominate while others occur to a lesser extent. It would be beneficial to give greater attention to each mechanism within a single study to achieve successful doping through multiple mechanisms at higher levels.    3.  Most studies focus on the reduction of fluorine functional groups after doping, often neglecting hydroxyl functional groups, despite their significant impact on electrochemical performance. Greater emphasis should be placed on this aspect, especially since the effect of doping on hydroxyl groups can be easily diagnosed.    4.  It would be beneficial to conduct studies on doping that focus on the mechanism of surface adsorption, as there is a notable lack of research in this area.    5.  Further investigation into the different nitrogen doping configurations within the carbon lattice of MXene would be highly valuable. The contribution of each of the three forms (pyridinic, pyrrolic, and graphitic nitrogen) to performance enhancement requires further clarification. and then it is possible to control to some extent the selection of the best electrochemically performing configuration among the three forms during the doping process.
abstract: Efforts to enhance the properties of MXene have been ongoing since its discovery in 2011. Various strategies have been explored to improve its performance for many applications. One such strategy is doping MXene with heteroatoms. Doping has been studied for several applications, including supercapacitors, with particular attention given to nitrogen doping. This review focuses on doping MXene with nitrogen for supercapacitor applications. It discusses the effects of doping on the chemical, physical, and structural properties of MXene, the doping mechanisms (lattice substitution, functional substitution, and surface adsorption), and the contributions of each mechanism to the enhancement of electrochemical performance. Additionally, the review discusses doping methods and their impact on the performance of MXene as supercapacitor electrodes. It presents results from experimental studies and discusses several of these findings. Finally, it provides recommendations to guide future research and optimize outcomes in this field.

title: Defect enriched luminescent MXene-derived TiO2 for supercapacitors
authors: Ghrutanjali Sahu, Annu Balhara, Laxmidhar Besra, Divya Nechiyil, K. Sudarshan, Jyoti Prakash, Santosh K. Gupta, Sriparna Chatterjee
conclusion: The work focuses on comprehensively understanding the intricate relationships between the structure, optical properties, and electrochemical performance of MXenes and their derivatives, which is crucial for advancing the development of high-performance materials for energy storage and conversion. We have synthesized MXene-derived TiO2 that demonstrates excellent PL properties and serves as an electrode material for energy storage in supercapacitors. This behavior is attributed to the intrinsic features of MXene, which impart the MXene-derived TiO2 with various types of defects, such as surface defects, oxygen vacancies, and titanium vacancies. The exceptional PL and supercapacitive performance of MXene-derived TiO2 are mainly ascribed to the presence of titanium vacancies. Furthermore, the addition of NiO reduces titanium-related vacancies and enhances positron annihilation corresponding to the second positron lifetime component, likely indicating contributions from the interface. This finding has been corroborated using EPR (electron paramagnetic resonance) analysis. However, the nanocomposite of MXene-derived TiO2 and NiO does not show significant improvement in light emission or supercapacitor performance, as the addition of NiO leads to a reduction in defect density. abstract: To utilize the intriguing properties of MXene and titania, here in this work, we have synthesized defect-enriched TiO2 by thermal annealing of MXene phase (Mxene-derived-TiO2) and characterized using X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, Field emission, and transmission electron microscopy. Such uniquely derived MXene-derived-TiO2 displayed bright blue light photoluminescence (PL) under near UV excitation. The electrochemical analysis underscores the superior electrochemical performance of MXene-derived-TiO2, particularly in terms of specific capacitance and pseudocapacitive behavior, making them highly suitable for supercapacitors. The oxygen and titanium vacancies present in MXene-derived-TiO2 are responsible for its excellent PL and supercapacitor action. Such defect-induced origin of PL and supercapacitive action is further validated by the addition of NiO. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy (PALS) suggested addition of NiO to Mxene-derived-TiO2 leads to a reduction in defect density of titanium vacancies and is reflected in the lowering of PL intensity and resulted in inferior supercapacitive properties.

title: Fabrication of Ti3C2Tx MXene/polyaniline composite films with adjustable thickness for high-performance flexible all-solid-state symmetric supercapacitors
authors: Wenlong Luo, Yudi Wei, Zhao Zhuang, Zhongtai Lin, Xue Li, Chunping Hou, Tingxi Li, Yong Ma
conclusion: In summary, we have successfully prepared MXene/PANI composite films with adjustable thickness by changing the PANI dosage by suction filtration of MXene nanosheets and PANI nanofibers. The introduction of PANI nanofibers can effectively increase the electrochemical performances of the films, because conductive PANI nanofibers can provide a path for charge carriers and increase the interlayer spacing of MXene nanosheets to facilitate electrolyte ion diffusion. However, it is found that the amount of PANI nanofibers is not positively correlated with the specific capacitance of the films. The reason is that excess PANI nanofibers obviously increase the film thickness, seriously worsening the diffusion and transfer paths of electrons and ions. The device based on the optimal film exhibits a specific capacitance of 272.5 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , and after 4000 cycles, the capacitance retention rate is about 71.4%. Moreover, the devices exhibited energy density of 31.18 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1079.3 W kg−1 , indicating that it has excellent energy storage performance. The film used as an excellent flexible electrode material with good cycle stability and high specific capacitance, thereby contributing to the development of flexible all-solid-state supercapacitors.
