Xue Li: Visualization, Investigation. Chunping Hou: Supervision. Tingxi Li: Software, Validation. Yong Ma: Writing – review & editing.
abstract: In here, we successfully fabricated flexible Ti3C2Tx (MXene)/polyaniline (PANI) films with adjustable thickness by changing the amount of PANI nanofibers utilized as high-performance supercapacitor electrode materials. Firstly, MXene nanosheets and PANI nanofibers were prepared by the minimum strength stratification method and the redox method, respectively. And then the MXene/PANI films were synthesized by simple physical mixing and suction filtration of these two components. The electrochemical performances of the composite films show that the introduction of PANI nanofibers increases the specific capacitance of the MXene film. The reason is that conductive PANI nanofibers can not only provide a path for charge carriers, but also increases MXene layer spacing beneficial to electrolyte ion infiltration. However, with increasing amount of PANI nanofibers, the specific capacitance of the composite film shows a trend of first increase and then decrease. This fact is a result of that excess PANI nanofibers lead to an increase in the thickness of the composite film, which increases the ion and electron transport paths. The assembled device based on the optimal composite film exhibits a high specific capacitance of 272.5 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and a capacitance retention rate of about 71.4% after 4000 cycles at 2 A g−1. The devices exhibited a high energy density of 31.18 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1079.3 W kg−1, indicating that it has excellent energy storage performance.

title: MoO3-x-assisted MXene-derived TiO2/C-graphene composite structure for high-capacitance electrode materials of ionic liquid-based supercapacitors
authors: Liangqi Jing, Yujuan Chen, Li Sun, Kelei Zhuo, Dong Sun, Xiao Su, Mengya Yang, Jianji Wang
conclusion: In conclusion, the formation of multi-component hybrid materials (Mo-MX-G) is accomplished via a one-step hydrothermal approach, whereby MoO3-x nanoparticles are grown in-situ upon the framework of MXene-derived TiO2 /C -graphene composite. Benefiting from the superior energy storage crystalline structures of TiO2 and MoO3-x as well as their heterostructures, the meticulously designed Mo-MX-G material not only provides abundant active sites but also exhibits superior charge transfer kinetics. In the hydrothermal process, the presence of GO effectively inhibits the interlayer stacking of MXene and facilitates the formation of TiO2 nanoparticles anchored on the MXene-derived disordered carbon substrate. Particularly, the introduction of MoO3-x inhibited the stacking of the nanosheets and formed the heterostructure with TiO2 , and thus significantly enhanced the Li-ion storage ability of the composite. Beneficial from the synergistical effects of its multi-components, the as-prepared composite material exhibits excellent charge storage ability in IL-based electrolytes, delivering a specific capacitance of 353.8 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 . In addition, the ASC device assembled by the Mo-MX-G anode and the UPGA cathode in the IL-based electrolyte achieves a specific capacitance of 30.1 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and an energy density of 28.3 W h kg−1 at a power density of 1193.0 W kg−1 . This study presents an innovative approach to the design of hybrid electrode materials aimed at improving charge storage capabilities within ionic liquid-based electrolytes, with the additional expectation of achieving supercapacitors that exhibit enhanced energy density. CRediT authorship contribution statement Liangqi Jing: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Methodology, Investigation. Yujuan Chen: Validation, Project administration. Li Sun: Validation, Investigation. Kelei Zhuo: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Project administration, Methodology,
abstract: Supercapacitors (SCs) are considered among the most promising energy storage solutions for future application. Ionic liquid (IL)-based electrolytes, characterized by their wide electrochemical stability windows, noninflammability, and low toxicity, are considered one of the most ideal electrolyte types for use in SCs. However, because of the substantial ion size for ionic liquids, the advancement of energy density in IL-based supercapacitors is hampered by diminished charge storage capacities of electrode materials within IL electrolytes. Herein, we demonstrate a MoO3-x-assisted MXene-derived TiO2/C-graphene composite material (Mo-MX-G) synthesized by in-situ growing MoO3-x nanoparticles on the surface of MXene-derived TiO2/C-graphene composites in one-step hydrothermal process. In the hybrid material, TiO2 nanoparticles and α-MoO3-x nanoparticles form heterostructures which are beneficial to charge transport and storage. Anatase TiO2 and α-MoO3-x nanoparticles exhibit advantageous crystal structures for Li-ion storage and transfer, evidenced by their remarkable capacity. These nanoparticles are anchored on an amorphous carbon substrate to boost the composite's electrical conductivity. Owing to synergistical effects of its constituent components, the composite material exhibits significantly enhanced charge storage performance in IL-based electrolytes, achieving a specific capacitance of 353.8 F g−1. An assembled asymmetric SC device (UPGA//Mo-MX-G, UPGA refers to urea phosphate-derived graphene aerogel) exhibits an energy density of 28.3 W h kg−1 at a power density of 1193 W kg−1. This work provides an advanced strategy for designing high-performance hybrid materials utilized in IL-based SCs.

title: A review of recent progress in the synthesis of 2D Ti3C2Tx MXenes and their multifunctional applications
authors: Mojtaba Rostami, Alireza Badiei, Ghodsi Mohammadi Ziarani
conclusion: 3  Conclusion and future perspectives  To ensure excellent quality Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes for versatile applications such as HER, RBs, and SCs, the etching process and conditions need to be carefully manipulated. While 2D Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes exhibit excellent properties for various applications, their properties are strongly affected by surface termination functional groups and coupled materials. While the non-aqueous MS etching method has been investigated to enhance the physical and chemical characteristics of MXenes, such as mechanical properties and electrical conductivity, the accordion-like structure of the resulting MXenes renders them inappropriate for making nanoscale complexes. Cl-terminated MXenes offer the best HER catalytic activity due to their termination modification, which enhances better stability, interlayer spacing and Cl-ion conductivity. The hybridization of transition metal compounds with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes improves light absorption, electron transfer, and separation, as well as active sites. The hybridization process would be aided by the presence of edge-terminal groups that are evenly distributed on the surface of 2D Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes, particularly hydrophilic oxide groups bound to Ti. The MS etching process is the most effective way to balance the stability and activity of HER catalysts based on transition metals in an alkaline electrolyte. The findings of this study greatly increase the range of uses for MXene and MAX nanomaterials by providing a novel method for the manufacture of additional MAX-phase materials at lower temperatures. Additionally, different Lewis acid MS show that it is possible to create unique MAX phases by replacement reactions.  The MS 3 method stands out among other MXene synthesis techniques because it eliminates the need for hazardous reactants and inert gas protection. The two carbide/nitride MXenes may be quickly synthesized using this approach, and it is easily scaled up to etch up to 60 g of the MAX phases. In conclusion, the MS 3 -MXene production process represents a significant breakthrough in the field, and is expected to generate substantial interest among both MXene researchers and industry professionals due to its potential for rapid and scalable production of high-quality MXene materials. The precursor material, hexagonal Ti 3 AlC 2 , featured a spiral chiral symmetry structure with diameters ranging from 200 nm to 2 m, and was made utilizing the “one-pot melting and Lewis salt additive” method. The resulting hexagonal Ti 3 AlC 2 nanomaterial maintained its interlayered structure and a well-defined layered microstructure with a large interlayer distance, which played a key role in ensuring its excellent long-term cycle stability. The flexible hexagonal Ti 3 C 2 nanosheets production has significantly advanced the investigation development of Ti 3 C 2 nanomaterials in the field of electrochemical energy storage (SCs and RBs), especially in terms of achieving super specific capacitance and long cycle stability. The surface terminal groups can undergo one-pot production from in single-step MS method, which considerably reduces the modification procedures and broadens the range of surface endings available. In this method, no acidic liquid waste is generated after creation, and the salt can be recycled, making it an environmentally-friendly, low-cost, fast and sustainable approach.  The utilization of TBAOH-treated MS-Ti 3 C 2 T x as an anode material in LIBs demonstrated a remarkable improvement in energy storage through enhanced electrochemical performance, super specific capacity, improved wettability, and outstanding rate capability. The increase in N content and reduction of F element in Ti 3 C 2 T x resulted in the development of N-N-Ti 3 C 2 T x electrode, which showed excellent capacitance retention, superior specific capacitance, good rate performance, high electrochemical activity area, and good electrical conductivity. These findings pave the way for the progress of Ti 3 C 2 T x nanomaterials with outstanding retention performance and high specific capacitances, highlighting the significance of surface chemistry tuning of MXene in enhancing their electrochemical properties. The study provides valuable insights for the development of a new generation of MXene negative electrodes that can be used in high-power batteries.  MXenes have garnered considerable attention due to their potential utility across diverse domains, encompassing the HER, RBs, and SCs. Nonetheless, they are also encumbered by specific constraints necessitating mitigation for further progress in these arenas. (i) HER: Limitations: (a) limited active sites: MXenes present a constrained quantity of active sites for the HER owing to surface termination and diminished surface area. (b) High overpotential: Achieving efficient HER performance with MXenes typically mandates high overpotentials. (c) Poor stability: MXenes are susceptible to surface oxidation in oxygen-rich environments, culminating in performance deterioration. Strategies to Overcome Limitations: (a) Surface functionalization: Augmenting the number of active sites for HER by introducing functional groups or doping MXenes. (b) Alloying: Enhancing catalytic activity and mitigating overpotential through MXene alloying with other metals, with molten salt Lewis acid etching representing a significant approach. (c) Surface Passivation: Enhancing MXene stability in oxygen-rich environments by developing protective coatings of metal oxide or metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). (ii) RBs: Limitations: (a) Volume expansion: MXenes undergo substantial volume expansion during cycling, resulting in mechanical degradation and capacity loss. (b) Limited specific capacity: MXenes often exhibit restricted specific capacity due to their low theoretical capacity. Strategies to overcome limitations: (a) Structural Engineering: Accommodating volume changes and enhancing mechanical stability by designing composite structures or nanoarchitectures with MOF derivatives and 2D nanomaterials. (b) Alloying and Intercalation: Increasing specific capacity and enhancing electrochemical performance by introducing other elements or ions into MXenes' structure, with molten salt Lewis acid etching being a key strategy. (c) Surface modification: Augmenting stability and performance through protective layer coatings or incorporation into conductive matrices. (iii) SCs: Limitations: (a) Low mass transfer: MXenes may exhibit constrained ion diffusion kinetics, resulting in low rate capability and energy density. (b) Limited capacitance retention: Capacitance degradation over cycling due to structural alterations and surface oxidation can afflict MXenes. Strategies to overcome Limitations: (a) Porosity Enhancement: Improving ion diffusion and augmenting accessible surface area through the introduction of hierarchical or porous structures. (b) Electrode thickness reduction: Enhancing rate capability by fabricating MXene electrodes with reduced thickness to shorten ion diffusion pathways. (c) Electrochemical stabilization: Mitigating capacitance degradation and enhancing stability through control of MXene surface chemistry or application of surface coatings, with molten salt Lewis acid etching playing a significant role. In addition to the aforementioned strategies, ongoing research endeavors are directed toward exploring novel synthesis methodologies, optimizing MXene compositions, and advancing characterization techniques to comprehensively address and surmount MXene limitations across various applications. These concerted efforts aim to bolster MXene performance, stability, and scalability, thereby facilitating their wider adoption in energy storage and catalytic domains.
abstract: In the last decade, two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal carbides and/or nitrides identified as MXenes (Mn+1XnTx) have shown great potential owing to their unique electronic and chemical properties such as high metallic conductivity, hydrophilicity, various surface termination functional groups (Tx), and sheet-like 2D structures. Most recent years, molten salt (MS)‐Shielded Synthesis (MS3) has been prepared 2D Ti3C2Tx MXenes with controllable morphology and surface termination functional groups, eco-friendly, low-cost, fast and large production for versatile applications. Furthermore, a MS etching strategy utilizing Lewis acidic salts as etchants has been proposed to prepare 2D Ti3C2Tx MXenes from MAX phase. This review highlights the recent advances in synthesizing Ti3C2Tx nanosheets using the MS etching method in various fields, including hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), rechargeable batteries (RBs), and supercapacitors (SCs). Utilizing the MS method in the production of Ti3C2Tx nanosheets has demonstrated increased efficiency and has been implemented to increase the density and availability of active chemical and electronic sites for improved performance. Additionally, various nanostructures and hybridizations of low-cost transition metals have been fabricated. The suitability of these materials for multifarious applications has been thoroughly discussed.

title: Scalable assembly of polyaniline/Ti3C2Tx MXene modified cotton yarn flexible electrode for high-performance wearable energy storage
authors: Yang Zhang, Shenao Zhang, Kangxin Qi, Yazi Wang, Wei Chen, Jian Xu, Yusen Wang, Diwei Gu, Xiangxiang Pi, Bin Sun, Wangyang Lu
conclusion: In summary, the PTC yarn electrode, with the core of cotton yarn and the sheath of PT layer, was fabricated via scalable coating method. The cotton yarn regards as robust skeleton, endowing large mechanical properties, various deformation ability and integration ability for the PTC yarn electrode. Besides, the Ti3 C2 Tx layer on cotton yarn provides continuous conductive pathways for electron transfer. Moreover, the PANI nanoparticles as fillers can not only impede the self-restacking of Ti3 C2 Tx layer exposing larger surface area and richer ions diffusion channels, but also deliver pseudo-capacitance for adequate redox reaction sites. Due to the designed structure and synergistic effect, the PTC yarn electrode displays large capacitance (417.6F g−1 at 1 A g−1 ) and good rate performance (54 % capacitance retention at 10 A g−1 ) in three-electrode system. After assembling to symmetric F-SCs, the flexible device displays high capacitance of 175.6F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 , huge energy density of 6.1 Wh kg−1 , admired long-term cycling performance (98.5 % capacitance retention after 2000 cycling) and remarkable mechanical endurance, illustrating a huge application potential in wearable system. CRediT authorship contribution statement Yang Zhang: Writing – review & editing, Validation, Software,
abstract: Developing miniaturization, adaptability and weavability fiber-shaped supercapacitors (F-SCs), presenting adequate active sites, interconnected electrolyte diffusion channels and good mechanical endurance, has been pivotal issues for controlled, reliable and stable power source in intelligent wearable system. Here, the flexible PANI/Ti3C2Tx modified cotton (PTC) yarn electrode was fabricated via coating method on a large scale. Ti3C2Tx flakes regard as a binder and anchor on the cotton yarn along with PANI nanoparticles to construct a conductive framework. Besides, embedding PANI nanoparticles obtaining favorable synergistic effect can not only provide large pseudo-capacitance, but also impede the self-restacking of Ti3C2Tx flakes, causing penetrative ions channels, abundant redox active sites and large surface area. What’s more, the tough skeleton of cotton yarn endows remarkable mechanical endurance for electrode and device. As a result, the PTC yarn shows large mass capacitance (417.6F g−1 at 1 A/g) and superior rate performance (225.7F g−1 at 10 A/g) in three-electrode system. Moreover, the symmetric solid-state F-SCs deliver high capacitance of 175.6F g−1 at 0.5 A/g, incredible energy density (6.1Wh kg−1) and stable charge/discharge performance (98.5% capacitance retention after 2000 cycling). More importantly, the F-SCs exhibit impressive capacitance retention under deformation settings and ever integrated into the textile, which proves the bright future in the smart garment application.

title: Unveiling the potential of M2X MXenes: Structure, properties, synthesis strategies, and supercapacitor applications
authors: Onkar Jaywant Kewate, Iftikhar Hussain, Megha Prajapati, Rita Kumari, Yosephine Intan Ayuningtyas, Dattakumar S. Mhamane, Mukund G. Mali, Mohan V. Jacob, Jeng-Yu Lin, Chhaya Ravi Kant, Sathyanarayanan Punniyakoti
conclusion: 7  Conclusion  In recent decades, the blossoming of supercapacitor applications has gained significant attraction for the materials science community. Extensive research on supercapacitors has been going on due to their exceptional characteristics. For an electrode material of supercapacitors, various materials have been utilized to boost the electrochemical performance. After graphene, in 2011 another wonder material was discovered known as MXenes. These MXenes have unique and excellent properties which help to improve the performance of various applications, especially supercapacitors. Owing to these advantages, the authors are presenting a thorough review article on the M 2 X MXenes. The review article is divided into various sections such as the introduction, structures, properties, synthesis approaches, M 2 X MXenes for supercapacitors, and conclusion, challenges, and future perspectives. In the introduction section, an overview of MXenes, various energy storage systems, a variety of electrode materials, and M 2 X MXenes is discussed appropriately. Next, MXenes consist of various structures. Here, only the structure of M 2 X MXenes is mentioned. In the coming section, diverse properties such as electronics, optical, magnetic, thermal, chemical, and mechanical are appropriate to supercapacitors explained properly. Afterward, the most important part is the synthesis of M 2 X MXenes. In this, a wide range of etching methods such as HF, MILD , molten salts, electrochemical, hydrothermal, supercritical, and Lewis acid for various M 2 X MXenes are explained thoroughly. Fluoride salt-based etching techniques, particularly those that employs minimally fluorinated or completely fluoride-free etchants, are gaining more recognition because of their enhanced safety, effectiveness, and environmental friendliness. In addition, to environmental and safety factors, these etching techniques produces MXenes with controlled terminations, enhancing their properties for specific applications (e.g., supercapacitors). Reduces defects and oxidation compared to traditional HF methods. Avoids severe handling hazards associated with HF-based methods. However, to avoid a completely HF-free process there is a requirement for green methods. Following the synthesis approaches, various M 2 X (Ti 2 CT  x  , Nb 2 CT  x  , V 2 CT  x  , Ta 2 CT  x  , Cr 2 CT  x  , Mo 2 CT  x  , V 2 NT  x  , Mo 2 NT  x  ) MXenes utilized as an electrode material for supercapacitors are discussed thoroughly. However, there remain obstacles to solve in the study of M 2 X-based materials for electrodes of supercapacitors.
abstract: 2D MXenes have received significant attention due to their remarkable properties, including superior electrical conductivity, chemical stability, tunable surface chemistry, structural flexibility, and excellent thermal and magnetic characteristics, making them highly suitable for supercapacitors. Since their discovery in 2011, M3X2 MXenes have been widely studied, while M2X MXenes, despite their equally impressive properties, have been comparatively less explored. M2X MXenes offer promising potential for a wide range of applications, particularly in energy storage systems like supercapacitors. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current energy storage crisis and the increasing demand for advanced materials. It introduces the fundamentals of MXenes, with a detailed focus on M2X MXenes, and explains their structure, properties, and various synthesis methods. The review also highlights the application of M2X MXenes in supercapacitors and also provided a detailed discussion of their advantages and challenges. In conclusion, the article outlines the key challenges and future directions in the field, aiming to serve as a valuable guide for MXene research and supercapacitor development.

title: Enhanced photoluminescence emission and pH sensitivity in oxygen-dominated functional group of highly stable Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: Sheetal Sharma, Manoj Kumar Gupta, Vinod Kumar Singh
conclusion: In this study, we successfully synthesized the two-dimensional nanomaterial Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene at low temperatures, resulting in reduced crystallite size of 3.8 nm and revealing its distinct surface chemistry and layered structure with interlayer spacing of 1.13 nm, as confirmed by different characterization techniques. The results confirmed the complete removal of aluminium from the MAX phase due to the absence of a peak at 39 ° and identified the presence of an Oxygen-dominated functional group through FTIR. Photoluminescence studies demonstrated a broad emission spectrum ranging from ultraviolet to visible light, with notable blue–green emission attributed to the active -O termination groups. The MXene nanosheets also significantly enhance luminescence properties by increasing the photoluminescence intensity with varying excitation wavelength and improving the spectral stability. Moreover, the pH-dependent photoluminescence analysis revealed a decrease in excitation intensity with lower pH levels, indicating a shift in the intrinsic properties and hence the optical behavior of Ti 3 C 2 T x . Additionally, Cyclic voltammetry (CV) and Zeta potential show outstanding stability of MXene, and UV–Vis-NIR spectroscopy indicated that Ti 3 C 2 T x exhibits a band gap of 2.4 eV, affirming its semiconducting nature which is also evident from I-V measurement. Overall, this research highlights that Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene possesses enhanced photoluminescence with broad light emission characteristics influenced by -O termination groups and demonstrates that pH plays a crucial role in modulating its optical properties. Vinod Kumar Singh: Writing – review & editing, Supervision.
abstract: Transition metal carbides, commonly known as MXenes, represent a promising family of two-dimensional nanomaterials characterized by diverse surface functional groups that vary with the synthesis method. This study investigates the enhanced luminescence of MXene nanosheets, increasing photoluminescence intensity due to improved charge transfer, and the influence of pH on the photoluminescence excitation spectrum of Ti3C2Tx MXene, which features oxygen-dominated functional groups. The Ti3C2Tx MXene was well-synthesized using hydrofluoric acid (HF), as confirmed with X-ray diffraction analysis, which revealed the hexagonal structure of Ti3C2Tx with a crystallite size of 3.8 nm, while electron microscopy images illustrated its distinct layered morphology with the inter-layer spacing of 1.13 nm which reveals good flexibility and tensile strength of the MXene. Photoluminescence studies demonstrated significant light emission with enhanced photoluminescence intensity with varying excitation wavelength in the blue–green region, spanning from 400 nm to 690 nm. Notably, pH-dependent photoluminescence analysis indicated a decrease in excitation intensity at pH 2, suggesting a loss of the material’s intrinsic properties under acidic conditions. Furthermore, cyclic voltammetry and zeta potential reveal outstanding stability of MXene over time. The electrical measurement reveals the semiconducting nature of Ti3C2Tx, which is evident from its band gap. This research highlights the critical role of pH in modulating the optical properties of Ti3C2Tx MXene, paving the way for potential applications in optoelectronic devices and sensors.

title: Electrochemical investigation of MnMoO4 incorporated MXene Ti3C2Tx for energy storage applications
authors: P. Sivaharini, J. Vigneshwaran, Sujin P. Jose, C. Gopinathan
conclusion: In conclusion, we have thoroughly examined the structural and electrochemical characteristics of the MnMoO4 -Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite, focusing on its application as an electrode material for supercapacitors. The XRD analysis revealed distinctive peaks corresponding to both MnMoO4 and Ti3 C2 Tx . Our study on the MnMoO4 -Ti3 C2 Tx composite electrode demonstrated excellent specific capacitance of 598 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1 , showcasing remarkable rate capability, and maintaining a better capacitance retention of 92.4 % over 10,000 consecutive cycles. The SEM images illustrated the presence of multilayer exfoliated structures, facilitating electrolyte penetration and creating an ion-conductive pathway within the electrode material. The exceptional electrochemical performance can be attributed to the composite's structural stability, substantial electroactive surface area (198 m2 g−1 ), and enhanced electron/ion transport facilitated by the multivalent oxidation states of Mn and Mo ions. This research establishes a significant foundation for further exploration into energy storage devices. CRediT authorship contribution statement P. Sivaharini: Conceptualization, Investigation, Methodology, Validation, Writing – original draft. J. Vigneshwaran: Formal analysis, Validation. Sujin P. Jose: Conceptualization, Formal analysis,
abstract: The storage of massive amounts of energy is a major obstacle to the production of electricity and scientists have been searching for ways to store energy and boost the efficiency. A Manganese molybdenum oxide/Titanium Carbide (MnMoO4-Ti3C2TX) composite was successfully synthesized using a one-pot facile hydrothermal method. The structural, morphological, and textural properties of the as-synthesized composite were analyzed through X-ray diffraction (XRD), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Fourier Transform infrared (FTIR), Energy Dispersive X-Ray Analysis (EDX), and Brunauer Emmett Teller (BET) studies. The phase purity of MnMoO4-Ti3C2TX was confirmed through XRD analysis and the formation of exfoliated Ti3C2TX in the composite is evident from the accordion-like structure observed in SEM images. The capacitance behavior of the MnMoO4-Ti3C2TX composite was demonstrated through cyclic voltammetry (CV), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD) studies. Significantly, the specific capacitance of the composite was determined to be 598 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 in 1 M KOH and a cycling stability of 92.4 % even after 10,000 cycles at a constant current density of 3 A g−1. This work highlights the supercapacitive behavior of the MXene-metal oxide composite, suggesting its potential use as electrode material for supercapacitors.

title: High-performance hybrid supercapacitors based on MXene/SnS2/CNT composites on nickel foam electrodes
authors: Chii-Rong Yang, Yang-Yi Lin, Ching-Tang Lin, Shih-Feng Tseng
conclusion: This study prepared MXene/SnS2 /CNT composites using a hydrothermal method for high-performance hybrid supercapacitors as a positive electrode. After the characteristic analysis, the MXene/SnS2 /CNT composites had a large specific surface area and the lamellar microstructures could provide more active sites for electrolyte adsorption, which was beneficial for the electrochemical performance of the supercapacitor. The electrochemical performance of MXene/SnS2 /CNT was better than that of MXene, SnS2 , and MXene/SnS2 . abstract: This research proposed the synthesized MXene/SnS2/CNT composites using a one-step hydrothermal method as the positive electrode for the hybrid supercapacitor (HSC). The MXene/SnS2/CNT composites provided high active sites and had the lowest charge transfer resistance of 2.2 Ω and charge transfer resistance of 4.48 Ω. Hence, a high specific capacitance (Cs) of 1049 F/g could be obtained at a current density of 1 A/g. The Cs of MXene/SnS2/CNT at a current density of 1 A/g was 10.27, 2.6, and 1.36 times higher than that of MXene (105.37 F/g), SnS2 (410.53 F/g), and MXene/SnS2 (771.03 F/g), respectively. This indicated that MXene/SnS2/CNT had excellent capacitance performance. When the current density was increased to 10 A/g, MXene/SnS2/CNT could still maintain a rate capability of 71 %. The Cs values of HSC at current densities of 3 and 5 A/g were 79 and 61 F/g, respectively, which were a good rate capability of 69 and 53 % compared to the Cs value of 114 F/g at a current density of 1 A/g. Furthermore, the HSC exhibited a high power density of 7020 W/kg at a low energy density of 11.7 Wh/kg. In this study, the developed HSCs were used for LEDs lighting and computer driving.

title: High performance asymmetric supercapacitors based on Ti3C2Tx MXene and electrodeposited spinel NiCo2S4 nanostructures††Electronic supplementary information (ESI) available. See DOI: 10.1039/d2ra00991a
authors: Mansi Pathak, S. R. Polaki, Chandra Sekhar Rout
error: Could not extract conclusion using any method
abstract: ABSTRACT Spinel metal sulfides have been investigated for a wide range of applications mostly in electrochemical energy storage owing to their better electronic conductivity and high reversible redox activity. Herein, we report a facile fabrication approach for the binder-free supercapacitor electrodes based on spinel NiCo2S4 (NCS) on various substrates such as Cu-foil (CF), Ni-foam (NF), and vertical graphene nanosheets grown on carbon tape (VG) via a single step-controlled electrodeposition technique. The obtained electrodeposited NiCo2S4 grown on Cu-foil (denoted as CF-NCS) in symmetric assembly shows a high specific capacitance of 167.28 F g−1 compared to NCS grown on Ni-foam and VG substrates, whereas, symmetric NiCo2S4 grown on a VG substrate device exhibits better cycling performance (81% for 3000 cycles) compared to CF-NCS and NF-NCS. Furthermore, an asymmetric supercapacitor was assembled in combination with MXene (Ti3C2Tx) as a negative electrode (denoted as TCX). As a result, the CF-NCS//TCX device exhibits a high areal capacitance of 48.6 mF cm−2 at 2 mA cm−2 of current density. We also report good specific capacitance of 54.57 F g−1 at 2 A g−1; in addition, the CF-NCS//TCX assembly delivers maximum areal and gravimetric energy density of 14.86 mWh cm−2 and 14.86 Wh kg−1 respectively. In contrast, the VG-NCS//TCX device showed improved cycling stability with 85% of capacitance retention over 5000 cycles owing to its highly porous structure and multiple conductive networks in the VG substrate and provides structural stability to NCS with fast ion diffusion. This experiment favors 2D MXene as a capacitive electrode that provides a replacement for carbon-based electrodes in asymmetric assembly with superior electrochemical performance. Hence, the hierarchical NCS structure grown on the various substrates in combination with MXene serve as a promising material for energy storage application.

title: Ultra-broadband perfect light absorber based on circular truncated cone structure Ti3C2Tx MXene across the visible to near-infrared region
authors: Bingzhen Li, Qingqing Wu, Fangyuan Li, Yan Li, Xiao Zhou, Songlin Yu, Wangjun Ren, Jijun Wang
conclusion: In conclusion, we have introduced an ultra-broadband and wide-angle PLA for the solar energy harvesting. This innovative PLA is constructed from a periodic array of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene-based CTC structures adhered to a Ti3 C2 Tx MXene substrate. Our PLA boasts an average near-unity absorbance of over 99 % across the 280 - 1623 nm, with a remarkable relative bandwidth of 141.1 %. This exceptional performance is attributed to the excitation of multiple high-order guided modes, the LSPR mode, and the efficient coupling between adjacent CTC structures. Furthermore, the inherent lossy nature of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene plays a pivotal role in enhancing the ultra-broadband absorption, as evidenced by simulated power flow and loss density distributions within the unit cell. Notably, our PLA is polarization-agnostic and maintains high absorption (over 99.5 %) across a wide range of incident angles (up to 50° ) for TE and TM modes. Additionally, its resilience against various materials underscores its versatility in design and fabrication. Our rigorous optical simulations confirm the successful implementation of this PLA, achieving a practical solar energy absorption efficiency of 99.38 %. Given its outstanding performance, we anticipate that our work will significantly contribute to the development and practical deployment of advanced thermal emitters, solar energy collectors, and thermophotovoltaic systems. Disclosures The authors declare no conflicts of interest. CRediT authorship contribution statement Bingzhen Li: Writing – original draft, Visualization, Validation, Methodology, Investigation,
abstract: Broadband perfect light absorbers (PLAs) are critical for advancing technologies such as stealth systems, thermal photovoltaics, and optical imaging, where efficient, spectrum-wide light absorption is essential. Here, we propose a novel, low-cost PLA design featuring a circular truncated cone (CTC) nanostructure composed of Ti₃C₂Tx MXene. Finite element method (FEM) simulations reveal exceptional performance, with over 99.5 % average absorbance across 280–1623 nm and a 141.1 % relative bandwidth, validated by equivalent circuit modeling (ECM). This efficiency stems from synergistic interactions between guided mode excitation, localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs), and intrinsic losses within the CTC geometry. The design maintains >99 % absorption, exhibiting polarization- and angle-insensitivity for transverse electric/magnetic modes, while geometric tunability enables customization for diverse applications, including solar harvesting, thermoelectrics, and thermal imaging. This work advances PLA technology by delivering ultra-broadband, robust, and adaptable absorption, addressing key limitations in existing designs.

title: MoSe2 nanosheets anchored on Ti3C2 MXene hybrid nanostructure for boosting electrochemical performance of supercapacitor
authors: Nagaraju Macherla, Manjula Nerella, Ravindranadh Koutavarapu, Jaesool Shim
conclusion: This work reports the successful synthesis of an optimized MoSe2 /e-Ti3 C2 Tx MXene hybrid nanostructure for supercapacitor applications with high performance. Careful optimization of synthesis parameters like % HF (60 %) for the synthesis of Ti3 C2 Tx and hydrothermal reaction time of 18 h for MoSe2 , proved that synthesis parameters are important to achieve improved structural robustness along with electrochemical behavior. MoSe2 /e-Ti3 C2 Tx showed a specific capacity of 259 C g−1 at a current density of 0.5 A g−1 with excellent cycling stability, retaining 96.6 % capacitance after 5000 cycles. In addition, the supercapacitor fabricated with MoSe2 /e-Ti3 C2 Tx hybrid nanostructure delivered a maximum energy density of 12.92 Wh kg−1 with power density of 1001.02 W kg−1 , retained 80 % it's capacity after 5000 cycles at 8 A g−1 . The remarkable performance of MoSe2 /e-Ti3 C2 Tx hybrid nanostructure over pure MoSe2 is due to the growth of MoSe2 nanosheets on the stacked layers of MXene and the strong interfacial interaction by forming covalent bonding with MXene. The results obtained bring into focus the paramount importance of tuning parameters in the development of advanced materials for energy storage. abstract: The significant advancements in supercapacitor technology promote the hunt for developing innovative electrode materials with enhanced electrochemical properties. This study delves into the comprehensive study of expanded MXene layers (e-Ti3C2Tx) decorated with flower-like MoSe2 nanosheets (MoSe2/e-Ti3C2Tx) with a straightforward hydrothermal method by optimizing synthesis parameters (HF%, hydrothermal reaction time). XRD, FESEM, and XPS results revealed that MoSe2 nanosheets are successfully anchored on MXene layers and developed strong interstitial contact. The electrochemical analysis demonstrated significant enhanced energy storage capacity along with promising cycle life for heterojunction MoSe2/e-Ti3C2Tx hybrid nanostructured electrode. The MoSe2/e-Ti3C2Tx hybrid nanostructured electrode delivered a specific capacity of 259 C g−1 at a current density of 0.5 A g−1, whereas MoSe2 delivered only 184 C g−1. In particular, hybrid nanostructure electrodes exhibited excellent cycle life (96.6 % after 5000 cycles). Moreover, the supercapacitor device assembled with the MoSe2/e-Ti3C2Tx hybrid nanostructure delivered a maximum energy density of 12.92 Wh kg−1 with power density of 1001.02 W kg−1,and retained 80 % of it's capacity after 5000 cycles at 8 A g−1. The enhanced properties of MoSe2/e-Ti3C2Tx hybrid nanostructure clearly reveals its promising application for the advanced supercapacitor.

title: In-situ preparation of a fluorine-free MXene/MnO2 composite for enhancing performance of supercapacitor
authors: Huifang Zhang, Jie Wang, Xiaohong Song, Mingqiang Liu, Kefeng Xie
conclusion: The fluorine-free Ti3 C2 Tx /MnO2 composite was synthesized in-situ using a high concentration of NaOH with KMnO4 . This method avoids the use of hazardous HF acid, making it both safe and environmentally friendly. When utilized as an electrode material for supercapacitors, this composite demonstrates impressive properties, including high specific capacitance, favorable CV characteristics, and outstanding rate capability. In this composite, MnO2 nanoparticles are evenly dispersed on the surface and within the interlayers of Ti3 C2 Tx , effectively increasing the material's specific surface area and mitigating the layer-stacking effect. Moreover, the in-situ generated MnO2 exhibits stronger binding forces and closer adsorption compared to subsequently reloaded MnO2 .Within the potential range of – 0.6 to 0.2 V, the composite achieves a peak specific capacitance of 182.75 F/g. Notably, after undergoing 10,000 charge-discharge cycles, the material retains 85.65 % of its initial capacitance, showcasing exceptional durability and stability. The DFT calculation demonstrated that the heterojunction exhibits superior electrical properties compared to the individual components, MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx . This study introduces an innovative approach for the environmentally friendly and efficient synthesis of MXene-based composites. Xiaohong Song: Software. Mingqiang Liu: Visualization, Data curation. Kefeng Xie: Writing – review & editing, Supervision, Conceptualization.
abstract: MXene (Ti3C2Tx) is a promising electrode material for supercapacitors due to its excellent conductivity, high specific surface area, and strong hydrophilicity. However, traditional MXene preparation methods often rely on hazardous hydrofluoric (HF) acid, posing safety risks and environmental concerns. In this study, a fluorine-free MXene synthesis method was developed using a high-concentration NaOH solution combined with KMnO4 as an etchant. MnO2 was incorporated into Ti3C2Tx layers via redox reactions, forming an interlayer structure that effectively inhibits restacking of the in-situ generated Ti3C2Tx nanosheets. Acting as a conductive substrate, Ti3C2Tx facilitates rapid electron transfer and mitigates MnO2 vol expansion during charge-discharge cycles. The resulting Ti3C2Tx/MnO2-based supercapacitor demonstrated a high specific capacitance of 182.75 F/g and maintained 85.65 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations further revealed that the Ti3C2Tx/MnO2 heterojunction enhances electron transport efficiency. The synergistic interaction between MnO2 and Ti3C2Tx not only improves the overall conductivity but also significantly boosts energy storage capacity. This work presents an environmentally sustainable approach for fabricating high-performance supercapacitors.

title: Defect passivation and transformation of Ti3C2Tx MXene hollow microsphere for superior electrochemical performance and sodium-ions storage
authors: Ningning Liu, Xiaochen Zhang, Jinfeng Chen, Fei Yu, Jie Ma
conclusion: In summary, 3D porous Ti3 C2 Tx MXene hollow microsphere doped with N, S and V atoms (N, S, V-MHM) has been rationally designed and used as the cathode material for electrochemical Na+ capture in CDI. DFT calculation and characterizations revealed that N and S atom doping can replace the unstable end groups of Ti3 C2 Tx (−F and −OH) and cap the oxidizable edge, and the Ti vacancy defects can be passivated through V atom doping. The vacancy defect passivation and heteroatomic doping defect transformation leads to the regulation of electronic structure and generation of active sites in the lattice structure, improving of chemical stability and electrochemical capacity of N, S, V-MHM. The 3D hollow structure accelerates the charge/mass transfer and mitigates volume expansion during ion insertion/expulsion of MXene, which further modifies the intercalation pseudocapacitance kinetics and structure stability. The obtained N, S, V-MHM electrode displays high ions adsorption capacity (141.77 mg g−1 at 1.2 V for 60 min) and long-term cycling stability (≈94.6% capacitance retention after 215 salt adsorption/desorption cycles). The in situ EQCM-D test indicates that hydrated Na+ dominated counter-ion adsorption play a key role during the charge and discharge process. This study contributes to the development of electrochemically stable MXene-based electrode with balanced high-capacity performance by passivating defects and transforming strategy through heteroatom doping. Compliance with ethics requirements This article does not contain any studies with human or animal subjects . abstract: The commercialization of MXene-based electrodes for sodium ion capture in aqueous solutions is limited by poor stability, which is attributed to edge and surface defects. In this study, 3D Ti3C2Tx MXene hollow microsphere (MHM) is constructed, and a systematic defect passivation and transformation approach is presented to achieve the high stability of MHM when employed as electrode material in capacitive desalination (CDI). Metal atom vanadium (V) and non-metal atoms nitrogen (N) and sulfur (S) are meticulously selected to modulate the defect environment of Ti3C2Tx MXene. The doping mechanism is thoroughly investigated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and density functional theory (DFT) analysis for the first time: N and S atoms substitute the carbon and replace oxidizable surface groups, V atom bonds with carbon and oxygen and is trapped by Ti vacancy defects. This approach effectively passivates the oxidizable defects and transforms them into new heteroatomic doping defects, leading to the regulation of electronic structure and creation of additional active sites, which enhances stability and sodium capture efficiency for CDI. The optimized N, S, and V co-doped MHM (N, S, V-MHM) electrode shows high electrosorption capacity and rate (141.77 mg g−1 and 2.36 mg g−1 min−1 at 1.2 V) with outstanding cycling stability. In situ EQCM-D measurement underscores the critical role of hydrated sodium ions de/adsorption during charging/discharging processes. This work elucidates a pathway for constructing high-performance and ultra-stable MXene-based electrodes through defect passivation and transformation.

title: Flexible electrode based on multi-scaled MXene (Ti3C2Tx) for supercapacitors
authors: Xuefeng Zhang, Yong Liu, Shangli Dong, Jianqun Yang, Xudong Liu
conclusion: In this contribution, we synthesized a flexible electrode based on multi-scaled Ti3 C2 Tx through vacuum filtration of the mixture of Ti3 C2 Tx nanoparticles prepared by HF etching and the Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets obtained by a HCl + LiF method. The Ti3 C2 Tx nanoparticles existing between Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets can play an effective role in preventing the self-restacking of nanosheets, providing more unimpeded channels for electrolyte ions access, and ensuring high-rate performance. On the other hand, the Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets act as conducting “bridges” and connect the Ti3 C2 Tx nanoparticles, facilitating electron transfer during the charge-discharge process. Although the specific capacitance of the prepared flexible electrode based on multi-scaled MXene is higher than that of the reported MXenes composites, and graphenes composites, but it is still slightly lower than that of the surface modified MXene films and N-doped MXene electrodes [6 ,34 ,35 ]. However, this work provides a new strategy for design and development of other MXenes-based materials with high specific capacitance performance for the flexible and highly integrated supercapacitors. Acknowledgement This work was supported by the Opening Fund of Key Laboratory of Harbin Institute of Technology .
abstract: MXenes is one of the most promising flexible electrode materials for supercapacitor. However, the nanosheets in the MXenes electrode by vacuum filtration are prone to restack during preparation, which largely hinders the full utilization of their surfaces and active sites. In this contribution, the self-restacking of MXene nanosheets (prepared by etching with HCl + LiF) could be prevented effectively by introducing MXene nanoparticles (prepared by etching with HF) as interlayer spacers. The Ti3C2Tx-10 flexible (the electrode with 10% mass fraction nanoparticles) exhibits an excellent specific capacitance of 372 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 which is much higher than that of Ti3C2Tx film, and an impressive cycling stability up to 95% capacitance retention after 5000 cycles. The significant improvement in electrochemical performance is mainly due to that the open sandwich-like structure of the flexible electrode based on multi-scaled Ti3C2Tx provides huge surface area and more active sites.

title: Hydrothermal synthesis of layered NiS2/Ti3C2Tx composite electrode for supercapacitors
authors: Lijun Si, Qixun Xia, Keke Liu, Wen Guo, Nanasaheb Shinde, Libo Wang, Qianku Hu, Aiguo Zhou
conclusion: In this research, a NiS2 /Ti3 C2 Tx MXene composite was effectively made by combining k negatively charged Ti3 C2 Tx nanoplates with positively charged NiS2 nanocubes via hydrothermal technique. As expected, the generated NiS2 /Ti3 C2 Tx composites produced exhibit desirable performances for use in supercapacitors with high capacity and good cycling stability. When combined with a Ti3 C2 Tx MXene negative electrode to form an ASC device, the NiS2 /Ti3 C2 Tx //Ti3 C2 Tx ASC device delivers an energy density of 15.4 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 351.6 W kg−1 . The processing of many other low-dimensional materials for a wide range of applications in energy storage, catalysis, gas sensors, and solar cells could be aided by this 2D/3D heterostructure design. CRediT authorship contribution statement Lijun Si: Methodology, Software, Investigation, Writing – original draft. Qixun Xia: Conceptualization, Data curation,
abstract: MXene shows potential to be used as electrodes in energy storage devices due to its unusual layered structure. MXene-based electrodes can store high rate faradaic pseudocapacitive energy because of their high surface area, metallic conductivity, thermal/chemical stability, and quick surface redox reactions. We present a hierarchy of NiS2/MXene nanohybrids made using a simple and low cost hydrothermal method. The strong interfacial connection and good electronic coupling between the NiS2 nanocube and MXene nanoplates improve structural stability and electrical conductivity as well as the electrolyte ion diffusion kinetics. Therefore, the obtained battery-type NiS2/MXene composite electrodes delivered 72.0 mAh g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1 with high cycle stability in 1 M KOH electrolyte, and the fabricated asymmetric supercapacitor (ACS) demonstrates energy densities of 15.4 Wh kg−1 at power density of 351.6 W kg−1. It elucidates the mechanism and strategy for the development of MXene-based nanohybrid materials for electrochemical energy storage devices.

title: Facile synthesis of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets using aryl diazonium tetrafluoroborate for multiple applications
authors: Bibek Chaw pattnayak, Niranjan Panda, Sasmita Mohapatra
conclusion: A new method has been developed to produce high-quality Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanosheets using an easy, one-step HF-free sonochemical method. The delaminated MXene nanosheets exhibit excellent stability even after 30 days. Additionally, the MXene shows superior photothermal performance with a conversion efficiency of 59 %. Moreover, the MXene electrode demonstrates the highest specific capacitance of 1133 F/g at a current density of 1 A/g, which is much higher than that reported in recent literature. Furthermore, the obtained MXene electrode shows a specific capacitance retention of 91 % even after 10,000 GCD cycles. Overall, these Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanosheets synthesized using the HF-free one-step sonochemical method with 4-CBDF etchant show versatile application potential in photothermal therapy and energy storage, and may attract further research interest. Supportive information Calculation of photothermal conversion efficiency, 1H NMR and HRMS plot of 4-CHDF, Elemental mapping, Raman spectra, TEM image, XPS spectra, temp change vs time plot for MXene Ti3C2Tx. CRediT authorship contribution statement Bibek Chaw pattnayak: Writing – original draft, Investigation, Formal analysis, Data curation. Niranjan Panda: Methodology. Sasmita Mohapatra: Writing – review & editing, Supervision, Project administration,
abstract: The development of an HF-free and environmentally benign method for etching the middle aluminum layer (Al) from the Ti3AlC2-MAX phase is a challenging task in titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) MXene synthesis. Herein, we designed a diazonium salt-based ultrasonic method to prepare MXene. We have explored 4-carboxy benzene diazonium tetrafluoroborate (4-CBDF) as a delaminating agent, which can dissolve the Al layer directly from the MAX phase. 4-carboxy benzene diazonium (4-CBD+) ion promotes the intercalation as well as exfoliation simultaneously during the etching of the MAX phase and directly results in Ti3C2Txnanosheets without undergoing any additional delamination process. Synthesized MXene nanosheets show excellent photothermal performance with a conversion efficiency of 59 %. This MXene-coated GC electrode exhibits the highest capacitance of 1133 F/g at a current density 1 A/g, which maintains a retention capacitance of 91% even after 10,000 GCD cycles. The present method provides a fundamental insight into the development of MXene-based next-generation photothermal materials and supercapacitors.

title: Hydrothermal synthesis of MoS2/MXene composites for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Jung-Jie Huang, Yu-Wu Wang, Yu-Jie Lin, Yu-Xuan Zhang
conclusion: This study used an MXene framework to mitigate the restacking and agglomeration of MoS2 in the electrodes of capacitors. Through hydrothermal synthesis, MoS2 was grown on MXene base to create MoS2 /MXene heterostructure materials. Ultrasonic spray coating was employed to fabricate MoS2 /MXene electrodes, thereby ensuring the uniformity and quality of the materials. The structural advantages of MXene effectively prevented the restacking of MoS2 , which enabled the electrodes to maintain favorable dispersion and high overall capacitive performance. The electrochemical performance and stability of MoS2 /MXene were investigated under different (NH4 )6 Mo7 O24 ·4H2 O:C2 H5 NS concentration ratios. Among MoS2 /MXene electrodes prepared under different (NH4 )6 Mo7 O24 ·4H2 O:C2 H5 NS concentration ratios, the electrode prepared under a concentration ratio of 0.04:0.4 M exhibited the optimal electrochemical performance and stability. Therefore, the capacitive performance of MoS2 /MXene electrodes prepared under the aforementioned concentration ratio and subjected to different annealing temperatures was examined. Among the MoS2 /MXene electrodes annealed at various temperatures, that annealed at 850 °C had the optimal performance. At 850 °C, MoS2 transitioned from a 1 T/2H mixed phase to a more stable 2H phase; thus, the electrode annealed at this temperature exhibited higher crystallinity than did the electrodes annealed at different temperatures. Moreover, it exhibited the highest specific capacitance among the electrodes. The specific capacitance of the MoS2 /MXene electrode annealed at 850 °C (88.00 F/g) was approximately 1.46 times higher than that of an unannealed MoS2 /MXene electrode (60.41 F/g). Thus, the MoS2 /MXene electrode annealed at 850 °C had high charge storage capacity and excellent electrochemical performance. Furthermore, after 15000 charge–discharge cycles at a high current density of 20 A/g, the capacitance retention of the aforementioned electrode remained 100 %, which indicated its exceptional long-term cycling stability, durability, and reliability. In summary, the results of this study confirmed that thermally annealed MoS2 /MXene composites are promising high-performance electrode materials for supercapacitors. abstract: This study explores the use of an MXene framework as a substrate for MoS2 nanomaterials in supercapacitor thin-film electrodes, tackling the issues of reduced specific capacitance and poor energy storage performance caused by MoS2 agglomeration. The results show that integrating MoS2 with the MXene base effectively reduces agglomeration, enhancing structural stability and conductivity. After annealing, the MoS2 phase shifted from a mixed 1 T/2H to a more stable 2H phase, optimizing the composition and increasing crystallinity. Consequently, the specific capacitance of the MoS2/MXene electrode rose from 60.41 to 88.00 F/g, representing a 1.46-fold improvement in electrochemical performance. Notably, after 15,000 charge–discharge cycles, the electrode retained 100 % of its capacitance, demonstrating outstanding cycling stability. Overall, the findings confirm the high electrochemical reversibility and long-term stability of MoS2/MXene composites, positioning them as promising candidates for advanced energy storage applications.

title: High-performance supercapacitor based on 3D Ti3C2Tx electrodes and sulfonated lignin gel electrolyte
authors: Jiabei Li, Tursun Abdiryim, Ruxangul Jamal, Kai Song, Hongtao Yang, Jiachang Liu, Yanqiang Zhou, Guoliang Zhang, Wenjing Zhang, Jinglei Chen
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: the studied HSC device exhibits good flexible electrochemical performance, with minimal changes in specific capacitance at different bending angles, indicating high mechanical stability. This makes the device highly promising for potential integration into flexible energy storage solutions and wearable electronic applications. 4 Conclusion In this study, a dual innovation in the flexible energy storage field was achieved through the development of CoNi-OH/3D Ti3 C2 Tx hybrid electrodes and sulfonated lignin (SL)-based double crosslinked gel electrolytes, addressing a key challenge in supercapacitor performance and scalability. By using polystyrene (PS) nanospheres as templates, Ti3 C2 Tx was transformed from a two-dimensional lamellar structure into a hollow spherical three-dimensional network, leading to a several-fold increase in specific surface area, suppression of self-stacking, accelerated ionic diffusion, and enhanced electrochemical active sites. The specific capacitance of the CoNi-OH/3D Ti3 C2 Tx hybrid electrode reaches an astonishing 2020 ± 50 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 . The SL-doped PEDOT/SL/PAM/ KOH gel electrolyte exhibits high ionic conductivity (2.83 ± 0.2 S m−1 ), mechanical flexibility (elongation at break: 995 % ± 60 %), and uniform cross-linking. HSC devices assembled with these components demonstrate a favorable energy density (87 Wh kg−1 ) and power density (750 W kg−1 ) with excellent stability, 99.5 % ± 0.1 % coulombic efficiency and 83.7 % ± 0.2 % capacity retention after 7000 cycles at 3 A g−1 . The material also exhibits excellent flexibility and maintains stable electrochemical performance under various bending angles. The great potential of CoNi-OH/3D Ti3 C2 Tx electrodes and PEDOT/SL gel electrolytes for flexible energy storage applications provides valuable insights into the future development of this field. This study not only achieved a breakthrough in the performance of flexible supercapacitors, but also provided a biomass-derived electrolyte design strategy and MXene morphology engineering paradigm that can be generalized to other energy storage systems. Tursun Abdiryim: Writing – review & editing, Supervision, Software, Resources, Project administration,
abstract: Supercapacitors are highly efficient energy storage systems. The electrode substances and electrolytes, which form their primary components, are key areas of research for scientists. In this study, the transition metal material Ti3C2Tx and Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT)-based polyacrylamide dual-crosslinked network polymers with good conductivity are selected as the cathode material and gel electrolyte, respectively. To address issues such as self-aggregation of Ti3C2Tx during use, insufficient energy density, and poor dispersibility of 3,4-Ethylenedioxythiophene (EDOT) during the preparation of the hydrogel, polystyrene nanospheres are first used as templates to convert Ti3C2Tx from a two-dimensional sheet to a three-dimensional spherical structure, followed by the introduction of bimetallic cobalt–nickel hydroxide (CoNi-OH) to effectively enhance its performance. In addition, sulfonated lignin (SL) is incorporated into the hydrogel to improve the dispersibility of PEDOT in water-based solvents, promoting the development of a uniform hydrogel. The results show that the fabricated composite CoNi-OH/3D Ti3C2Tx exhibits a specific capacitance of up to 2020 ± 50F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1. The assembled asymmetric supercapacitor demonstrates a specific capacitance of 278.3 ± 30F g−1. At a power density of 750 W kg−1, it exhibits an energy density of 87 Wh kg−1. After 7,000 cycles of testing, the device shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.4 % ± 0.1 % and maintains 83.7 % ± 0.2 % of its initial capacitance at a current density of 3 A g−1. These findings indicate that the CoNi-OH/3D Ti3C2Tx electrodes and PEDOT/SL gel electrolytes have significant potential for development in the energy storage field.

title: High-performance Zn-ion hybrid supercapacitor based on 3D K+-intercalated Ti3C2TX hydrogel cathode
authors: Haiping Wang, Xingyu Wang, Xinmiao Liu, Shuwei Zhang, Shutong Meng, Wenjie Yan, Xin Zhang, Zhansheng Lu, Zenghui Qiu, Haijun Xu, Jiaqi He
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  K + intercalation of Ti 3 C 2 T X inhibits the self-stacking of MXene material due to interlayer van der Waals forces, thus enlarging the layer spacing and achieving fast zinc ion diffusion kinetics; and the reduction of the intercalated Ti 3 C 2 T X with GO by ascorbic acid generates a RGO hydrogel in a composite 3D system, which further contributes to the fast zinc ion diffusion kinetics. The use of this material in the cathode for ZHSCs results in excellent electrochemical performance, which feature a high specific capacitance of 253.86 F g −1 at a current density of 1 A g −1 and an impressive energy density of 141.03 Wh kg −1 at 999.99 W kg −1 . Notably, after 5000 charge-discharge cycles at a current density of 10 A g −1 , the ZHSC maintained a capacitance retention rate above 87.96 %, highlighting its exceptional cycling stability. Our study provides robust evidence that 3D K + -Ti 3 C 2 T X -RGO integration endows ZHSCs with exceptional electrochemical properties. This finding holds profound significance for advancing the development of ZHSCs. Furthermore, our research findings address the inherent limitations of MXene and offer valuable insights that could inspire novel avenues for exploring the energy storage applications of MXene.
abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion hybrid supercapacitors (ZHSCs) exhibit great potential for energy storage and conversion devices, owing to their inherent safety and cost-effectiveness. Nevertheless, the structure of traditional porous carbon cathodes hinders the zinc-ion diffusion kinetics, rendering the energy densities of conventional ZHSCs uncompetitive and severely impeding their practical applications. 2D transition metal carbides/nitrides, known as MXenes, exhibit excellent conductivity and abundant surface functional groups, qualifying them as ideal candidates for constructing high-capacity cathodes in high-performance ZHSCs. This study presents the fabrication of a ZHSC utilizing 3D porous K+-intercalated Ti3C2TX-reduced graphene oxide (K+-Ti3C2TX-RGO) hydrogel as cathode, paired with a zinc foil as anode. Upon treatment with KOH solution, Ti3C2TX undergoes K+ ion intercalation into its nanosheets, resulting in partial elimination of terminal -F groups and expansion of the MXene interlayer spacing. Subsequently, large-scale graphene oxide (GO) was employed as a conductive binder to interconnect the intercalated multilayer Ti3C2TX, and a reducing agent was incorporated to facilitate self-assembly into a hydrogel. This approach augmented the accessibility of ions and facilitated their transport within the resultant structure. The ZHSC, fabricated with this composite cathode, synergistically integrates the supercapacitor’s high-power density and the battery’s high energy density. The results indicate that the ZHSC exhibited excellent electrochemical performance, featuring a high specific capacitance of 253.86 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and an impressive energy density of 141.03 Wh kg−1 at 999.99 W kg−1. Notably, after 5000 charge-discharge cycles at 10 A g−1, the ZHSC maintained a capacitance retention rate above 87.96 %, highlighting its exceptional cycling stability.

title: ZIF-8/ Co-C3N4-GNR/MXene nanocomposites: A novel electrode material with excellent electrochemical properties for supercapacitors
authors: Rozhin Darabi, Mehdi Shabani-Nooshabadi
conclusion: In summary, the ZIF-8/Co-C₃N₄-GNR/MXene/NF nanocomposite exhibited a maximum specific capacitance of 1125 F·g⁻¹ . It also demonstrated excellent cyclic stability, retaining 87 % of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles. The outstanding electrochemical performance of the ZIF-8/Co-C₃N₄-GNR/MXene/NF electrode is primarily attributed to its porous nanostructure, high conductivity, and large surface area, which provide abundant active sites for charge storage. These findings suggest that the NF/ZIF-8/Co-C₃N₄-GNR/MXene//AC/NF device holds strong potential for enhancing performance in energy storage applications. CRediT authorship contribution statement Rozhin Darabi: Writing – original draft, Investigation. Mehdi Shabani-Nooshabadi: Writing – review & editing, Supervision.
abstract: The combination of MXenes with metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), along with the incorporation of graphene nanoribbons (GNRs), results in highly promising materials for energy storage applications. Owing to their unique structure, high porosity, and strong interfacial connectivity, these composites exhibit excellent mechanical stability and enable rapid ion and electron transport. The synergistic integration of MXenes, MOFs, and GNRs with the excellent electrical conductivity and 2D structure of MXenes, high porosity and tunable surface area of MOFs, and the mechanical strength and flexibility of GNRs, provides the composite with a high surface area, excellent electrical conductivity, and robust structural stability. In this study, we report a multi-component nanocomposite, ZIF-8/Co-C₃N₄-GNR/MXene, synthesized using a simple method. Key factors influencing capacitance, power density, and energy density were optimized to achieve superior electrochemical performance. According to our knowledge, this is the first synthesis of this specific composite structure, offering strong potential for advanced supercapacitor design. Electrochemical performance was evaluated using cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The ZIF-8/Co-C₃N₄-GNR/MXene composite demonstrated a high specific capacitance of 1125 F·g⁻¹ at a current density of 1 A·g⁻¹ , with an energy density of 100 Wh·kg⁻¹ and a power density of 400 W·kg⁻¹ . Furthermore, it maintained approximately 87 % of its initial capacitance after 10,000 cycles, highlighting the nanocomposite's strong potential as an electrode material for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitors and its suitability for next-generation electronic devices.

title: Review: 2D MXenes based electrochemical sensors and supercapacitors for biomedical and energy storage applications
authors: Sourav Karmakar, Anuprava Mandal, Naresh Kumar Mani, Rinky Sha
conclusion: 6  Conclusion & future outlook  MXenes similar to graphene have recently attracted a significant attention among research communities because of their promising physico-chemical, and electronic characteristics, which position them as a possible substitute for graphene. With a focus on sensing performances, including sensitivity, LOD, selectivity, stability, linearity, dynamic range, and their viability in real samples, this review provides a comprehensive analysis of the various methods that MXenes are synthesized as well as the latest advancements in electrochemical biosensors that are designed to detect a variety of biomarkers. The impressive metallic conductivities, vast surface area, diverse composition, and remarkable hydrophilicity make these materials useful for developing electrochemical sensing devices. Consequently, there is a promising outlook for their use as sensitive electrochemical sensors in detecting a wide range of analytes. Although there has been notable advancement, the domain still faces numerous obstacles to overcome for the successful commercialization of MXene-based electrochemical biosensors, which can be outlined as follows:   (1)  Limited resistance to oxidation: the process of MXenes oxidizing in oxygen-rich solvents. (2) Scalability in synthesis presents challenges, particularly in achieving commercial-scale production. The environmental hazards associated with HF necessitate the exploration of alternative, milder etchants such as LiF/HCl. In recent years, less harmful and environmentally friendly etching techniques such as H 3 PO 4 , DES, and TBAOH have been introduced to alleviate the problem.    (3)  Irregular surface termination and absence of fluorine: it is essential to steer clear of random functionalization of the MXene surface by employing a different approach than the traditional HF-based etching method. Additionally, the presence of fluorine on the MXenes' surface hinders their use in biomedical applications and the immobilization of biomarkers.    (4)  Surface imperfections: the process of delaminating MXene through ultrasonication can lead to the formation of surface imperfections that may alter the distinctive physiochemical properties of MXenes. Moreover, addressing the technological hurdles is crucial for the successful advancement of electrochemical biosensors into commercial applications.     The upcoming sensors must prioritize the followings:   (1)  broadening of sensing devices to encompass a diverse array of biomarkers through simultaneous non-invasive immunoassays, enabling the monitoring of individuals' health at the molecular level.    (2)  the development of secure and dependable biosensing diagnostic platforms that leverage valuable insights from population studies and their correlation to blood-based clinical assays. This area is anticipated to evolve over time with significant advancements in production, processing, electrochemical conversion, and integration.     Further, this review highlights the various MXenes based electrodes, including pristine MXenes, doped MXene, MXenes/carbonaceous nanocomposites, MXenes/transition metal oxide composites, MXenes/transition metal-dichalcogenides composites for the application of supercapacitors. The heteroatom doped MXenes and various MXenes composites exhibit better electrochemical performance and much suitable for practical applications due to its high specific surface area, high ionic and electronic conductivity, modified electronic structure, rich of active sites, enhanced inter-planar spacing, better chemical stability, improved operating voltage window, and prevention of the restacking problems of MXene nanosheets. As a result, the modified electrodes offered high specific capacitance, excellent cycling stability, and excellent rate capability. Despite the fact, that MXene-based electrodes showed remarkable progress as an energy storage device for supercapacitor applications they also faced various challenges. Therefore, further research in the field of sustainable energy storage should be done to overcome those challenges. Hereby, some future recommendations for supercapacitor applications are shortlisted.   1.  To enhance the electrochemical performance of pristine-MXenes, the surface chemistry of MXenes should be modified using appropriate synthesis process.    2.  Researchers should focus on the novel composite based MXenes to increase the energy density with high power density and prevent the restacking problem of MXene nanosheets and the electrodes should be engineered with defects and heteroatom doping to enhance the electrochemical performances.    3.  To explore the various properties of MXenes researchers should focus on the combined experimental and theoretical studies.    4.  Exploration of non-Ti-based MXenes, double-M MXenes, and double-X MXenes for the application of supercapacitors are also highly demanded.    5.  For better cycling stability, the degradation of material properties at the time of cycling should be carefully observed by material characterization techniques like in-situ XRD and Raman studies and should find out the root cause of capacitance degradation. Therefore, we can get an idea about the changes of the material properties during cycling and it can be resolved by modifying the synthesis techniques and other modifications.    6.  MXenes show promising performance in aqueous electrolytes but the limited potential window for aqueous electrolyte limits the electrode to achieve high energy density and the leakage of aqueous electrolyte restrict the practical applications of the devices. Therefore, the use of non-aqueous electrolytes and solid electrolytes are preferable.     Overall, the rigorous research in this area will enable 2D MXenes to overcome these obstacles for the practical applications. Therefore, this review is anticipated to have a significant influence on the investigation and development of 2D MXenes-based electrochemical sensors for use in supercapacitors and biomedical applications.
abstract: MXenes, composed of early transition metal carbides and/or nitrides, have become one of the most versatile two-dimensional materials. High metallic conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, rich surface functional groups, large specific surface area, good redox capabilities, hydrophilicity, high energy storage ability, layered structure for ion intercalations, and other remarkable properties have made MXenes increasingly popular in a range of scientific applications, including sensors and energy storage. A thorough analysis of the characteristics and synthesis routes of MXenes is presented, highlighting the importance of these approaches in tailoring MXene nanostructures for use in supercapacitors and sensing. The recent advancements in MXene-based electrochemical sensors for the detection of several vital biomolecules, such as glucose, ascorbic acid, uric acid, dopamine, microRNAs, l-methionine, melatonin, cortisol, etc., are fully inspected in this review paper with a focus on sensing performances, including sensitivity, limit of detection, selectivity, dynamic range, stability, linearity, and their viability in real samples. Further, this review highlights various MXenes based electrodes, including pristine MXenes, doped MXene, MXenes/carbonaceous nanocomposites, MXenes/transition metal oxide composites, MXenes/transition metal-dichalcogenides composites for the application of supercapacitors, emphasizing their usefulness in practical applications as well as their capacitive characteristics, including specific capacitance, cyclic stability, energy and power densities, and others. A deeper understanding of how MXenes is attributed to each supercapacitor is provided by discussing basic charge-storage mechanisms. The limitations of the current methods and the future outlooks of MXenes based electrochemical biosensors and MXenes based supercapacitors are also discussed where appropriate.

title: MnOx/Ti3C2Tx MXene/Carbon Nanofibers composite fiber film electrode with good flexibility derived by combining electrospinning technique with carbonization treatment
authors: Bingshan Kong, Chenji Xia, Xiaoqing Bin, Bowen Gao, Wenxiu Que
conclusion: The MnOx /Ti3 C2 Tx MXene/CNFs composite film electrode has been successfully prepared by an electrospinning technique and followed a carbonization treatment. By combining excellent pseudocapacitive MnO2 with high electrical conductivity CNT provides a high capacitance, while Ti3 C2 Tx MXene with good flexibility can effectively relieve the stress and strain during the carbonization treatment. Hence, the as-derived MMC/CNFs film electrode delivers an excellent specific capacitance of 211.57 F·g−1 at the scan rate of 2 mV·s−1 , cycling stability and mechanical property. This work provides a feasible approach for preparing MXene-based flexible fiber film electrode with good electrochemical performance. We state that the work described has not been published previously, it is not being considered for publication elsewhere, and its publication is approved by all authors and tacitly or explicitly by the responsible authorities where the work was carried out. CRediT authorship contribution statement Bingshan Kong: Writing – original draft, Investigation, Formal analysis. Chenji Xia: Writing – review & editing, Conceptualization. Xiaoqing Bin: Writing – review & editing. Bowen Gao: Writing – review & editing. Wenxiu Que: Writing – review & editing.
abstract: The restack of MXene nanosheets greatly affects its electrochemical performance and application, while electrospinning technique can spin two-dimensional MXene nanosheets into one-dimensional nanofibers, which can prevent the self-stacking of MXene nanosheets. Herein, MnOx/Ti3C2Tx MXene/CNFs (carbon nanofibers) composite fiber films with good flexibility were prepared by combining an electrospinning technique and a carbonization treatment, in which the pseudo capacitive material MnO2 mixed with carbon nanotube (CNT) was introduced into Ti3C2Tx MXene. The synergistic effect of MnOx, Ti3C2Tx MXene and CNFs improves the capacitance and flexibility of the composite fiber film, and the specific capacitance of the MnOx/Ti3C2Tx MXene/CNFs fiber film electrode delivers 211.57 F·g−1 at a scanning rate of 2 mV·s−1. After 3000 cycles at a current density of 5 A·g−1, it can still maintain 95% of the initial capacitance. The results indicate that the MnOx/Ti3C2Tx MXene/CNFs composite fiber films have great potential for flexible supercapacitors.

title: Few-layered Ti3C2Tx MXene synthesized via water-free etching toward high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Siqi Gong, Fan Zhao, Yaning Zhang, Huiting Xu, Meng Li, Junjie Qi, Honghai Wang, Zhiying Wang, Yuqi Hu, Xiaobin Fan, Wenchao Peng, Chunli Li, Jiapeng Liu
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: In conclusion, we report a novel water-free etching strategy for synthesizing few-layered Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes in deep eutectic solvents at near-ambient temperature. Benefiting from the absence of water and macromolecular structure of DES, the as-synthesized few-layered Ti3 C2 Tx (DES-Ti3 C2 Tx ) MXene presents abundant −O terminations and low oxidation degree. As a consequence, the DES-Ti3 C2 Tx MXene displays outstanding specific capacitance of 320 F/g at 2 mV/s. Impressively, the DES-Ti3 C2 Tx MXene exhibits splendid long-term stability that 97% specific capacitance retention can be acquired over 50 000 cycles at high current density of 50 A/g. Therefore, this study provides a new thought for preparing high performance MXene-based materials by water-free etching method.
