abstract: MXene has drawn considerable attention in energy storage due to particular physicochemical properties. At present, among most near-ambient temperature preparation methods, water is usually served as the main solvent. However, MXene is usually subjected to fast structural degradation on account of water molecules attacking in aqueous solution. Herein, we report a novel water-free etching strategy for synthesizing few-layered Ti3C2Tx MXenes in deep eutectic solvents at near-ambient temperature. Benefitting from the absence of water and macromolecular structure of deep eutectic solvents, the as-synthesized few-layered Ti3C2Tx (DES-Ti3C2Tx) MXene presents abundant −O terminations and low oxidation degree. As a consequence, the DES-Ti3C2Tx MXene displays excellent specific capacitance of 320 F/g at 2 mV/s. Impressively, the DES-Ti3C2Tx MXene exhibits splendid long-term stability that 97% specific capacitance retention can be acquired over 50 000 cycles at high current density of 50 A/g. Therefore, this study offers a new thought for preparing high performance MXene-based materials by water-free etching method.

title: Enhanced electrochemical energy storage performance by mediating BaTiO3 nanoparticles into the multilayers of Ti3C2Tx MXene
authors: Jitesh Pani, Hitesh Borkar
conclusion: In summary, we have successfully intercalated the BaTiO3 nanoparticles into the layers of Ti3 C2 . The enhancement in surface area have been confirmed through BET analysis. These intercalated MXene provides more active surface area by resolving the restacking issue which leads to improved electrochemical interactions for enhanced energy storage. The studies revealed enhancement of the electrochemical capacitance though increment in surface area, which has been confirmed though EIS and Dunn’s method calculation. Finally, the practical applicability of the BTO intercalated TM has been tested through LED glowing application. abstract: MXenes belong to the family of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal carbides, have been identified as advanced energy materials with exceptional performance. In this paper, we employed a strategy to intercalate BaTiO3 (BTO) nanoparticles into the two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx MXene sheets and use as electrode materials for electrochemical performances. BTO intercalated MXenes prove more active areas for improved electrochemical performance. As a result, the BTO intercalated Ti3C2Tx MXene electrode exhibits a high specific capacitance of 254.28F/g at 1 A/g and a retention ratio 74% after 10,000 cycles. The electrochemical stability study confirms that restacking issues were resolved. Thus, the intercalation of BTO enhanced the reaction kinetics of the MXenes and facilitate the charge storage valuable mechanism for next-generation smart energy storage devices.
keywords: Restacking Nidhi, Nahid Tyagi, Gaurav Sharma, Manoj Kumar Singh, Synergistic effect of PANI nanofibers on MXene sheets for high performance electrodes in supercapacitor applications, Polymer, Volume 326, 2025, 128328, ISSN 0032-3861, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.polymer.2025.128328. (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0032386125003143) Abstract: Development of advanced composite materials for supercapacitor electrodes is crucial for achieving high performance energy storage devices. This research presents the electrochemical properties of 2D MXene (Ti3C2Tx) sheets by integrating them with polyaniline (PANI) nanofiber using polymerization method. The electrochemical measurements were finding by utilizing of graphite sheet as a current collector. The results demonstrate that the Ti3C2Tx/PANI nanocomposite has a remarkable capacitance of 854 F/g at a current density of 1A/g with 1 M H2SO4 electrolyte. Moreover, it demonstrates at an immersive retention capacity of 88 % after 2000 cycles of charging and discharging, even at 5 A/g current density. Ti3C2Tx/PANI has 48.6 μS/cm ionic conductivity and a diffusion coefficient of 196.1 × 10−12 cm2/s as calculated by EIS measurements. Therefore, Ti3C2Tx/PANI nanocomposite can be regarded a promising electrode material for supercapacitor applications. Keywords: Ti3C2Tx/PANI synthesis

title: Oxygen vacancy enriched Na+ intercalated MnO2 for high-performance MXene (Ti3C2Tx)-based flexible supercapacitor and electrocatalysis
authors: B. Thanigai Vetrikarasan, Abhijith R. Nair, Surendra K. Shinde, Dae-Young Kim, Ji Man Kim, Ravindra N. Bulakhe, Shilpa N. Sawant, Ajay D. Jagadale
conclusion: In summary, we synthesized oxygen vacancy-induced Na-MnO2-x cathode through the electrodeposition method. The Na-MnO2-x exhibited a high specific capacitance of 395 F g−1 at the scan rate of 5 mV s−1 . Besides, the electrode revealed an extremely long life of 10,000 cycles at a current density of 5 A g−1 , which reveals 85.9 % capacitance retention. This can be ascribed to the oxygen vacancy creation on Na-MnO2 providing excellent electrochemical reaction sites. Moreover, we assembled ASC devices, in which Na-MnO2-x //Ti3 C2 Tx ASC reveals a high ED of 25.7 Wh Kg−1 at the PD of 1000 W Kg−1 , with high capacitance retention of 98.8 % after 10,000 cycles at a current density of 5 A g−1 . The flexible Na-MnO2-x //Ti3 C2 Tx ASC displayed superior volumetric ED of 510.3 mWh Kg−1 at the PD of 40,483 mW Kg−1 with an appreciable potential window of 2 V. The Na-MnO2-x exhibits an appreciable electrocatalytic activity with an overpotential of 439.7 and 381.2 mV to drive current density of 10 mA cm−2 corresponds to HER and OER respectively. Therefore, the oxygen vacancy created Na-MnO2-x cathode improves the electrochemical performance in the practical application of flexible electrochemical energy storage and electrocatalysis. abstract: The increased interest in smart and portable electronic gadgets has led to the development of flexible and wearable energy storage systems. Herein, the oxygen vacancy-enriched Na-MnO2-x is synthesized using a simple, scalable, and inexpensive electrodeposition method. The oxygen vacancy enrichment effectively enhances the conductivity and reaction kinetics of the Na-MnO2 electrode. The Na-MnO2-x film electrode reveals an excellent specific capacitance of 395 F g−1 at the scan rate of 5 mV s−1 with high capacitance retention of 85.9 % after 10,000 cycles at a current density of 5 A g−1. To verify the practicability, three asymmetric supercapacitors (ASCs) (Mn3O4//Ti3C2Tx, Na-MnO2//Ti3C2Tx, and Na-MnO2-x//Ti3C2Tx) are fabricated and their respective performances are contrasted. The Na-MnO2-x//Ti3C2Tx ASC reveals a maximum energy density of 25 Wh kg−1 at the power density of 1000 W kg−1, along with excellent capacitance retention of 98.8 % after 10,000 cycles. In addition, to validate the suitability of Na-MnO2-x electrode for flexible energy storage, the flexible Na-MnO2-x//Ti3C2Tx ASC is fabricated that operates in the potential window of 2 V in PVA: Na2SO4 polymer gel electrolyte and delivers a high volumetric energy density of 510.3 mWh cm−3 at a power density of 40,483 mW cm−3. Moreover, the electrocatalytic activity of Na-MnO2-x thin films reveals an overpotential of 439.7 and 381.2 mV to drive a current density of 10 mA cm−2 corresponding to HER and OER, respectively. Therefore, the electrodeposited, oxygen vacancy-enriched Na-MnO2-x film electrode has great potential to be used for both flexible energy storage and electrocatalysis.

title: Synthesis and fabrication of MXene/copper selenide composite for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitor
authors: M. Manikandan, M. Muthulakshmi, Seyadu Abuthahir, E. Papanasam, Dr Deepak Dubal, Sajid Ali Ansari, E. Manikandan
conclusion: In summary, MCuSe has been successfully synthesized using the hydrothermal method. The prepared electrodes have shown excellent electrochemical capacitance, with a specific capacity of MCuSe 570 F/g at 1 A/g with capacitance retention of 98 % after 1000 cycles. Here, 93 % Capacitance retention is observed and Coulombic efficiency of 98 % is observed even after 5000 cycles. abstract: MXene-Copper selenide (MCuSe) composite is prepared using the hydrothermal method for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitor. The synthesized materials were characterized using basic characterization such as XRD, BET, FESEM, TEM with EDS and XPS to confirm the phase formation, surface area and morphology. A composite material with improved ion transport, increased conductivity, superior cyclic stability and specific capacitance is produced when MXene is incorporated into a CuSe matrix. These improvements are explained by the complementary interaction of the highly conductive, layered MXene nanosheets and CuSe nanoparticles. The electrode setup of the electrochemical analysis reveals the specific capacity (Csp) for CuSe and MCuSe are 380 F/g and 570 F/g at 1 A/g current density. An Asymmetric Supercapacitor (ASC) is developed using MCuSe and an activated carbon electrode, the device delivered a Csp of 167 F/g at 1 A/g and a high energy density and power density of 59.38 Wh Kg−1, 2055.46 W Kg−1, respectively with cyclic stability of 93 % after 5000 cycles. For next-generation supercapacitors, the MXene-CuSe composite offers an electrode material that is more robust and efficient.

title: In situ oxygen doped Ti3C2Tx MXene flexible film as supercapacitor electrode
authors: Yapeng Tian, Maomao Ju, Yijia Luo, Xiaoqing Bin, Xiaojie Lou, Wenxiu Que
conclusion: The facile in situ oxygen doped Ti3 C2 Tx MXene nanosheets have been successfully synthesized by etching the oxygen doped Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase with fluorinated acid salt, which avoids the complex post-treatment. The substitution of carbon atoms in the Titanium octahedron by the oxygen atoms has been also proved by the experimental results and density-functional theory (DFT). The results indicate that the introduction of oxygen atoms can effectively enhance the interlayer space of MXene and promote the conversion from –OH to the -O termination. Moreover, the introduction of appropriate oxygen atoms can improve the electronic conductivity of the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, interface charge transfer between the solid electrode materials and the electrolyte ions, and the interface capacitance, but with sluggish proton transfer within the oxygen doped MXene. Moreover, the electrochemical energy storage for the oxygen doped MXene firstly increases to 306.0C g−1 for the O-Ti3 C2 Tx -0.05 film electrode, then appears a downward trend due to the excessive oxygen doping origin from the formation TiO2- x Fx . The quantitative analysis results indicate that the enhanced capacitance is mainly attributed to the diffusion-controlled capacitance and interface capacitance, which result from the enhanced quantum capacitance due to the improvement of the density of state, the higher Ti active center, and the higher adsorption energy. In short, the oxygen heteroatom is in favor of the quantum capacitance and higher Ti active center, thus giving rise to the enhancement of electrochemical performance for 2D MXene electrode materials. This strategy is of great potential for the future optimization of the 2D MXene electrode material design.
abstract: Heteroatom doping has been proven to be an effective strategy to improve the electrochemical energy storage capacity of two-dimensional MXenes. However, the heteroatom for MXenes is mainly focused on the N atoms, while the effects and underlying mechanisms of O substituted partial C atoms of MXene have not been explored so far. Herein, comprehensive research is firstly performed to reveal the oxygen doping mechanism in Ti3C2Tx MXene by the experimental characterization and the density functional theory simulation. The in situ oxygen doped Ti3C2Tx nanosheets, in which oxygen atoms substitute partial carbon atoms in the titanium octahedron, are synthesized by etching the oxygen doped Ti3AlC2 MAX phase, which is more facile than the complex post-doped process. The introduction of appropriate oxygen atoms can effectively improve the interlayer space, electronic conductivity, and interface charge transfer of the Ti3C2Tx MXene as a supercapacitor electrode. Further, the electrochemical performances demonstrate that the oxygen doped MXene (O-Ti3C2Tx-0.05) film electrode can deliver a higher capacity of 306.0 C g−1 compared to the pristine Ti3C2Tx electrode (216.8 C g−1). Besides, the quantitative analysis results imply that the enhanced capacitance is mainly attributed to the diffusion-controlled capacitance and interface capacitance, which result from the higher Ti metal active center, the enhanced quantum capacitance, and the higher adsorption energy.

title: Recent advances in MXene-polymer composites for high performance supercapacitor applications
authors: Sanam Bashir, Lala Gurbanova, Ibrahim A. Shaaban, Muhammad Sufyan Javed, Md Rezaul Karim, Syed Shoaib Ahmad Shah, Muhammad Altaf Nazir
conclusion: 7  Conclusion and outlook  Supercapacitors have made extensive use of conducting polymers because of their high theoretical capacity, cheap access to raw ingredients, inexpensive preparation costs, straightforward synthesis techniques, etc. In barely 10 years, MXene has generated a significant curiosity from scholars due to its exceptional conductivity comparable to that of metal and enormous graphene-like usable ion surface area. This paper examines the latest achievements in the research of MXene/conducting polymer composites and supercapacitors are conducted on electrode materials, composite material manufacture, SSCs, and ASCs. MXene and conducting polymers has been the subject of much research, but some obstacles still stand in the way of their widespread use. From the standpoint of material preparation, conductive polymers need careful control over the duration of polymerization and the design of preparation schemes since they have distinct morphologies and are prone to agglomeration. Strong, corrosive acids such concentrated HCl and HF are used to etch MXene compounds. It is clear from the papers previously cited in the text that MXene produced using various etching techniques differs in size, shape, and surface functional groups. More convenient and mild etching techniques must be investigated for the mass synthesis of MXene. Furthermore, the MXene precursor's MAX phase use rate is rather low, therefore when looking into more easy and gentle etching technique, it's important to think about ways to increase the MAX phase's utilization rate.  From the standpoint of material storage, low temperature can lessen MXene's oxidation, but they cannot stop converting MXene to TiO 2 containing molecules of water and oxygen. The researchers used end-group protection to lessen the interaction between oxygen and water molecules and functional groups on the surface of MXene to address the problem of improved MXene material utilization. For instance, Wu et al. [ 262 ] used sodium citrate for MXene's end-group protection; the outcomes shown that the end-base protection significantly extended MXene's storage period. However, MXene's storage mechanism remains a challenging issue that prevents its widespread use.  From the perspective of electrode material use, MXene is highly susceptible to self-stacking because, when the transition metal is removed away, there is no support material left. When charging and discharging, conducting polymers swell, this impairs their performance in electrochemistry. Along with fixing the problems of conducting polymer expansion when charging and discharging and MXene self-accumulation, the successful union of conductive polymers with MXene confers advantageous properties on the electrode material, such as enhanced stability and more adjustable usage conditions (such as pH and temperature).  Additionally, MXene has been progressively employed in numerous applications since its beginnings, such as adsorption, sensors, batteries, SCs, and electromagnetic shielding. Nonetheless, MXenes' component parts and surface functional groups differ, making them varied. The structure, chemistry, and form of conducting polymers also differ. Numerous elements of MXene's characteristics are yet unknown, and its potential has not been completely utilized. Along with the need to address the previously outlined outstanding concerns, theoretical simulation calculations and experiments may be combined in the future. In addition to increasing research efficiency and cutting down on needless exploration time, an efficient computer system should be able to create composite materials with various topologies based on various application scenarios. Because of its exceptional and distinctive qualities, MXene is anticipated to be used in a wider range of research domains as its study progresses.  MXene/conducting polymer composites have great potential in high-performing supercapacitors as a result of their synergic properties i.e. high conductivity of MXene and pseudocapacitance of polymers. However, some challenges of MXene oxidation, polymer swelling, restacking, and harsh etching techniques constrain real world application. Future work should entail the development of green, scalable etching processes, improvements on the stability of MXene through surface passivation, and the utilization of the control of morphology in polymerization. Counteracting self-stacking and agglomeration, on the one hand, with the help of 3D architectures and, on the other hand, with the spacer materials, is essential. Combination of computational modeling and machine learning could advance the design of optimized composites' design. Besides, in situ characterization and long-term device evaluation will be critical in transforming material-level progress to real energy storage systems. By using theoretical, experimental, and engineering methodologies, it is possible to tune these composites for flexible, effective, and scalable supercapacitor applications.  The main challenge is that numerous prior documented attempts have relied on polymer materials and MXene, as well as their composites with MOFs, phosphates, sulphides, oxides, and other chemicals. When researching ESDs for supercapacitor applications, researchers encounter a significant obstacle due to the limited availability of MXene/polymer material. Therefore, combining battery-grade polymers will boost the energy and power density of the devices. Furthermore, the composite of polymer-based materials with MXene (because to its remarkable hydrophilicity) would enhance the device's performance and spark the next generation's curiosity about ESDs, as polymer-based materials exhibit extraordinary EIS performance.  Chemical and thermodynamic stability are also important considerations for the materials being used. MXene is susceptible to oxidation when exposed to H 2 O and O 2 . Therefore, a detailed investigation into the preparation or regulation of MXene to ensure long-term stability is necessary. While sodium ascorbate has been employed as an antioxidant, there is an urgent need for a more efficient way to increase MXene's resistance to oxidation.  Additionally, for applications requiring temperatures greater than room temperature, it is necessary to design new polymer capacitors based on MXene. The current review discussed the various methods of producing MXene and its mechanical, electrical, thermal, optical, magnetic, dielectric, structural, compositional, and functional characteristics. It also highlighted recent advancements in the development of MXene and polymer-based composites-based high-performance supercapacitor devices. The mechanical, electrical, and thermal characteristics of MXene-polymer composites are further highlighted. Last but not least, the development and uses of the next-generation SCs take into account the difficulties and potential future developments associated with MXene/polymer nanocomposites. In numerous applications, MXene/polymer nanocomposites have shown their significant latent potential. Therefore, we hope that our analysis would help researchers identify suitable composite energy storage devices based on MXene and polymers to enhance desirable qualities. In order to create MXene/polymer composites with remarkable and all-encompassing electrochemical performance, future researchers will also find this review helpful as they continue to improve MXene stripping and dispersion techniques.
abstract: MXene/conducting polymers are excellent electrode materials that have drawn a great deal of scientific focus for energy storage applications. When these two distinct material types, MXene and polymers are combined, the flaws that arise from their use as electrode materials alone can be resolved. MXene/conducting polymer composites show promise as improved electrode materials because of their superior mechanical characteristics, mass load, flexibility, specific surface area, and theoretical capacity. Numerous instances of employing conducting polymers with MXene as electrodes are detailed in order to further highlight the modifications caused by these composites. The latest developments in the study of conducting polymer composites and MXene-based supercapacitors (SC) are generally covered in this review, covering various properties of MXene and MXene-polymers composites, electrode materials, materials preparation, and the two types of supercapacitors: symmetrical (SSC) and asymmetrical (ASC). Understanding the utilizing of composites of MXene and conducting polymers in SC research is the purpose of this work, which also offers recommendations for additional study of these intriguing materials.

title: Shear exfoliation of DMSO intercalated Ti3C2Tx during 3D printing process and its performance as a supercapacitor at high and low temperatures
authors: Mengmeng Yuan, Jingdi Shang, Libo Wang, Qixun Xia, Qianku Hu, Yukai Chang, Aiguo Zhou
conclusion: In summary, we developed an additive-free MXene Ti3 C2 Tx aqueous ink for direct 3D printing of forked finger structure electrodes by a simple DMSO intercalation and shear delamination method. The fabricated MXene electrode exhibited a porous structure which enabled fast electron conduction and ion diffusion, leading to high areal special capacitance and high energy/power density. Direct ink writing technology fabricates quasi-solid state MSC devices demonstrating high areal capacity (2497.8 mF cm−2 at 2 mV s−1 ) and excellent cycling stability of 84 % retention over 7000 cycles. At the same time, it has good specific capacity at high and low temperatures, but its poor cycling stability requires further improvement. However, the performance of supercapacitor at high and low temperatures needs to be further improved by improving the performance of gel electrolyte. The Due to high specific surface area, good metal conductivity and hydrophilicity, wider layer spacing with excellent flexibility, MXene ink will be widely used in energy storage, sensors and electromagnetic shielding and other fields.
abstract: Extraordinary electrical conductivity, hydrophilic nature and excellent mechanical flexibility of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXene) enable it to be intriguing contender for MSCs applications. However, the preparation process of MXene ink used in 3D printing is relatively complicated, and the ink is generally obtained by concentrating low concentration single-layer MXene. In this study, DMSO intercalated MXene precipitation was directly used for 3D printing, and MXene with increased interlayer spacing and reduced interlayer force was peeled off using shear force during the extrusion process of 3D printing. Finally, an interdigital electrode for MSC was successfully manufactured. The obtained 3D printed MSC demonstrated ultra-high areal capacitance of 2497.8 mF cm−2 at scan rate of 2 mV s−1, energy density of 222.02 μW h cm−2 and sustaining 84 % capacitance over 7000 long cycles. In addition, the prepared MSCs have good specific capacity over a wide temperature range (−40 °C–60 °C), and the capacity is positively correlated with temperature. However, the long cycle stability of MSCs at high and low temperatures is poor, and the performance needs further improvement. This work provides a reference for the next generation of scalable printed electronic products.

title: Recent advance in the construction of 3D porous structure Ti3C2Tx MXene and their multi-functional applications
authors: Wenke Hao, Sijia Ren, Xiaodong Wu, Xiaodong Shen, Sheng Cui
conclusion: 4  Summary and outlook  This review has summarized the definition and preparation of MXene-based fibers/whiskers and films/nanosheets, and emphasized on the different kinds of and MXene-based 3D macro aggregations for wide applications including supercapacitors, piezoresistive sensors, electromagnetic shielding, microwave absorption, seawater desalination and catalysis attributed to their rapid electron transfer rate, large specific surface area, contactable active sites, and stable porous channels. Many achievements have been made during the past few years in the construction of different kinds of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations using carbon-based materials, metal oxides, spinel, polymers, metal-based nanoparticles, etc., as the second phase, yet challenges and opportunities remain as follows:  (1) Further enhancement of the mechanical strength of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations. Many MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have been obtained so far, however, the weak interaction of the electrostatic interaction, hydrogen bonding, and van der Waals forces between MXene nanosheets and the other components, have induced the weak mechanical performance, which can be only used in the laboratory scale and have limited their further industrialization applications. Therefore, we should try to effectively control the abundant functional groups on the surface of MXene via the green chemical synthesis route, therefore to improve the interaction strength between the MXene and other components via the strong intermolecular forces and covalent bond, etc. Furthermore, the design of structures, such as the oriented structure and recrystallization texture, should be attracted more attention for the further enhancement of the mechanical strength of the 3D porous material, therefore to obtain more robust and stronger MXene-based 3D macro aggregations.  (2) Construction of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations with controllable pore structures. MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have been frequently prepared by sacrificial template and lyophilization methods, but the pore sizes prepared by these methods are mostly in the range of several tens of micrometers, therefore have limited their specific surface area and their wide applications as supercapacitor, catalysts, and adsorbents. Therefore, the design of controllable pore structures is in highly demand, and the control of building sub-micron-level structures should be explored by combining multiscale theoretical calculations via density functional theory, molecular dynamics, and mesoscopic dynamics, as well as the in-situ characterization techniques such as the in-situ FTIR (Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy), TEM (Transmission Electron Microscope), XAS (X-ray Absorption Spectra), Raman (Raman spectra), etc to further achieve precise control of the pore structures.  (3) Decrease the fabrication cost and explore more applications of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations. As is reported in this work, the unique properties of MXene-based 3D macro aggregations have led to their different application in certain fields, such as supercapacitors, electromagnetic interference shielding, pressure sensors, seawater desalination, and catalysis. However, industrial applications of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations are still in their infancy due to the single and expensive fabrication route of the MXene nanosheets, therefore, the cost-effective fabrication technique for MXene nanosheets with high performance should be developed in further study. In addition, the excellent thermal, electric, and mechanical properties of the MXene-based 3D macro aggregations should be expanded to many other fields in the future, such as thermoelectric material, superconducting material, solar cell, biocompatibility, electrocommunication, anti-microbico, etc.
abstract: MXene, a new two-dimensional nanomaterial, has attracted much attention due to its hydrophilicity, excellent electrical conductivity, stability, electrochemical property, etc. We have given a brief introduction to the preparation of MXene nanosheets, as well as the 1D and 2D MXene-based materials with their applications. However, the spontaneous aggregation and re-stacking of nanosheets in 1D and 2D MXene due to hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces are not beneficial to the industrialization applications, and therefore, the construction of 3D porous structures is an effective way to solve this issue. However, the small transverse dimensions and weak mechanical properties of MXene itself do not allow for the spontaneous formation of strong, stable, and self-supportable 3D porous structure. Therefore, combining MXene with other materials, such as carbon-based materials, metal oxides, spinel, polymers, metal-based nanoparticles, have been considered as the most effective method for the preparation of 3D MXene-based porous structure. Thus, in this review, we have illustrated the current construction techniques of 3D porous Ti3C2Tx MXene including template method, self-assembly method and 3D printing method, etc. The wide applications of 3D MXene in supercapacitors, electromagnetic shielding, seawater desalination, piezoresistive sensors and catalysis via microstructures structures regulation, are also summarized in this work. Finally, the prospects regarding the 3D MXene-based composites with strong mechanical property, pore structures regulation, cost-effective synthesis route and the new applications fields are proposed. This work will help to develop a more exquisite design of 3D MXene-based materials for their future commercial applications.

title: FeCo2O4@FeCo2S4 core-shell nanospheres intercalating into Ti3C2Tx for high-performance all-solid-state supercapacitors
authors: Na Chen, Guo-Tao Xiang, Qi Sun, Jia-Lei Xu, Bin Lu, Wen-Cheng Hu, Yong-Da Hu, Jin-Ju Chen
conclusion: In summary, core-shell FeCo2 O4 @FeCo2 S4 nanospheres were anchored into lamellar MXene nanosheets by solvothermal combined with a self-assembly method. The FeCo2 O4 @FeCo2 S4 -MXene electrode benefiting from the synergistic effect of the two materials exhibits a promising energy storage capacity of 1090.6 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 . Furthermore, All-solid-state FeCo2 O4 @FeCo2 S4 -MXene//AC asymmetric supercapacitor shows a high energy density of 49.8 Wh kg−1 at 800 W kg−1 and an outstanding cycle stability of 87.85 % after 20000 charge/discharge cycles. These results demonstrate the enormous potential of FeCo2 O4 @FeCo2 S4 -MXene in practical supercapacitors.
abstract: Electrode materials with high electrochemical activity and outstanding stability is of great significance to improve the performance of supercapacitors. A composite material comprised of core-shell FeCo2O4@FeCo2S4 nanospheres and MXene nanosheets was synthesized through solvothermal combined with self-assembly. The FeCo2O4@FeCo2S4-MXene hybrids as electrode materials exhibit a high specific capacitance of 1090.6 F g−1 at 1 A g−1. All-solid-state supercapacitor using FeCo2O4@FeCo2S4-MXene as the positive electrode possesses a high energy density of 49.8 Wh kg−1 at 800 W kg−1and great cycle life with 87.85 % retention over 20,000 cycles at 1 A g−1. The synergistic effect of FeCo2O4@FeCo2S4 and MXene is the main reason for the exceptional electrochemical performance. FeCo2O4@FeCo2S4 anchored to MXene prevents the restacking of MXene, while MXene provides a conductive network for accelerating carrier transfer and a skeleton for preventing FeCo2O4@FeCo2S4 from collapsing during long-term cycling. In view of the above excellent performance, this study provides a feasible idea for future research on high-performance supercapacitors.

title: Advances in MXene-based composites for next-generation flexible supercapacitors: From design and development to applications
authors: Priya Siwach, Latisha Gaba, Sajjan Dahiya, Rajesh Punia, A.S. Maan, Kuldeep Singh, Mohd. Shkir, Anil Ohlan
journal: Advances in Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: 7  Conclusion and future perspectives  The demand for flexible supercapacitors is an ongoing force driving researchers towards an exploration of suitable electrode materials. The quest concludes with MXenes, as its amazing attributes portray it as a potential candidate. Despite the intriguing features, MXenes encounter certain challenges when it comes to real-world applications. Prior to employing MXenes in FSCs, it is imperative to address factors such as agglomeration tendency, oxidation, degradation, and the need for synchronization of mechanical and electrochemical performance. In the Evaluation, this review provides a curtailed introduction of MXene and further encompasses the current advancement in the MXene-based electrode materials for flexible supercapacitors. This review gains significance by offering insights into the fundamentals of flexible supercapacitors, including a detailed discussion of flexibility aspects, variables affecting the performance of electrode materials, followed by an exploration of different flexible MXene electrodes. The discussion incorporates the diverse available substrates and their applications in MXene-based electrode materials, different configurations of flexible devices and gel-based electrolytes. The focused efforts of researchers have propelled MXene-based FSCs forward, resulting in substantial progress and significant advancements. However, reviewing the findings of the review, various important aspects and future prospectives emerge:   1)  The extraordinary attributes of MXenes, including surface chemistry, metallic conductivity, hydrophilicity and layered structure, are an outcome of their synthesis approach. In other words, the properties of MXenes are tunable according to different synthesis methods. Hence, significant research needs to be directed towards developing facile, scalable, cost-effective and environment-friendly synthesis routes. The traditional preparation methods of MXenes involve the use of hazardous etching agents. For instance, HF is the most commonly used acid, which not only pollutes the environment but also negatively impacts the yield and the electrochemical performance of the resulting material. Developing novel green synthesis approaches by varying different etching conditions results in distinct morphologies, modified surface chemistry and tunable properties of MXenes. In this context, initial efforts towards green synthesis of MXenes include examples such as the electrochemical etching method [ 183–186 ], Alkali etching method [ 187 ], Photo Fenton method [ 188 ], and the in-situ hydrothermal method [ 189 , 190 ].    2)  The most abundantly synthesized and commercially available MXenes are based on Titanium. However, depending on different elemental compositions and surface termination groups, various MXenes are predicted. Further exploration of the breadth of MAX phases and the development of new double M or double X MXenes may significantly impact the MXenes' properties, such as mechanical stability, structural diversity and electrical conductivity. Hence, diversification of the MAX phase is imperative since this will eventually lead to the commercialization of MXenes.    3)  Despite achieving milestones in energy storage applications, challenges such as the oxidation and agglomeration of MXene nanosheets continue to hinder their performance. Certainly, the abundance of surface functional groups enhances the capacitive performance, however, these groups adversely affect the physiochemical stability of MXene. Therefore, substantial efforts are needed to design novel and safer synthesis methods. Strategies such as encapsulating MXenes with organic solvents, forming effective composites, and maintaining proper storage conditions will effectively enhance their stability and extend their lifespan.    4)  To enable the transition of MXenes from bench to bedside, scalability must be prioritized. Currently, the conventional top-down etching approach limits large-scale production. Therefore, the development of high-yield, bottom-up, and cost-effective synthesis methods is essential. Advancing scalable fabrication techniques is crucial to fully harness the potential of MXene-based flexible supercapacitors for real-world energy storage solutions.    5)  Aqueous electrolytes are widely used due to their high ionic conductivity, ease of synthesis, and cost-effectiveness. However, their practical application is limited by several drawbacks, including a narrow electrochemical stability window that restricts energy density, as well as the risk of leakage, which raises safety concerns. Whereas, Gel electrolytes, with inherent flexibility, high conductivity, thermal and chemical stability, are ideal for FSCs. Therefore, progress in suitable and efficient solid-state and non-aqueous electrolytes will pave the way for the development of FSCs for the next generation.    6)  Device design—including configuration and substrate selection—is a crucial aspect in the engineering of flexible supercapacitors (FSCs). Common architectures such as bridge–island layouts, interdigital patterns, 3D-printed structures, twisted fibers, and origami designs are frequently employed. However, achieving high energy storage in flexible formats remains a key challenge, necessitating innovative design strategies. MXene stands out as a versatile material, utilized across various device components, with particular emphasis on its role as an electrode. Strategic selection of MXene morphologies (0D, 1D, 2D) based on specific application needs is essential, as the structure and dimensionality of the electrode directly influence device stability and performance.  An equally vital component of flexible devices is the substrate, which must be ultrathin, flexible, conductive, and lightweight. For next-generation devices, MXene-based substrates—such as yarns, fabrics, fibers, and ultrathin metal networks—offer significant potential to enhance performance and functionality. Moreover, the exceptional electrical conductivity of MXenes presents a major opportunity for device miniaturization, as highly conductive MXene films can eliminate the need for additional current collectors.    7)  Balancing flexibility with electrochemical performance remains a key challenge in flexible supercapacitors (FSCs). Variations in device configurations, shapes, and dimensions complicate direct comparisons of mechanical flexibility, even under similar deformation conditions. As flexibility is critical to mechanical stability, standardized quantitative evaluation methods are essential. Enhancing energy storage capacity is equally important, and advancing MXene-based hybrids offers a promising pathway to achieving optimal synergy between flexibility and performance.    8)  Integrating MXene-based flexible supercapacitors (FSCs) into the rapidly evolving landscape of wearable electronics has become imperative. When embedded in smart textiles, sensors, healthcare devices, and portable gadgets, MXene FSCs serve as reliable power sources for these systems. To align with advancing technologies, these devices must also exhibit multifunctional properties such as transparency, self-powering, sensing, photothermal response, electrochromic properties, and self-healing capabilities [ 191 , 192 ]. For instance, multifunctional AgNP@Ti 3 C 2 T  x  /PU composites have demonstrated self-healing/transparency/photothermal functionalities for wearable devices [ 193 ]. Realizing such multifunctional FSCs will pave the way for the next generation of smart energy storage devices.  Continued efforts in this field will revolutionize MXene-based flexible SCs, leading to their widespread commercial application and significantly improving our quality of life.
abstract: Flexible supercapacitors (FSCs) are ubiquitously integrated into advancing miniaturized gadgets, wearables and portable electronic technologies. The allure of FSCs lies in their flexibility, compact size, and lightweight, which has compelled extensive investigation in the domain of FSCs. The performance of supercapacitor devices is largely determined by the choice of electrode material and the interaction at the electrode-electrolyte interface. In this context, MXene, an expeditiously expanding class of 2D materials, have garnered significant attention in the exciting field of flexible devices, owing to their high electrical conductivity, distinctive layered structure, substantial surface area, excellent hydrophilicity, and abundant surface terminal groups. These interesting attributes of MXene critically influence interfacial charge storage and transport mechanisms. This review strives to discuss the latest developments in MXene and MXene-based electrode materials for flexible supercapacitors. The review thoughtfully presents the aspects of flexibility, followed by discussions on device designing and fabrication. The role of substrate in fostering flexibility, requisite for solid-state electrolyte, and the influence of diverse device architecture on interfacial stability are closely scrutinized. The review incorporates a comprehensive discussion of the factors impacting the performance of MXene materials, with a particular focus on the features including composition, structure, electrode-electrolyte interaction, electrode morphology and device architecture. Besides, this review extensively investigates fabrication routes, electrochemical performance and mechanical resilience of MXene and MXene-based composites for FSCs. Armed with these insights, the review proposes a prospective roadmap delineating the challenges and opportunities in the advancement of MXene-based electrode materials for flexible supercapacitors.

title: MXene-based ternary composites for supercapacitors: Advancements and challenges
authors: Kabir O. Otun, Azfarizal Mukhtar, Ismail Hossain, Jibril Abdulsalam
conclusion: 9  Conclusions  MXene, a two-dimensional material with high conductivity, surface functional groups, and intercalation capacitance properties, is promising for modifying supercapacitor electrode composition due to its potential to change electrode composition and advance supercapacitor technology. The electrical, mechanical, and electrochemical charge storage capabilities can be enhanced by modifying their surface chemistry; as a result, these materials are well suited for further investigation in supercapacitors. The developments in MXene-based nanocomposites for supercapacitor applications were mostly covered in this review. Additionally, charge storage mechanisms of MXenes stores in supercapacitor devices are also highlighted. The advantages of mixing MXene material with traditional active ingredients such metal sulfides, metal oxides, conductive polymers, and carbon-based compounds are discussed. The most recent advancements in those MXene-based nanocomposites and their uses in supercapacitors are presented in detail. We conclude that:   i.  Ternary MXene composites can be prepared by different methods including vacuum infiltration, solvent-assisted self-assembly, hydrothermal, ultrasonication, electrospinning, among others. However, the synthesis technique adopted influence the surface functional groups, sheet size and interlayer, and ultimately, the electrochemical performance.    ii.  Synthesis of ternary MXene composites prevents MXene materials from restacking, and allows the active surface area accessible to ions, leading to superior electrochemical performances.    iii.  The MXene-carbon/conducting polymer ternary composites have demonstrated superior electrochemical performance when compared with that of the pristine MXene and carbon/conducting polymer composite. The highly conductive two-dimensional MXene nanosheets with good electrical contact and the carbon/conducting polymer composite material together form an efficient conductive network, which provides sufficient electron supply for the Faradaic reaction of PANI.    iv.  A ternary composite of transition metal sulfide and oxide with MXene shows improved energy density than metal-oxide/MXene binary composites and pure MXenes. This enhancement is due to high theoretical capacitance of transition metal sulfides as compared to metal oxide.    v.  The incorporation of metal oxide into the ternary composite resulted in an improvement in its specific capacitance and energy density by creating a larger potential window. Comparing a binary composite electrode to a ternary composite electrode, the latter provided almost twice as much specific capacitance. Because of its improved conductivity and intercalative pseudocapacitive charge storage, the ternary composite demonstrated superior electrochemical performance.    vi.  The remarkable electrochemical stability of ternary MXene and MOF composites is key to delivering high hybrid supercapacitor performance since it guarantees steady performance under a variety of operating situations and increases the device's lifespan. This stability is essential to sustaining capacitance and efficiency throughout multiple cycles of charge and discharge.    vii.  The use of ternary composites in sophisticated microsupercapacitors with high energy and power densities has also demonstrated considerable promise. This was made possible by the strong pseudocapacitance, metallic conductivity, and simplicity in solution processing of MXenes with other flexible materials.     To sum up, ternary composites based on MXene have advanced tremendously and have a lot of potential applications in supercapacitors. The importance of research in pairing MXene with other potential materials is still quite high. Because of its comprehensive performance, flexible MXene-based composites are expected to become the next generation of supercapacitor electrode materials for advanced energy storage applications. Understanding surface chemistry, designing distinctive structures that support high-performance supercapacitors, and comprehending their capacitive energy storage process will all be crucial in this regard.
abstract: The acceleration of the global energy transition and the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) depend on promoting innovation in energy storage technologies. MXenes and their composites have emerged as novel electrodes for electrochemical energy storage. Numerous investigations into MXene binary nanocomposites have shown that they can deliver enhanced electrochemical performance when compared to their pristine forms. However, strong van der Waals forces between layers in MXene nanosheets can result in restacking, which lowers capacitance and slows kinetics, thereby limiting their practical applications. To achieve an enhanced electrochemical performance, attention has been shifted to MXene-based ternary nanocomposites for supercapacitors. In comparison to the previous binary system, these unique ternary MXenes display newly produced features and high-performance activity. This promotes synergism and results in superior capacitance, charge transfer kinetics, high specific energy and power, and enhanced stability. Nevertheless, based on the review of the literature, not much work has been done to prepare and investigate this novel ternary nanostructure for supercapacitors. Therefore, this review provides insights into recent advances in MXene-based ternary composites with a view to establishing the connection between their properties and supercapacitor performance. The performance of MXene-based ternary composites in supercapacitors and micro-supercapacitors are enumerated, including their practical applications. Finally, challenges and outlooks for further improving the performance of ternary composites in energy storage are highlighted.

title: High-rate electrospun Ti3C2Tx MXene/carbon nanofiber electrodes for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Hyewon Hwang, Segi Byun, Seoyeon Yuk, Seulgi Kim, Sung Ho Song, Dongju Lee
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, free-standing Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/CNF electrodes with various MXene sizes were prepared by electrospinning for use in flexible supercapacitors. This versatile and simple technique provided a large surface area and aligned Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets for good dispersion in the fibers. These electrodes demonstrated good gravimetric capacitance up to 120 F/g at 2 mV/s, and maintained a higher capacitance value of 90 F/g at 300 mV/s in comparison to pure CNF electrodes. They also exhibited outstanding flexibility, as demonstrated by dynamic bending tests. Based on these results, MXene-based nanofibers have great potential for applications in flexible and versatile electronic devices beyond energy storage, including electrocatalysis, absorption, and filtration.
abstract: Increasing the capacitance and rate performance of the carbon-based electrodes used in flexible supercapacitors remains a key challenge for commercial viability. To meet these requirements, free-standing Ti3C2Tx MXene/carbon nanofiber (CNF) electrodes were prepared by electrospinning of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and carbonization for application as flexible supercapacitor electrodes. The effects of Ti3C2Tx MXene size on fiber formation and electrochemical performance were investigated. Ti3C2Tx MXene/CNF electrodes exhibited a specific capacitance of 90 F/g at a fast scan rate of 300 mV/s, which is almost 2.3 times higher than that of a pure PAN-derived CNF (38 F/g at 300 mV/s), while showing similar capacitance values of around 120 F/g at the slow scan rate of 2 mV/s. Due to the high degree of mechanical flexibility of CNFs, MXene/CNF based flexible supercapacitors also demonstrate long-term cycling stability (98% retention after 10 K charge-discharge cycles), and outstanding flexibility in dynamic bend tests. These results suggest that the MXene/CNFs have great potential for applications in flexible and versatile electronic devices.

title: Synergistic effects in CuO/SnO2/Ti3C2Tx nanohybrids: Unveiling their potential as supercapacitor cathode material
authors: Tholkappiyan Ramachandran, M.P. Pachamuthu, G. Karthikeyan, Fathalla Hamed, Moh'd Rezeq
conclusion: Our studies concentrated on the synthesis and exploration of the synergistic effects of a novel nanosheet-like structure comprising copper oxide (CuO) and tin oxide (SnO2 ) dispersed MXene. Through a successful ultrasonicated coprecipitation method, we achieved the synthesis of CuO/SnO2 /MXene nanohybrids, which were thoroughly characterized using SEM, HRTEM, XRD, XPS, and BET methods, approving the presence of synergistic effects between MXene and CuO/SnO2 . Electrochemical investigations revealed that CuO/SnO2 /Ti3 C2 Tx presented significant electrochemical performances, with a high capacitance of 683.5 Fg-1 at 1 Ag-1 in a 2 M H2 SO4 electrolyte and an impressive cycling stability of 85 % after 10,000 cycles. Importantly, this performance surpassed that of MXene-Ti3 C2 Tx and CuO/SnO2 alone. The remarkable results are attributed to the active site availability, synergistic effects, surface area and enhancing electrical conductivity. This research presents a promising avenue for advancing supercapacitor electrode materials, utilizing a novel nanosheet structure to harness synergistic effects for superior electrochemical performance. CRediT authorship contribution statement Tholkappiyan Ramachandran: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Validation, Methodology, Investigation, Conceptualization. M.P. Pachamuthu: Writing – review & editing, Validation, Investigation, Formal analysis, Data curation. G. Karthikeyan: Resources, Data curation. Fathalla Hamed: Supervision,
abstract: In the field of materials science, a synergistic effect occurs when the combined physical and chemical properties of a composite material show significant improvement compared to the properties of its individual components. In this study, we synthesized a novel nanosheet-like structure composed of copper oxide (CuO) and tin oxide (SnO2) dispersed on MXene (Ti3C2Tx) sheets using an ultrasonicated coprecipitation method, and then we explored its synergistic effects. The CuO/SnO2/MXene nanohybrids were characterized through SEM, HRTEM, XRD, XPS, and BET analysis, confirming successful synthesis and evident synergy between MXene and CuO/SnO2. The electrochemical behaviour of the nanohybrid structure was investigated using different electrochemical techniques. CuO/SnO2/MXene revealed a high capacitance of 683.5 Fg-1 at 1 Ag-1 in a 2 M H2SO4 electrolyte, with 85 % cycling performance after 10,000 cycles. Notably, this performance surpassed that of MXene-Ti3C2Tx and CuO/SnO2 separately, which achieved only 102.8 and 378.2 Fg-1 capacitance with 60 % and 76 % cycling stability, respectively. These incredible results are attributed to CuO/SnO2/MXene nanohybrids' synergistic effects, whereby enhance the surface area, electrical conductivity, and availability of active sites and enhanced electrochemical performance. This research offers a promising solution for advancing supercapacitor electrode materials through the creation of a novel nanosheet structure that leverages synergistic effects.

title: PANI-MnO2 and Ti3C2Tx (MXene) as electrodes for high-performance flexible asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Yudi Wei, Wenlong Luo, Xue Li, Zhongtai Lin, Chunping Hou, Mingliang Ma, Jianxu Ding, Tingxi Li, Yong Ma
conclusion: In summary, the fabrication of flexible asymmetric supercapacitor has been demonstrated by combining PANI-MnO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx − MXene electrode materials on CC in PVA/H2 SO4 electrolyte. CC/PANI-MnO2 presents improved electrochemical performances with a high specific capacitance of 634.0 F g−1 (380.4 C g−1 ) at 1 A g−1 . The device with good flexibility can successfully work in an extended 1.5 V potential window, which can be up to twice than that of a symmetrical device. Its capacitance can reach up to 21.1 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and the capacitance remains at 83% after 4000 charge-discharge cycles at 1 A g−1 . Moreover, two devices connected in series can power a 1.8 V LED. The device shows an energy density of 47.25 μWh cm−2 at a power density of 2.40 mW cm−2 . Therefore, the flexible asymmetric supercapacitor can be a promising candidate for exploiting next new generation flexible electrochemical energy storage devices. CRediT authorship contribution statement Yudi Wei: Conceptualization, Methodology, Software, Data curation, Writing – original draft. Wenlong Luo: Visualization, Investigation. Xue Li: Visualization, Investigation. Zhongtai Lin: Visualization, Investigation. Chunping Hou: Supervision. Mingliang Ma: Supervision. Jianxu Ding: Supervision. Tingxi Li: Software, Validation. Yong Ma: Writing – review & editing.
abstract: Polyaniline (PANI) and manganese dioxide (MnO2) are forward-looking electrode materials due to their high specific capacitance. But poor cyclic stability of PANI and low power density of MnO2 limit their development. In this paper, PANI and MnO2 were synthesized on carbon cloth (CC) by electrochemical polymerization with the addition of LiClO4. The capacitance of CC/PANI-MnO2 increases to 634.0 F g−1 (380.4 C g−1) at 1 A g−1. And its decent electrochemical performances can be ascribed to the synergistic effect of PANI and MnO2. Moreover, an asymmetric supercapacitor based on CC/PANI-MnO2 as positive electrode and CC/MXene as negative electrode were assembled to broaden the potential range. The device has capacitance of 21.1 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and the capacitance retention of 83% after 4000 cycles. The device shows an energy density of 47.25 μWh cm−2 at a power density of 2.40 mW cm−2. Furthermore, the ductility of the device was explored to resist the bending and stretching from external forces. The research of flexible asymmetric supercapacitors herein further improves the practical application of energy storage devices.

title: MXene material for supercapacitor applications: A comprehensive review on properties, synthesis and machine learning for supercapacitance performance prediction
authors: Daisy Maria Saju, R. Sapna, Utpal Deka, K. Hareesh
conclusion: 9  Summary & outlook  MXenes, a novel class of TMCN, has attracted immense interest in research field by their immense potential in SC applications aided by the exceptional electrical conductivity, rich surface functionality, high SSA, and hydrophilicity. In contrast to conventional electrode materials for SC, MXenes exhibit a unique combination of properties that enable better charge storage mechanism in SC. Nevertheless, the electrochemical properties of the material depends on the other factors including interlayer spacing, surface functional groups, and methods of synthesis. This article has reviewed the properties, methods of synthesis, composites and the studies done till date in the above arena. Different method of synthesis, influencing the structural integrity, morphology, and other properties of MXene have been explored. Attempts to enhance supercapacitive performance and to mitigate the limitations of MXenes including self-restacking and oxidation have driven extensive research into DTM MXenes and MXene-based composites. Industrial perspective of MXene-based SCs with a comparative market analysis is also included in the review. A crucial aspect of the review is the integration of ML methods to predict performance of SC. ML algorithms including ANN, RF, RT, RS, and SISSO have been widely used to explore materials for application in energy sector and also analyze datasets and then predict Csp, energy density, capacitance retention and such features with the help of data studied. This has opened new avenues to escalate the development of highly efficient SCs.  To unlock full potential of MXene-based SCs, several challenges need to be addressed. Developing environment-friendly, fluoride-free synthesis methods without compromising the yield or structural integrity that is important for large-scale synthesis must be focused on. Future research should explore methods to overcome restacking and improvising charge transport dynamics of the material. Although, significant progress has been achieved in MXene material for application in SC, further exploration is inevitable to broaden their application scope and optimize their supercapacitive performance. In-depth understanding of the charge storage mechanism of MXenes when subjected to varying operational conditions is also significant for enhancing performance of MXene. Key features like cyclic stability and environmental stability demands focus as it ensures long-term reliability in practical applications. Interweaving ML for accurate prediction of MXene based materials demands collaboration among the computational and experimental researchers. Addressing these challenges will enable MXenes to revolutionize energy storage industry.
abstract: Rapidly increasing population has raised demand for energy thus elevating the research on energy storage devices. Supercapacitors, with its wide range of features including high capacitance, high power density, and high cyclic stability has proved itself to be a remedy to the energy crisis faced globally. The advent of MXenes, a class of two-dimensional transition metal carbides or nitrides (TMCN) having excellent features including good electrical conductivity, pseudocapacitive nature and hydrophilic nature makes it as a potential material for the efficient electrode for supercapacitor application. This material offers a blend of metallic conductivity and abundant redox-active sites, therefore enabling charge storage mechanisms like electric double-layer capacitance and pseudocapacitance mechanisms contributing to clean and affordable energy. In this paper, we review the advancements in research on MXene material for supercapacitor application, including the properties, synthesis techniques of MXene ranging from HF etching to environment friendly fluoride-free approaches, MXene-based materials for supercapacitor application, and much more. Additionally, ML approaches for predicting supercapacitor performance are also discussed. This review provides a holistic and forward-thinking perspective of MXenes in supercapacitor applications, addressing critical challenges and outlining future research directions that are indispensable to bridge the gap that exists between academic advancement and industrial implementation.

title: Synergistically boosting the performance of asymmetric supercapacitors: in-situ construction of NiCo2S4 on amino-functionalized and Zn2+-predoped multilayer MXene
authors: Min Lu, Mingwu Chen, Xiaohui Xu, Xinyan Wang, Wenxiao Zhang, Xinyu Li
conclusion: Based on a two-step modification strategy, the Zn-N-MX was designed to solve the problems of low conductivity and reduced electron transport capacity caused by surface functionalization and agglomeration of multilayer MXene. Zn-N-MX/NCS was further synthesized. The optimized electrode has a high specific capacitance of 1546.76 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 , which is significantly better than MX/NCS (1311.11 F g−1 ). The fabricated Zn1.0 -N-MX/NCS//AC ASC demonstrates remarkable electrochemical performance. It exhibits a high specific capacitance of 150 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 . Regarding its cycle stability, it retains 87.5 % of its initial capacitance after 5000 cycles. Moreover, at a power density of 800 W kg−1 , a high energy density of 53.3 Wh kg−1 is achieved. The multi-dimensional control strategy for the structure and electrical properties of MXene, proposed in this study, effectively promotes the practical application of supercapacitors. CRediT authorship contribution statement Min Lu: Writing – original draft, Project administration,
abstract: MXene’s inherent tendency to aggregate and agglomerate poses critical challenges for its application in energy storage. This phenomenon results in reduced interlayer spacing, a decline in the number of active sites, diminished ion adsorption capacity, and obstructed ion transport pathways, all of which severely limit its practical utility. To address these limitations, this study presents a novel multi-dimensional performance optimization strategy for supercapacitor composite electrode materials. Amino functional groups were first adsorbed onto the surface of multilayer Ti-based MXene as a means of modification, giving rise to amino-MXene (N-MX). Subsequently, Zn2+ ions were intercalated into N-MX to fabricate Zn-amino-MXene (Zn-N-MX), which served as a substrate. Upon this, transition metal nickel–cobalt based sulfides were grown in situ and progressively nucleated, culminating in the synthesis of Zn-N-MX/NiCo2S4 composites (Zn-N-MX/NCS). The introduction of amino functional groups effectively reshapes the chemical surroundings on the surface of MXene and reduces the steric hindrance of Zn2+ insertion. At the same time, the coordination bond formed by the amino group and the metal ion further promotes the stable anchoring and embedding of Zn2+ ions in the interlayer, as if opening up a “fast lane” for their embedding. In addition, the homogeneous dispersion of NiCo2S4 nanoparticles in the MXene layer provides a complementary “quick channel” for ion migration, thus boosting the comprehensive electrochemical properties of Zn-N-MX/NCS. The composite manifests a conspicuously enhanced electrochemical performance of 1546.76 F g−1 at 1 A g−1. After Zn-N-MX/NCS was integrated into an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) Zn-N-MX/NCS//AC, it exhibits a high energy density of 53.3 Wh kg−1 at 800 W kg−1.

title: Hybrid microsupercapacitors based on Ti3C2Tx MXene and covalent organic frameworks
authors: Yusuf Khan, Vinayak S. Kale, Jehad K. El-Demellawi, Yongjiu Lei, Wenli Zhao, Sharath Kandambeth, Prakash T. Parvatkar, Osama Shekhah, Mohamed Eddaoudi, Husam N. Alshareef
conclusion: 4 Experimental section 4.1 Materials and chemicals 4.2 Preparation of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene 4.3 Preparation of in-situ growth of Hex-Aza-COF-3 4.4 Preparation of lignin-based LSG electrode 4.5 Preparation of hybrid MSCs 5 Characterization 6 Electrochemical measurements and calculations CRediT authorship contribution statement Acknowledgement
abstract: The growing demand for emerging electronic applications, including energy storage, sensors, and portable devices, has created a pressing need to develop miniaturized flexible energy storage components with convenient device architecture. Here, we report an in-plane hybrid micro-supercapacitor made of covalent organic frameworks and Ti3C2Tx MXene as positive and negative electrodes, respectively. The devices utilize three-dimensional laser-scribed graphene (LSG) as a current collector for both electrodes using a CO2-laser-based technique due to its good resolution for in-plane device fabrication, and high porosity of LSG that can facilitate better rate performance. The constructed hybrid supercapacitor has a maximum areal capacitance of 131.46 mF/cm2 and a voltage window of 1.2 V. The findings provide a new strategy to fabricate a hybrid supercapacitor for self-powered device applications at the microscale.

title: Interlayer-engineered MXene Nanosheets confining CoGa-LDH enable ultrafast charge transfer kinetics for high-energy potassium-ion supercapacitors
authors: Chenxi Li, Mai Li, Xiang Peng, Inaam Ullah, Haotian Hu, Jiayi Shen, Ayesha Irfan, Wendong Xu, Paul K. Chu
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: This work demonstrates a rational design strategy to synergistically integrate bimetallic CoGa-LDH with Ti3 C2 Tx MXene, overcoming the inherent challenges of MXene restacking and limited active-site exposure in LDHs. Optimizing the Co/Ga atomic ratio enables structural refinement, where self-assembly suppresses MXene restacking and generates oxygen vacancies via competitive coordination between metastable metal ions and surface hydroxyl groups. The vacancies dynamically reconfigure the electronic environment to enhance the charge transfer kinetics and create abundant redox-active interfaces. The Co1 Ga1 -LDH/MXene composite delivers exceptional single-electrode performance, achieving a high specific capacitance of 1345.3 F/g at 1 A/g and 94.45 % Coulombic efficiency, significantly outperforming the Ga-deficient counterparts (Co1 Ga0 -LDH/MXene: 162.6 F/g; Co1 Ga0.5 -LDH/MXene: 644 F/g). DFT calculations reveal that Ga3+ incorporation modulates the electronic structure by shifting the Co d -band center from −1.84 eV to −1.67 eV and optimizing the K+ adsorption energy to −2.36 eV to collectively enhance the redox activity and ion diffusion. To demonstrate the commercial feasibility, the ASC device shows a high energy density (77.44 Wh/kg) at a power density (1125 W/kg) as well as excellent cycling stability. This study reveals a promising approach to overcome the technical challenges that have hampered the development of high-performance SCs. abstract: Two-dimensional MXenes, with their accordion-like morphology and facile exfoliation into monolayers, offer an ideal platform for immobilizing electroactive materials. However, composites fabricated from MXenes through conventional methods exhibit inhomogeneous dispersion, sluggish charge redistribution, and poor interfacial coupling, limiting their potassium-ion storage performance. Herein, an interlayer-engineered CoGa-LDH/MXene heterostructure is fabricated via Peltier effect-driven rotational hydrothermal synthesis with tunable Co/Ga ratios. This approach ensures atomic-level confinement of layered double hydroxide (LDH) within MXene interlayers while strengthening interfacial coupling and ion transport kinetics. The resulting heteroarchitecture synergizes the high pseudocapacitance of CoGa-LDH and the metallic conductivity of MXene, enabling ultrafast ion/electron transport and suppressing self-aggregation. Optimized Co1Ga1-LDH/MXene delivers a remarkable specific capacitance of 1345.3 F/g and exceptional cyclability (85.13 % retention after 6000 cycles), surpassing most reported LDH-based supercapacitors. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the heterointerface enhances K+-ion adsorption energy and modulates charge distribution, accelerating redox kinetics. When the Co1Ga1-LDH/MXene composite is assembled into an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC), the device achieves an energy density of 77.4 Wh/kg at 1125 W/kg, with sustained performance under rigorous cycling. This work elucidates the confinement engineering of MXene-based compounds and their potassium storage mechanisms, providing critical references for high-energy-density supercapacitors in alkaline systems.

title: Highly durable and conductive Korea traditional paper (Hanji) embedded with Ti3C2Tx MXene for Hanji-based paper electronics
authors: Jaehoon Jeong, Hae-Jun Seok, Hak Shin, Su Bin Choi, Jong-Woong Kim, Han-Ki Kim
conclusion: Hanji, which is known for its exceptional mechanical strength and chemical stability, was integrated with highly conductive MXene using a spray-coating strategy to fabricate paper electrodes. As the spray-coating cycles increased, the higher Ti3 C2 Tx content covered the entangled fibers of the Hanji network, resulting in a sheet resistance as low as 0.62 Ohm square−1 after 5 spray-coating cycles. Dynamic bending, folding, rolling, and twisting fatigue tests were conducted to demonstrate the excellent robustness of MXene/Hanji electrodes. Regardless of the dynamic fatigue mode, there were noticeable electrical resistance changes and disconnections between the fibers and MXene. To evaluate its suitability for paper electronics, we applied MXene/Hanji composite electrodes to EMI shielding, heaters, supercapacitors, and temperature sensors. As observed, the Hanji electrodes achieved an EMI shielding efficiency of 43.3 dB, wherein that more than 99.99 % of incident waves could be shielded. Further, they exhibit a favorable thermal conductivity of 1.33 W m−1 K−1 , effectively releasing the heat generated from EMI shielding. In addition, the MXene/Hanji-based paper heater reached a high saturation temperature of 76.2 °C at a low input voltage of 3 V, exhibiting uniform and long-lasting heating performance due to the low resistivity of the MXene. Furthermore, the MXene/Hanji symmetric supercapacitors showed impressive electrochemical performances with a high areal capacitance of 139.6 mF cm−2 at a current density of 1 mA cm−2 and an initial capacitance retention of 79.3 % after 1000 charge-discharge cycles. The MXene/Hanji-based temperature sensor was also evaluated by measuring resistance changes as a function of temperature. In the range of the human body temperature, the resistance of the sensor decreased as the temperature increased, and displayed stable resistance changes with excellent TCR values for the accuracy of the sensor. In conclusion, the conductive MXene coated Hanji substrate presented herein could serve as an exceptional platform propelling the use of paper electrodes in next-generation electronics. abstract: Lightweight, low-cost, eco-friendly, and mechanically flexible Ti3C2Tx (MXene) electrodes require for paper electronics. We develop a highly durable and conductive traditional Korean paper (Hanji) covered with MXene for Hanji-based paper electronics. The effective networking of MXene on the cellulose structure of Hanji leads to a highly conductive and flexible Hanji which acts as a multi-functional paper for Hanji-based paper electronics. Owing to the synergetic combination of Hanji and MXene, the as-prepared Hanji/MXene exhibits a low sheet resistance of 0.62 Ohm square−1, and outstanding mechanical stability without breaking the Hanji fibers. To further evaluate the potential of our Hanji/MXene composite, its performance in electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, interconnectors, heaters, supercapacitors, and temperature sensor applications is investigated. Shielding and heater paper samples employing Hanji/MXene-based electrodes show an EMI shielding efficiency (EMI SE) of 43.3 dB and saturation temperature of 76 °C at a low voltage of 3 V. Moreover, the Hanji/MXene-based supercapacitors exhibit a capacitance of 139.6 mF cm−2 at a current density of 1 mA cm−2. Furthermore, the Hanji/MXene-based temperature sensors exhibit an effective sensing performance over a wide temperature range. Overall, the successful operation of Hanji-based EMI shielding devices, interconnectors, heaters, supercapacitors, and temperature sensors indicates that Hanji/MXene serves as a promising conductive paper substrate for multi-functional paper electronics.

title: Optimization of MXene/CNT free-standing composite electrodes for enhanced electrochemical performance in symmetric supercapacitors
authors: Yasar Ozkan Yesilbag, Ahmed Jalal Salih Salih
conclusion: This study demonstrates that MXene/CNT composite electrodes, particularly the MX1 electrode with 10 % CNT content, exhibit superior electrochemical and structural properties for energy storage applications. The homogeneous distribution of CNTs within the MXene matrix enhances interlayer spacing, improves ion diffusion, and maintains electrode flexibility without compromising structural integrity. Electrochemical measurements reveal that the MX1 electrode outperforms others in terms of specific capacitance, rate capability, and cycle stability, achieving the highest specific capacitance of 254 F g⁻1 at 0.5 A g⁻1 and retaining 85 % of its capacitance after 5000 cycles. Additionally, the SSC assembled with the MX1 electrode performs efficiently at high voltages and low scan rates, achieving a power density of 13.9 kW kg⁻1 and an energy density of 14.1 Wh kg⁻1 . These findings highlight the significance of optimizing CNT content and electrode architecture to achieve high-performance energy storage systems. CRediT authorship contribution statement Yasar Ozkan Yesilbag: Writing – review & editing, Resources, Conceptualization. Ahmed Jalal Salih Salih: Visualization, Methodology.
abstract: The integration of one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) materials into three-dimensional (3D) structures shows great potential for improving energy storage. This study investigates the optimization of interlayer spacing in MXene structures by incorporating conductive materials. Free-standing Ti3C2Tx MXene and carbon nanotube (CNT) composite electrodes were fabricated via vacuum filtration, with CNT weight ratios of 10 %, 20 %, and 30 %. The MXene/CNT10 (MX1) composite exhibited superior electrochemical performance, with a specific capacitance of 254 F g⁻1 and remarkable durability, retaining 101.2 % of its initial capacitance after 10,000 cycles. A symmetric supercapacitor (SSC) using the MX1 electrode achieved a stable voltage window of 0–1.2 V, a specific capacitance of 70.1 F g⁻¹, and retained 85 % of its capacitance after 5000 cycles. With an energy density of 14.1 Wh kg⁻1 and a power density of 13.9 kW kg⁻1, MXene/CNT composites demonstrate significant potential for advanced energy storage applications.

title: Tailoring surface terminals of Ti3C2Tx MXene microgels via interlayer domain-confined polyphosphate ammonium for flexible supercapacitor applications
authors: Yongfang Liang, Hailong Shen, Jianghai Li, Hongying Zhao, Jiaheng Xu, Haifu Huang, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou, Jin Guo
conclusion: In summary, we design a simple interlayer domain-confined strategy to widen the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene interlayer spacing and trigger its microgelation via cross-linking APP between layers. The APP not only acts as a binder to induce Ti3 C2 Tx gelation, but also provides both nitrogen and phosphorus sources for MXene. Furthermore, this allows us to effortlessly assemble Ti3 C2 Tx microgels into MXene film electrodes. After heated at 350 °C for 3 h, the Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h film has about 2.0 at.% nitrogen doping and 0.89 at.% phosphorus doping, as well as the reduce of –F functional group. The nitrogen present in the Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h sample is predominantly in the form of pyrrolic nitrogen (N2), which offers superior electrochemical performance enhancement. Additionally, the P atoms interact electrostatically with the surface –O groups, and the formation of P–O bonds enhances redox activity, providing more active sites for charge storage. DFT further indicates that the introduction of N and P atoms increases the density of electronic states near the Fermi level of Ti3 C2 Tx , predicting higher electronic conductivity. Consequently, the Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h film exhibits remarkable mechanical flexibility and electrochemical properties. Specifically, the Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h film electrode boasts a high specific capacitance of 597.8 F/g and exceptional cycling stability, maintaining 98.5 % of its performance even after 10,000 cycles. Moreover, a quasi-solid-state flexible Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h supercapacitor achieves an impressive energy density of 12.5 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 250 W kg−1 . Remarkably, its electrochemical properties remain virtually unchanged even under bending conditions. Therefore, Ti3 C2 Tx /APP-A-3h emerges as a promising candidate for high-performance flexible electrode materials in energy storage applications. This study presents a novel approach for MXene gelation and heteroatom doping, paving the way for enhanced electrochemical energy storage performance in MXene electrodes.
