abstract: Developing miniaturization, adaptability and weavability wire-shaped supercapacitor (F-SC) with admirable electrochemical performance and exceptional mechanical properties, has been a pivotal issue for wearable system. Here, we fabricated flexible F-SCs assembled by heterogeneous polyaniline (PANI)/bacterial cellulose (BC)/Ti3C2Tx (PBT) hybrid fiber. BC nanofibers, as both reinforcement and spacer, can link with the adjacent Ti3C2Tx flakes together to enhance the mechanical properties and prevent the restacking of Ti3C2Tx flakes to accelerate the ion diffusion. And the PANI nanoparticle plays a crucial role in providing more active sites to improve the electrochemical performance. Besides, the continuous Ti3C2Tx sheet arrangement in hybrid fiber guarantees favorable conductivity and forms a smooth pathway for electron migration. Thus, the PBT fiber shows high mechanical property (123.42 MPa), mass capacitance of 337 F g−1 in 1 A g−1, superior rate performance (129 F g−1 at 10 A g−1) and exceptional cycling stability (84.1 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycling). Moreover, the solid-state symmetric F-SC displays capacitance of 259 F g−1, 86 % capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles, maximum energy density of 7.28 Wh kg−1 and favorable mechanical endurance, which displays a promising future in smart wearable system.

title: Synergistic integration of amorphous MoSx nanoparticles with Ti3C2Tx MXene layers for high-performance ammonium-ion supercapacitors
authors: Jinhe Wei, Fei Hu, Chenglong Lv, Xinyu Quan, Qiuyun Ouyang
conclusion: In summary, we have developed excellent host electrode material with the crystalline Ti3 C2 Tx /amorphous MoSx on carbon cloths for wearable ammonium-ion supercapacitor. The ultra-thin nanosheets are uniformly covered in the Ti3 C2 Tx layer, which simultaneously reduces accumulation. The formation of sulfur vacancies and defects can further enhance the electronic properties of the material and increase the formation of hydrogen bonds. At the same time, the amorphous structure can protect the composite structure from collapsing in the NH4 + insertion/de-insertion. Impressively, the resultant Ti3 C2 Tx @MoSx electrode yields an excellent specific capacity of 196.94 mAh·g−1 and remarkable capacitance retention (more than 91.01 % after 10000 cycles). The constructed symmetric ammonium-ion supercapacitor shows the maximum energy density of 50.08 Wh·kg−1 at a power density of 500.81 W kg−1 , along with outstanding cycling stability, maintaining 85.98 % of its specific capacity after 10000 cycles. The design not only provides a new host material for NH4 + storage but also proposes a new strategy to increase the electrochemical properties of MoS2 . abstract: The introduction of non-metallic charge carriers in electrochemical energy storage devices offers a significant advantage in compatibility with aqueous electrolytes. However, the development of suitable electrode materials for these carriers remains comparatively slower than other energy storage technologies. Here, the amorphous MoSx nanoparticles grow in situ on the surface of Ti3C2Tx nanosheets as host material for ammonium-ion supercapacitors. The Ti3C2Tx nanosheets provide a growth environment with large specific surface area for MoSx. The synergistic effect of heterojunction enhances the specific capacity of the composite. Amorphous MoSx nanoparticles form via an ethylene glycol solvent strategy. Compared with MoS2, the amorphous MoSx exhibits abundant defects and sulfur vacancies, which facilitate rapid NH4+ insertion/de-insertion and promote hydrogen bond formation. Specifically, the Ti3C2Tx@MoSx delivers a high specific capacity of 196.94 mAh·g−1 at 1 A·g−1 and retains 91.01 % of its initial specific capacity after 10000 cycles. Moreover, the assembled symmetric supercapacitor achieves energy density of 50.08 Wh·kg−1 at 500.81 W·kg−1 and satisfactory cyclic stability. This work highlights the broad potential of composite engineering in optimizing the performance of ammonium-ion supercapacitor and reveals its important role in improving energy storage efficiency and performance stability.

title: An intercalated structure MXene@CCNS: cuttlefish ink-derived carbon nanospheres composite Ti3C2Tx MXene for supercapacitors
authors: Dawei Wang, Yue Lian, Qiuping Zhou, Hongliang Fu, Yongfeng Hu, Jing Zhao, Huaihao Zhang
conclusion: In summary, we have prepared a heterostructured composite MXene@CCNS, composed of MXene and cuttlefish ink-derived carbon nanospheres through an electrostatic self-assembly method, and investigated the impact of heterostructure on material's ion/electron transport capability and capacitive performance. The heterostructure formed by intercalating cuttlefish ink-derived carbon nanospheres into MXene layers effectively increases the spacing between MXene layers, and prevents them from self-stacking. As a result, larger active surface area and more active sites are exposed on MXene, which enhances the ion adsorption capacity and shortens the ion transport path to improve the capacitive properties. Furthermore, the heterostructure mitigates volume changes of electrode material during continuous charging and discharging cycles, leading to enhanced stability. DFT calculations further prove the elevated charge transfer by this heterostructure. Accordingly, the MXene@CCNS delivers 264 F g−1 of specific capacitance at current density 0.5 A g−1 , and also demonstrate favorable rate performance and cycle stability. The assembled symmetric supercapacitor based on this electrode material offers 12.8 Wh kg−1 of energy density at 0.2 kW kg−1 of power density while maintaining a capacitance retention of 91.7 % even after 5000 cycles. Qiuping Zhou: Validation, Resources, Investigation. Hongliang Fu: Visualization, Methodology, Conceptualization. Yongfeng Hu: Resources. Jing Zhao: Visualization, Resources,
abstract: The Ti3C2Tx MXene with unique two-dimensional layered structure is a promising material for energy storage. However, the self-stacking behavior of MXene nanosheets limits its electrochemical performance. In this study, a heterostructured composite has been developed by intercalating cuttlefish ink-derived carbon nanospheres into layers of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheet through an electrostatic self-assembly method. This design effectively increases the interlayer spacing of MXene, and prevents it from tightly stacking. The heterostructure enlarges the specific surface area and exposes more active sites, thus improving the charge storage capacity and ion/electron transport. In Addition, the heterostructure buffers the volume changes of electrode material during charge-discharge processes, resulting in enhanced cycling stability. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirmed that the heterostructure effectively modulates the electronic structure of MXene. Compared to pure MXene, the composite exhibits significantly improved specific capacitance (264 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1), better rate capability (76.9 % capacitance retention from 0.5 A g−1 to 10 A g−1) and greater cycling stability (93.4 % capacitance retention after 5000 cycles). Based on this electrode material, the assembled symmetric supercapacitor achieves 12.8 Wh kg−1 of energy density at 0.2 kW kg−1 of power density and a capacitance retention of 91.7 % after 5000 cycles.

title: g-C3N4/MoO3 heterostructure decorated Ti3C2Tx MXene film as a flexible electrode for supercapacitors with high energy density and low temperature tolerance
authors: Qing Xu, Yuqing Chen, Yongjie Huang, Chunyan Xu, Chun Hu, Ningyi Jiang, Liying Yang, Shougen Yin
conclusion: In summary, a self-supporting g-C3 N4 /MoO3 -Ti3 C2 Tx hybrid film was prepared by vacuum filtration method, which exhibits good electrochemical performance in a wide temperature range from −20 to 40 °C. The optimal electrode exhibits a specific capacity of 1168 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 in 1 M H2 SO4 electrolyte and satisfactory cyclic stability with capacitance retention of 96.8 % after 5000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . When used as the electrode for the button-type asymmetric SCs, it also presents an energy density of 316 Wh kg−1 , a power density of 1250 W kg−1 , and remarkable cyclic stability. Even at low temperature (−20 °C), the CMM asymmetric SC demonstrates an energy density of 230 Wh kg−1 , a capacitance retention of 81 % and coulombic efficiency of 92 % after 5000 cycles. It is believed that the incorporation g-C3 N4 /MoO3 heterostructure on MXene nanosheets prevents the re-stacking of MXene nanosheets, expands the potential window, effectively enhancing the performance of SCs. Our work provides an effective and simple strategy of incorporation g-C3 N4 /MoO3 heterostructure on MXene nanosheets to improve the stability of MXene in application of energy storage. Chun Hu: Investigation. Ningyi Jiang: Data curation. Liying Yang: Writing – review & editing,
abstract: The stackable and collapsible nature of MXene films results in a low volumetric energy density for supercapacitors (SCs) used in mini-portable electronic devices. Herein, a self-supporting carbon nitride (g-C3N4)/molybdenum trioxide (MoO3)‑titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) MXene (CMM) hybrid film was prepared by vacuum filtration method. The electrochemical properties of the CMM hybrid electrode indicates that the incorporation of g-C3N4/MoO3 heterostructure can effectively enhance the specific capacitance of CMM, which exhibits good electrochemical performance in a wide temperature range from −20 to 40 °C. As expected, compared with the g-C3N4/Ti3C2Tx (402 F g−1), MoO3/Ti3C2Tx (625 F g−1), Ti3C2Tx (509 F g−1) electrodes, the optimal CMM electrode with 40 wt% g-C3N4/MoO3 exhibited a specific capacity of up to 1168 F g−1 in 1 M H2SO4 electrolyte at 20 °C with a current density of 1 A g−1. Moreover, it also shows satisfactory cyclic stability with capacitance retention of 96.8 % after 5000 cycles at 10 A g−1. In addition, it demonstrates an energy density of 316 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 1250 W kg−1 at 20 °C when used as the electrode for button-type asymmetric SCs. Even at −20 °C, the CMM asymmetric SC presents an energy density of 230 Wh kg−1, a capacitance retention of 81 % and coulombic efficiency of 92 % after 5000 cycles. Our work proposes a simple and effective method of incorporation g-C3N4/MoO3 heterostructure on MXene nanosheets to improve the stability of MXene in application of energy storage.

title: Compression-tolerant supercapacitor based on NiCo2O4/Ti3C2Tx MXene/reduced graphene oxide composite aerogel with insights from density functional theory simulations
authors: Maozhuang Zhang, Degang Jiang, Fuhao Jin, Yuesheng Sun, Jianhua Wang, Mingyuan Jiang, Jiangyong Cao, Bo Zhang, Jingquan Liu
journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science
conclusion: In summary, we have developed heterostructured NCO/MGA-300 with hierarchical and interconnected porous structures by using an intrinsically conductive and compressible MGA as host template. Benefiting from the synergistic effects of hierarchical porous structures and heterostructures, the NCO/MGA-300 electrode exhibits exquisite electrochemical performance in terms of high gravimetric capacitance (1633F g−1 at 1 A g−1 ), excellent rate performance (1492F g−1 at 10 A g−1 ), and stable cycling stability (∼86.6%) after 10,000 charge–discharge cycles, superior to reported compressible flexible capacitors. Based on the compressible NCO/MGA-300 electrodes, the assembled aNCMSC devices can retain intact structure and stable electrochemical performances under different strains, or after 100 compression-release cycles, suggesting the high reliability and security of the NCO/MGA electrodes. We thus believe this work should contribute to achieve advanced electrodes with both good compressibility and high energy storage capability for wearable devices, and this synergistic effect of heterostructures can also be applied to other metal oxides and two-dimensional carbons materials during the compounding process. abstract: Compression-tolerant electrodes are critical for developing next-generation wearable energy storage devices. However, most of previous studies on compressible electrodes focus on carbon-based materials, whereas metal-based materials such as spinel metal oxide with faradaic nature have been rarely studied due to their lack of compressibility. Herein, NiCo2O4 (NCO) microtubes assembled by ultrathin and mesoporous nanosheets, are deposited on/into Ti3C2Tx MXene/reduced graphene oxide aerogel (MGA), an intrinsically compressible host template with high conductivity and specific surface areas. The optimized NCO/MGA-300 sample shows a reversible compressive strain of 60% and a superior durability. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the NCO/MGA-300 heterojunction has high electronic conductivity, fast electron transfer ability, and low adsorption energy for OH– ions. As a result, the NCO/MGA-300 electrode exhibits superb electrochemical performance in terms of its high gravimetric capacitance (1633F g−1 at 1 A g−1), rate performance (1492F g−1 at 10 A g−1), and remarkable cycling stability of 86.6% after 10,000 charge-discharging cycles. Moreover, an assembled asymmetric supercapacitor based on compressible NCO/MGA-300 shows stable electrochemical performances under different compressive strains (20%. 40% and 60%), or after 100 compression-release cycles. This research finding demonstrates the possibility of metal-based electrode for wearable devices with high energy storage capability and good compressibility.

title: All-MXenes zinc ion hybrid micro-supercapacitor with wide voltage window based on V2CTx cathode and Ti3C2Tx anode
authors: Tao Huang, Bowen Gao, Sairao Zhao, Haizhou Zhang, Xingxing Li, Xiao Luo, Minglei Cao, Chuankun Zhang, Shijun Luo, Yang Yue, Yanan Ma, Yihua Gao
conclusion: 4 Experimental part 4.1 Preparation of delaminated 2D-Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets 4.2 Synthesis of 2D-V2 CTx nanosheets 4.3 Synthesis of PAM hydrogel electrolyte 4.4 Preparation of flexible Ti3 C2 Tx -based electrodes 4.5 Preparation of flexible V2 CTx -based electrodes 4.6 Preparation of flexible Zn-based electrodes 4.7 Fabrication of asymmetric hybrid micro-supercapacitors 4.8 Characterization methods 4.9 Electrochemical measurements and calculations Acknowledgements
abstract: To further improve the electrochemical performance for the wearable and microelectronic devices, we reported an all-MXenes zinc ion hybrid micro-supercapacitor (ZIHMSC) with a wide voltage window (1.60 V) based on V2CTx as the cathode and Ti3C2Tx as the anode. The flexible V2CTx and Ti3C2Tx electrodes are fabricated by the electrophoretic deposition method, which is simple and conducive to the realization of positive and negative electrodes matching. Benefiting from the synergistic effect of the two MXenes and the unique configuration, our ZIHMSCs also achieve fast ion and electron transfer kinetics, showing better rate capability than the MXene/Zn system. And the ZIHMSCs achieve excellent electrochemical performance, with high area capacitance of 200.1 mF cm−2, well stability over 5,000 charge/discharge cycles, and high energy density of 71.6 μWh cm−2 at 400.7 μW cm−2. The reason for the wide voltage window of the ZIHMSC was well revealed by the large work function difference between the two electrode materials of V2CTx and Ti3C2Tx and the redox potential of the electrolyte. And the electrochemical energy storage mechanisms are well investigated by ex-situ XPS and XRD. In addition, the ZIHMSC displays well flexibility and mechanical property, suffering from 15,000 bending cycles under 90°. The ZIHMSCs can successfully drive digital tubes and meters and enable digital meters to operate for more than 600 s, proving their practical application potential.

title: Synthesis and characterization of a nanocomposite consisting of Ti3C2Tx (MXene) and WS2 nanosheets for potential use in supercapacitors
authors: Pınar Talay Pınar, Mehmet Gülcan, Yavuz Yardım
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  Ti 3 C 2 Tx-MXene, WS 2 nanosheets, and MXene/WS 2 nanocomposite materials were prepared using a straightforward and efficient single-step strategy. Electrochemical measurements were conducted on Ti 3 C 2 T x- MXene and MXene/WS 2 nanomaterials, revealing CV curves indicative of good EDLC behavior, resembling a double-layer capacitor. WS 2 -GCE, MXene-GCE, and MXene/WS 2 -GCE exhibited low charge transfer resistance (R ct ) values of 5.25 Ω, 3.41 Ω and 2.29 Ω, respectively, alongside maximum C s values of 47 F/g (WS 2 -GCE), 71 F/g (MXene-GCE) and 373 F/g (MXene/WS 2 -GCE) achieved at current densities of 0.4 A/g for each material.  The performance of the MXene/WS 2 nanocomposite on the GCE electrode can be attributed to several key factors related to its composition and structure. MXene's high electrical conductivity facilitates efficient electron transfer during electrochemical reactions, while WS₂ enhances performance by providing a large surface area and excellent catalytic properties. The combination of these materials, along with the use of polyvinylidene fluoride as a binder in the modification process, improves the composite's adhesion to the GCE surface, enhancing the electrode's mechanical stability and electrochemical performance. The high capacitance of the MXene/WS₂ composite results from the synergy between its components, surpassing similar previous studies. Its 2D structure promotes electron and ion transport, with MXene sheets forming a conductive network and channels that improve ionic mobility. This design increases active sites for WS 2 , enhances electrode-electrolyte contact, and enables efficient ion diffusion and electron transport during charge/discharge cycles. We anticipate that the efficient performance of the MXene/WS 2 composite will contribute to the advancement of other TMDs and MXene-based materials for supercapacitor applications. Additionally, this composite has the potential to extend its applications to areas such as separation, adsorption, catalysis, and electrochemical sensing.
abstract: With the growing demand for high-performance supercapacitor materials, this study explores the synthesis and electrochemical evaluation of Ti3C2Tx (MXene), WS2 nanosheets, and MXene/WS2 nanocomposites. The aim is to develop materials with enhanced energy storage capabilities. To this end, the performance of MXene/WS2 nanocomposites was compared to that of the individual materials. MXene, WS2 nanosheets, and MXene/WS2 nanocomposites were synthesized through chemical and hydrothermal methods, and their morphology was characterized using scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, while Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the presence of functional groups. Electrochemical analysis of WS2, MXene, and MXene/WS2 was conducted in a 1 M H2SO4 electrolyte using cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The specific capacitance (Cs) values for WS2 were 58 F/g (at 5 mV/s) and 47 F/g (at 0.4 A/g); for MXene, the Cs values were 98 F/g (at 5 mV/s) and 71 F/g (at 0.4 A/g), while MXene/WS2 exhibited much higher Cs values of 322 F/g (at 5 mV/s) and 373 F/g (at 0.4 A/g). EIS results indicated a lower charge transfer resistance (Rct) for MXene/WS2 (2.29 Ω) compared to WS2 (5.25 Ω) and MXene (3.41 Ω). These findings demonstrate that MXene/WS2 nanocomposites have superior electrochemical properties, making them promising candidates for high-energy supercapacitor applications.

title: 2,6-Diaminoanthraquinone modified MXene (Ti3C2Tx)/graphene as the negative electrode materials for ionic liquid-based asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Li Sun, Lujia Chai, Liangqi Jing, Yujuan Chen, Kelei Zhuo, Jianji Wang
conclusion: In summary, DAAQ-modified MXene and graphene composites (DAAQ-M/G-y ) were successfully fabricated through covalent and non-covalent interactions. DAAQ-M/G-40 as the negative electrode exhibits an outstanding specific capacitance of 226 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1 in EmimBF4 electrolyte, which is mainly due to the high electronic conductivity and added Faradaic contribution. Anchored-DAAQ with redox activity can undergo fast reversible Faradaic reactions to contribute capacity. At the mass-balancing mass-ratio of the negative and positive electrodes, the HQ-RGO-360//DAAQ-M/G-40 ASC device delivered a high energy density of 43 Wh kg−1 with an excellent cycle stability. MXene-based composites modified by organic molecules would provide alternative electrode materials for developing excellent energy storage devices. Liangqi Jing: Methodology, Investigation. Yujuan Chen: Validation, Project administration. Kelei Zhuo: Writing – review & editing, Project administration, Methodology,
abstract: Due to insufficient energy density, supercapacitors (SCs) with preeminent-power and long cycle stability cannot be implemented in some practical applications. Exploring hybrid materials with redox activity to emerge high specific capacitance in ionic liquid (IL) electrolytes can solve this problem. Herein, we report a redox-organic molecule 2,6-diaminoanthraquinone (DAAQ) modified MXene (Ti3C2Tx)/Graphene (DAAQ-M/G) composite material. With the assist of graphene oxide (GO), MXene and graphene fabricate a three-dimensional (3D) interconnected structure as a conductive framework, which inhibits self-stacking of MXene monolayers and ensures high electronic conductivity. Meanwhile, DAAQ is loaded onto the M/G framework through covalent/non-covalent functionalization. The DAAQ as a spacer effectively enlarges the interlayer spacing of MXene nanosheets, and meanwhile produces reversible redox reactions during charge/discharge processes to provide additional Faradaic contribution to capacity. Therefore, the specific capacitance (capacity) of the DAAQ-M/G as the negative electrode material reaches to 226 F g−1 (306 C g−1) at 1 A g−1 in 1-ethyl-3-methylimidazolium tetrafluoroborate (EmimBF4) electrolyte. Furthermore, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) is assembled using DAAQ-M/G as the negative electrode and self-prepared organic molecule hydroquinone modified reduced graphene oxide (HQ-RGO) material as the positive electrode, with a high energy density of 43 Wh kg−1 at high power density of 1669 W kg−1. The ASC can maintain 80% of initial specific capacitance after 9000 cycles. This research can provide better support to develop advanced organic molecules-modified MXene composite materials for ionic liquid-based SCs.

title: Significantly enhanced electrochemical performance of Al-Ti3C2Tx MXene synthesized from Al-Ti3AlC2 MAX phase
authors: Haiyan Chen, Kefan Chen, Mingqing Lai, Ping Cai, Lixian Sun, Ruixiang Gao, Yaoben Xu, Siyuan Li, Tangyou Sun, Fen Xu, Hongliang Peng
conclusion: In conclusion, Ti3 AlC2 and Al-Ti3 AlC2 MAX phases were used to synthesize Ti3 C2 Tx and Al-Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes, respectively, by the same method of HF:HCl etching and LiCl intercalation. The freestanding Ti3 C2 Tx and Al-Ti3 C2 Tx film electrodes were further prepared through vacuum filtration from the Ti3 C2 Tx and Al-Ti3 C2 Tx dispersions. Compared with the Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode, the Al-Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode with slightly increased interlayer spacing and obviously higher conductivity offers more efficient ions transport and charge transfer, thereby achieving significantly enhanced electrochemical performance. The Al-Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode achieves enhanced capacitance (399 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 ) and higher rate performance (63.6 % retention from 1 to 10 A g−1 ). Moreover, the Al-Ti3 C2 Tx -based flexible sandwiched supercapacitor also exhibits superior energy storage performance. The impressive results indicate that Al-Ti3 C2 Tx MXene synthesized from Al-Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase possesses the great application potential in flexible supercapacitors. Ping Cai: Writing – review & editing, Supervision, Resources, Project administration,
abstract: MXenes, a type of two-dimensional nanomaterials consisting of transition metal carbides/nitrides, have emerged as promising electrode materials for supercapacitors. Especially, Ti3C2Tx MXene prepared from Ti3AlC2 MAX phase shows great application potential in flexible supercapacitors due to its facile synthesis, excellent conductivity and film-forming property. In contrast to conventional Ti3AlC2, excessive aluminum is incorporated in the synthesis process to produce Al-Ti3AlC2. In this study, Ti3AlC2 and Al-Ti3AlC2 MAX phases are used to synthesize Ti3C2Tx and Al-Ti3C2Tx MXenes, respectively, by the same method of HF:HCl etching and LiCl intercalation. The freestanding Ti3C2Tx and Al-Ti3C2Tx film electrode is separately prepared through simple vacuum filtration. The presence of excess aluminum during the Al-Ti3AlC2 synthesis facilitates to form more homogeneous grains structure with relatively larger particle sizes and an improved stoichiometric MAX phase with a Ti:C ratio closer to 3:2. The resulting Al-Ti3C2Tx nanosheets show improved oxidation resistance with relatively uniform and larger dimensions, which facilitate the higher conductivity with slightly increased interlayer spacing for the Al-Ti3C2Tx film. Therefore, the Al-Ti3C2Tx film electrode shows more efficient ions transport and charge transfer, and thus achieves significantly enhanced capacitance (399 F g−1 at 1 A g−1) and rate performance (63.6 % retention from 1 to 10 A g−1) compared to the Ti3C2Tx film electrode (342 F g−1 at 1 A g−1, 55.6 % retention from 1 to 10 A g−1). Moreover, the Al-Ti3C2Tx-based flexible sandwiched supercapacitor also exhibits superior energy storage performance. The impressive results indicate that Al-Ti3C2Tx MXene synthesized from Al-Ti3AlC2 MAX phase possesses the great application potential in flexible supercapacitors.

title: VOx anchored Ti3C2Tx MXene heterostructures for high-performance 2.2 V supercapacitors
authors: Kiran Kumar Garlapati, Surendra K. Martha, Bharat B. Panigrahi
conclusion: In summary, this work presents the synthesis of VOx -anchored Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes via solvothermal followed by an annealing process for supercapacitor applications. Pure vanadium oxide synthesis results in the formation of VO2 porous spheres, and heterostructure synthesis shows VO2 porous spheres, V2 O3 porous rods, and uniformly grown VOx on Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes, as confirmed by HRTEM. The decomposition of Ti3 C2 Tx surface functional groups and entrapped H2 gas creates a reducing environment during annealing, leading to the growth of quasi-metallic V2 O3 along with semi-conducting VO2, as elucidated from ex-situ synthesis and DSC analysis. The heterostructure of VOx anchored Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes benefits from the (i) metallic conductive Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes and quasi-metallic V2 O3 for quick e− transfer, (ii) more redox active sites offered mixed phase formation of VO2 and V2 O3 and (iii) layered structure of Ti3 C2 Tx to permit easy electrolyte ions migration into the electrode. The optimized heterostructure VOx M2 delivers a higher specific capacitance of 364 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 than pure VO2 and Ti3 C2 Tx in a stable voltage window of 1.9 V owing to the high decomposition potential of 0.5 M K2 SO4 electrolyte and intrinsic activation barrier of VOx anchored Ti3 C2 Tx electrode. The developed SSC delivers an energy density of 45.7 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1.1 kW kg−1 with 78 % capacity retention after 10000 cycles. The SSC shows a stable open circuit voltage of 1.34 V after 12 h with a leakage current of 0.09 mA cm−2 owing to the SSC's vanadium redox couple-driven pseudocapacitive charge storage mechanism. This work demonstrates a strategy to employ pseudocapacitive materials as anode and cathode for symmetric supercapacitors to mitigate self-discharge and improve the energy density of supercapacitors. The developed VOx anchored Ti3 C2 Tx MXenes show its feasibility for practical applications. CRediT authorship contribution statement Kiran Kumar Garlapati: Writing – original draft, Visualization, Validation, Methodology, Investigation,
abstract: Pseudocapacitive materials with superior electrochemical properties have attracted significant interest in developing high-performance supercapacitors. Herein, VOx anchored Ti3C2Tx MXene pseudocapacitive materials are synthesized via a solvothermal method to synergize metallic electrical conductivity and redox activity. Pure vanadium oxide synthesis results in VO2 formation, while in the presence of Ti3C2Tx, quasi-metallic V2O3 and VO2 (VOx) are observed due to the decomposition of surface functionalities of Ti3C2Tx. The growth of the V2O3 phase increases with an increase in the weight concentration of Ti3C2Tx. The optimal composition of heterostructure delivers a specific capacitance of 364 F g−1 in a stable potential window of −0.9 V–1 V, surpassing the specific capacitance of pure VO2 (245 F g−1) and Ti3C2Tx (140 F g−1) in 0.5 M K2SO4 electrolyte. Furthermore, the developed symmetric supercapacitor (SSC) delivers an energy density of 45.7 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1.1 kW kg−1 with cyclic stability of 78 % for 10000 cycles with a self-discharge open circuit potential of 1.34 V. This work highlights a strategy to develop anodic and cathodic active pseudocapacitive material based SSC to improve energy density and mitigate self-discharge.

title: Enhancing the ion accessibility of Ti3C2Tx MXene films by femtosecond laser ablation towards high-rate supercapacitors
authors: Xianhong Zheng
conclusion: In summary, we developed a femtosecond laser ablation strategy for fabricating highly flexible MXene ribbons towards the high-rate supercapacitors. The fabricated MXene ribbons demonstrated good dimension evenness and porous edge structure with exposed lamellar MXene channels. In addition, the MXene ribbons had high specific capacitance of 1308.3 mF/cm2 and good rate capability. Moreover, MXene ribbons showed good cycling performance, and there were a 95% capacitance retention and 92% coulombic efficiency after 30,000 GCD cycles. The good electrochemical performance of MXene ribbons was attributed to the synergetic effects between the femtosecond laser ablation induced high specific surface and edge effects. Especially, ribbons edges with continuous MXene flake channels shortened the H+ transport pathways and impregnated with sufficient electrolyte and H+ intercalation. To the best of our knowledge, the electrochemical performance of MXene ribbons exceeds that of most MXene-based supercapacitors. This work provides a new approach for improving the electrochemical performance of MXene-based electrodes, and lays the foundation for the development of high-performance energy storage devices. CRediT authorship contribution statement Xianhong Zheng: Conceptualization, Methodology, Visualization, Investigation, Data curation, Supervision, Writing – review & editing.
abstract: MXenes have attracted tremendous attention in the area of electrochemical energy-storage devices owing to their high electrical conductivity, pseudocapacitance and two-dimensional lamellar structure. Nevertheless, MXene flakes intrinsically tend to lie flat and restack, resulting in highly tortuous ion transport pathways and inferior ion accessibility. Herein, we develop a femtosecond laser ablation strategy to fabricate flexible and high-performance MXene ribbon supercapacitor electrodes. The fabricated MXene ribbons have porous edges with exposed continuous lamellar channels, which shortens the H+ transport pathways, impregnates with sufficient electrolyte, benefits for H+ intercalation and ion storage. The resultant MXene ribbons exhibit high specific capacitance (1308.3 mF/cm2), good rate capability and long cycling life (95% capacitance retention and 92% coulombic efficiency after 30,000 cycles). This work provides a new strategy for the rational structure design of high-rate MXene-based supercapacitor electrodes and lays the foundation for the next generation high-performance energy storage devices.

title: Bacterial cellulose/Ti3C2Tx MXene hybrid fiber for high-performance flexible fiber-shaped supercapacitors
authors: Yang Zhang, Shaoyi Wu, Yusen Wang, Xiangxiang Pi, Diwei Gu, Shenao Zhang, Jian Xu, Kangxin Qi, Wangyang Lu
conclusion: In summary, our work proposed BCT fiber via wet spinning method as robust and flexible electrode for FSC. BC nanowire can significantly hinder the self-restacking effect of Ti3 C2 Tx flakes and construct porous structure, leading to rich active sites and interconnected ion diffusion channels. Accordingly, the BCT fiber provides high capacitance (201.94 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 ) and good rate performance (65.63 F g−1 at 10 A g−1 ). Moreover, the assembled symmetrical FSC based on BCT fiber presents favorable mass capacitance and excellent energy density, demonstrating a bright future in smart wearable system. CRediT authorship contribution statement Yang Zhang: Writing – review & editing, Validation, Software,
abstract: Effective design and construction of robust, flexible and highly electrochemical fiber shaped electrode with hierarchical nanostructures are critical for wearable energy storage device. Here, bacterial cellulose (BC) intercalated Ti3C2Tx (BCT) fiber was fabricated by wet spinning method for fiber shaped supercapacitors (FSC). BC can significantly impede the self-restacking of Ti3C2Tx flakes causing a porous structure and connect the adjacent Ti3C2Tx sheets constructing high mechanical strength. As a result, the BCT fiber provides high capacitance and good rate performance in three-electrode system. Moreover, the assembled symmetrical FSC based on BCT fiber presents favorable mass capacitance and excellent energy density, demonstrating a bright future in smart wearable system.

title: The phosphorus doping modification of Ti3C2Tx MXene films assisted by tripolyphosphate-crosslinking for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Dan Lu, Yiwei Lu, Yongfang Liang, Jianghai Li, Jiaheng Xu, Jinyu Wu, Haifu Huang, Shuaikai Xu, Xianqing Liang, Wenzheng Zhou
conclusion: In summary, a simple method for improving the electrochemical properties of Ti3 C2 Tx by hetero-atomic doping is reported. In this method, KTPP was used as phosphorus source and the Ti3 C2 Tx was doped by heat treatment. The effect of heat treatment time and temperature on the doping effect of phosphorus was investigated. It was found that the comprehensive electrochemical performance of Ti3 C2 Tx -P-300°C-3h was excellent. The P-doping ratio in Ti3 C2 Tx reaches 1.25 %, the interlayer spacing is regulated and the generation of P−O bond optimizes the redox reaction on the surface of Ti3 C2 Tx . The specific capacitance of Ti3 C2 Tx -P-300 °C-3 h as the electrode material of supercapacitor reaches 365.1 F g−1 , which is twice as high as the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx (183.1 F g−1 ). The study of the relationship between peak current and scanning rate shows that the surface capacitance contribution of all P-doped Ti3 C2 Tx was higher than that of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . When Ti3 C2 Tx -P-300°C-3h based flexible supercapacitor device is bent at 0°, 60°, 90° and 120°, its CV curves, GCD curves and the retention rates of specific capacitance have no obvious changed with angle change, showing the Ti3 C2 Tx -P-300°C-3h based flexible supercapacitor device has good flexibility. When the power density is 483.03 W kg−1 , the supercapacitor device has a high energy density of 10.76 Wh kg−1 . Therefore, the facile and cost-effective KTPP assistance strategy endows MXene film with P-doping, remarkable mechanical flexibility and pseudocapacitance performance, which provides a promising reference route for MXene doping modification, surface functional group regulation and performance improvement. Jinyu Wu: Writing – review & editing, Validation, Investigation. Haifu Huang: Writing – review & editing, Resources,
abstract: MXenes is a new two-dimensional material with good electrical conductivity and high theoretical pseudocapacitance, which is widely used in various energy storage devices. Heterogeneous atom doping is one of the effective strategies to adjust the properties of MXenes and improve its electrochemical performance. In this work, a facile and cost-effective KTPP (potassium tripolyphosphate, phosphorus source) assistance strategy is demonstrated to dope Ti3C2Tx MXene with phosphorus atoms by heat treatment. The results show that the phosphorus doping level reached 1.25 at.%. As expected, the specific capacitance of the phosphate-doped Ti3C2Tx electrode is 365.1 F g−1 at the scanning rate of 10 mV s−1, which is twice that of the pristine Ti3C2Tx (183.1 F g−1). Besides, the flexible supercapacitor device assembled with Ti3C2Tx-P-300°C-3h sample has a high energy density of 10.76 Wh kg−1 at 483.03 W kg−1 power density and the capacitance retention rate is 84.51 % after 5000 cycles at the current density of 1 A g−1. With bent at different angles (0°, 60°, 90°, 120°), the specific capacitance values of flexible supercapacitor devices have not changed significantly, and the capacitance retention rate reached 90.09 %. The reason for the enhanced electrochemical performance is that the phosphorus doping can increase the active sites of Ti3C2Tx, bring PO bonds that enhance activity, optimize the redox reaction process, and accelerate the ion transport rate. Therefore, a simple and effective method to improve the electrochemical performance of Ti3C2Tx MXene is proposed in this work.

title: 2D/3D Ti3C2Tx/HCl etched Ni-Mn Prussian blue analogue nanocomposite as advanced electrode material for flexible solid-state supercapacitors
authors: Selvadhas Nirmala Kanimozhi, Abdullah Mohammed Alswieleh, Andrea Sorrentino, Jegadesan Subbiah, Anandan Sambandam
conclusion: This study presents the successful design and application of a novel 2D/3D nanocomposite, Ti3 C2 @Ni-Mn PBA, which effectively addresses some of the key challenges associated with MXenes in energy storage applications. By employing a straightforward fabrication method involving the etching of the Ni-Mn PBA surface, the material was seamlessly anchored onto the conductive Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets, resulting in a nanocomposite with significantly enhanced electrochemical performance. The Ti3 C2 @Ni-Mn PBA nanocomposite achieved a high specific capacitance of 900 F/g, outperforming its individual components and demonstrating its ability to compete with leading nanomaterials in the field. When incorporated into a two-electrode asymmetric supercapacitor, the device delivered a remarkable energy density of 44 Wh/kg and a power density of 2640 W/kg. Additionally, it successfully powered a multifunctional display for approximately 2 min, showcasing its practical utility in real-world applications. An innovative aspect of this work lies in the development of a flexible, binder-free electrode coupled with an ionic liquid-based gel electrolyte (PVA/KOH/EMP-TFSI). This design provides the device with enhanced mechanical stability, excellent ionic conductivity, and extended durability, paving the way for its integration into wearable and portable electronics, areas of rapidly growing interest. The robust device architecture maintained an outstanding 100 % capacitance retention and a 75 % coulombic efficiency over 1000 charge-discharge cycles, highlighting its reliability for long-term use. Moreover, the unique synergy between the 2D structure of Ti3 C2 Tx and the 3D open framework of Ni-Mn PBA-augmented by etched surface voids-facilitates rapid ion transport, reduced polarization, and improved charge transfer kinetics. This hybrid approach not only enhances the material's energy storage capacity but also contributes to its exceptional rate capability and reversibility. In light of these findings, the Ti3 C2 @Ni-Mn PBA nanocomposite represents a significant step forward in the development of high-performance, sustainable energy storage solutions. Future investigations should focus on further optimizing the material's synthesis, exploring its behaviour with other electrolytes, and scaling its production to meet industrial demands. abstract: Since their discovery in 2011, MXenes, derived from their parent MAX phases, have garnered immense attention in the domain of energy storage due to their exceptional attributes. However, their performance is often hindered by nanosheet restacking, which limits stability and ion diffusion. To address this challenge, we propose a novel 2D/3D nanocomposite comprising Ti3C2Tx MXene and a 3D Prussian blue analogue (Ni-Mn PBA). The integration of Ni-Mn PBA mitigates the restacking of MXene nanosheets, enhancing electrode stability, while Ti3C2Tx serves as a highly conductive substrate, facilitating efficient ion transport. This synergistic interaction results in superior electrochemical performance. Herein, we report the synthesis of Ti3C2Tx@Ni-Mn PBA via chemical etching, which partially modifies the PBA structure to expose internal surfaces and promote ion diffusion through its open framework. The 2D/3D nanocomposite exhibits a specific capacitance of 316 F/g at a current density of 5 mA/cm2, surpassing the performance of pristine Ti3C2Tx and Ni-Mn PBA. When assembled into an asymmetric supercapacitor, the device achieves an energy density of 44 Wh/kg and a power density of 2640 W/kg, demonstrating its practical application by powering a multifunctional display for nearly 2 min. Additionally, a solid-state supercapacitor employing an ionic liquid-based gel electrolyte (PVA/KOH/EMP-TFSI) was developed, extending the operating voltage to 1.7 V and further enhancing the energy density of the device. This study highlights the potential of Ti3C2@Ni-Mn PBA nanocomposites as advanced materials for next-generation flexible energy storage systems.

title: Rationally constructed CeO2/Ti3C2Tx-MXene heterostructure for rapid and efficient visible light photocatalytic activity and enhanced supercapacitor performance
authors: Nagaraju Macherla, Govinda Dharmana, Manjula Nerella, Thirumala Rao Gurugubelli, Ravindranadh Koutavarapu, Jaesool Shim
journal: Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, CeO 2 nanospheres were successfully compounded with Ti 3 C 2 MXene via solvothermal method. A smaller crystallite size is noticed from XRD for CeO 2 /MX5 resulted in reduced particle size of CeO 2 nanospheres (∼87 nm) which were uniformly dispersed over 2D nanosheets of MX. Consequently, a larger specific surface area is realized for CeO 2 /MX5 (114.20 m 2 g −1 ) with abundant mesoporosity. XPS surface analysis designates the dual oxidation states (Ce 4+ and Ce 3+ ) of Ceria owing to the rich abundance of reactive oxygen species. Optical study describes the reduced bandgap trend (red-shift) of composites with increasing MX and lower charge transfer resistance is obtained for CeO 2 /MX5. Improved TC photodegradation efficiency (96.05 % in 120 min) of the optimized composite was due to enhanced charge separation and nano-phased heterostructure. Holes and superoxide ions play a vibrant role in the degradation mechanism and the high stability of the optimized composite even after three consecutive cycles. The significant enhancement is electrochemical activity is realized by achieving enhanced specific capacitance (522 F g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 ) along with a capacitance retention of 92.01 % after 5000 cycles. Based on the above merits, the prepared heterostructure was found to be an efficient photocatalyst for degrading TC pollutant from water bodies upon light irradiation and Supercapacitor.
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) Ti3C2Tx MXene (MX) benefits from substantial surface area, higher electric conductivity, and abundant surface terminations that can be tightly coupled with other materials, and has found broad application prospects in energy storage and photocatalysis. By this, CeO2 nanospheres were rationally compounded with MX to obtain nanocomposites (NCs) (CeO2/MX1, CeO2/MX3, CeO2/MX5, and CeO2/MX7) via a facile one-step solvothermal method. X-ray diffraction examination discloses the cubic structure of CeO2, and shrinkage in average crystallite size is noticed up to 5 % of MX. Field emission scanning electron microscopy images show uniform CeO2 nanospheres decorated on MX 2D matrix, and particle size distribution results are well aligned with crystallite size trends. Optical absorption divulges a progressive red shift in the absorption edge with increasing MX content, demonstrating enhanced light harvesting and effective charge migration through the heterojunction formed at the CeO2/MX interface. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy studies indicate a smaller charge transfer resistance for CeO2/MX5, highlighting interfacial conductivity and rapid charge transfer characteristics. Consequently, CeO2/MX5 attains a robust photocatalytic tetracycline (TC) degradation surpassing pristine CeO2 and other CeO2/MX NCs. As a supercapacitor electrode, CeO2/MX5 delivers a specific capacitance of 522 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and retains 92 % of its initial capacitance after 10000 GCD cycles. This work underscores the effective integration of CeO2 with 2D MX to achieve a versatile platform for environmental remediation and energy storage applications.

title: MXene (Ti3C2Tx)/cellulose nanofiber/polyaniline film as a highly conductive and flexible electrode material for supercapacitors
authors: Tao Yuan, Zhen Zhang, Qian Liu, Xiu-Tong Liu, Ya-Ning Miao, Chun-li Yao
conclusion: In conclusion, flexible MXene/CNF/PANI composite films with excellent electrical properties were successfully prepared in this study. MXene/CNF/PANI films show a high areal specific capacitance of 2935 mF cm−2 at 1 mA cm−2 , good rate capability with 90.2 % capacitance retention at 5 mA cm−2 , and excellent cycling stability (94 % capacitance retention after 2000 cycles), making it a promising electrode material for supercapacitor. The SC which used the PVA/H2 SO4 gel electrolyte and the MXene/CNF/PANI films as electrodes, possessed a significantly high areal capacitance of 522 mF cm−2 at 5 mA cm−2 , and the SCs also had good electrical stability. The SC provides 94.7 μWh∙cm−2 areal energy density at 573 μW∙cm−2 areal power density, and it has good cycles stability (81.5 % retention after 4000 cycles). This proves that the added CNF/PANI can not only enhance the mechanical properties of the film, but also improve the electrochemical properties of the film. It is also proved that the improved electrochemical performance of the composite conductive films is not only due to the high electrochemical activity of MXene and PANI, but also because CNF provides charge carriers with a path and improves electrolyte ion diffusion by increasing the MXene nanosheet interlayer spacing. The results of this research will facilitate the development of MXene-based hybrid films and high-performance SCs. abstract: In recent years, supercapacitors based on cellulose nanofiber (CNF) films have received considerable attention for their excellent flexibility, lightweight, and unique structure. In this study, MXene (Ti3C2Tx) /CNF/polyaniline (PANI) hybrid films with good conductivity and flexibility were prepared by a convenient vacuum filtration method. Combined with PANI, MXene creates an open structure with high conductivity, which facilitates ion and electron transport among the materials and provides the composite with high electrochemical activity. The MXene/CNF/PANI electrode presents a high areal specific capacitance of 2935 mF cm−2 at the current density of 1 mA cm−2, excellent cycling stability with high capacitance retention of 94 % after 2000 cycles at 10 mA cm−2 and high electrical conductivity (634.4 S∙cm−1). As a further application of this film, it is used as a free-standing electrode to fabricate a quasi-solid-state supercapacitor with high performance, which has an ultra-thin thickness of 0.344 mm, a significantly high areal specific capacitance (522 mF cm−2) at 5 mA cm−2, a high areal energy density of 94.7 μWh∙cm−2 and a high areal power density of 573 μW∙cm−2. This work shows the great potential of the developed high-performance and flexible cellulose-based composites for fabricating electrodes as well as supercapacitors.

title: Electrochemical investigation of Ti3C2Tx (MXene), N-Ti3C2Tx, and the Ti3C2Tx/Co3O4 hybrid composite deposited on carbon cloth for use as anode materials in flexible supercapacitors††Electronic supplementary information (ESI) available. See DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/d4na01024h
authors: Lan Nguyen, Adnan Ali, Brahim Aissa, Sosiawati Teke, Roshan Mangal Bhattarai, Avik Denra, Oai Quoc Vu, Young Sun Mok
error: Could not extract conclusion using any method
abstract: Supercapacitors have been studied as a potential complementary technology for rechargeable batteries, fuel cells, and dielectric capacitors. Wearable energy storage systems need freestanding, flexible electrodes for maximum functioning. Optimal energy storage system performance demands an optimal balance between mechanical component flexibility and electrode energy storage and release efficiency. This work specifically focuses on investigation and comparison of the electrochemical performance of the synthesized Ti3C2Tx, N-Ti3C2Tx, and the Ti3C2Tx/Co3O4 hybrid composite. Co3O4 NPs have been synthesized using an innovative and cost-effective novel synthesis route employing a “microplasma discharge reactor”. This offers significant benefits, including the effective prevention of hazardous reducing agent generation in comparison to other routes. Upon exposure to 1 A g−1 current density, the Ti3C2Tx/Co3O4 hybrid composite electrode demonstrates a maximum gravimetric capacity of 128 F g−1 and a specific capacitance of 576.7 F g−1, exhibiting a significant 95.06% increase in specific capacitance compared to Ti3C2Tx. Furthermore, from the kinetic analysis of the CV curves, it has been noticed that the contributions of the diffusion-controlled and pseudocapacitive-controlled processes are 60% and 40%, respectively, in the charge storage for the applied Ti3C2Tx/Co3O4 hybrid composite electrode.

title: Sulfur-tuned MoS2 quantum dot decorated Ti3C2Tx (MXene) electrode materials for high performance supercapacitor applications
authors: Sumanta Bera, Tapas Kumar Mondal, Yan-Kuin Su, Shyamal Kumar Saha
conclusion: In summary, the few layers of Ti3 C2 Tx 2D sheets have been successfully prepared by the chemical etching of the aluminum layer from the Ti3 AlC2 MAX phase. MoS2 quantum dots with tunning the sulfur ratio are grown on the Ti3 C2 Tx nano sheets to stave off the restacking. The low conductivity of the MoS2 quantum dots is overcome by using Ti3 C2 Tx 2D with superior electronic conductivity. The SCs of the composite samples are increased remarkably due to the combined effect of unsaturated sulfur S 2 2 − on the edge of MoS2 and the Ti3 C2 Tx highly conductive 2 D sheets and delivered the superior potential windows. The S-rich MSM composite has delivered the SC of 985 Fg−1 at a CD of 1 Ag−1 within the potential range from −0.5 V to 0.6 V. Also, S-rich MSM has retained 96.53% of its initial SC after 104 cycles at a CD of 10 Ag−1 . Additionally, over the potential ranges from −0.3/0.4 V to −0.7/0.8 V, it is also workable. Therefore, we eagerly considered that the MoS2 quantum dot and Ti3 C2 Tx composite will be promising electrode materials for supercapacitor application. abstract: Recently, two dimensional materials have been considered as the exciting and most promising materials in the field of energy storage applications. Literature results show that the non-bridging ‘S’ in MoS2 quantum dot act as efficient active sites for catalytic activity. But, the MoS2 quantum dots with sufficient non-bridging sulfur do not possess high electronic conductivity which is required for supercapacitor electrode applications. Therefore, exploiting large number of active sites and superior electronic conductivity in the present work we have decorated Ti3C2Tx sheets by MoS2 quantum dots with a large number of non-bridging ‘S’. We have synthesized three composite samples by varying ‘S’ components and seen that the sulfur rich samples show the highest value of specific capacitance (SC) of about 985 Fg−1 because of the presence of unsaturated sulfur S22−ligands. The unique combination of MoS2 quantum dot and Ti3C2Tx shows excellent performance over a wide range of potential windows (-0.3/0.4 V to −0.7/0.8 V) with a high energy density 165.53 WhKg−1 at a power density 1100 WKg−1. Also, the SC retention values after 104 cycles are obtained over 96.53% at a current density (CD) 10 Ag−1.

title: Electrophoretic deposition of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheet N-carbon cloth as binder-free supercapacitor electrode material
authors: Zhichao Li, Xinyu Liu, Xuyun Wang, Hui Wang, Jianwei Ren, Rongfang Wang
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this work, the binder-free Ti 3 C 2 T x(EPD) /ENCC was developed through the electrophoretic deposition of Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets onto the ENCC substrate as the flexible supercapacitor electrode material. It was found that the rich oxygen-containing functional groups resulted in the well-dispersed Ti 3 C 2 T x on the ENCC substrate via the hydrogen binding effect. The composite electrode displayed an area-specific capacitance of 2080.1 mF·cm −2 at 1 mA·cm −2 current density. In addition, a good rate performance was observed when the current density increased from 10 to 50 mA·cm −2 . The assembled EDLC achieved a long-term stability with a 91% retention after 10,000 GCD cycles at 20 mA·cm −2 .
abstract: Despite the existing advances of Ti3C2Tx MXene as supercapacitor electrode material, its capacitance can be further enhanced through the composite strategy. In this work, the nitrogen-doped superhydrophilic carbon cloth (ENCC) was firstly prepared by N-doping of carbon cloth (CC), and then Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets were electrophoretically deposited to yield the binder-free Ti3C2Tx(EPD)/ENCC as supercapacitor electrode material. As a result, the composite electrode exhibited an area-specific capacitance of 2080.1 mF·cm−2 at 1 mA·cm−2 current density. The analysis implied that the varying Ti valence states provided certain psedocapacitance to the capacitance of the as-prepared electrode, though the main contribution was still dominantly from the electric double layer capacitance (EDLC). Further, the assembled symmetric supercapacitor yielded a wide voltage window of 1.8 V, and a good cyclic stability with 91% capacitance retention after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles at 20 mA·cm−2. Overall, the employed composite strategy enabled the good dispersion of the MXene flakes on the surface of the flexible substrate. Meanwhile, the large number of functional groups (-OH, -F, etc.) on the surface of Ti3C2Tx MXene interacted with the carbon layer through hydrogen bonding effects, which endows it as an ideal electrode for electrochemical capacitors.

title: Tailoring interlayer spacing of Ti3C2Tx MXene with organic acid doped polyaniline and polypyrrole for more stable supercapacitors
authors: João V.M. Lima, Hugo G. Lemos, Rafael A. Silva, Jéssica H.H. Rossato, Miguel H. Boratto, Carlos F.O. Graeff
journal: Journal of Alloys and Compounds Communications
conclusion: In this work, we fabricated aqueous inks by incorporating water-dispersible PANI and PPy doped with DBSA organic acid to Ti3 C2 Tx for SCs. XRD showed that the CPs were allocated among MXene sheets. XPS analysis indicated an increased protonation of the CPs, suggesting that the functional groups of Ti3 C2 Tx may act as dopants for the polymers. The increased interlayer spacing and enhanced conductivity of Ti3 C2 Tx /CP improved electrochemical performance, as showed by measurements at a three-electrode setup. Optimal concentration of CPs (10 wt%) increased capacitance from 175 F g−1 (Ti3 C2 Tx ) to 255 F g−1 (Ti3 C2 Tx /PANI) and 270 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 (Ti3 C2 Tx /PPy). Investigations of energy storage mechanisms by Trasatti and Dunn's methods revealed that CPs increase capacitive contribution in terms of surface capacitance, indicating a larger exposed electroactive area, faster electron transfer, and smaller diffusion distance of the ions when compared to pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . Additionally, Ti3 C2 Tx /PPy showed larger contribution of pseudocapacitance feature, attributed to the favourable redox reactions of the CP at the optimized potential window. Similar trend was observed by the symmetric solid-state SCs based on Ti3 C2 Tx and Ti3 C2 Tx /CPs electrodes, in which PANI and PPy increased specific capacitance in 72 % and 208 %, respectively. Cycling stability of the devices also exhibited an impressive capacitance retention after 5000 CV cycles of 100 % and 98 % for PANI and PPy, respectively, against only 88 % of the pristine device. These results indicate that the polymeric nanoparticles doped with the DBSA organic acid acted as effective interlayer spacers, preventing MXene re-stacking during the charge and discharge cycles. In conclusion, we demonstrate a viable method to fabricated efficient and more stable Ti3 C2 Tx /CPs electrodes for SCs. The use of water-dispersible PANI and PPy as additives, besides increasing capacitance and stability of SCs, provides an environmentally and “green” alternative for the device assemble, in addition to reduced costs. abstract: Polyaniline (PANI) and polypyrrole (PPy) are promising for use as spacers materials to prevent re-stacking of MXene layers and to increase their electrochemical properties. However, these conducting polymers (CPs) may undergo hydrolysis during long charge-discharge cycles. The use of organic acids to dope CPs may lead to better polymer cyclic stability. However, PANI and PPy used as spacers in MXene are mainly doped with inorganic acids. Herein, we applied dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid (DBSA) doped PANI and PPy as effective spacers and additional pseudocapacitance agents for Ti3C2Tx MXene. Taking advantage of the favored dispersibility of the functional inks in water, we easily prepared the electrodes by drop casting. X-ray diffractograms confirmed that the CPs are effectively allocated among MXenes sheets. Spectroscopic analyses showed that the functional groups of Ti3C2Tx may work as effective dopants for PANI and PPy. The enhanced interlayer spacing of MXenes and increased high conductivity of CPs boosted capacitance from 175 F g−1 (Ti3C2Tx) to 255 F g−1 and 270 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 after addition of 10 wt% of PANI and PPy, respectively, at a three-electrode setup. The Dunn’s and Trasatti’s methods showed greater pseudocapacitive contribution after addition of PPy and greater double layer capacitance contribution after addition of PANI. Similarly, symmetric solid-state SCs exhibited enhancement of 72 % in specific capacitance for Ti3C2Tx/PANI and 208 % for Ti3C2Tx/PPy, when compared to pristine Ti3C2Tx. SCs based on Ti3C2Tx/CPs also yielded outstanding capacitance retentions (>98 %) after 5000 cycles against only 88 % of the Ti3C2Tx pristine device. These results indicate that the organic doped-CPs modulated interlayer spacing of MXene sheets, preventing their re-stacking during the charge and discharge cycles. Finally, the aqueous Ti3C2Tx/CPs based inks is an eco-friendly and low-cost alternative to fabricate SCs with enhanced capacitance and stability.

title: High-performance flexible supercapacitor based on PEDOT:PSS wrapped delaminated Ti3C2Tx composite: Experimental and DFT validation
authors: Gourab Nandy, Swati Shaw, Subhradip Ghosh, Ashok Kumar Dasmahapatra
conclusion: In this work, we have adequately synthesized delaminated Ti3 C2 Tx (d-Ti3 C2 Tx ) by a low-cost method, integrating the mixed acid etching method followed by DMSO intercalation. Furthermore, PP/d-Ti3 C2 Tx binary composites have been prepared with different ratios by the solvent mixing method and coated on the flexible activated carbon cloth. The conformation of the prepared composites was validated by several characterization techniques such as XRD, RAMAN, UV–Vis, FTIR, FESEM, EDS, and FETEM. In three electrodes electrochemical performance PP, and d-Ti3 C2 Tx with a ratio 1:2 respectively (P1M2) exhibit great results in 1 M H2 SO4 electrolyte. The P1M2 electrode shows a brilliant specific capacitance value of 741. 23 F g−1 at a scan rate of 5 mV/s, and 718. 67 F g−1 at a current density of 3. 5 A g−1 . P1M2 electrode shows brilliant E s 35. 93 Whkg−1 (at P s 1049. 90 Wkg-1 ), and 5. 68 Whkg−1 (at Ps 5996. 48 Wkg-1 ). Detailed DFT calculations confirmed that the charge transfer is doubled in the case of PEDOT:PSS@Ti3 C2 Tx in comparison to PEDOT@Ti3 C2 Tx . The charges flow from PEDOT and MXene to PSS. Consequently, PSS possesses the electron-rich region. The DFT calculated solar absorption spectrum for PEDOT:PSS, Ti3 C2 Tx , and PEDOT:PSS@Ti3 C2 Tx agree very well with the experiments. Such excellent agreement substantiates the proposed morphology of the composite i.e. PEDOT wrapped d-Ti3 C2 Tx , aided by multiple PSS carrier pathways. For a flexible and wearable electronic device, we prepared a P1M2-P1M2 SSC and a P1M2-rGO ASC assembly using a gel electrolyte (PVA-H2 SO4 ). The highest specific capacitance has been achieved at 260. 23 F g−1 (at 0. 5 A g−1 ) by the P1M2-P1M2 SSC device; whereas P1M2-rGO ASC has a value of 176. 46 F g−1 (at 0. 1 A g−1 ). The specific energy (specific power) was from 13. 01 Whkg−1 (600 Wkg-1 ) to 2. 63 Whkg−1 (12035 Wkg-1 ) for the SSC device; and from 35. 29 Whkg−1 (240 Wkg-1 ) to 26. 22 Whkg−1 (1200 Wkg-1 ) for ASC device. Both SSC and ASC exhibit excellent performance over various bending and twisting cycles, ASC can operate in a larger potential window and longer durations at low current regions. Moreover, the ASC device shows excellent specific capacitance retention of 89.03 % for 5000 GCD cycles. Subsequently, a red LED was glowed using three ASC devices in series. Hence the P1M2 electrode possesses enormous potential to be used in portable and wearable electronics. CRediT authorship contribution statement Gourab Nandy: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Validation, Methodology, Formal analysis, Data curation, Conceptualization. Swati Shaw: Writing – original draft, Validation, Investigation, Formal analysis, Data curation, Conceptualization. Subhradip Ghosh: Writing – review & editing, Validation, Supervision, Software,
abstract: Exploring new electrode materials with cyclic stability and energy storage capacity is crucial for high-performance energy storage in portable electronics. Herein, we present PEDOT:PSS (PP)/delaminated MXene (d-Ti3C2Tx) binary nanocomposites for electrode material for flexible supercapacitor (FSC). PP/d-Ti3C2Tx (1:2 wt ratio, P1M2) on activated carbon cloth results in an excellent specific capacitance of 718.67 F g−1 at a current density of 3.5 A g−1 in 1 M H2SO4. PEDOT chains wrap the d-Ti3C2Tx nanosheets by an opposite electrostatic interaction, while PSS chains act as web-like carrier pathways between two adjacent nanosheets. First principle DFT simulations demonstrate that charge storage in PEDOT:PSS@Ti3C2Tx is enhanced compared to PEDOT@Ti3C2Tx, which describes the effect of PSS chains in the composite. Computationally obtained absorption spectra align well with experimental results, validating the proposed morphology. To employ the P1M2 electrode for FSC, P1M2-P1M2 symmetric solid-state supercapacitor (SSC) and P1M2-rGO asymmetric solid-state supercapacitor (ASC) have been fabricated using 1 M PVA-H2SO4 gel electrolyte. P1M2-P1M2 SSC and P1M2-rGO ASC exhibit a high specific capacitance of 260.23 F g−1 (0.5 A g−1) and 176.46 F g−1 (0.1 A g−1) receptively. Larger potential window, excellent specific capacitance retention of ∼89 % for 5000 GCD cycles, and great performance retention over the bending and twisting conditions make the ASC device a marvelous candidate for the portable energy storage device. The ASC device shows change in specific energy (specific power) from 35.29 W h kg−1 (240 W kg−1) to 26.22 W h kg−1 (1200 W kg−1). An assembly of three such ASC devices glows a red LED for ∼2 min.

title: Fabrication of a flexible asymmetric supercapacitor using molybdenum selenide and titanium carbide mxene (MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx) nanocomposite on carbon cloth
authors: Kuppu Sakthi Velu, Sonaimuthu Mohandoss, Yong Rok Lee, Jeong Hyun Seo
conclusion: Herein, flower-like MoSe2 -decorated Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheets were successfully prepared via a simple hydrothermal method and applied on CC for ASC studies. The as-prepared MoSe2 and Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited flower- and sheet-like surface morphologies, confirmed via FE-SEM and HR-TEM image analysis. FE-SEM of the MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite exhibited flower-like MoSe2 petals decorating the sheets-like Ti3 C2 Tx surfaces, with TEM images clearly showing the nanostructure grains embedded on the Ti3 C2 Tx sheets. AFM analysis provided insights into the surface topography, revealing the hexagonal symmetry of MoSe2 nanoflowers, the honeycomb lattice structure of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets, and the successful decoration of MoSe2 on the Ti3 C2 Tx sheets in the composite. XPS analysis confirmed the chemical composition and bonding states, confirming the presence of Mo, Se, Ti, C, O, and F elements in the nanocomposite. The XRD pattern confirmed the 1T-phase or metallic nature of MoSe2 -decorated Ti3 C2 Tx . Raman spectra further highlighted the specific phases of the MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite. The ASC studies using MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx //KOH//AC nanostructured electrode achieved an excellent specific capacitance 660 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 current density, with an energy density of 33.3 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 1683 W kg−1 . EIS analysis indicated enhanced electrical conductivity and charge transfer capabilities, further confirming the suitability of the material for energy storage applications. Cycle stability tests demonstrated the outstanding durability of the MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite, with a capacity retention of 97.35 % after 10,000 cycles at a high current density of 10 A g−1 . The solid-state supercapacitor device assembled with the MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite demonstrated a specific capacitance of 223.12 F g⁻1 , an energy density of 7.74 Wh kg⁻1 , and a power density of 292.60 W kg⁻1 . It exhibited a capacity retention of 96.04 % and a Coulombic efficiency of 98.69 % over 10,000 cycles. The MoSe2 @Ti3 C2 Tx nanocomposite emerged as a highly promising material with superior morphological, structural, and electrochemical characteristics. Its unique combination of flower-like MoSe2 and Ti3 C2 Tx sheets, along with excellent cycle stability, underscores its potential for practical and high-performance applications in energy storage, particularly in supercapacitors. CRediT authorship contribution statement Kuppu Sakthi Velu: Writing – original draft. Sonaimuthu Mohandoss: Writing - review & editing. Yong Rok Lee: Supervision, Writing - review & editing. Jeong Hyun Seo: Supervision, Writing - review & editing.
abstract: Herein, we developed 1T-phase flower-like molybdenum selenide (MoSe2) decorated on titanium carbide MXene (Ti3C2Tx) nanocomposites using a simple hydrothermal method and hydrofluoric acid etching. The as-prepared MoSe2 nanoflower, Ti3C2Tx sheet, and MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx nanocomposite were comprehensively characterized using various techniques, including FE-SEM with EDS mapping, TEM, XPS, and XRD analysis. FE-SEM images revealed a captivating flower-like nanocomposite structure, where the hexagonal lattice of the MoSe2 monolayer is skillfully enveloped within the Ti3C2Tx sheet, forming an esthetically complex architecture. EDS mapping confirmed the presence of Mo, Se, Ti, C, O, and F in the MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx nanocomposite. TEM images displayed the nanoflower structure enveloped in the sheet-like MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx nanocomposite. XRD patterns confirmed the hexagonal crystalline structure of MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx. The electrochemical performance of MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx as a symmetric supercapacitor surpassed that of the pristine MoSe2 nanoflower and Ti3C2Tx sheet. Moreover, the asymmetric supercapacitor configuration, comprising CC/MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx//activated carbon/CC electrodes, demonstrated exceptional electrochemical performance, delivering a specific capacitance of 660 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1, alongside an energy density of 33.3 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 1683 W kg−1. The MoSe2@Ti3C2Tx nanocomposite, coated onto carbon cloth as the working electrode in a solid-state supercapacitor device, achieved a specific capacitance of 223.12 F g−1, an energy density of 7.74 Wh kg−1, and a power density of 292.60 W kg−1.

title: Flexible, temperature-tolerant supercapacitor based on Ti3C2Tx MXene in ionic liquid gel electrolyte
authors: Jingdi Shang, Libo Wang, Ying Gao, Ji’a Yang, Qixun Xia, Qianku Hu, Aiguo Zhou, Bo Wang
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  A simple PVDF-HFP-EMIMBF 4 gel polymer electrolyte was fabricated using the casting method, and a solid-state supercapacitor was assembled with Ti 3 C 2 T x as the electrode material. The ionic polymer electrolyte broadens the operating window of MXene-based capacitors, enhancing its energy and power densities. Moreover, the EMIMBF₄-PVDF-HFP gel polymer electrolyte extends the operational range of the designed capacitor, allowing it to maintain a high specific capacitance at 100 °C, making it suitable for extreme conditions. The capacitor also exhibits stable capacitance under torsional and repeated bending conditions. More importantly, the constructed device demonstrates excellent specific capacitance at 180° bending and 360° twisting angles and retains remarkable stability after 1000 bending cycles at 180°. These findings confirm its potential to enhanced energy density by extending the voltage window of flexible solid-state energy devices.
abstract: Due to its unique structure and performance, Ti3C2Tx has been widely investigated as an electrode material for flexible energy storage devices using hydrogel as a solid electrolyte. The composition and structure of hydrogels determine their poor performance at high temperatures and there is little research on MXene flexible devices at high temperature. In this work, we designed a method for preparing capacitors with Ti3C2Tx as the electrode material and ionic liquid as the electrolyte. By leveraging the high permeability of ionic polymer solution, a seamless electrode-electrolyte interface is constructed. The device can achieve a maximum capacitance of 173.8 mF cm−2 at a 5 mV s−1 scan rate, with a maximum specific energy density and power density of 96.57 μWh cm−2 and 1.74 mW cm−2, respectively. The capacitor retains 89.5 % of its initial capacitance after 20,000 cycles, demonstrating excellent cycle stability. Importantly, the supercapacitor can operate at 100 °C with a specific capacitance of 278.66 mF cm−2. In addition, the designed device can retains 100 % or more of its capacitance even after 1000 cycles of 180° bending，demonstrating robust mechanical performance. This work provides a reference for studying the application of MXene in high-temperature flexible supercapacitor.

title: Integrating V-doped CoP on Ti3C2Tx MXene-incorporated hollow carbon nanofibers as a freestanding positrode and MOF-derived carbon nanotube negatrode for flexible supercapacitors
authors: Ishwor Pathak, Bipeen Dahal, Debendra Acharya, Kisan Chhetri, Alagan Muthurasu, Yagya Raj Rosyara, Taewoo Kim, Syafiqah Saidin, Tae Hoon Ko, Hak Yong Kim
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this work, unique nanostructures of vanadium-doped cobalt phosphide nanorods uniformly anchored over Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene-integrated hollow carbon nanofibers and cobalt nanoparticles distributed carbon nanotubes at carbon nanofibers were judiciously designed. The freestanding V-CoP@MX/HCF (positrode) and Co-CNT@CNF (negatrode) exhibit superior specific capacitances of 1896.8 F g −1 and 405.5 F g −1 , respectively, at 1 A g −1 and a high cycling life. The as-developed flexible asymmetric device (V-CoP@MX/HCF//Co-CNT@CNF) displays a desired energy density of 72.4 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 800.12 W kg −1 and demonstrate superior cycling performance over 10,000 cycles. The device is adequately flexible and displays a stable performance at different bending angles. Additionally, the two ASCs in series connection lit up a 1 W LED for ∼ 10 min, demonstrating the device’s application potential. Overall, this work highlights unique engineering approaches to rationally design novel and efficient freestanding positive and negative electrodes for supercapacitors, which will significantly contribute to the rising demand for flexible energy storage devices.
abstract: Novel architectural electrode materials that are freestanding and exhibit improved electrochemical performances in flexible asymmetric supercapacitors are urgently needed; however, designing these materials is challenging. Herein, a Ti3C2TX MXene-aligned hollow carbon fiber (MX/HCF) is engineered and vanadium-doped cobalt phosphide nanorod arrays are grown on it (V-CoP@MX/HCF) and applied for supercapacitor positrode. V doping modulates the surface structure and electronic environment of CoP nanorods grown over conductive and flexible MX/HCFs. As expected, the optimized V-CoP@MX/HCF exhibits a better electrochemical performance (1896.8Fg−1) than that of CoP@MX/HCF and CoP@HCF. For the negative electrode, zeolitic imidazolate framework-67 (ZIF-67) grown on electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) fibers is converted to cobalt nanoparticle-encapsulated nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes at carbon nanofibers (Co-CNT@CNF) by a simple heat treatment without the burden of external catalysts and reducing gases. The as-designed freestanding Co-CNT@CNF delivers a specific capacitance of 405.5Fg−1 with superior cycling stability. A flexible asymmetric supercapacitor (V-CoP@MX/HCF//Co-CNT@CNF) is designed that unveil remarkable electrochemical properties, such as a high energy density of 72.4 Wh kg−1 at 800.12 W kg−1 and good capacitance retention (91.4 %) after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles. Furthermore, the device can maintain a consistent performance regardless of the bending degree. More importantly, this work provides new opportunities to rationally design novel freestanding cathodes and anodes for high-performance flexible asymmetric supercapacitors.

title: Ti3C2Tx MXene based hybrid electrodes for wearable supercapacitors with varied deformation capabilities
authors: Jingmin Zhang, Degang Jiang, Leiping Liao, Liang Cui, Rongkun Zheng, Jingquan Liu
conclusion: In summary, we have demonstrated a simple template method for the preparation of the arbitrary-shaped and N-doping MGC hybrid foam through the procedures of “dip-coating”, reduction, freeze-drying and annealing treatment. Significantly, the commercial MF cannot only works as cost-efficient and arbitrary-shaped template, but also introduces the heteroatom nitrogen into the Ti3 C2 Tx /rGO nanosheets. Because of the interconnected and alternating Ti3 C2 Tx /rGO cellular walls, the resultant N-doped MGC-500 hybrid foam incorporates good compressibility and electrochemical performance, making it an ideal material as freestanding electrode. Thanks to the enhancement of PVA-H2 SO4 electrolyte, the as-prepared SSC device showed stable capacitance at different compressive states. In addition, the compressed SSC still exhibited good flexibility and stability at different bending or twist angles. In a word, this template method for fabrication of SSC based on MGC hybrid foam may pave the way for the future development of scalable, arbitrary-shaped and free-standing electrode materials with multiple deformation capabilities.
abstract: Free-standing electrodes with high electrical conductivity, good deformability and durability are critical for flexible electronics, especially in field of wearable energy storage devices. Here, three dimensional (3D) Ti3C2Tx MXene/reduced graphene oxide (rGO)/carbon (MGC-500) hybrid electrode fabricated by the simple template method is presented. Commercial melamine foam (MF) worked as template not only enables the Ti3C2Tx/rGO nanosheets to form a porous architecture, but also introduces the heteroatom nitrogen into the Ti3C2Tx/rGO nanosheets during the annealing process. The as-prepared MGC-500 electrode shows a gravimetric capacitance of 276F g−1 at a current density of 0.5 A g−1. When the MGC-500 hybrid electrodes are assembled into an all solid-state supercapacitor, it shows a stable electrochemical performance at different compressive strains. Notably, we find that the MGC-500 foam electrode coated with PVA-H2SO4 gel electrolyte can be compressed into flexible film at 80% of compression. And the supercapacitor devices assembled by the film also exhibit stable capacitance under different modes of deformations such as bending and twist. The developed template approach offers a simple strategy to fabricate free-standing Ti3C2Tx MXene electrode for energy storage devices that can withstand varied deformations, and also can be extended to other members of the large MXene family.

title: Designing an electrochemical energy storage device using recycled Ti3C2Tx MXene and reduced graphene oxide spent wastewater adsorbents
authors: Marcelo A. Andrade, Olivier Crosnier, Patrik Johansson, Thierry Brousse
conclusion: This study expands the concept of directly repurposing spent wastewater adsorbents into functional energy storage devices through the electrochemical behavior of various heavy metal cations in various electrolytes. Our findings demonstrate that the adsorption of redox-active heavy metals brings tunable faradaic contributions that synergistically merge with the pristine capacitance, improving the total capacities. Beyond the initial proof-of-concept, we demonstrate how newly explored adsorbents and adsorbates, including Pb2+ , Cu2+ , and multi-cation combinations, such as Hg2+ and Cu2+ , significantly expand the tunability of redox activity of recycled rGO and MXene-based electrodes, with the former being superior for both adsorption of Cu2+ cations and as electrodes. Furthermore, the coupling of different adsorbed cations enables the tuning of the voltage plateau, and we also present the assembly and evaluation of full cells using recycled metal-loaded adsorbents as both positive and negative electrode materials. The unique electrochemistry of each cation is also determined by the choice of electrolyte, influencing how effectively the redox activity can be used. Furthermore, the capacity fading, caused by cation dissolution, is also electrolyte-dependent and improved upon by multiple and quite different types of aqueous electrolytes, although not yet completely mitigated. Overall, this study paves the way for a new class of multifunctional materials derived from environmental waste streams, offering both ecological remediation and alternative energy solutions.
