Olivier Crosnier: Writing – review & editing, Supervision, Conceptualization. Patrik Johansson: Writing – review & editing, Validation. Thierry Brousse: Writing – review & editing, Supervision, Project administration, Conceptualization.
abstract: This study presents an end-to-end approach for recycling hazardous waste heavy-metal-loaded adsorbents into electrode materials for electrochemical energy storage. Using reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene as adsorbents for Hg²⁺, Cu²⁺, and Pb²⁺ from model wastewater solutions, we demonstrate their successful transformation into redox-active electrodes without any additional treatment. The recycled electrodes present superior capacity as compared to their pristine counterparts, while introducing distinct reversible redox features. Ultimately, the different recycled materials were assembled in full cell configurations, combining different metal-loaded adsorbents, yielding synergistic redox plateaus and an up to 50 % enhancement in the initial energy storage capacity, depending on the metal pair and electrolyte used. The versatility of this recycling strategy was demonstrated across three aqueous electrolytes, including a water-in-salt electrolyte, revealing tunable redox behavior dependent on both metal and electrolyte characteristics. Furthermore, using a more complex model wastewater solution, containing two different metal cations, leads to a multi-contaminant adsorbent that exhibits additive electrochemical responses, thereby establishing proof-of-concept for the reuse of real-world wastewater adsorbents into energy storage devices.

title: Butanedioic acid unlock shelf-stable Ti3C2Tx (MXene) dispersions and their electrochemical performance in supercapacitor
authors: Jai Kumar, Razium Ali Soomro, Baomin Fan, Jiayi Tan, Ning Sun, Bin Xu
conclusion: A chemically modified MXene nanosheet covered with succinic acid has been developed. This nanosheet exhibits exceptional antioxidation properties in aqueous solutions. Succinic acid effectively filled the reactive sites of MXene nanosheets by chemical bonding, hence preventing aqueous and oxygen assaults. The examination of the ultraviolet-visible (UV–Vis.) spectrum indicates that the impact of SSA on the water-based dispersion of Ti3 C2 Tx (0.05 mg mL−1 ) relies on its concentration. The antioxidant activity is maximally achieved when the concentration of SSA added to the dispersion reaches 1 mg mL−1 . After being exposed for 42 days, the MXene dispersion showed no signs of oxidation, and a time constant of 243 days was found by fitting first-order reaction kinetics. An electrochemical study demonstrates that the Ti3 C2 Tx membrane electrode, following 42 days of SSA protection, retains exceptional electrochemical performance. In addition, multi-scale simulation results show that SSA tends to be adsorbed on the edges and basal surface defects of Ti3 C2 Tx . Electron transfer occurs between the O atom on the carboxylic acid carbonyl group (-COOH) and the Ti atom at the defect site, which makes SSA chemically adsorbed on MXene oxidation-sensitive sites. Therefore, the addition of succinic acid functionalized modification can significantly prolong the lifespan of MXene nanosheets and fully satisfy the needs of a new MXene water-based solution, making it suitable for future applications. Razium Soomro: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Visualization, Validation. Jai Kumar: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Methodology, Investigation, Data curation, Conceptualization. Jiayi Tan: Methodology, Formal analysis, Data curation, Conceptualization. Baomin Fan: Writing – original draft, Software, Investigation.
abstract: MXene experiences significant oxidation and gradual deterioration in aqueous media due to its inadequate chemical stability, which hinders its further advancement. This study presents a simple and effective approach to prevent the degradation of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets in aqueous media by chemically encapsulating with butanedioic acid (succinic acid (SSA)). Specifically, the impact of pH and antioxidant content on the rate of oxidation of Ti3C2Tx is investigated together with their electrochemical behavior at different intervals. The research demonstrates that the oxidation rate of MXene must be prevented at a suitable concentration of antioxidants; higher doses of antioxidants cause aggregation, while lower concentrations accelerate the oxidation process. Furthermore, fluctuations in pH levels within the dispersion indicate that under acidic conditions, MXene experiences a greater level of oxidation as a result of elevated proton reactivity, which ultimately leads to material degradation. On the other hand, alkaline environments tend to reduce oxidative reactions, leading to increased stability of MXene. Consequently, MXene-SSA can demonstrate long-term stability in water for up to 35 weeks. The electrochemical properties of SSA-encapsulated MXene sheets are assessed as a supercapacitor electrode throughout a time gradient. In comparison to fresh MXene (299 F g−1 at 1 A g−1), the specific capacitances of SSA-protected MXene (321 F g−1 at 1 A g−1) remain unchanged after a long time. Based on DFT calculations, it has been observed that succinic acid creates beneficial hydrogen bonding interactions with Ti sites that possess a lower coordination number, hence improving the stability of Ti3C2Tx.

title: Heterostructured bimetallic–sulfide@layered Ti3C2Tx–MXene as a synergistic electrode to realize high-energy-density aqueous hybrid-supercapacitor
authors: Muhammad Sufyan Javed, Xiaofeng Zhang, Salamat Ali, Abdul Mateen, Muhammad Idrees, Muhammad Sajjad, Saima Batool, Awais Ahmad, Muhammad Imran, Tayyaba Najam, Weihua Han
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In summary, we have successfully embedded NCS nanoflowers into exfoliated Ti 3 C 2 T  x  –MXene nanosheets through a facile hydrothermal process to build a heterostructure NCS@MXene composite electrode. The nanoflowers of NCS were uniformly dispersed over the MXene layers and formed a sandwich-like structure. An optimized HS−NCS@MXene sample exhibits a remarkable capacitance/capacity of 2637 F g –1 (1582 C g –1 ) at 2.5 A g –1 with stable cycling life (96%) over 10,000 cycles. The assembled HS−NCS@MXene//AC–AHSC can operate at a broad potential range of 1.6 V and deliver a high capacitance 226 F g –1 at 1.5 A g –1 with stable cyclic life (92%) up to 20,000 cycles. Moreover, the HS−NCS@MXene//AC–AHSC also possesses the highest energy density of 80 Wh kg –1 at a power density of 1196 W kg –1 , exceeding the recently published similar work. The excellent results were verified by DFT calculations, which suggest that the conductivity of HS−NCS@MXene is better than pristine MXene and NCS. The synergistic effects of NCS and MXene enable the HS−NCS@MXene composite to deliver outstanding electrochemical performance for AHSCs.
abstract: Aqueous hybrid supercapacitors (AHSCs) exhibit promising electrochemical performance with long cyclic stability and high power density. However, the low-energy density restricted their development to commercialization. To improve the energy density, we proposed a heterostructured (HS) composite of nickel–cobalt–sulfide (NCS) nanoflowers embedded in exfoliated Ti3C2Tx−MXene layers (HS−NCS@MXene). The NCS nanoflowers were uniformly dispersed inside the MXene layers and formed a sandwich-like structure. The HS−NCS@MXene exhibited remarkable pseudocapacitive performance in a three-electrode system. The capacitance can reach 2637 F g−1 (1582 C g−1) at 2.5 A g−1 with stable cycling life over 10,000 cycles and retained 96% capacity of the initial value. Post−mortem investigations confirmed that the charge storage mechanism in HS−NCS@MXene composite is a combination of Faradic and electrochemical double-layer storage. An AHSC was assembled by coupling the HS−NCS@MXene as a positive electrode and activated carbon as a negative electrode (HS−NCS@MXene//AC–AHSC). The HS−NCS@MXene//AC–AHSC can operate in a potential range up to 1.6 V and deliver a high capacitance of 226 F g−1 at 1.5 A g−1 with stable cyclic life (92%) up to 20,000 cycles. Moreover, the HS−NCS@MXene//AC−AHSC also possessed a high energy density of 80 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1196 W kg−1, which exceeds most recently published works. The synergistic effect of NCS and MXene enables the HS−NCS@MXene composite to deliver outstanding electrochemical performance for AHSCs.

title: Cellulose nanofiber/MXene (Ti3C2Tx)/liquid metal film as a highly performance and flexible electrode material for supercapacitors
authors: Tao Yuan, Zhen Zhang, Qian Liu, Xiu-Tong Liu, Shao-Qu Tao, Chun-li Yao
conclusion: In summary, this paper introduces the CNF/MXene/GI composite films with high capacitance and mechanical flexibility. The CNF/MXene/GI films exhibit a notable areal specific capacitance of 871.3 mF cm−2 at 1 mA cm−2 , along with exceptional cycling stability (96.9 % capacitance retention after 2000 cycles), thus demonstrating their potential as a promising electrode material for supercapacitors. Moreover, when the CNF/MXene/GI films were employed as electrodes in the supercapacitor, a high areal capacitance of 188.2 mF cm−2 at 5 mA cm−2 was achieved, accompanied by satisfactory electrical stability. Furthermore, the supercapacitor demonstrated an areal energy density of 106.7 μWh∙cm−2 at an areal power density of 420 μW∙cm−2 , while maintaining good cycle stability (83.7 % retention after 5000 cycles). In this work, a supercapacitor electrode material with high capacitance and mechanical flexibility was demonstrated by adding liquid metal to the CNF matrix and combining it with MXene. As spacers, CNF and GI effectively separate adjacent MXene sheets, increase MXene's ion-accessible surface area, and provide a rich channel for ion diffusion. GI acts as a bridge between the MXene lamella, making the temporal structure of the material more complete, overcoming the self-stacking phenomenon of MXene films, and improving the electron transport rate. This study presents a promising approach towards the advancement of cellulose-based flexible electrodes, while concurrently propelling the progress of flexible supercapacitors characterized by high storage capacity and exceptional mechanical properties. CRediT authorship contribution statement Tao Yuan: Writing – review & editing, Writing – original draft, Software, Resources, Data curation. Zhen Zhang: Data curation. Qian Liu: Writing – review & editing. Xiu-Tong Liu: Formal analysis. Shao-Qu Tao: Data curation. Chun-li Yao: Writing – review & editing.
abstract: In recent times, there has been significant interest in the utilization of cellulose nanofiber (CNF) films as the foundation for supercapacitors due to their three-dimensional structure, flexibility and eco-friendliness. An ultrasonic and vacuum filtration method was used to prepare a hybrid film consisting of MXene (Ti3C2Tx), CNF and liquid metal (LM). The combination of CNF and LM with MXene produces a porous structure with higher electrical conductivity, which facilitates the transportation of ions and electrons within the composition and confers the material with heightened electrochemical properties. The CNF/MXene/LM electrode has a significant area capacitance of 871.3 mF cm−2 at a current density of 5 mA cm−2. The hybrid film demonstrates excellent stability, maintaining a high conductivity of 546.4 S∙cm−1 and retaining 96.9 % capacitance after 2000 cycles at a current density of 10 mA cm−2. By utilizing the thin film as an electrode, a high-performance quasi-solid supercapacitor was fabricated, with a remarkably thin thickness of only 0.319 mm. Supercapacitors show exceptional electrical properties, including a surface-specific capacitance of 188.2 mF cm−2 at a current density of 5 mA cm−2. This study indicates that flexible electrodes made from cellulose nanofiber have extensive potential in the realm of supercapacitors.

title: Supercapacitor featuring Ti3C2Tx MXene electrode: Nanoarchitectonics and electrochemical performances in aqueous and non-aqueous electrolytes
authors: Anu M A, Merin Tomy, Manimehala U, Xavier T S
conclusion: In this study, we effectively synthesised Ti3 C2 Tx MXene by the HCl+LiF etching method. The successful synthesis is confirmed by XRD, FESEM, FTIR, and XPS. The Brunauer-Emmett Teller (BET) method is used to analyse the synthesised material's surface area and pore size, which were found to be 42.53 m2 /g and 37.37 nm respectively. As a result, there are more active reaction sites and improved ion and electron transport, boosting electrochemical performance. A deeper comprehension of the electrode's electrochemical behaviour is provided by the Dunns technique, which aids to determine capacitive contributions to the overall charge storage. At a scan rate of 5 mV/s, the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene electrode shows a specific capacitance of 212 F/g in an aqueous H2 SO4 electrolyte and 299 F/g in an aqueous H3 PO4 electrolyte. The predominant charge storage method for Ti3 C2 Tx MXene is still cation intercalation without redox peaks. The specific capacitance of a symmetric device with Ti3 C2 Tx MXene electrodes in a 1 M H3 PO4 and H2 SO4 electrolyte is 151 F/g and 81 F/g, respectively, when operated at a current density of 0.8 A/g. A very reversible charge-discharge process and significant coulomb efficiency are indicated by nearly similar charge-discharge cycles. The SC prototype exhibits cyclic stability of 94% and 95% in H2 SO4 and H3 PO4 aqueous electrolyte respectively showing the exceptional stability of the electrodes and electrolyte. Its ability to maintain mass-specific capacitance over time signifies its maturity and effectiveness, facilitating its widespread adoption and accelerating the transition towards a sustainable energy future. The specific capacitance of a symmetric device with Ti3 C2 Tx MXene electrodes was measured as 203 F/g in a 1 M H₃PO₄ gel electrolyte and 141 F/g in a 1 M H₂SO₄ gel electrolyte, both at a current density of 1 A/g. The power density and energy density of a SC device using H3 PO4 gel electrolyte are 800 W/Kg and 72 Wh/kg, respectively. Therefore, symmetric SC devices with gel electrolytes have the potential to provide a large operational voltage window offering affordable solutions for dealing with upcoming energy challenges. Manimehala U: Writing – review & editing. Xavier T S: Validation, Supervision, Resources, Conceptualization.
abstract: Ti₃C₂Tx MXenes, synthesized via HCl+LiF etching, show promise as pseudocapacitive electrodes for electrochemical energy storage, addressing the low voltage limitation of aqueous supercapacitors (SCs). This study explores Ti₃C₂Tx MXene electrodes in aqueous and gel electrolytes, specifically H₂SO₄ and H₃PO₄. Electrochemical testing, based on Dunn's approach, confirms supercapacitor-like performance, with specific capacitances of 299 F/g in 1 M aqueous H₃PO₄ and 212 F/g in H₂SO₄ at a 5 mV/s scan rate. Remarkably, in symmetric SCs with 1 M H₃PO₄, Ti₃C₂Tx MXene retains 95% capacitance at 1 V after 25,000 cycles, demonstrating excellent stability. Additionally, Ti₃C₂Tx in a 1 M gel H₃PO₄ electrolyte achieves a higher energy density of 72 Wh/kg within a 1.6 V window than with gel H₂SO₄, highlighting the impact of electrolyte choice. These findings underscore MXenes' potential as stable, high-rate electrodes for sustainable supercapacitors.

title: Oxalate-assisted synthesis of MnCo2O4 nanoparticles on layered MXene (Ti3C2Tx) for supercapacitor application
authors: S. Emami, M. Hasheminiasari, S.M. Masoudpanah, R. Omrani, S.P. Ghaemi
conclusion: Through an oxalate-assisted hydrothermal method, the synthesis of MnCo2 O4 /MXene composites was achieved with different quantities of MXene nanosheets. By adding the MXene, the morphology was changed from columnar-like to a particular one in which the small MnCo2 O4 nanoparticles were crystallized and dispersed on the MXene nanosheets, leading to the increase of specific surface area from 13.5 to 53.3 m2 g−1 . The enhancement of specific capacitance from 1116 to 1500 F g−1 by combining the MnCo2 O4 with 25 wt% MXene was related to the morphological evolution and improvement of electrical conductivity. Furthermore, the MnCo2 O4 –25 wt% MXene//activated carbon capacitor showed a comparable energy storage capability, including an energy density of 43.5 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1411 W kg−1 . abstract: The synthesis of MnCo2O4/Ti3C2Tx composite powders was achieved through a hydrothermal method facilitated by oxalate assistance. To assess the influence of MXene levels (0, 25, and 50 wt%) on microstructure, structure, and electrochemical performance, modern characterization methods were applied in this study. The mixed manganese‑cobalt oxalates were precipitated on the layered MXene by adding a proper amount of oxalic acid to the Nitride solution. The MnCo2O4 nanoparticles were then crystallized by heat treatment at 450 °C for one hour in a nitrogen gas atmosphere. The pristine MnCo2O4 had a columnar-like morphology, which was transformed into a fine particulate microstructure by combining with MXene. These pristine MnCo2O4 powders indicated a higher specific capacitance of 1116 F g−1, significantly exceeding the 640.5 Fg−1 recorded for the pristine layered MXene. The Incorporation of 25 wt% layered MXene enhanced the specific capacitance to a remarkable 1500 Fg−1, attributed to its finer microstructure. Under a current rate of 1 Ag−1, the capacitor composed of MnCo₂O₄-25 wt% MXene//activated carbon achieved an energy density of 43.5 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1411 W kg−1.

title: Ultra-thin nanosheets of Ti3C2Tx MXene/MoSe2 nanocomposite electrode for asymmetric supercapacitor and electrocatalytic water splitting
authors: C. Arulkumar, R. Gandhi, S. Vadivel
conclusion: A one-step in-situ hydrothermal approach yielded a MoSe2 /MXene composite with good electrochemical characteristics. At 1 Ag−1 , the specific capacitance 1531.2 Fg−1 at 1 Ag−1 for the MoSe2 /MXene composite electrode) is superior to MXene and MoSe2 electrodes. MoSe2 nanosheets added to MXene's interlayer spacing increased its electroactive surface area, which was largely responsible for the improved electrochemical performance. Even after 10,000 recharging cycles, the completed ASC device provides 58.8 Whkg−1 of energy, 800.3 Wkg−1 of power, and 94.1% capacitance resiliency. Furthermore, the MoSe2 /MXene hybrid in both supercapacitor and HER has also shown improved cycling stabilities. Increases in conductivity, speed of charge transfer, and the abundance of active sites in conjunction with MXene and metal selenides for multimodal applications in energy storage and transformation are all likely due to strong interface contact between MoSe2 and MXene. CRediT authorship contribution statement C. Arulkumar: Conceptualization, Writing – original draft. R. Gandhi: Conceptualization, Writing – original draft. S. Vadivel: Writing – review & editing.
abstract: Nanohybrid anode materials for highly efficient asymmetric supercapacitors are developed with a hydrothermal approach using organ-like (Ti3C2Tx) MXene as a main basis. The MoSe2/Ti3C2Tx hybrid supercapacitor has a high specific capacitance of 1531.2 Fg−1 at 1 Ag−1 and a low potential of 200 mV at 10 mAg−1. Additionally, the Tafel slope of 37.7 mV dec−1 for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) makes this supercapacitor an excellent electrochemical performer. The supercapacitor with Ti3C2Tx/MoSe2nanohybrid as the positive electrode shows excellent performance. Even after 10,000 cycles, it retains a capacitance of 94.1% with a high current density of 5 Ag−1, a high specific energy of 58.8 Whkg−1 and a high specific power of 800.3 Wkg−1. In comparison with unmodified MoSe2, it increases conductivity, speed of charge transfer, and active sites which is explained by the strong interfacial connection between MXene and Ti3C2Tx crystals.

title: MXene/carboxymethylcellulose-polyaniline (Ti3C2Tx/CMC-PANI) film as flexible electrode for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitors
authors: Hanping Xu, Linlin Cui, Zijie Lei, Mincai Xu, Xiaojuan Jin
conclusion: 4  Conclusions  In summary, an ultrathin, porous and flexible Ti 3 C 2 T x /CMC-PANI film was successfully synthesized via a facile vacuum filtration process. Particularly, the introduction of CMC-PANI as the intercalator into the Ti 3 C 2 T x interlayer for conditioning Ti 3 C 2 T x flakes effectively alleviated the self-restacking problem of Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets, thus facilitating the diffusion and transport of ions. Moreover, the interwoven CMC-PANI connects horizontally adjacent Ti 3 C 2 T x nanosheets to establish interconnected electrical conductivity and ion channels, making the TCP film internal structure more uniformly and orderly, thereby achieving a high mechanical strength (≈ 35.6 MPa). The TCP-0.75 film electrode has a mass loading of about 5 mg cm −2 and can be used directly as an electrode for supercapacitors without any additives. Consequently, the TCP-0.75 film exhibits the largest area specific capacitance of 1161.4 mF cm −2 (812.9 mC cm −2 ) at 1 mA cm −2 , and a superior rate performance (maintains 58.4% of the initial value at 50 mA cm −2 ). Moreover, the fabricated asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device presents a high area energy density of 158.7 µW h cm −2 at a power density of 700.1 µW cm −2 , and good cycles stability (retention of 89.6% after 15,000 charging/discharging cycles). This rational design that balances flexibility and electrochemical performance provides a novel insight to address the inherent defects of MXene and further develop high-performance energy storage devices.
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) MXene (Ti3C2Tx) materials have received widespread attention as potential electrodes for supercapacitors due to their solution processability, metallic conductivity and excellent energy storage properties. Unfortunately, the self-stacking and interlayer interactions of Ti3C2Tx flakes cause them to acquire poor electrochemical characteristics. Herein, the interwoven carboxymethylcellulose-polyaniline (CMC-PANI) composites were prepared by in-situ polymerization of aniline on the surface of CMC, which was subsequently used as the intercalators to expand the layer spacing of Ti3C2Tx nanosheets via a facile self-assembly process. The interwoven CMC-PANI bridges horizontal Ti3C2Tx nanosheets to construct interconnected conductive and ion channels, making the internal structure of the Ti3C2Tx/CMC-PANI (TCP) film more uniformly and orderly, thereby achieving a high mechanical strength (≈ 35.6 MPa). Meanwhile, the TCP film exhibits a maximum area specific capacitance of 1161.4 mF cm−2 (812.9 mC cm−2) at 1 mA cm−2, and a superior rate performance (maintains 58.4% of the initial value at 50 mA cm−2). Moreover, the fabricated asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device presents a high area energy density of 158.7 µW h cm−2 at a power density of 700.1 µW cm−2 and good cycle stability (retention of 89.6% after 15,000 charging/discharging cycles). This rational design balancing flexibility and electrochemical performance provides a broadened idea to solve the inherent defects of MXene and further develop high performance energy storage devices.

title: Mg2+ induced Ti3C2Tx MXene@microfibrillated cellulose into composite aerogels in a framework of melamine sponge for high-rate performance supercapacitors
authors: Debin Cai, Shuai Wu, Li Guo, Yanzhong Wang
conclusion: In summary, a series of three-dimensional porous Mg-MFMX@MS composite aerogels were successfully prepared via the induced gelation of MXene@MFC in the framework of melamine sponge with Mg2+ as a cross-linking agent and microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) as an additive to regulate their structures. Three-dimensional porous MS is an ideal support to enhance the mechanical strength of Mg-MFMX@MS aerogels. The inserted Mg2+ not only induces the formation of MXene/MFC composite hydrogels, but also improves the interlayer spacing of Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets. As an additive, MFC can combine with Ti3 C2 Tx nanosheets to form hydrogen bonds, which can impede the restacking of MXene nanosheets and improve the mechanical stability of composite aerogels. The experimental results show that the Mg-MFMX composite aerogels are uniformly distributed in the framework of MS with high porosity and mass loading. At a scan rate of 10 mV s−1 , the prepared Mg-10%MFMX@MS aerogel showed the largest area capacitance of 685.77 m F cm−2 . Thanks to its three-dimensional structure, the areal capacitance is still 497.41 mF cm−2 at a high scan rate of 1000 mV s−1 , and the capacitance retention rate is 72.5 %, which is better than the previously reported MXene-based aerogels [19 ,42 ,45 ,63–65 ]. Furthermore, the energy density of the asymmetric supercapacitor assembled with activated carbon reaches up to 101.15 μWh cm−2 at a power density of 17,000 μW cm−2 , and the capacitance retention is up to 115 % after 10,000 cycles, indicating the superior stability. This article provides a simple approach for preparing MXene-based aerogels with 3D porous interconnected structure and high mechanical strength for high-rate performance supercapacitors. abstract: Inducing Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets to self-assemble into three-dimensional aerogels is an effective strategy to solve their accumulation and improve the performance of supercapacitors. However, MXene aerogels are prone to collapse in practical applications due to their low mechanical strength. Here, the low-cost melamine sponge (MS), which adsorbs Mg2+ ions on the skeleton surface serves as a support and induces the gelation of MXene nanosheets and microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) mixed solution to form composite hydrogels, and thereby obtaining MXene composite aerogels with high loading mass and mechanical strength. The experimental results show that the Mg-10%MFMX@MS aerogel has the largest area capacitance of 685.77 mF cm−2 at a scan rate of 10 mV s−1. Thanks to its excellent three-dimensional structure, even at a high scan rate of 1000 mV s−1, the area capacitance is still 497.41 mF cm−2, and the capacity retention rate is 72.53 %, showing high-rate performance. It is worth noting that the constructed asymmetric activated carbon supercapacitors achieved high energy densities of 128.78 μWh cm−2 and 101.15 μWh cm−2 at 850 μW cm−2 and 17,000 μW cm−2, respectively. In addition, the asymmetric supercapacitor has high cycling stability and a capacity retention rate of 115 % after 10,000 cycles. This work provides a feasible strategy for fabricating Ti3C2Tx MXene aerogels with high-rate performance and high strength.

title: Construction of high-performance solid-state asymmetric supercapacitor based on Ti3C2Tx MXene/CuS positive electrode and Fe2O3@rGO negative electrode
authors: Xiaobo Chen, Huiran Ge, Wen Yang, Jianli Liu, Peizhi Yang
conclusion: In summary, we have successfully fabricated asymmetrical supercapacitor devices composed of few-layered Ti3 C2 Tx MXene wrapped CuS nanosparticles as the positive electrode and Fe2 O3 @rGO electrode as the negative electrode by a cost-effective method. For as-synthesized MXene/CuS nanohybrids, the high conductivity few-layered Ti3 C2 Tx MXene sheets can construct a successive conductive network, while the CuS nanosparticles have abundant redox-active sites, ensuring the superb electrochemical performance of electrodes. As a result, an optimized MXene/CuS electrode exhibits a remarkable capacity/capacitance of 1541.6C g−1 (2569.3 F g−1 ) at 1 A g−1 with prominent stability (93.5 %) over 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . To improve the energy density of the asymmetrical supercapacitor, Fe2 O3 @rGO based negative electrode with excellent performance was fabricated. The Fe2 O3 @rGO negative electrode exhibits an excellent specific capacity of 255.6C g−1 at 1 A g−1 and long operational life retaining 92.8 % of the initial capacity after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . Further, the assembled solid-state supercapacitor of MXene/CuS//Fe2 O3 @rGO yielded an operating voltage window of 1.7 V, a specific capacity of 313.7C g−1 (184.5 F g−1 ) at 1 A g−1 , an extraordinary energy density of 74.1 Wh kg−1 at the power density of 849.8 W kg−1 , and stable cyclic life (91.3 % capacity retention) up to 10,000 cycles at 8 A g−1 . The demonstration of results not only demonstrate MXene/CuS and Fe2 O3 @rGO composites have great potential for electrodes in asymmetric supercapacitor but provides a novel perspective for rational design for 2D material-based composite for asymmetric supercapacitor applications. Jianli Liu: Experimental support, Correcting the manuscript. Peizhi Yang: Project administration, Writing - review & editing.
abstract: The reasonable and logical construction of electrode materials along with greater electrochemical features and solid architectural design is an effective strategy for boosting the electrochemical performance of supercapacitors. In this paper, Ti3C2Tx MXene/CuS composites have been synthesized using an electrostatic attraction connection of negatively charged 2D few-layered Ti3C2Tx MXene sheets with positively charged CuS nanoparticles and are investigated as an asymmetric supercapacitor active material. The addition of MXene enhances the conductivity and specific surface area of the MXene/CuS electrode compared to their individual components. The as-prepared MXene/CuS electrode exhibits a high specific capacity (1541.6C g−1 (2569.3 F g−1)) at 1 A g−1 and an excellent cycle performance with 93.5 % capacity retention after 10,000 cycles. Furthermore, Fe2O3 nanoparticles/reduced graphene oxide (rGO) nanosheets (Fe2O3@rGO) composite electrode is also produced. The designed Fe2O3@rGO negative electrode with a wide operation voltage window of 1.1 V can deliver a capacity of 255.6C g−1 at 1 A g−1. Ultimately, the MXene/CuS//Fe2O3@rGO device displays energy density of 74.1 Wh kg−1 and power density of 849.8 W kg−1. In addition, the ASC shows excellent cycling stability of 91.3 % capacity retention after 10,000 cycles.

title: Protective hydrothermal treatment to improve ion pathway in Ti3C2Tx MXene for high-performance flexible supercapacitors
authors: M. Lai, K. Chen, D. Wang, P. Cai, L. Sun, K. Zhang, B. Li, C. Yuan, Y. Zou, Z. Wang, H. Peng
conclusion: In conclusion, the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx dispersion is treated by protective hydrothermal method to effectively improve ion pathway in Ti3 C2 Tx MXene. The protective hydrothermal treatment is simply conducted in the hydrothermal kettle (filled with N2 atmosphere) placed in vacuum oven. The optimal Ti3 C2 Tx is achieved by the hydrothermal treatment at 150 °C for 12h and thus recorded as h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h. The hydrothermal treatment contributes to the larger lattice spacing and decreased flake size for the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h nanosheets, and thus enables the significantly increased interlayer spacing and pores with obviously larger specific surface area for the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film, which can effectively improve ion transport pathways and enhance ions accessibility with more pseudocapacitive active sites. According to DFT calculations, a small number of oxides (TiO2 nanoparticles) produced during the hydrothermal treatment also facilitate to increase the capacitive performance of h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h. Therefore, the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrode offers significantly increased capacitance and rate performance. Compared with the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode (324.7 F g−1 /581 F cm−3 at 1 A g−1 ), the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrode shows significantly higher capacitance (498 F g−1 /1911 F cm−3 at 1 A g−1 ) with excellent rate performance (63 % retention from 1 to 20 A g−1 ) and cycling stability (98.2 % retention after 20 000 cycles), which are among the best electrochemical performances of undoped Ti3 C2 Tx based film electrodes reported so far. An ultra-high capacitance of 3.23 F cm−2 at 1 A g−1 is achieved for thick h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrode of 33.1 μm thickness. The flexible supercapacitor device with symmetric h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrodes and PVA-H2 SO4 gel electrolyte enables excellent energy storage performance (117 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and 23.4 Wh kg−1 at 299.8 W kg−1 ) with high cycling stability (84 % retention after 3000 cycles) and bending stability, outperforming most of previously reported Ti3 C2 Tx -based flexible supercapacitor devices. The impressive results indicate that the h-Ti3 C2 Tx @150 °C/12h film electrode possesses great application potential in flexible energy storage devices and the simply protective hydrothermal treatment could be also applicable to other MXenes. abstract: The strong re-stacking of Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets severely blocks ion transport pathway and sacrifices electrochemical performance. Here, a protective hydrothermal treatment is used to improve ion pathway in Ti3C2Tx MXene. The protective hydrothermal treatment is simply conducted in the hydrothermal kettle (filled with N2 atmosphere) placed in vacuum oven. The optimal Ti3C2Tx is achieved by the hydrothermal treatment of 150 °C for 12h, and recorded as h-Ti3C2Tx@150 °C/12h. The h-Ti3C2Tx@150 °C/12h film electrode achieves significantly improved ion transport pathways and enhanced ion accessibility with more pseudocapacitive active sites due to the increased interlayer spacing and pores as well as decreased flake size. According to DFT calculations, a small number of oxides (TiO2 nanoparticles) produced during the hydrothermal treatment also facilitate to increase the capacitive performance of h-Ti3C2Tx@150 °C/12h. Therefore, the h-Ti3C2Tx@150 °C/12h film electrode achieves significantly increased capacitance and rate performance. The h-Ti3C2Tx@150 °C/12h film electrode exhibits excellent capacitance (498.3 F g−1 and 1911 F cm−3 at 1 A g−1) and rate performance (63 % retention from 1 to 20 A g−1) with high cycling stability (98.2 % retention after 20 000 cycles), which are among the best electrochemical performances of undoped Ti3C2Tx based film electrodes reported so far. Thick h-Ti3C2Tx@150 °C/12h film electrode of 33.1 μm thickness exhibits an ultra-high areal capacitance of 3.23 F cm−2 at 1 A g−1. Moreover, the h-Ti3C2Tx@150 °C/12h-based flexible symmetric supercapacitor device exhibits excellent energy storage performance (117 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 and 23.4 Wh kg−1 at 299.8 W kg−1) with high cycling stability (84 % retention after 3000 cycles) and bending stability, outperforming most of previously reported Ti3C2Tx-based flexible supercapacitors. The impressive results indicate the great application potential of the h-Ti3C2Tx@150 °C/12h film in flexible energy storage devices.

title: Ti3AlC2 MAX phase and Ti3C2TX MXene-based composites towards supercapacitor applications: A comprehensive review of synthesis, recent progress, and challenges
authors: Onkar Jaywant Kewate, Sathyanarayanan Punniyakoti
conclusion: 7  Conclusion  Due to the exhaustion of energy sources like fossil fuels and growing energy needs, it is essential to find an alternative energy source. Recent decades have seen a surge in attention for supercapacitors owing to their distinctive properties like good power density, quick charging/discharging time, and longer cycle life. From the last decade, MXenes are emerging as a two-dimensional material in academic and industrial sectors for next-generation applications, especially for energy storage. Among from different types of MXenes, Ti 3 C 2 T X MXenes are widely attracted towards the supercapacitor due to their noteworthy benefits such as excellent conductivity, rapid surface terminations, hydrophilicity, unique surface chemistry, thermal conductivity, and structural diversity. The study of Ti 3 C 2 T X MXenes as an electrode for supercapacitors has witnessed significant growth within the last decade.  This review focuses on the latest research developments pertaining to MXenes and supercapacitors. In the recent period, various types of MXenes and their composites are synthesized and studied. Among the different MXenes. Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene is widely studied and still research is going on. In the current review, various synthesis methods for the MAX phase are well discussed. Among all approaches, the high-temperature method is the most efficient and widely used technique for making MAX phases. For preparing MXenes, the etching methods widely used are HF acid etching, fluoride-based etching, and f-free etching methods. Normally, fluoride-based compounds were used as an etchant. Till now HF etching and LiF-HCl etching approaches are used widely. Here, it is essential to keep in mind that the etching conditions would result in MXenes with a variety of distinctive morphologies and tunability surfaces. As a result, it is critical to choose a suitable approach for the objectives of the research. Delamination and intercalation using various acid-salt combinations as etchants are well described. When different acid-salt combinations were intercalated, it is observed that the c-LP considerably increased and changed depending on the functional groups. The interlayer distance of sheets is important along with this it improves the performance of supercapacitors by applying intercalation.  Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene is largely researched for supercapacitor electrodes due to its distinctive surface chemistry, significant surface area, electrical conductivity, and Young's modulus. It was found that the combination of these other materials, such as carbon/polymer/transition metal oxide materials, with Pure Ti 3 C 2 T X MXenes for supercapacitor electrode material, improved the overall mechanical strength and enhanced electrochemical performance. Activated carbon, CNTs, and 2D graphene have all been studied with Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene as an interlayer spacer in recent research to reduce restacking. Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene has strong pseudocapacitance, significant electrical conductivity, and extended cycle life as a result of the presence of transition metal oxides. However, the mechanical property possessed by Ti 3 C 2 T X /transition metal oxide composites are often observed to be low. The low temperature and environmentally friendly fabrication of the MAX phase is still found to be difficult. The less harmful and effective etching method to prepare Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene with improved oxidation stability and less restacking of MXenes sheets is a challenging task. Above mentioned factors which will directly affects the power density, energy density, and cycling stability of supercapacitor performance with notable advancements in supercapacitor electrodes in recent years, Ti 3 C 2 T X MXene shows exceptional promise for energy storage applications.  Thus, the current review gives an understanding of various synthesis of Ti 3 AlC 2 MAX phase and Ti 3 C 2 T X MXenes, there their electrochemical behaviour with other composites which will throw some light on the field of MXenes-based supercapacitors.
abstract: The global need for energy is increasing due to the growth in population and the widespread use of energy-consuming devices. In recent times, supercapacitors have emerged as a better option owing to their high-power density, quick charging/discharging, and extended cycle life. A burgeoning 2D material that consists of carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides called MXenes, has emerged as a superior active electrode material for supercapacitors owing to its novel structure, stability, enhanced electrical conductivity, large surface area, hydrophilicity, hydrophobicity and availability of abundant active sites. In addition to their favorable attributes, MXenes exhibit certain limitations that have to be addressed like sheet restacking and aggregation, which impede the progress of research on various applications, especially supercapacitors. The major focus of this article pertains to the synthesis techniques employed for the Ti3AlC2 MAX phase, as well as the diverse methods of etching, intercalation, and delamination utilized for the preparation of Ti3C2TX MXenes. In addition, investigations conducted on the efficacy of utilizing Ti3C2TX MXene in combination with polymer, carbon, and transition metal oxide based materials to enhance supercapacitor performance are reviewed. This review includes important challenges and up-to-date studies along with an analysis of research gaps and future directions in supercapacitor applications.

title: Synergistic Ti3C2Tx MXene quantum dot/nanosheet Hybrid: Elevating supercapacitor performance
authors: Bheem Kumar, Avinash Rundla,  Priyanka, Mahaveer Singh, Divya Rani, Pushpendra Kumar, Kedar Singh
conclusion: This study demonstrates the successful synthesis and characterization of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx , Water@Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol@Ti3 C2 Tx , highlighting their synergistic improvements in electrochemical performance. Ti3 C2 Tx was synthesized via the etching of MAX-phase precursors in an acidic solution to remove the Al layer, forming a combination of nanosheets and MQDs that enhance the surface area for charge and ion transport. The materials were characterized via XRD for their crystal structure, FTIR for their functional groups, TEM for their morphological analysis, and UV–vis and PL spectroscopy for their optical properties. Electrochemical studies were performed in a three-electrode system with 1 M H2 SO4 as the electrolyte, with the materials coated on nickel foil used as working electrodes. CV, GCD, and EIS analyses demonstrated significant enhancements in the specific capacitance and charge transfer properties of Water@Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol@Ti3 C2 Tx compared with those of pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . Both materials exhibited higher specific capacitances across varying current densities (1–5 Ag-1 ) and scan rates (10-200 mVs−1 ). The EIS results further revealed a reduced Rct and Rs in Water@Ti3 C2 Tx and Ethanol@Ti3 C2 Tx , indicating superior electrochemical kinetics. These findings underscore the potential of functionalized Ti3 C2 Tx materials for advanced energy storage applications. abstract: Supercapacitors are promising energy storage devices, offering a unique combination of high energy and power densities. This study systematically investigated the synergistic effect of a Ti3C2Tx-MXene quantum dot (MQD)/nanosheet hybrid on supercapacitor performance. Ti3C2Tx MQDs are synthesized through a two-step process: first, Ti3C2Tx MXene 2D sheets are prepared via acidic etching of precursor materials. A combined hydrothermal (water-based) and solvothermal (ethanol-based) treatment at 150 °C reduces the sheet size, producing MQDs. The electrochemical performance of the MQD/nanosheet hybrid was evaluated via a three-electrode configuration with 1 M H2SO4 as the electrolyte. Galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) tests at current densities ranging from 1 to 5 Ag-1 revealed a significant improvement in the specific capacitance under all tested conditions. Similarly, CV at scan rates of 10–200 mVs−1 demonstrated an enhanced charge storage capability and superior rate performance, which was attributed to the synergistic effects of the MQDs. EIS confirmed the reduced charge-transfer resistance and excellent capacitive behavior across a wide frequency range. The enhancement in the results is due to the high surface area, remarkable electrical conductivity, and abundant electrochemically active sites of the MQDs. This study highlights the potential of Ti3C2Tx MQD/nanosheet hybrids as high-performance materials for next-generation supercapacitors, paving the way for their integration into advanced energy storage systems.

title: Hierarchical MOF-derived Selenide/Ti3C2Tx hybrids for high-performance supercapacitors
authors: Yuhan Cui, Jing Sun, Yining Wang, Lijie Zhao, Jiawei Wang, Yunpeng Wu, Wenxi Zhang, Zengyuan Fan, Yuzhe Tang, Yue Song, Zhongmin Su
conclusion: 4  Conclusion  In this study, 2D/2D composites were fabricated utilizing 2D MXene as the substrate and 2D MOF as a precursor. Subsequently, MXene/Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se-5 wavy bimetallic selenide materials were synthesized through a hydrothermal selenization method employing MOF as a sacrificial template. The macroporous structure of 2D-MXene in combination with the wave-like microstructure of Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se constitutes a multi-layered architecture with enhanced conductivity and accelerated electron transfer rate. At the same time, MXene/Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se composites as electrode materials have high specific surface area and synergistic effect on binary metal selenides, significantly improving supercapacitors’ storage performance. Therefore, the specific capacitance of the MXene/Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se electrode can reach 1126 F g −1 at 1 A g −1 current density, and the capacitance retention can reach 70.98 % after 10,000 charge-discharge cycles at 10 A g −1 . After assembling the asymmetric supercapacitor (BC//MXene/Mn 0.8 Ni 0.2 Se-5), when the power density is 750 W kg −1 , the energy density of 46.18 Wh kg −1 can be provided, and the specific capacitance of the device after 10,000 charge and discharge cycles is 79.06 % of the initial value. The excellent long-cycle stability indicates that the device has a practical application prospect. In conclusion, our work not only provides an efficient approach to enhance the specific capacitance performance of selenide supercapacitor electrode materials but also reveals the significance of topography engineering optimization and furnishes valuable perspectives for the rational design of more two-dimensional structures with excellent electrochemical properties for energy storage configuration.
abstract: The slow kinetics and poor structural stability prevent 2D transition metal selenides from wide application in supercapacitors. However, as a representative of new two-dimensional materials, Ti3C2TX (MXene) has excellent transport properties and rich surface functional groups, which can well make up for the shortcomings of metal selenides. The optimized morphology engineering from a combination of MXene and 2D bimetallic selenide will bring the performance of supercapacitor electrode material to a new level. In this paper, MXene/Mn0.8Ni0.2Se composites are creatively prepared by ultrasonic stirring and solvothermal synthesis. The hierarchically layered composite electrode material composed of MXene nanosheets and selenide nanosheets is successfully synthesized and its electrochemical performance as electrode material for supercapacitors is studied. The results show water not only promotes the deprotonation of triethylamine to participate in coordination but also causes triethylamine to generate OH−, which makes it easier to form layered products and restrict the growth of NiMn-Metal Organic Framework (MOF) into a three-dimensional structure. Subsequently, during the selenization process, a small amount of water and disodium ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid are added to further promote the stability of the 2D/2D structure. The wavy hierarchically layered structure can shorten the diffusion path of metal ions and enhance electronic conductivity. As a supercapacitor material, under the current density of 1 A g−1, the specific capacitance of MXene/Mn0.8Ni0.2Se is 1126 F g−1. This capacity is higher than most selenide capacities reported to date. In addition, the energy density of the asymmetric supercapacitor constructed with activated carbon as cathode and Mn0.8Ni0.2Se as anode can reach 46.18 Wh kg−1 when the power density is 750 W kg−1. The outstanding specific capacitance and high energy density endow it with great potential for practical application.

title: Synergistic in-situ intercalation and surface modification strategy for Ti3C2Tx MXene-based supercapacitors with enhanced electrochemical energy storage
authors: Zhiyu Li, Mingyue Jiang, Fangfei Wu, Lili Wu, Xitian Zhang, Lu Li
conclusion: In summary, a synergistic in-situ intercalation and surface modification strategy for enhancing the electrochemical performance of Ti3 C2 Tx is demonstrated. Ag nanoparticles were intercalated into the interlayers of Ti3 C2 Tx using an in-situ reduction method to open ion diffusion channels and expose active sites, followed by annealing treatment to remove the deleterious termination. Benefitting from the structural modification, the obtained a-Ag/Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode possess an enhanced specific capacitance of 471 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 with a 2-fold increase in intercalation pseudocapacitance compared to the pristine Ti3 C2 Tx . The enlarged interlayer space was able to transport ions rapidly and stably through the support of Ag NPs, giving the a-Ag/Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode process an exceptional rate performance of 88.3 % capacitance retention as the current density increase to 15 A g−1 and a stability of 100 % capacitance retention after 20,000 cycles. In addition, the asymmetric supercapacitor with a negative electrode of a-Ag/Ti3 C2 Tx and a positive electrode of RuO2 @CC delivers a high energy density of 24.6 Wh kg−1 . The present study demonstrates an effective strategy to improve the electrochemical energy storage of the Ti3 C2 Tx negative electrode by designing the intercalation and termination. abstract: Ti3C2Tx MXene with unique physicochemical properties is a promising negative electrode for high performance supercapacitors, but its full potential for energy storage is limited by inherent restacking and unfavorable F surface termination. Here, a synergistic in-situ intercalation and surface modification strategy for enhancing the electrochemical performance of Ti3C2Tx is demonstrated. Ag nanoparticles were intercalated into the interplanar s of Ti3C2Tx using an in-situ reduction method to open ion diffusion channels and expose active sites, followed by annealing treatment to remove the deleterious termination. Benefitting from the structural modification, the obtained a-Ag/Ti3C2Tx film electrode possess an enhanced specific capacitance of 471 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 with a 2-fold increase in intercalation pseudocapacitance compared to the pristine Ti3C2Tx, accompanied by improved rate performance and cyclic stability. Furthermore, the asymmetric supercapacitor with a negative electrode of a-Ag/Ti3C2Tx and a positive electrode of RuO2@CC delivers a high energy density of 24.6 Wh kg−1. The present study demonstrates an effective strategy to improve the electrochemical energy storage of the Ti3C2Tx negative electrode by designing the intercalation and termination.

title: Tag paper substrate enhanced self-assembled graphene oxide-Ti3C2Tx MXene composites for supercapacitors applications via laser processing
authors: Xiu-Yan Fu, Hua-Rui Li, Ruo-Yu Shu, Hao-Bo Jiang, Meng-Nan Yao, Jia-Nan Ma
conclusion: In conclusion, we proposed a new strategy to fabricate LIRGO-based supercapacitors, in which self-assembled GO-M composites and paper substrates collaborate. On the one hand, the self-assembled GO-M not only hinders the restacking of GO sheets to some degree but also renders the LIRGO high conductivity after the DLW of GO. Conversely, the numerous cellulose network structures offered by the paper substrates enabled LIRGO to exhibit better capacity and flexibility. Therefore, R-GO-M-P-based supercapacitors show good electrochemical performance, including a significantly higher specific capacitance value of 15.5 mF/cm2 compared to that of RGO-G (4.05 mF/cm2 ) and a good stability of 93.35 % retention of specific capacitance after 1000 cycles of charge-discharge tests. Moreover, R-GO-M-P-based supercapacitors also exhibited excellent flexibility, where after 1000 cycles of bending tests, the specific capacitance retention was as high as 142 %. Notably, in-series R-GO-M-P supercapacitors can be obtained using a programmable DLW process, that extends the working potential extension for powering an LED. We believe that this study will enhance the applications of LIRGO-based supercapacitors in future electronics. abstract: Laser-induced reduced graphene oxide (LIRGO) has exhibited great potential for energy storage device applications. However, challenges remain in regard to solving the restacking of graphene oxide (GO) sheets and conductivity differences after laser processing. In this study, we used direct laser writing (DLW) to fabricate self-assembled graphene oxide-Ti3C2Tx MXene (GO-M) composites on tag paper for planar supercapacitors. Due to the cooperation of interaction between electronegative GO and Ti3C2Tx MXene and introduction of paper substrate with cellulose network structure, the as-prepared composite (R-GO-M-P) based supercapacitor exhibits much higher specific capacitance (15.5 mF/cm2) than that of LIRGO on glass substrate (4.05 mF/cm2). We observed a good stability of 93.35 % specific capacitance retention scores after 1000 charge-discharge cycles. Moreover, the R-GO-M-P-based supercapacitor also displayed excellent flexibility due to the existence of paper substrate, with a 142 % specific capacitance retention after 1000 bending test cycles. The integrated R-GO-M-P-based supercapacitors were fabricated according to a programmable DLW pattern, that achieved an extended working potential of 2.4 V and could power an LED. We hope that this study offers a new strategy for the development of high-performance LIRGO-based supercapacitors.

title: Probing the synergistic effect of MXene (Ti3C2Tx) and MWCNTs on NiWO4 for superior water-splitting and supercapacitor studies
authors: Amna Irshad, Mirza Mahmood Baig, Seung Goo Lee, Imran Shakir, Zeid A. ALOthman, Muhammad Farooq Warsi, Muhammad Shahid
conclusion: A simple approach is used to fabricate NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs. The fabricated samples are analyzed via different physio-chemical characterizations. The prepared materials are used to study water splitting and supercapacitors. The cyclic voltammetry experiment in non-Faradaic regions finds the electrochemical active surface area. NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs exhibits more ECSA (216 cm2 ) as compared to NiWO4 and NiWO4 /MXene. Tafel slope is explored to evaluate the kinetics of the catalyst for HER and OER performance. NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs shows Tafel slope of 77 and 91 mV/dec for HER and OER, respectively. The CNTs-based composite shows good response for oxidation and reduction reactions during cyclic voltammetric measurements. The prepared samples show pseudocapacitive behaviour during the electrochemical study. NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs composite exhibits more discharge time of 500 s compared to NiWO4 (276 s) and NiWO4 /MXene (390 s). NiWO4 , NiWO4 /MXene, and NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs show specific capacitance of 690, 975, and 1250F/g, respectively. The efficient performance of NiWO4 /MXene@CNTs for both water splitting and supercapacitor study is attributed to the increased surface area, more exposed active sites, and less charge transfer resistance. These attributes make it an excellent candidate for advanced electrochemical study. CRediT authorship contribution statement Amna Irshad: Writing – original draft, Methodology. Muhammad Shahid: Conceptualization.
abstract: The main focus of the ongoing worldwide research is the production and storage of green energy via electrochemical study. MXene (2D) and multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs (1D)) play enormous roles in enhancing the efficiency of nanomaterials for electrochemical measurements. A wet chemical approach is employed to synthesize NiWO4. The nanocomposite of NiWO4 with MXene and MWCNTs is prepared via ultrasonication approach. Structural, morphological and elemental aspects of the prepared samples are investigated via different characterization techniques. Hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions are performed in an alkaline solution. NiWO4/MXene@CNTs shows Tafel slope of 77 and 91 mV/dec for HER and OER, respectively. Supercapacitor performance is evaluated via cyclic voltammetry (CV) and galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD) experiments. The current response shown by the materials is best analyzed through CV measurements. NiWO4/MXene@CNTs composite exhibits discharge time of 500 s as compared to NiWO4 (276 s) and NiWO4/MXene (390 s). NiWO4/MXene@CNTs composite shows specific capacitance and retention of 1250 F/g and 80 %, respectively. The resistance faced by the materials during electrochemical measurements is analyzed using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. MXene and MWCNTs boost the efficiency of NiWO4 via synergistic effect and make it a potential material for water splitting and supercapacitor study.

title: Human-friendly flexible solid-state biodegradable supercapacitor based on Ti3C2Tx MXene film without adhesive structure
authors: Xiaofeng Zhang, Muhammad Sufyan Javed, Hongjia Ren, Xinze Zhang, Salamat Ali, Kaiming Han, Awais Ahmad, Ammar M. Tighezza, Weihua Han, Kui-Qing Peng
conclusion: In this study, Ti3 C2 Tx films were prepared by vacuum filtration, which showed superior electrochemical performance in FSBSCs. The adhesive-free structure of Ti3 C2 Tx film reduces the internal resistance of the electrode material and promotes the transport of electrons. In addition, the larger crystal plane spacing of Ti3 C2 Tx film provides more active sites for electrolyte ions, improving electrochemical performance. The Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode shows a remarkable electrochemical performance, including a peak capacitance of 768 F/g at 1 A/g, impressive rate capability (65.1% at 20 A/g), and notable capacitance retention (98.9%) after 10,000 charge/discharge cycles at 10 A/g. The assembled Ti3 C2 Tx //NaCl-PVA//Ti3 C2 Tx -FSBSC exhibited a high capacitance of 112 F/g at 1 A/g and a high energy density of 62.3 Wh/kg at 1,000.8 W/kg, coupled with exceptional cycle stability, retaining 98.9% after 5,000 cycles. We carried out biodegradation experiments, Ti3 C2 Tx film electrode and assembled solid-state biodegradable supercapacitor (SBSC) devices showed good degradability in a H2 O2 solution and could be completely degraded within 30 h. In addition, the DFT calculations proved the excellent performance of the Ti3 C2 Tx electrode material through excellent electronic properties, higher E ads, and lower diffusion energy barrier of the Na+ ions. This work provides a new direction for the development of safer and more effective implantable biodegradable bioenergy storage devices. abstract: With the rapid development of biomedical technology, biodegradable and implantable energy storage devices for biosensor and bioelectronics applications have attracted the great attention of scientists. However, the limited energy density, poor biocompatibility, and excessive space occupation of existing biodegradable energy storage devices pose major challenges to their application in the biomedical field. To address these challenges, in this work, flexible Ti3C2Tx film with an adhesive-free structure construction is proposed as electrode material for the flexible solid-state biodegradable supercapacitor (FSBSC). The morphology and structure of MXene films were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). A 0.9% NaCl saline, similar human body fluids was used as the electrolyte solution to construct symmetrical FSBSC (Ti3C2Tx//NaCl-PVA//Ti3C2Tx-FSBSC) Poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA). The Ti3C2Tx//NaCl-PVA//Ti3C2Tx-FSBSC exhibits a high capacitance of 112 F/g at 1 A/g, excellent rate capability (73.2% at 20 A/g), long lifetime (81.6% after 10,000 cycles), and high specific energy/power (62.3 Wh/kg at 1000.8 W/kg). The charge storage mechanism was analyzed using ex situ XRD, TEM, and density function theory (DFT). DFT results show that the Ti3C2Tx (Tx = O)) electrode possesses metallic properties. The calculated adsorption energies (Eads) and smaller diffusion barriers of Na+ ions further proved the outstanding performance of the Ti3C2Tx electrode. Moreover, the apparatus is entirely biodegradable, thereby paving a promising path for the progression of bioelectronics and biomedical energy storage technologies.

title: Sandwich-like high-performance Ti3C2Tx MXene/NiCo2O4 nanosphere composites for asymmetric supercapacitor application
authors: Wei Wang, Guohui Chen, Weiqi Kong, Junshu Chen, Linyu Pu, Jiaxu Gong, Huan Zhang, Yatang Dai
conclusion: In general, Ti3 C2 Tx MXene/NiCo2 O4 composites were prepared by electrostatic self-assembly of modified NiCo2 O4 nanoparticles. The Ti3 C2 Tx MXene/NiCo2 O4 composites showed excellent electrochemical properties, and their capacities were much higher than that of the NiCo2 O4 microspheres. Moreover, the Ti3 C2 Tx MXene/NiCo2 O4 (M2-N1) composite showed excellent rate performance (10 A g−1 and 81 % initial capacity) and cycling stability (82.2 % after 5000 cycles). In addition, an asymmetric M2-N1 supercapacitor showed excellent electrochemical performance and cycling stability (88.2 % capacity retention after 5000 cycles) and a high energy density of 36.67 Wh kg−1 at a 800 W kg−1 power density. This work provides a strategy for the preparation of composite materials with high stabilities and high energy densities, and it has good application prospects. abstract: NiCo2O4 is a promising electrode material for supercapacitors due to its low cost, high theoretical specific capacitance and good cycling stability. However, NiCo2O4 has the disadvantages of poor electronic and ionic conductivities and easy agglomeration. Moreover, the irreversible structural damage caused by the NiCo2O4 volume expansions during charging and discharging limits its use in supercapacitors. Herein, we fabricated sandwich Ti3C2Tx MXene/NiCo2O4 composites via an electrostatic self-assembly method. The problem of easy agglomeration of the NiCo2O4 nanospheres was solved by intercalating Ti3C2Tx MXene layers with the NiCo2O4 nanospheres. Furthermore, the Ti3C2Tx MXene layer was also utilized as a protective layer to limit serious volume expansion and protect the structure of NiCo2O4 nanospheres from destruction. The results showed that the prepared Ti3C2Tx MXene/NiCo2O4 composite exhibited a high specific capacitance of 1025 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1 and had an initial capacity of 81 % when the current density was increased to 10 A g−1. The Ti3C2Tx MXene/NiCo2O4 composite cathode and activated carbon anode were assembled in an asymmetric supercapacitor, which showed an energy density of 36.67 Wh kg−1 at 800 W kg−1 and a capacity retention of 88.2 % after 5000 cycles.

title: Ammonia-assisted heterocyclic amine exerts soft delamination and interlayer engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene for fabricating stable supercapacitors
authors: Arumugam Sangili, Binesh Unnikrishnan, Shun Ruei Hu, Han-Wei Chu, Hung-Lung Chou, Ren-Siang Wu, Chih-Ching Huang, Huan-Tsung Chang
conclusion: Highly stable Ti3 C2 Tx modified with heterocyclic aromatic amines were prepared from the multilayer-MXene without sonication. Our study provides a significant understanding of 5-Az for assisting the soft delamination, enhancing the chemical stability of Ti3 C2 Tx against air oxidation, and enhancing its electrochemical activities by increasing the active sites and interlayer spacing of adjacent Ti3 C2 Tx sheets. The 5-Az-protected Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited high oxidation resistance in aqueous medium and was stable for up to 500 days. 5-Az acted as the active species for intercalation and assisted in the soft delamination of the m -Ti3 C2 Tx layers into single-layer Ti3 C2 Tx . Based on our experimental and computational explorations, we concluded that the NH4 OH-5-Az/Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited excellent chemical oxidation stability over 150 days at room temperature, over 24 days at 70 °C, and over 24 h in 10 mM H2 O2 solution due to surface passivation by 5-Az via covalent and hydrogen bonding with the surface Ti-atoms. NH4 OH-5-Az/Ti3 C2 Tx enables an increased electrolyte-accessible area, enhanced charge-transport properties, and improved charge storage and discharge performance. In a three-electrode system, the NH4 OH-5-Az/Ti3 C2 Tx exhibited a specific capacitance of 631 F g−1 at a current density of 2 A g–1 and capacitance retention of 90 % even after 10,000 cycles at 10 A g−1 . Our NH4 OH-5-Az/Ti3 C2 Tx SSC displays energy and power densities of 59.1 Wh kg–1 and 1440 W kg–1 , respectively, showing their great potential in various energy applications. abstract: The application of two-dimensional titanium carbide MXenes (Ti3C2Tx) for electrochemical energy storage and conversion has garnered considerable attention in recent years. For practical applications, gradual delamination, phase shift, and/or structural disintegration of MXene flakes in aqueous conditions are the challenges needed to be addressed. Herein, a unique and effective approach for in situ manipulation of MXene edge and surface by gentle delamination using 5-azaindole (5-Az; a heterocyclic amine) and ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH) has been developed. In the presence of NH4OH, 5-Az enables soft delamination of multilayer MXene without sonication, and more importantly, allows in situ functionalization of its surface and edges via a nucleophilic substitution reaction at the Ti-atom sites at room temperature. In addition, the easy intercalation of 5-Az in the multilayer MXene allows for an increase in its interlayer spacing when it is made into a film or electrode, which is beneficial for various electrochemical applications. The 5-Az functionalization provides exceptional stability of MXenes for up to 500 days in water at room temperature. The NH4OH-treated- and 5-Az-functionalized MXene (NH4OH-5-Az/Ti3C2Tx) shows increased interlayer spacing (1.67 nm) when compared to the MXene treated with NH4OH (NH4OH-Ti3C2Tx) (1.25 nm), enhanced ion- and charge-transport properties resulting in a remarkable specific capacitance of 631 F g–1 at 2 A g–1 with capacitance retention of 82 % after 150 days. Having high specific capacitance and excellent stability, the NH4OH-5-Az/Ti3C2Tx prepared through the proposed simple and effective approach holds great potential as high-performance electrodes for supercapacitors.

title: Hybrid nano-architectural engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene heterostructures for supercapacitor applications: A review
authors: Mojtaba Rostami, Parisa Rezvaninia, Ahmad Amiri, Ghodsi Mohammadi Ziarani, Mohammad Reza Ganjali, Alireza Badiei
conclusion: 3  Conclusions and future outlook  Despite the challenges in the architectural engineering of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene, these materials remain a promising candidate for SC devices. By addressing these challenges and working towards future goals, we can develop more efficient and effective Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene-based SC devices to alleviate the current energy crisis and shortcomings of existing energy storage devices. SCs, in particular, are crucial for meeting high-energy peak power demands over short periods in certain areas. They possess desirable properties such as long cycling stability, good safety and high power density. The electrical double-layer method, however, places a cap on the capacitance of conventional SCs that use Ti 3 C 2 T  x  -based nanomaterials. As a result, researchers have turned to pseudo capacitive materials, like transition metal phosphides/oxides/sulfides/hydroxides, layered double hydroxides/oxide/phosphides/sulfides, MOFs, MOF-derived hybrid NAs, COFs and Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene, for the creation of SCs with excellent performance and secondary rechargeable batteries. This field has received significant attention in the past several years.  To enhance the effectiveness of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  -based SC devices and mitigate restacking resulting from excessive functional groups, we propose the utilization of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  -based hybrid NAs with materials such as COFs, LDH, TMC, MOFs, and MOF derivatives. Furthermore, we will delve into their capacitive performance. It is a potential strategy to improve the active sites and encourage rapid ion diffusion speeds in MOFs to use pseudocapacitive redox centers. However, MOFs' weak conductivity, which is insufficient for several fields, prevents their practical implementation. To address this challenge, a viable solution involves creating an aerogel structure with hierarchical porosity by growing MOFs within a two- and 3D Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene framework that exhibits high conductivity (MOFs@Ti 3 C 2 T  x  aerogel). This hybrid material combines the advantageous functional properties of both MOFs and Ti 3 C 2 T  x  , providing high surface areas and is expected to demonstrate brilliant electrochemical energy storage behavior.  The bimetallic sulfide LDH/Ti 3 C 2 T  x  nanocomposite, with its unique 2D hierarchical structure and large S BET , can potentially expand the electrochemical performance of SCs. This is because it can make the entire electrode material more electronically conductive and structurally stable, which speeds up electron transport and reduces the length of ion diffusion routes during charge/discharge operations. Furthermore, because of their in-plane charge delocalization, extensive π-conjugation, broad ion-accessible surface, and adequate redox active sites, which help to boost Pseudocapacitance, 2D MOFs are interesting electrode materials. It is indeed evident that Ti 3 C 2 T  x  has the potential to become a superior electrode material for energy storage devices. However, there are still numerous areas that need to be explored to fully realize its potential. Some primary future goals highlighted via recent studies include: (i) Developing new synthesis methods to improve the scalability and cost-effectiveness of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene production. (ii) Increasing the electrical conductivity of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene via techniques like doping or surface alterations. (iii) To improve the electrochemical activity of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene, novel nanocomposite materials based on MXene are being investigated. (iv) Investigating the long-term stability and reliability of energy storage technologies based on Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene. (v) Constructing useable Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene-based energy storage (SCs) technology, Examples include in electric vehicles or renewable energy systems. (vi) Conducting advanced scientific research to better understand tunability, the surface chemistry and interlayer structure of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene for optimal device fabrication. (vii) Developing extra heterostructure and hybrid materials NAs based on other MXene family members, particularly non-Ti-based MXene, to enhance performance and improve the applications available. (viii) Fabrication of transparent, flexible and miniaturized Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene based SCs could greatly expand their practical applications. (ix)The generation of magnetic Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes and the creation of conductivity in Ti 3 C 2 T  x  could also create a new possibilities for energy storage and other applications. (x) Standardization and cost reduction of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene-based electrodes for device manufacturing would make them more accessible to a wider range of users. Finally, the presence of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXene-based electrodes in the international energy market would guarantee that their potential advantages are felt globally. Addressing these goals will require continued research and innovation within the domain of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  -based SCs. Nevertheless, Ti 3 C 2 T  x  will undoubtedly remain to have a significant role in the advancement of storing energy technology with extremely effective performance given the encouraging outcomes so far.  The quest for cost-effective, versatile, and durable energy storage solutions has been a driving force behind advancements in electronics and related fields amidst the current era of industrialization. Among the myriad options 2D stratified nanomaterials have emerged as promising contenders for high-efficiency energy storage devices, owing to their Chemical, structural, and physical properties. Notably, 2D Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes, a class of transition metal carbides/nitrides characterized by thin thickness, tunable electrochemical properties, high conductivity, and abundant active edge sites, have garnered significant attention in material science circles.  In the realm of electrochemical energy storage technologies, particularly SCs, Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes stand out as excellent electrode materials. However, the practical utilization of MXenes has encountered challenges stemming from issues such as aggregation, oxidation, and restacking within their layers. To surmount these hurdles, this study investigates various categories of 2D nanomaterials exhibiting noteworthy electrochemical activity. These encompass COFs, TMCs, LDHs, MOFs, and MOF derivatives, which hold promise for synergistic integration with Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes. Nanoarchitectural engineering techniques are employed to enhance the performance of these 2D nanomaterials, both individually and in composite configurations with the metallic conductive 2D Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes, within SCs.  Core Findings: (I) The investigation highlights the potential of diverse 2D nanomaterials and their composite nanoarchitectures (NAs) for improving the performance of supercapacitors. (ii) Notable electrochemical activity is observed in various 2D nanomaterials, including COFs, TMCs, LDHs, and MOFs, suggesting their suitability for energy storage applications. (iii) Integration of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes with these 2D nanomaterials enhances the electrochemical performance of supercapacitors, indicating the feasibility of composite approaches for energy storage device optimization.  Problems Addressed: (I) Challenges associated with MXenes, such as aggregation, oxidation, and restacking, are acknowledged and addressed through the exploration of alternative 2D nanomaterials and composite strategies. (ii) By diversifying the range of materials considered for energy storage applications, the study seeks to mitigate the limitations imposed by MXene-related issues.  Results Achieved: (i) The investigation demonstrates the feasibility of enhancing supercapacitor performance through the strategic integration of Ti 3 C 2 T  x  MXenes with various 2D nanomaterials. (ii) Improved electrochemical activity and stability are observed in composite nanoarchitectures, indicating the potential for overcoming MXene-related challenges and advancing energy storage technologies.  Limitations of the Advantages Studies: (I) While the study explores the potential of diverse 2D nanomaterials and composite approaches, it may not comprehensively address all possible challenges or solutions in the field of energy storage. (ii) Practical implementation and scalability of the proposed nanoarchitectures may require further investigation and validation.  In conclusion, this review contributes to the ongoing efforts to develop high-performance energy storage solutions tailored to the demands of the contemporary industrial revolution. By examining a range of 2D nanomaterials and their composite configurations, the study offers insights into promising avenues for advancing supercapacitor technology.
abstract: The rising need for cost-effective, versatile, and durable energy storage devices has propelled progress in electronics and associated fields in the present era of industrialization. Due to their tactile, structural, and aesthetic qualities, two-dimensional (2D) stratified nanomaterials have developed as attractive rivals for high-efficiency energy retention devices. 2D MXenes, a type of transition metal carbides/nitrides via thin thickness, adjustable electrochemical characteristics, high conductivity, and a plentiful supply of active edge sites, have drawn much attention in the area of material science. For advanced electrochemical energy storage technologies like supercapacitors (SCs), Ti3C2Tx MXenes are particularly well-suited as electrode materials. The utilization of MXenes has faced inhibitions due to the aggregation, oxidation, and restacking phenomena occurring within their layers. To overcome these obstacles, this investigation delves into various categories of 2D nanomaterials exhibiting notable electrochemical activity. These encompass covalent organic frameworks (COFs), transition metal chalcogenides (TMCs), layered double hydroxides (LDHs), metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), and their derivatives, which hold promise for synergistic coupling with Ti3C2Tx MXenes. Nanoarchitectural engineering structures are employed to enhance the performance of these 2D nanomaterials, both individually and in composites with the metallic conductive 2D Ti3C2Tx MXenes, within SCs. The review summarizes the present developments, challenges, and future perspectives associated with applying Ti3C2Tx MXenes nanomaterial and their hybrid composite nanoarchitectures (NAs) for SC. This review endeavors to advance high-performance energy storage innovations that meet the demands of the contemporary industrial revolution. It achieves this by exploring the potential of diverse 2D nanomaterials and their composite nanoarchitectures (NAs).

title: Enhanced performance of Fe2O3/MXene based supercapacitors with redox-electrolyte strategy
authors: Jing Xu, Xinye Xu, Xiaoqing Bin, Yingyi Liao, Xuedong He, Wenxiu Que
conclusion: We propose a dual-optimization strategy: (1) the Fe2 O3 /MXene composite electrodes were fabricated via filtration process and annealing treatment, where Fe2 O3 nanoparticles are uniformly anchored on MXene nanosheets to both mitigate re-stacking of Ti3 C2 Tx MXene and provide additional redox-active sites; (2) A hybrid redox electrolyte (3 M H₂SO₄ + 30 mM CuSO4 ) was introduced to synergistically enhance charge storage via Cu2+ /Cu+ redox reactions. Thus, the optimized Fe2 O3 /MXene-5 composite electrode achieves a specific capacitance of 643.8 F g−1 at 2 A g−1 , which is attributed to reconstructed interfacial charge distribution that facilitates rapid ion adsorption and electron transfer. Furthermore, the fabricated Fe2 O3 /MXene-5–ASC delivers a high energy density of 20.1 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 1292.5 W kg−1 . This approach is anticipated to demonstrate significant potential as an electrolyte modification strategy, owing to strong interfacial interactions between Fe2 O3 /MXene based supercapacitors and redox electrolytes. Moreover, it could be extended to diverse composite systems, paving the way for further advancements in designing high-performance materials in the future.
